United States Undergraduate Admissions and Need-Based Financial Aid

Common App Scholarships and Fully Funded University Opportunities

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | Fall 2027 Entry

What this opportunity is: A collection of US universities that accept applications through Common App and provide need-based financial assistance, institutional scholarships or dedicated financial support pathways for international, refugee and displaced students.

Application platform: Common Application

Financial aid providers: Individual universities

Destination: United States of America

Study level: First-year undergraduate / Bachelor's degree

Target applicants: International students, refugees, displaced students and applicants from financially disadvantaged backgrounds who demonstrate academic potential and financial need.

Funding: Need-based grants, institutional scholarships, full demonstrated-need packages and selected merit scholarships.

Application limit: Up to 20 colleges on one Common App account.

Application period: 2026–2027 application cycle for Fall 2027 admission.

Last researched: 4 November 2026.

Before You Apply: Understand What Common App Is

Common App is not a scholarship provider. It is an online platform that allows students to prepare one main undergraduate application and submit it to participating colleges and universities.

Each university independently decides whether to admit you, whether you qualify for financial aid and how much assistance you will receive.

The universities featured on this page have been selected because they have institutional need-based financial aid policies, substantial scholarship opportunities or participation in a recognised refugee and displaced-student initiative.

This is particularly important for students who cannot afford international tuition, accommodation, food and other university expenses without substantial financial assistance.

Understanding the Different Funding Policies

1. Need-blind admission and full demonstrated need

Need-blind admission means the university does not consider your family's ability to pay when deciding whether to admit you. Once admitted, the university commits to meeting 100% of your demonstrated financial need according to its own calculation.

This is one of the most attractive policies for international applicants who need substantial financial assistance.

2. Need-aware admission and full demonstrated need

Need-aware admission means the university considers your financial circumstances during the admission process. Requesting a large amount of financial aid may make admission more competitive.

However, some need-aware universities promise to meet 100% of the demonstrated financial need of students they admit and fund.

3. Need-based scholarships

These are grants or scholarships determined by your family's financial circumstances rather than academic achievement alone. They may cover a substantial portion of tuition and living expenses.

Some universities combine need-based assistance with merit scholarships and campus employment.

4. Merit-based scholarships

Merit scholarships recognise academic performance, leadership, extracurricular involvement, talent or other achievements. Some are substantial, but many cover only part of the total cost.

Do not assume that receiving a merit scholarship automatically means you can afford the remaining expenses.

The list contains both highly selective universities and institutions with comparatively broader admission profiles. However, a university with a higher overall admission rate does not necessarily have a higher admission rate for international students requesting substantial financial assistance.

Global Student Haven Initiative: A Dedicated Pathway for Displaced Students

The Global Student Haven Initiative is a collaboration between participating American universities intended to help refugees, displaced students and people affected by conflict or natural disasters access undergraduate education in the United States.

Its founding institutions are:

  • Bowdoin College
  • California Institute of Technology (Caltech)
  • Dartmouth College
  • New York University
  • Pomona College
  • Smith College
  • Trinity College, Connecticut
  • Williams College

Participating institutions commit to providing financial aid to first-year undergraduate students with demonstrated need whom they admit. The initiative also seeks to connect displaced students with support services after arrival, including appropriate housing and other campus assistance.

Important: Global Student Haven is not a separate scholarship that students receive simply by registering. You must still apply to the participating university and satisfy its admission and financial aid requirements.

The initiative is not exclusively restricted to refugees. Its participating institutions also aim to support other students affected by conflict, displacement and humanitarian crises.

The initiative primarily focuses on first-year undergraduate applicants. Financial aid for transfer applicants is determined separately by each institution. Graduate applicants are not covered by the initiative.

Visit the official Global Student Haven Initiative website

Understanding Acceptance Rates and Your Admission Chances

One of the most important things to consider before applying is how selective a university is.

A university may have excellent financial aid but receive thousands of applications for a limited number of places. This means that having a full-need financial aid policy does not automatically make admission easy.

How the acceptance-rate categories work

  • Below 5%: Extremely selective. Treat these universities as high-reach applications.
  • 5%–15%: Very competitive. Admission remains difficult, especially for applicants requiring substantial international financial aid.
  • Above 15%: Comparatively broader admission rates, but this does not mean admission is likely. Check the international admission rate separately.
  • Not reported: Do not assume the university has a high acceptance rate simply because no figure is available.

Important: A high acceptance rate is not a guarantee of funding

Some universities admit a larger proportion of international students but provide limited financial assistance. Others offer excellent funding but admit very few international applicants.

For students who cannot finance their education independently, the financial aid policy must remain a priority alongside the admission rate.

Do not choose a university simply because its acceptance rate looks attractive. First establish whether its financial aid can cover the expenses you cannot afford.

Why international acceptance rates matter

International students may be evaluated in a different admissions category from domestic students. At some institutions, international applicants requesting substantial aid compete within a particularly limited financial aid budget.

For example, Oberlin reports that approximately 8–10% of international applicants are admitted in a typical year. It also explains that applicants able to contribute at least $35,000 annually are more competitive in its international admission process.

Macalester similarly explains that international applicants needing contributions below $40,000 face the greatest competition in its selection process.

These details are important for students who need almost complete funding. A university may technically meet full demonstrated need but still be highly selective about admitting students who require large financial aid packages.

Always look for the latest Common Data Set, international admissions statistics and financial aid reports before deciding where to apply.

Very Important: You Can Only Add 20 Colleges to Common App

Do not waste your 20 college choices

Common App allows applicants to add and apply to a maximum of 20 colleges to their My Colleges list.

This means you cannot simply add every university on this page without considering your priorities.

Once you submit an application to a college, you cannot remove that college from your My Colleges list. You should therefore plan your choices carefully before submitting.

Official limit: 20 colleges per Common App account.

Confirm the 20-college limit with Common App

How to prioritise your 20 choices

Your college list should reflect your academic qualifications, intended programme, financial circumstances and admission competitiveness.

A possible planning strategy is:

  • 5–6 highly selective universities: Include institutions such as Harvard, Princeton, Yale, Brown, Dartmouth and Amherst if their academic programmes and financial aid policies suit you.
  • 7–9 other competitive institutions: Consider institutions such as Colby, Grinnell, Macalester, Oberlin, Smith, Denison and Mount Holyoke.
  • Remaining choices: Consider refugee-focused pathways and universities with other verified financial aid opportunities, including Global Student Haven institutions.

This is only an example of how to distribute your choices. It is not a formula that guarantees admission.

Questions to ask before adding a university

  • Does the university offer my intended undergraduate programme?
  • Does it accept international applicants through Common App?
  • Does it provide need-based financial assistance to international students?
  • Does it meet 100% of demonstrated need or only provide partial awards?
  • Does it consider financial need during admission?
  • Can it support a student who needs almost complete funding?
  • Does it require the CSS Profile or another financial aid application?
  • Can I meet the academic and English-language requirements?
  • Are there additional costs that its financial aid package does not cover?
  • Is the application deadline still open?
Portico recommendation:

Do not fill all 20 spaces with universities that have acceptance rates below 5%. Diversify your choices. Equally, do not select a university with a higher acceptance rate if it cannot provide enough financial assistance to make attendance possible.

Eligibility Criteria

General eligibility for international applicants

  • Applicants should be completing or have completed secondary school and be applying for their first undergraduate degree.
  • Applicants must satisfy the academic requirements of their chosen university.
  • Applicants must demonstrate sufficient English proficiency where required.
  • Students requesting need-based aid must submit the required financial information during the admission process.
  • Applicants should be prepared to submit academic transcripts, national examination results, recommendation letters and other required documents.
  • Applicants must complete the university-specific questions and supplemental essays.
  • International applicants must follow the institution's citizenship and residency classification rules.

Eligibility for refugee and displaced applicants

Refugee students living outside the United States may apply as international applicants according to their citizenship and the university's classification policy.

A refugee living in Kenya who holds South Sudanese citizenship, for example, should not automatically select the US refugee or asylee category in Common App. That category is intended for people who have the relevant US immigration status.

Common App generally classifies foreign nationals without US citizenship or permanent residency under the non-US citizenship option. Individual universities may request additional information about refugee status.

Refugee documentation may help universities understand an applicant's educational circumstances, displacement, interrupted schooling and financial situation. Submit identity and refugee documentation when requested through the university's official process.

Financial eligibility

Students applying for need-based aid should provide an accurate account of their family's financial situation. Universities may request:

  • Parent or guardian income information.
  • Employment or unemployment documentation.
  • Family financial statements.
  • Information about family members and dependants.
  • Bank statements or asset information where required.
  • Explanations of unusual financial circumstances.
  • Documents explaining displacement or refugee circumstances where relevant.

If your parents or guardians have no formal employment, do not invent income figures. Contact the financial aid office and ask which alternative documents or explanations they accept.

Programme-Specific Academic Requirements

Admission to a university does not necessarily mean that every academic programme has identical requirements. Some universities have additional prerequisites for particular schools, departments or majors.

1. California Institute of Technology (Caltech)

Relevant programmes: Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied and Computational Mathematics.

  • Strong preparation in mathematics and science is essential.
  • Applicants are expected to demonstrate knowledge of calculus, chemistry and physics.
  • Caltech requires one recommendation from a STEM teacher and another from a humanities or social sciences teacher.
  • Applicants must submit academic records and required English translations.
  • International applicants requesting financial aid must apply for it at the time of admission.

Caltech is especially appropriate for students with strong interests in science, technology, mathematics and engineering. Its financial aid is need-aware for international students.

2. Cornell University

Relevant programmes: Computer Science, Information Science, Computer Engineering and Operations Research.

  • Students must select the appropriate undergraduate college or school when applying.
  • Engineering applicants should have strong preparation in mathematics and science.
  • Financial aid must be requested at the time of admission.
  • International applicants should review the specific financial aid forms and deadlines.
  • Some aid packages include a reasonable student loan component.

3. Northwestern University

Relevant programmes: Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science and Applied Mathematics.

  • Applicants should review the academic requirements of the specific undergraduate school.
  • Engineering applicants should demonstrate appropriate mathematics and science preparation.
  • International students must meet the university's English-language requirements.
  • Applicants requesting financial aid must submit the required forms within the relevant deadlines.

4. New York University

Relevant programmes: Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering and Information Systems.

  • Applicants must select the relevant undergraduate school or programme.
  • Computer Science is available through relevant NYU undergraduate academic units.
  • Engineering applicants should review NYU Tandon's additional academic information.
  • Students seeking the NYU Promise must carefully check the New York campus and first-year eligibility conditions.
  • International applicants must submit the appropriate financial aid documents by the deadline.

5. Mathematics and Computer Science programmes at liberal arts colleges

Amherst, Bowdoin, Williams, Grinnell, Macalester, Oberlin, Colby and Denison provide undergraduate pathways in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics or related fields.

These colleges generally offer a liberal arts education. This means students may combine computing with mathematics, economics, statistics, science and other disciplines.

However, not every liberal arts college offers a traditional standalone engineering degree. Students seeking a specialised engineering qualification should check the exact degree title and department before applying.

6. Smith and Mount Holyoke Colleges

Both institutions are women's colleges. They offer opportunities in Computer Science, Mathematics and Data Science-related disciplines.

  • Applicants should review each institution's current gender-related admission eligibility policy.
  • Students interested in engineering should investigate cooperative engineering pathways and the exact qualification awarded.
  • International applicants requesting institutional aid must follow the applicable financial aid procedures.

Important: These programme descriptions are starting points for research, not confirmation that every university offers a standalone Software Engineering degree.

What Can Need-Based Financial Aid Cover?

Financial aid packages differ from one university to another. Depending on the institution's policy and your calculated need, assistance may include:

  • Tuition: The cost of academic instruction.
  • Accommodation: University housing or an allowance for approved accommodation.
  • Meals: University dining plans or an allowance for food.
  • Mandatory fees: Required university charges.
  • Books and supplies: Academic materials and other approved expenses.
  • Health insurance: Where included in the financial aid budget.
  • Personal expenses: An allowance for necessary living expenses.
  • Travel: Some universities provide travel allowances or other assistance.

Costs students should verify separately

  • International flight tickets.
  • Passport processing costs.
  • Student visa application expenses.
  • SEVIS fees and other immigration-related costs.
  • Travel to the US embassy or consulate.
  • Initial arrival expenses.
  • Accommodation during university holidays.
Do not assume every cost is covered.

Even a university that meets 100% of demonstrated financial need may calculate expenses differently from another university. Ask the financial aid office for a written explanation of the complete package before accepting admission.

Important Financial Aid Conditions

Apply for financial aid when submitting your admission application

Many US universities require international students to request financial assistance at the time they apply for admission.

Some institutions will not allow an international student who initially applied without requesting aid to apply for institutional need-based funding in subsequent years.

If you know that you cannot afford university without assistance, do not select the option indicating that you will not need aid simply to improve your admission chances.

Understand your expected family contribution

Full demonstrated need does not automatically mean that the university will expect your family to pay nothing.

Each institution uses its own financial aid formula to calculate what it believes a family can contribute. The result may differ significantly between universities.

If your family has no realistic ability to contribute, explain this accurately and provide supporting financial information. Ask whether the university can consider exceptional circumstances.

Do not rely on future scholarships to close a funding gap

If a university offers you partial funding, do not assume you will find another scholarship after arriving in the United States.

International students may have limited access to external funding, and some scholarships are restricted to students who are already enrolled.

Your safest approach is to obtain a complete and affordable financial aid package before committing to attend.

Documents to Prepare Before Applying

Requirements differ by university. Prepare the following documents in advance so that you can respond quickly to application and financial aid requests.

Academic documents

  • Secondary school transcripts.
  • National examination certificates and results.
  • School reports where available.
  • Certified English translations where necessary.
  • School counsellor recommendation.
  • Teacher recommendation letters.
  • Predicted results if you are still completing secondary school and the institution requests them.

English and standardised tests

  • Duolingo English Test, TOEFL or IELTS, depending on the university's accepted tests.
  • SAT or ACT scores where required.
  • Evidence of English-language instruction if the university accepts it as an alternative.

Test requirements change. Do not assume that a university is test-optional simply because it was test-optional in an earlier application cycle.

Financial documents

  • Parent or guardian income statements where available.
  • Financial aid application forms.
  • CSS Profile where required.
  • Institution-specific financial aid forms where accepted.
  • Statements explaining unemployment or informal employment.
  • Documents supporting exceptional family circumstances.

Identity and refugee documents

  • Valid passport or other identity document as requested.
  • Refugee identification documentation where relevant.
  • Documents explaining displacement or interrupted schooling where requested.

Step-by-Step Common App Application Process

  1. Create a Common App account. Visit the official website and register as a first-year applicant if you have not previously enrolled in a postsecondary institution.
  2. Complete your personal profile. Provide accurate personal, citizenship, education and family information.
  3. Research universities. Compare their admission policies, academic programmes, international financial aid and deadlines.
  4. Build your college list. Remember that the maximum is 20 colleges. Add only institutions that you have researched carefully.
  5. Complete the main application. Enter your educational background, activities, achievements and personal essay.
  6. Complete university-specific questions. Every institution may request additional information, short essays or supplemental documents.
  7. Request recommendation letters. Ask your teachers and school counsellor well in advance.
  8. Apply for financial aid. Indicate your intention to request aid and complete the required CSS Profile or university-specific forms.
  9. Request an application fee waiver where eligible. Fee waiver policies vary, particularly for international applicants. Confirm the policy with each university.
  10. Submit before the deadlines. Check both the admission and financial aid deadlines. They may be different.
  11. Monitor your applicant portals. After applying, universities usually provide separate portals where you can check missing documents and financial aid requirements.
  12. Review your admission and financial aid offers. Compare the total amount of assistance, expected contribution and remaining expenses before accepting.

Early Decision, Early Action and Regular Decision

Early Decision (ED)

Early Decision is generally binding. If admitted, you are expected to attend the institution and withdraw other applications, subject to the institution's agreement and financial aid release rules.

Students who need to compare several financial aid packages should be particularly careful before choosing Early Decision.

Early Action (EA)

Early Action is generally non-binding. Students can receive an admission decision earlier without committing to attend. However, some institutions have restrictive early-action rules.

Regular Decision (RD)

Regular Decision allows students to apply to multiple institutions and compare their admission and financial aid offers before making a final decision.

For applicants who require almost complete funding, Regular Decision can be a practical choice because it allows them to evaluate different offers.

Always read the individual university's application agreement before selecting an admission round.

How Universities Evaluate Applicants

Most selective US universities use holistic admission. This means they evaluate several aspects of an applicant's background rather than relying exclusively on examination grades.

  • Academic performance: Secondary school grades and academic preparation.
  • Academic potential: Ability to succeed in the intended undergraduate programme.
  • Essays: Personal experiences, goals, values and intellectual interests.
  • Recommendations: Teachers' and counsellors' assessments.
  • Extracurricular involvement: Leadership, community participation, projects and other activities.
  • Personal circumstances: Educational opportunities, family circumstances, displacement and other relevant context.
  • Financial need: Considered during admission at need-aware institutions.

Refugee applicants can explain interrupted education, limited access to learning resources and other circumstances that affected their academic journey.

However, personal circumstances do not automatically guarantee admission or a scholarship.

How to Build a Strong and Realistic College List

  • Research before adding a university. Check its financial aid policy and confirm that international students are eligible.
  • Do not focus only on famous universities. Smaller liberal arts colleges may have substantial institutional resources for international students.
  • Consider your intended programme. Do not apply to a university simply because it provides full financial aid if it does not offer the degree you want.
  • Check the international admission rate. Overall acceptance rates may be misleading.
  • Understand need-aware admission. If you need a very large financial aid package, this may affect your admission competitiveness.
  • Apply for aid at the correct time. Some institutions will not consider international students for need-based assistance if they fail to request it during the initial application.
  • Do not rely on partial scholarships. If you have no alternative funding, prioritise universities with substantial need-based aid.
  • Keep track of deadlines. Admission and financial aid deadlines can differ.
  • Contact admissions offices. Ask questions about refugee documentation, financial aid forms and unusual educational circumstances.
  • Prepare individual applications carefully. Each university may have different essays, programme requirements and supplementary questions.

Research Every University Before You Apply

Your application decision should be informed, not rushed.

Portico Kakuma provides this directory as a starting point for discovering universities and financial aid opportunities. It does not replace individual university research.

Every student has a different academic background, financial situation, intended programme and set of priorities. A university that is suitable for one applicant may not be suitable for another.

Before submitting an application, go back to the university's official website and investigate:

  • The latest international admission requirements.
  • The current acceptance rate and international applicant statistics.
  • The exact undergraduate degree and major available.
  • Whether the programme has additional admission requirements.
  • Whether international applicants can request need-based aid.
  • Whether the university meets full demonstrated need or offers partial funding.
  • How the university calculates family contributions.
  • Whether the financial aid package includes housing, meals and health insurance.
  • Whether travel and visa-related expenses receive any support.
  • The application deadline and financial aid deadline.
  • The university's current testing and English proficiency policies.
  • Whether there are additional scholarships for refugee or displaced applicants.

If something is unclear, contact the admissions or financial aid office directly. Do not rely on old scholarship lists, social media posts or unofficial promises.

The purpose of this section is not simply to encourage students to apply to more universities. It is to help them identify institutions where their academic qualifications, intended programmes and financial circumstances are a reasonable match.

Application Fees and Fraud Prevention

Common App is free to create an account and complete the main application. Individual universities may charge application fees.

Students who cannot afford application fees should check whether Common App or the university provides a fee waiver. International applicants should confirm the specific policy before submitting.

  • Never pay an individual who promises guaranteed admission.
  • Do not pay unofficial agents to secure a scholarship.
  • Use official university websites and verified application portals.
  • Do not share passwords or sensitive documents with unverified contacts.
  • Be cautious of anyone promising a fully funded scholarship in exchange for money.

Universities make their own admission and financial aid decisions. No private individual can guarantee an admission offer.

UNHCR Refugee Scholarship

UNHCR DAFI Scholarship Programme

Undergraduate & Eligible Tertiary Programmes

Destination: Kenya and other participating countries

Study Level: Bachelor's degree and eligible tertiary programmes

Target Applicants: Eligible refugees

Funding: Scholarship support for education and related living costs

About the Scholarship

The Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative (DAFI) is a tertiary education scholarship programme supported by UNHCR and its partners. Since 1992, it has helped refugees access higher education and develop the skills needed to contribute to their communities.

In Kenya, DAFI supports eligible refugee students pursuing higher education at participating institutions. The programme is particularly important for students who have completed secondary school but face financial barriers to university or other eligible tertiary studies.

DAFI is competitive, and the availability of scholarships depends on funding, the annual selection process, and the requirements of the country programme.

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must meet the requirements in the current DAFI application announcement. These may include:

  • Being a refugee who meets the programme's status and documentation requirements.
  • Having completed secondary education and meeting the admission requirements of the intended tertiary institution.
  • Demonstrating strong academic potential and the ability to complete the chosen course.
  • Meeting the programme's financial-need and other selection criteria.
  • Choosing an eligible course and institution under the current call.
  • Submitting a complete application with the required supporting documents before the deadline.

Meeting the general criteria does not guarantee selection. Applicants should check the current Kenya-specific call for exact age, academic, residence, documentation, course, and institution requirements.

What the Scholarship Covers

DAFI support is intended to help scholars pursue their studies without being prevented by basic education and living expenses. Depending on the country programme and award, support may include:

  • University tuition and required academic fees.
  • Accommodation and food allowances.
  • Books, study materials, and other education-related expenses.
  • Local transportation.
  • Additional academic support, mentoring, or personal development opportunities.

The exact package varies by country and scholarship award. Applicants should confirm the benefits offered in the current Kenya call rather than assume every expense is covered in every case.

Documents to Prepare

The official application notice determines which documents are compulsory. Applicants may be asked to provide:

  • Recognised refugee identification or proof of refugee status.
  • Secondary school certificate and academic transcripts.
  • University admission letter, where required.
  • National or other identification documents, where applicable.
  • Academic references or recommendation letters, if requested.
  • A personal statement or motivation letter, if requested.
  • Any additional forms specified in the application announcement.

Do not submit this list as a substitute for the official checklist. Prepare documents according to the instructions for the current intake.

Application Period and Deadline

In Kenya, DAFI applications have commonly been announced around April or May. However, the opening date and deadline can change from year to year.

I have not confirmed an open Kenya DAFI application call for the current intake. Visit the official UNHCR Kenya education and announcements pages to check whether a new call has been published. Do not rely on deadlines from previous years.

How to Apply

  1. Read the DAFI information published by UNHCR Kenya.
  2. Check the latest scholarship announcement for eligibility, courses, institutions, and deadlines.
  3. Follow the application instructions provided by UNHCR and its implementing partner, Windle International Kenya.
  4. Complete the required application form and attach all requested documents.
  5. Submit before the stated deadline and follow any instructions about interviews or further verification.

Use only the application platform or submission method identified in the current official announcement.

Refugee Higher Education Support

Kenyatta University Refugee Scholarship

Final-Year Diploma and Degree Students

Programme Provider: Windle International Kenya in partnership with Kenyatta University

Destination: Kenya

Study Level: Diploma and Bachelor's Degree

Target Applicants: Needy refugee students already studying at Kenyatta University

Financial Support: Partial tuition-only assistance

Study Stage: Final year of study

Application Deadline: 27 November 2020 — historical call closed

Current Status: No confirmed new application window for this specific sponsorship

About the Scholarship

The Kenyatta University Refugee Scholarship refers to a tuition-support opportunity announced by Kenyatta University in partnership with Windle International Kenya to assist financially disadvantaged refugee students pursuing higher education at the university.

The published announcement targeted students who were already enrolled in diploma or degree programmes at Kenyatta University, were in their final year of study, and were struggling to pay their tuition fees.

The assistance was intended to help eligible students meet part of their outstanding tuition costs and continue towards completing their qualifications.

Important: This was not advertised as a general scholarship for new university applicants. The historical notice specifically targeted existing final-year students who were self-sponsored and in financial need.

The information on this page is based on the historical university announcement. It should not be interpreted as confirmation that applications are currently open.

Who Offered the Sponsorship?

The opportunity was announced through a partnership between Kenyatta University and Windle International Kenya.

Kenyatta University (KU) is a public university in Kenya offering diploma, undergraduate, postgraduate, and other academic programmes.

Windle International Kenya is an organisation involved in supporting access to education for refugees and other conflict-affected communities.

Under the historical announcement, students interested in the tuition assistance were directed to contact the KU Dadaab Centre for guidance on submitting their information.

Eligibility Criteria

According to the published announcement, applicants needed to meet the following conditions:

  • Be a refugee student in need of financial assistance.
  • Already be enrolled in a diploma or degree programme at Kenyatta University.
  • Be in the final year of the diploma or degree programme.
  • Be struggling to meet tuition fee payments.
  • Be self-sponsored rather than relying on an existing sponsor to pay the relevant tuition costs.

The announcement did not provide a comprehensive list of nationality, academic-grade, age, or language requirements. Applicants should not assume that additional conditions apply without confirmation from the university or its partner.

Eligibility limitation: A refugee who has completed secondary school but has not yet enrolled at Kenyatta University would not meet the final-year student condition stated in this particular announcement.

Academic Requirements

The historical notice did not publish a minimum KCSE grade, minimum GPA, or specific subject requirements for this tuition-support opportunity.

Applicants were expected to be registered Kenyatta University students pursuing a diploma or degree and approaching the completion of their studies.

Academic result slips were among the documents requested for consideration. The university or relevant office would need to confirm any additional academic requirements if a similar opportunity is announced again.

Meeting the stated conditions would not automatically guarantee financial assistance, as the published notice described support for students in need.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The historical sponsorship offered partial tuition-only support. It was intended to help needy refugee students who were struggling to pay their university tuition fees.

The published announcement does not establish that the sponsorship covered the following expenses:

  • Accommodation and hostel charges.
  • Food and daily living expenses.
  • Transport costs.
  • Books, stationery, computers, and other learning materials.
  • Personal expenses or other university charges outside tuition.

These expenses should not be assumed to be covered. Students would need to confirm the exact amount and eligible tuition costs with the university if another sponsorship round becomes available.

Funding classification: Partially funded. This opportunity should not be advertised as a fully funded scholarship.

Documents Required

The 2020 announcement instructed interested students to provide the following information and supporting documents:

  • Full official names: Names as recorded in the university's student records.
  • Registration number: The student's Kenyatta University registration number.
  • School or faculty: The academic school in which the student was enrolled.
  • Tuition fee statement: Documentation showing the student's tuition fees and outstanding balance.
  • Academic result slips: Results demonstrating the student's academic progress.
  • Letter of recommendation for support: The notice indicated that the KU Dadaab Centre would advise students about this requirement.

These are the documents listed in the historical notice. They should not automatically be treated as the complete requirements for a future application.

If a new call is announced, applicants should obtain the latest instructions before submitting sensitive documents or preparing additional paperwork.

How to Apply

The original announcement directed interested students to visit the KU Dadaab Centre and submit the requested details for consideration.

The following steps summarise the historical procedure and provide guidance for students seeking information about a possible future round.

  1. Confirm that you are already enrolled at Kenyatta University and are in the final year of a diploma or degree programme.
  2. Prepare your full official names, student registration number, and school or faculty details.
  3. Obtain your current tuition fee statement showing the amount payable or outstanding.
  4. Prepare your academic result slips.
  5. Contact the relevant university office to ask about the required recommendation letter and any additional documentation.
  6. Confirm whether the tuition-support opportunity has been reopened and obtain the current application instructions before submitting your documents.

The original notice directed students to the KU Dadaab Centre, Directorate Complex, third floor, Wing B, Room 330.

The historical announcement did not provide a general online application form for this specific sponsorship.

Selection Process

The published notice focused on needy, self-sponsored refugee students in their final year who were having difficulty paying tuition fees.

Applicants were asked to submit their student details, tuition fee statements, academic results, and a recommendation letter for support, with further guidance available from the KU Dadaab Centre.

The announcement did not publish a detailed scoring system, a fixed number of available awards, or a guarantee that every eligible student would receive assistance.

Students should therefore confirm the selection criteria and availability of funds directly with the university if a similar opportunity is offered in the future.

Application Deadline and Current Status

The historical announcement specified that the requested information had to reach the KU Dadaab Centre by Friday, 27 November 2020.

Status as of 20 October 2026: The published 2020 deadline has passed. No new application window for this specific refugee tuition sponsorship has been confirmed through the announcement referenced on this page.

Students should contact Kenyatta University or Windle International Kenya to ask whether this specific sponsorship has been offered again.

Kenyatta University may announce other financial assistance opportunities separately. Such programmes may have different eligibility criteria, application procedures, and funding arrangements, and should not be confused with this historical refugee sponsorship.

Application Fees and Fraud Prevention

The historical announcement did not specify an application fee for this tuition-support opportunity.

Applicants should confirm any official application procedure directly with the university and its partner. Do not pay unofficial agents or individuals who promise guaranteed scholarship selection.

Do not share original identity documents, passwords, or sensitive personal information with unverified contacts. Submit documents only through a process confirmed by the relevant institution.

Use the following official resources to verify the historical announcement and enquire about any future opportunities.

TAGDev 2.0 Scholarship

Undergraduate and Selected Postgraduate Programmes

Programme Provider: Egerton University, in partnership with the Regional Universities Forum for Capacity Building in Agriculture (RUFORUM) and the Mastercard Foundation

Study Location: Egerton University, Njoro, Kenya

Scholarship Type: Comprehensive, fully funded scholarship for selected applicants

Target Applicants: Economically disadvantaged young people, including refugees, displaced persons and persons with disabilities

Application Status: The 2026/2027 application round is closed. The next call has not been confirmed.

About the TAGDev 2.0 Programme

Transforming African Agricultural Universities to Meaningfully Contribute to Africa's Growth and Development (TAGDev 2.0) is a regional initiative designed to strengthen agricultural education, food systems, agribusiness and community development across Africa.

At Egerton University in Kenya, the programme supports academically capable young people who face financial and social barriers to higher education. Refugees and displaced persons are specifically encouraged to apply.

The programme aims to equip students with practical skills, leadership experience and entrepreneurial knowledge to contribute to agriculture, rural development and local communities.

Who Can Apply?

According to the programme's published guidance, the scholarship is open to eligible East African applicants and refugees residing in Kenya and Uganda. Applicants must also meet the admission requirements for an eligible degree programme and demonstrate financial need and commitment to the programme's focus areas.

Applicants should check the next official call for the exact requirements, which may include:

  • Meeting the academic admission requirements for the chosen degree.
  • Demonstrating financial disadvantage or belonging to a marginalised group.
  • Showing interest in agriculture, agribusiness, food systems or related development areas.
  • Demonstrating leadership potential and a commitment to community transformation.
  • Meeting the age limit and any recent-school-completion requirements specified in the new call.
  • Providing the required academic certificates, transcripts and supporting documents.

Important: Eligibility criteria can change between application rounds. Refugee applicants should check the next call for accepted refugee documentation, age limits, academic requirements and eligible programmes.

Eligible Study Programmes

The programme is focused on agriculture and related areas, rather than general-purpose degrees such as Computer Science or Software Engineering.

The 2026/2027 call at Egerton University listed these programmes:

  • Bachelor of Science in Agriculture
  • Bachelor of Science in Natural Resources Management
  • Bachelor of Science in Animal Science
  • Master of Science in Horticulture
  • Master of Science in Agribusiness Management
  • Master of Science in Food Science

These are the programmes listed for the 2026/2027 round. Applicants must check the next call to see which courses will be available for the next intake.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

TAGDev 2.0 describes its scholarship as comprehensive. Published programme information lists support for:

  • University tuition fees.
  • Accommodation and living expenses, including a stipend.
  • A laptop for study-related work.
  • Research costs where applicable.
  • Workshops, conferences and relevant training activities.
  • Internship, field attachment and community engagement activities.
  • Entrepreneurship training and transportation associated with programme activities.

The programme has also stated that refugee and displaced applicants may receive support with travel documents. Specific entitlements and arrangements should be confirmed in the official call and award conditions.

Funding note: The listed benefits describe the programme's published scholarship package. They should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every possible personal expense or immigration-related cost will be covered.

Application Process

When a new scholarship call opens, applicants should follow the instructions published by TAGDev 2.0 and Egerton University. Previous calls required applicants to complete both a scholarship application and a separate university admission application.

  1. Read the new scholarship call and confirm that your intended programme is eligible.
  2. Check the academic, age, residency and refugee-document requirements.
  3. Register on the RUFORUM Information Management System (RIMS) if instructed by the new call.
  4. Complete the scholarship application and the relevant university admission application.
  5. Prepare certified academic certificates, transcripts and all other required supporting documents.
  6. Submit each application through the official channels and before the published deadline.

Do not submit an application using an old form unless the programme confirms that the form is valid for the new intake.

Current Application Status

The application round for the 2026/2027 academic year is closed. The published deadline was 1 May 2026. No new application deadline should be assumed until Egerton University or TAGDev 2.0 announces another call.

Refugees in Kakuma and elsewhere in Kenya can monitor the official programme website for future announcements.

European Union Scholarship

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship

Master's Degree

Study Destination: Europe and participating countries worldwide

Study Level: Master's degree

Duration: Usually 1–2 years

Eligible Applicants: Students from all countries

Funding: Full scholarships available for selected candidates

About the Scholarship

The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) programme is funded by the European Union and brings together universities from different countries to deliver integrated master's degree programmes.

Students study at multiple participating universities, often in different countries, and may receive a joint degree or several degrees after completing the programme.

Scholarships are awarded to highly ranked applicants from around the world. Programmes cover a wide range of subjects, including computer science, artificial intelligence, engineering, data science, environmental studies, public health, education, and social sciences.

Important: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarships are for postgraduate study, not direct entry into a bachelor's degree after secondary school.

Eligibility Criteria

To apply, candidates generally need to meet the following requirements:

  • Applicants must hold a completed first higher education degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent of at least 180 ECTS) in a discipline relevant to the chosen Master's program.
  • Final-year undergraduate students may apply as long as they complete their degree and receive their diploma before the Master's program official start date.
  • There are no age limits or age restrictions to apply for or receive an Erasmus Mundus scholarship.
  • Candidates can apply to a maximum of three different Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programs per application cycle.
  • Applicants must be willing to undertake compulsory physical mobility across at least two different European countries during their studies.
  • Applicants who have already received an Erasmus Mundus scholarship in the past are ineligible to receive a second award.
  • Applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency through standardized tests (such as IELTS or TOEFL) according to the specific consortium requirements.
  • Applicants who have resided, worked, or studied in an EU member state for more than 12 cumulative months in the last 5 years are subject to specific regional category rules.

Applicants from other countries outside the European Union can apply. Refugees living in Kenya should check the selected programme's requirements for identity documents, residence status, travel documents, and visa arrangements.

Each master's consortium makes its own admissions and scholarship selections, so eligibility and selection criteria may differ.

What the Scholarship Covers

An Erasmus Mundus scholarship helps pay for studying across the programme's partner universities. It includes:

  • Monthly allowance: €1,400 per month for the full length of the programme, up to a maximum of 24 months (up to €33,600).
  • Tuition and participation costs: Scholarship holders are not charged tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs.
  • Travel, visa and installation: The monthly allowance is meant to help with these costs as well as living expenses. Some programmes handle this differently. For example, a programme may offer a separate travel and installation payment that reduces the monthly amount.

The allowance is a contribution to your costs. It does not promise that every expense will be covered. Payment arrangements, insurance and extra costs differ between programmes, so confirm them with your chosen master's programme before you apply.

Documents to Prepare

The exact checklist depends on the master's programme, but applicants commonly need:

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV): Detailed academic and professional CV formatted according to Europass standards.
  • Academic Transcripts & Degree Certificates: Official Bachelor's degree diploma and academic transcripts showing all course grades and grading keys.
  • Motivation Letter / Statement of Purpose: Tailored essay explaining academic background, interest in the consortium, and career aspirations.
  • Letters of Recommendation: Usually two to three academic or professional recommendation letters submitted on official letterhead.
  • Proof of Language Proficiency: Valid IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, or equivalent certificate as specified by the master's program.
  • Proof of Residence & Nationality: Valid international passport copy and official residence certificate or employer/university confirmation.

Some programmes request extra materials, such as a portfolio, research proposal, work experience evidence, or subject-specific tests. Follow the official checklist for your chosen course.

Application Period and Deadline

There is no single application deadline for every Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programme. Many programmes accept applications between October and January for studies beginning the following academic year.

New master's programmes selected in 2026 are expected to open student applications in autumn 2026 for programmes starting in 2027. Individual programmes may have different opening dates and deadlines.

Check the official catalogue and the website of each programme for its current application period. Do not assume that all programmes are open at the same time.

How to Apply

  1. Open the official Erasmus Mundus catalogue.
  2. Search for master's programmes that match your academic background and career goals.
  3. Open the programme website and review its entry requirements, participating universities, and scholarship details.
  4. Prepare your academic records, CV, motivation letter, references, and any other requested documents.
  5. Apply directly to the programme consortium using its official application portal.
  6. Indicate that you are applying for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship if the application instructions require it.
  7. Submit your application before the programme's deadline and monitor your email for updates.

You normally apply directly to the master's programme, not through a single central scholarship application portal.

Official Links

Use these official European Union resources to find eligible master's programmes, check scholarship conditions, and apply.

Regional Refugee Education & Inclusion

IGAD Regional Scholarship Programme

TVET, Undergraduate and Postgraduate Studies

Programme Provider: Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)

Programme Partners: IGAD Council of Higher Education and participating institutions

Destination: IGAD Member States

Study Level: TVET, Undergraduate and Postgraduate

Target Applicants: Eligible refugees, returnees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and other eligible displacement-affected applicants

Financial Support: Tuition, accommodation, subsistence and medical expenses, subject to programme limits

Maximum Published Support: Up to €3,189 per student per year under the published programme guidelines

Last Public Application Deadline: 30 June 2024 — closed

Current Status: No new public application deadline confirmed

About the Programme

The IGAD Regional Scholarship Programme is an educational initiative of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), a regional organisation whose member states include Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda.

The programme was established to improve access to higher education and skills development for young people affected by displacement, including refugees, returnees and internally displaced persons. It also supports the broader goal of strengthening educational opportunities for disadvantaged communities in the IGAD region.

The initiative is connected to regional commitments to improve education for refugees, returnees and host communities. It aims to help eligible students acquire relevant qualifications, develop professional skills and improve their opportunities for economic independence.

Depending on the applicable programme arrangements, supported studies may include technical and vocational education and training (TVET), undergraduate degrees and postgraduate qualifications at participating accredited institutions.

The programme is intended to help eligible students access and complete their education rather than simply provide a one-time cash award.

Important: The programme has specific citizenship, displacement, academic admission and financial need requirements. Being a refugee or living in an IGAD member state does not automatically guarantee eligibility or selection.

Countries Covered

The programme operates within the IGAD region, which comprises the following eight member states:

  • Djibouti
  • Eritrea
  • Ethiopia
  • Kenya
  • Somalia
  • South Sudan
  • Sudan
  • Uganda

The 2024 public call invited eligible applicants residing in IGAD member states to apply. Scholarship placements depended on the programme's requirements and available opportunities at accredited higher education institutions in the region.

Applicants should not assume that they can choose any university or study in any country without satisfying the programme's placement and admission conditions.

Eligibility Criteria

The published programme guidelines identify the following general eligibility requirements:

  • Belong to a displacement-affected community, such as refugees, returnees or internally displaced persons, and possess the required documentation.
  • Be a citizen of an IGAD member state, including applicants in refugee or displacement situations.
  • Be admitted to or already enrolled in an accredited higher education institution within the IGAD region.
  • Demonstrate financial need and satisfy the programme's requirements for disadvantaged applicants.
  • Meet the academic and other admission requirements of the proposed institution and programme.
  • Be prepared to pursue a field of study relevant to the educational and skills needs identified by the programme.

The programme guidelines also give particular consideration to women, persons with disabilities and other disadvantaged groups. At least 30% of scholarships were reserved for female students under the published guidelines.

The guidelines identify applicants from Somalia and South Sudan for special consideration because of the long-standing displacement affecting these populations.

These criteria describe the published programme framework. Applicants must check the requirements of any new call because eligibility rules and available opportunities may change.

Academic Requirements

Applicants are expected to demonstrate academic ability and readiness to succeed in their chosen programme. The published selection guidelines identify the following considerations:

  • Strong academic performance in previous studies.
  • Admission to, or enrolment in, an accredited public or private educational institution in the IGAD region.
  • A proposed field of study relevant to skills and labour market needs in the applicant's home country or region.
  • Clear educational and career goals.
  • The ability and potential to complete the proposed course successfully.

Applicants for postgraduate studies were expected under the published guidelines to have at least one year of relevant work experience, including institutional or self-employment experience.

The programme does not establish one universal KCSE grade, GPA or subject requirement for every course and institution. Applicants must also satisfy the admission requirements of their chosen institution and the conditions of the relevant scholarship call.

What the Scholarship Covers

Under the published programme guidelines, financial assistance may cover the following education and living expenses:

  • Tuition fees: Financial assistance towards the cost of the approved course.
  • Accommodation: Support towards eligible accommodation costs.
  • Subsistence: Assistance towards basic living expenses during the period of study.
  • Medical expenses: Support towards eligible medical costs or medical cover under the programme arrangements.

The published programme guidelines set a maximum financial support limit of €3,189 per student per year. The actual amount depends on the relevant training and living costs and the programme's financial arrangements.

This figure is a published programme limit, not a guarantee that every recipient receives the full amount or that all personal expenses will be covered.

The guidelines also state that the scholarship does not provide additional support for family members or dependants, including spouses and children. Application costs charged by partner institutions, including certificate certification and equivalency expenses, are also excluded.

Funding classification: Financial assistance towards approved education and living costs. Do not assume that the programme will cover every expense without any additional contribution from the student.

Duration of Support

The published programme guidelines describe a scholarship duration of approximately three to four years, depending on the programme of study.

The duration and amount of support available to an individual recipient depend on the approved course, programme conditions and applicable funding arrangements.

Applicants should confirm the exact duration of funding, continuation requirements and academic progress conditions in the official call before accepting an award.

Documents Required

The programme guidelines identify several documents that applicants may be required to provide. These include:

  • Valid travel or identity documentation: Documentation issued by the relevant competent authority.
  • Academic certificates: Authenticated certificates from previous national school-leaving examinations or other relevant qualifications.
  • Proof of financial need: Supporting evidence from parents, community or faith leaders, refugee agencies, or other accepted sources.
  • Letter of intent: A statement explaining the applicant's intended field of study and educational goals.
  • CV or résumé: A brief summary of education, skills, work experience and relevant activities.
  • Admission evidence: Proof of admission or enrolment at an accredited institution, where required by the applicable call.
  • Displacement documentation: Evidence of refugee, returnee or IDP status, where applicable.

This is a preparation checklist based on the published programme framework, not a guarantee that every document is required in every application round.

Applicants should follow the official instructions for the relevant intake and provide clear, truthful and consistent information.

Application Process

The application process depends on the official call published by IGAD. For the 2024 call, applicants were directed to the programme's official webpage to obtain information and submit their applications.

For a future application round, prospective applicants should follow these general preparation steps:

  1. Read the official scholarship announcement and download the applicable guidelines.
  2. Confirm your citizenship, displacement status, academic admission and financial need meet the stated requirements.
  3. Identify an accredited institution and a programme that satisfies the call's conditions.
  4. Prepare your academic certificates, identity or displacement documentation, proof of financial need, letter of intent and CV.
  5. Complete the official application form using the method specified in the new call.
  6. Review all answers and attachments for accuracy and completeness before submitting.
  7. Keep a copy of your application and any submission confirmation.
  8. Monitor official communications for information about shortlisting, additional documents and selection outcomes.

These are general preparation steps, not confirmation that applications are currently being accepted. Do not submit documents through an old form unless IGAD confirms that it is valid for a new intake.

Selection Process

The published guidelines assign a role in beneficiary selection to the IGAD Council of Higher Education (ICHE). Selection is intended to promote equitable access to education for eligible displacement-affected students.

Relevant considerations include:

  • Academic performance and readiness for the proposed course.
  • Admission to or enrolment in an accredited institution.
  • Financial need and the applicant's disadvantaged circumstances.
  • The relevance of the proposed field of study to skills needs in the region.
  • Educational goals, extracurricular activities and potential to succeed.

Applicants may be assessed or interviewed as part of the selection process, depending on the applicable programme arrangements.

The programme is competitive. Meeting the eligibility requirements or submitting an application does not guarantee selection, admission or funding.

Application Deadline and Current Status

IGAD announced its second call for applications on 4 April 2024. The published deadline was 30 June 2024, at midnight East Africa Time.

Status as of 20 October 2026: The 2024 public application deadline has passed. IGAD reported continued implementation of the regional scholarship programme and progress on the second cohort in July 2025. However, that report does not establish that a new public application window is open.

Applicants should check IGAD's official scholarship page for a new announcement before preparing to submit an application.

Portico Kakuma lists this opportunity for awareness and future reference. The presence of this page does not mean that applications are open.

Application Fees and Fraud Prevention

Applicants should use the official IGAD website and the application method specified in the relevant call.

Be cautious of individuals who promise guaranteed scholarship selection, admission or financial support in exchange for money or personal favours.

Do not submit sensitive personal documents to unverified contacts or rely on unofficial messages claiming that a new application round has opened.

Confirm the deadline, application requirements and any official fees directly with IGAD before taking action.

Official Links and Contact

Use the following official sources to review the programme, its published guidelines and any future application calls.

IGAD Regional Scholarship Programme IGAD — 2024 Scholarship Announcement IGAD — Programme Progress Update, July 2025 IGAD Scholarship Programme Guidelines (PDF)

Scholarship enquiries: scholarships@igad.int

For confirmation of a future application round, contact IGAD directly or consult the latest official programme announcement.

Fully Funded Scholarship

Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at USIU-Africa

Undergraduate Bachelor's Degrees

Programme Provider: United States International University–Africa (USIU-Africa) in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation

Study Location: Nairobi, Kenya

Study Level: First-time undergraduate degree

Funding: Full-cost scholarship

Eligible Applicants: Young Africans who meet the programme's academic and socioeconomic eligibility requirements, including eligible refugee and displaced youth

Application Status: Closed — no open call currently

Official Website: Visit the Official Programme Page

About the Scholarship

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at USIU-Africa provides full-cost scholarships to academically talented young Africans who face financial, displacement, gender, disability or other socioeconomic barriers to higher education.

The programme combines university education with leadership development, mentorship, career guidance and other support intended to help scholars contribute to their communities and Africa's development.

The programme is particularly relevant to eligible refugees and displaced young people who have the academic potential to pursue university education but face significant barriers to accessing it.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants generally need to meet the following requirements:

  • Be a citizen of an African country. The programme is not open to non-African nationalities.
  • Be applying for a first undergraduate degree.
  • Meet the programme's age requirement: generally 29 years or younger at the time of application, with an age limit of 32 for refugee or displaced youth and youth with disabilities.
  • Demonstrate financial need or relevant socioeconomic barriers to accessing higher education.
  • Meet the university's minimum academic entry requirements and the requirements for the intended degree programme.
  • Demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to improving their community through service or outreach.
  • Be interested in one of the undergraduate degree programmes approved for this scholarship.

Important for refugees: Refugees and displaced youth are among the programme's target groups. Applicants should prepare valid documentation of their circumstances and confirm the specific documents required in the next official call.

Academic Requirements

The official programme page states a minimum university entry grade of C+ or its equivalent, as determined under the applicable Kenyan university entry requirements.

Applicants educated outside Kenya may be considered if their qualifications meet the equivalent requirements.

Applicants interested in Pharmacy and certain Health Sciences programmes must meet additional academic requirements, including the required grades in relevant cluster subjects.

Meeting the minimum academic requirements does not guarantee selection. Applicants must also meet the programme's other criteria and successfully complete the selection process.

Approved Fields of Study

The programme's official page lists the following 13 undergraduate degree programmes:

School of Science and Technology

  • Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Technology
  • Bachelor of Science in Information Systems and Technology
  • Bachelor of Science in Data Science and Analytics
  • Bachelor of Science in Software Engineering

School of Pharmacy and Health Sciences

  • Bachelor of Pharmacy
  • Bachelor of Science in Epidemiology and Biostatistics

School of Communication, Cinematic and Creative Arts

  • Bachelor of Arts in Animation
  • Bachelor of Arts in Film Production and Directing

Chandaria School of Business Administration

  • Bachelor of Science in Finance
  • Bachelor of Science in International Business Administration
  • Bachelor of Science in Accounting

School of Humanities and Social Sciences

  • Bachelor of Arts in International Relations
  • Bachelor of Arts in Psychology

Note: Applicants must select a degree programme approved for the scholarship. The programme does not automatically cover every degree offered at USIU-Africa.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The programme provides comprehensive financial and personal support. Published benefits include:

  • Tuition and functional university fees.
  • A laptop, books and other learning materials.
  • Reasonable accommodation and meals.
  • Medical insurance.
  • A stipend to support living expenses.
  • Transport to and from home, subject to programme provisions.
  • Leadership and entrepreneurial training.
  • Psychosocial support and career counselling.
  • Mentorship and career development support.
  • Reasonable accommodation of disability-related needs.

These benefits are based on the programme's published information. Applicants should check the next call and scholarship award terms for the exact support available to their cohort.

Documents to Prepare

The exact checklist will be provided in the next official application call. Applicants can begin preparing:

  • Final secondary school certificate or official results.
  • Academic transcripts, where required.
  • National identity document, passport or other accepted identification.
  • Refugee or displacement documentation, where applicable.
  • Evidence of financial need, if requested.
  • Information about leadership, volunteering and community service.
  • Any additional forms or supporting documents specified in the call.

Do not submit documents to an unofficial agent. Follow the document instructions and submission method stated in the next official call.

How to Apply

Applications are accepted only when USIU-Africa publishes an official call for the relevant intake.

  1. Visit the official programme website and check whether a new call for applications has been announced.
  2. Read the call carefully to confirm eligibility, approved degree programmes, required documents and deadlines.
  3. Obtain and complete the application form specified for that intake.
  4. Prepare and submit the required supporting documents using the submission method stated in the call.
  5. Monitor your email and follow official instructions concerning shortlisting and interviews.
  6. If selected, follow the programme's instructions for the formal university admission process.

The programme has historically offered intakes associated with the May and September semesters. This does not mean applications are currently open or that the next intake's dates have been confirmed.

Selection Process

The published selection process includes these stages:

  1. Application submission.
  2. Review of applications.
  3. Shortlisting of eligible candidates.
  4. Interviews for shortlisted applicants.
  5. Final selection.
  6. Formal university admission for selected scholars.

Selection is competitive. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee an interview, scholarship award or admission.

Swedish Government Scholarship

Swedish Institute Scholarships

Master's Degree

Destination: Sweden

Study Level: Master's degree

Duration: Usually 1–2 years, depending on the programme

Funding: Full tuition and living support under eligible awards

Eligible Applicants: Citizens of specified countries, depending on the scholarship

About the Scholarship

The Swedish Institute (SI) is a Swedish government agency that offers scholarships to international students pursuing master's degrees at Swedish universities. Its scholarships support academic development, leadership, and contributions to sustainable development.

Two relevant programmes are the SI Scholarship for Global Professionals and the SI Scholarship Pioneering Women in STEM. They have different eligible-country lists and requirements, so applicants must check the rules for the specific scholarship and academic year.

Important: These scholarships are for master's studies, not undergraduate degrees immediately after secondary school.

1. SI Scholarship for Global Professionals

This scholarship supports professionals who want to pursue an eligible full-time master's programme in Sweden and use their education to contribute to sustainable development in their home countries.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Be a citizen of a country included in the scholarship's current eligible-country list.
  • Apply for an eligible, full-time master's programme at a Swedish university.
  • Meet the Swedish university admission requirements and the scholarship's application requirements.
  • Demonstrate relevant work experience and leadership experience.
  • Show how the intended studies can contribute to sustainable development in the applicant's home country or region.
  • Meet the scholarship's other restrictions and documentation requirements.

In the 2026/2027 application cycle, applicants generally needed at least 3,000 hours of documented work experience, alongside leadership experience. Requirements should be checked again when the next application call is published.

What It Covers

  • Full tuition fees paid directly to the Swedish university.
  • A monthly living allowance. The 2026/2027 scholarship information listed SEK 12,000 per month.
  • A one-time travel grant for eligible recipients from specified countries, subject to the programme's rules.
  • Insurance against illness and accidents.
  • Membership in the SI Network for Global Professionals and access to professional networking opportunities.
  • Access to the SI alumni network after the scholarship period.

The scholarship does not generally cover additional grants for family members or the university application fee. Check the current official terms for all exclusions and conditions.

2. SI Scholarship Pioneering Women in STEM

This scholarship supports eligible women pursuing selected master's programmes in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) at Swedish universities.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Be a woman and a citizen of a country included in the current programme's eligible-country list.
  • Apply for a master's programme specifically included in the scholarship's eligible-programme list.
  • Meet the Swedish university's academic and language requirements.
  • Complete the required university admission process and scholarship application.
  • Meet the current call's additional conditions.

For the 2026/2027 cycle, the eligible-country list included Kenya, but not every master's programme qualified. The eligible list and benefits must be checked again for the next intake.

Funding

This programme provides scholarship support for eligible master's studies. The precise coverage, eligible courses, and application requirements should be verified on the Swedish Institute's official page for the relevant academic year.

Explore Swedish Institute Scholarships

Documents to Prepare

Required documents vary by scholarship and application cycle. For the Scholarship for Global Professionals, applicants have commonly been required to prepare:

  • A valid passport or accepted identification document.
  • A curriculum vitae (CV) in the required format.
  • Proof of work and leadership experience using the prescribed forms.
  • Letters of reference.
  • A motivation statement explaining the intended studies and their contribution to sustainable development.
  • Academic records and any documents required for university admission.

Use the latest official templates and document instructions. Incomplete applications or documents that do not follow the prescribed format may be rejected.

Application Period and Deadline

For the 2026/2027 intake, applications for eligible master's programmes through Sweden's University Admissions system generally took place before the Swedish Institute scholarship application window in February 2026. Those application periods have passed.

As of 20 October 2026, check the Swedish Institute's official website for the next scholarship cycle's announcement, eligible programmes, and confirmed deadlines. Dates from a previous cycle should not be treated as the deadline for a future intake.

How to Apply

  1. Check the current eligible-country list for the specific SI scholarship.
  2. Find a suitable master's programme on the official Study in Sweden or University Admissions website.
  3. Confirm that the programme is eligible for the scholarship you intend to apply for.
  4. Apply for university admission before the relevant deadline and follow the required application steps.
  5. Prepare the SI scholarship documents using the official forms and instructions.
  6. Submit the separate scholarship application during the SI application window, if eligible.
  7. Monitor the official websites and your email for admission results and scholarship decisions.

Important Note for Applicants in Kenya

Scholarship eligibility is based on the citizenship requirements of the particular programme, not simply on living in Kenya. Kenya was included in the 2026/2027 eligible-country list for the Scholarship for Global Professionals.

Therefore, other citizens living in Kenya should not assume they qualify through Kenyan residence. Check the latest country list and contact the Swedish Institute if your citizenship or refugee documentation raises questions about eligibility.
