Refugee Education & Resettlement Pathway

WUSC Student Refugee Program (SRP)

Undergraduate Studies in Canada

Programme Provider: World University Service of Canada (WUSC)

Destination: Canada

Study Level: Undergraduate

Target Applicants: Eligible young refugees living in participating countries

Financial Support: Tuition and living support during the initial sponsorship period

Immigration Outcome: Selected participants may travel to Canada as permanent residents after immigration approval

2027–2028 Kenya Deadline: 13 March 2026 — closed

About the Programme

The Student Refugee Program (SRP) is managed by World University Service of Canada (WUSC), a Canadian international development organisation. Established in 1978, the programme combines access to post-secondary education with refugee resettlement to Canada.

It provides eligible young refugees with an opportunity to continue their education at participating Canadian universities, colleges, and CEGEPs. CEGEPs are post-secondary institutions found primarily in Quebec.

Unlike an ordinary scholarship, SRP also includes a resettlement pathway. Selected students are supported through Canada's Private Sponsorship of Refugees framework, subject to assessment and final approval by Canadian immigration authorities.

WUSC works with local partner organisations in countries where applications are accepted. In Canada, campus-based WUSC Local Committees help provide financial, academic, and social support to arriving students.

Important: SRP facilitates undergraduate study only. It is not a direct-entry master's or PhD scholarship, and selection by WUSC does not automatically guarantee approval to travel to Canada.

Countries Where Applications Are Accepted

WUSC currently lists the following countries of asylum for its Student Refugee Program:

  • Kenya
  • Uganda
  • Jordan
  • Lebanon

Applicants must be living in one of these participating countries and satisfy its residence, registration, academic, and other programme requirements. The programme is not open to applicants living anywhere in the world.

In Kenya, applications may be accepted from eligible refugees living in urban areas or in Kakuma and Dadaab refugee camps. The current call determines the precise requirements and application process.

Eligibility Criteria

For the 2027–2028 Kenya intake, applicants were required to meet the following general conditions:

  • Be registered with UNHCR and possess the required refugee registration documentation.
  • Have the Government of Kenya refugee identification card and original proof of registration required by the call.
  • Be living as a refugee in Kenya and have continuously resided in Kenya for at least three years at the time of application.
  • Have arrived in Kenya before 1 January 2023 for the 2027–2028 intake.
  • Be between 18 and 25 years old as of 1 January 2026.
  • Have completed secondary school and possess the required original academic certificates and result documents.
  • Meet the minimum academic grade for the country and secondary school qualification concerned.
  • Demonstrate sufficient English proficiency for undergraduate studies in Canada.
  • Be single, unmarried, and without children.
  • Face barriers to accessing or completing undergraduate post-secondary education.
  • Be considered eligible and suitable for resettlement under Canada's Private Sponsorship of Refugees framework.
  • Demonstrate maturity, self-reliance, and suitability for living and studying independently in Canada.

These requirements are specific to the published 2027–2028 Kenya call. Requirements for future intakes may change.

Minimum Academic Requirements

The 2027–2028 Kenya call published minimum academic requirements according to the country where the applicant completed secondary education. The following are examples from that call:

  • Kenya — KCSE: B+ for male applicants and B- for female applicants.
  • South Sudan — CSE: 65% for male applicants and 60% for female applicants.
  • Uganda — UACE: 12 points for male applicants and 10 points for female applicants.
  • Rwanda — REB/ACSE: At least four principal passes for male applicants and three for female applicants.
  • Somalia — SSLC: 70% for male applicants and 65% for female applicants.
  • Sudan — SSC: 60% for male applicants and 55% for female applicants.
  • Burundi and DRC: The call also lists minimum grades for the respective secondary school qualifications.

This is a selection of the published requirements, not the full country-by-country table. Applicants with qualifications from other countries may also be considered if they satisfy the other requirements. Consult the official Kenya call for the complete table and any applicable exceptions.

Academic eligibility is only one part of the assessment. Meeting the minimum grade does not guarantee shortlisting or selection.

What the Programme Provides

SRP is not a conventional cash scholarship paid directly to a student. Support is organised through WUSC, participating educational institutions, and campus Local Committees.

During the initial 12-month sponsorship period, support can include:

  • Free or reduced tuition and accommodation costs, arranged through the programme and participating institution.
  • Financial assistance for basic necessities.
  • Academic support and guidance as students adjust to their studies.
  • Social support from a campus-based WUSC Local Committee.
  • Assistance with integration into the Canadian university or college community.
  • Support with the programme's resettlement and pre-departure process.

The financial arrangements may include in-kind assistance rather than unrestricted cash payments. Applicants should not assume that every personal expense will be paid directly or that the same package applies at every institution.

After the initial 12 months, students are expected to work towards greater financial independence. Possible sources of continued support include institutional bursaries, scholarships, student loans where appropriate, and permitted employment income. Students should discuss their options with their institution and Local Committee.

Academic Opportunities in Canada

SRP facilitates admission to undergraduate studies at participating Canadian post-secondary institutions. Available courses and placements depend on institutional participation, admission requirements, and the programme's placement process.

Students may be placed in different provinces and communities. Applicants should be prepared to study and live wherever an appropriate placement is available; placement in a particular city, institution, or near family members is not guaranteed.

Students must meet the academic admission requirements of their assigned institution and be prepared to continue their studies successfully after the initial sponsorship period.

Documents Required

For the 2027–2028 Kenya application, applicants were instructed to submit their applications online and upload legible electronic copies of the requested documents. Required documents included proof of refugee registration and academic records.

Applicants should prepare the following where requested:

  • UNHCR proof of registration.
  • Government of Kenya refugee identification card.
  • Original secondary school certificate or diploma.
  • Official secondary school transcripts and result slips, as applicable.
  • Other academic documents required by the application form.
  • Any additional supporting documents requested in the call.

The programme requires applicants to possess the original official secondary education documents, not merely a statement that the documents will be obtained later. The 2027–2028 call included a limited exception for certain recent KCSE graduates awaiting original results, with specific evidence required before interviews.

Additional training certificates, references, or supporting documents may strengthen an application where relevant, but they do not replace compulsory documents.

All documents must be truthful, consistent, and legible. WUSC states that false documents or misrepresentation can lead to removal from the selection process and a possible ban from future consideration.

Application Process

  1. Read the latest WUSC SRP call for your country of asylum.
  2. Check every eligibility condition, including residence duration, age, marital and parental status, academic grades, and documentation.
  3. Prepare your original academic records and refugee identification documents.
  4. Complete the official online application form during the published application window.
  5. Upload all required documents as clear electronic files in the accepted format.
  6. Review every answer and attachment before submitting the form.
  7. Keep a copy of the submitted application and confirmation for your records.
  8. Monitor your email and follow instructions from WUSC or its country partner.
  9. If shortlisted, participate in the further assessment stages and provide any additional information requested.

Applications are accepted only during the official recruitment period. WUSC does not accept referrals from individuals as a substitute for applying through the official process.

Selection and Shortlisting

After the application deadline, WUSC reviews applications to determine whether candidates satisfy the programme's eligibility requirements. Only shortlisted applicants are contacted to progress to subsequent selection stages.

The process is competitive and considers eligibility, academic readiness, the barriers applicants face in accessing higher education, and suitability for the programme and resettlement. The precise stages and assessments are determined by WUSC's selection process for the relevant intake.

Submitting an application does not guarantee an interview, shortlisting, selection, admission to a particular institution, or approval for resettlement.

WUSC states that it does not set nationality-based quotas for applicants. Refugees of different nationalities may apply as long as they meet the requirements of a participating country.

Resettlement to Canada

A distinctive feature of SRP is its connection to Canada's Private Sponsorship of Refugees framework. WUSC selects eligible candidates and supports the resettlement process with its partners in Canada.

The process can take two years or longer. Final immigration decisions are made by Canadian immigration authorities, not by WUSC alone. Candidates must satisfy the relevant immigration requirements and admissibility checks before travel is approved.

Students who are approved through the programme arrive in Canada as permanent residents. Permanent residence gives them a different immigration status from that of an ordinary international student. They may later be eligible to apply for Canadian citizenship if they satisfy the applicable legal requirements.

Selection by WUSC is not a guarantee of a visa, travel approval, or admission to Canada. If Canadian authorities refuse a candidate's application or deny entry, the candidate's participation may be cancelled.

Application Deadline and Current Status

For the 2027–2028 academic intake, the Kenya application period ran from 13 February 2026 until 13 March 2026 at 5:00 p.m. East African Time.

Status as of 20 October 2026: The published Kenya application window is closed. The next application period should be confirmed through WUSC's official SRP website and country announcements.

Recruitment dates vary by country, and WUSC generally opens applications for a limited period each year. Do not use a previous intake's form or deadline as confirmation that a new application window is open.

Application Fees and Fraud Prevention

Applying to WUSC's Student Refugee Program is free. Applicants should not pay an application fee or provide money, gifts, or favours to a staff member or local partner to obtain selection.

Use only the official WUSC application link published for the relevant intake. Be cautious of people who promise guaranteed selection, admission, or resettlement in exchange for payment.

WUSC also expects honest and consistent information throughout the application and interview process. False documents or deliberately misleading information may lead to disqualification.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is WUSC SRP a scholarship?

WUSC describes SRP as a refugee resettlement programme that includes access to post-secondary education. It provides financial and social support during the initial sponsorship period, but it is not a conventional scholarship that simply pays a student cash.

Can someone apply directly from their country of origin?

Applicants must be living in one of WUSC's participating countries of asylum and meet the requirements of that country's application call. The programme is not a general application route for all students living anywhere in the world.

Can married applicants or applicants with children apply?

The published 2027–2028 Kenya call required applicants to be single, unmarried, and without children. Check future calls for any changes to this requirement.

Can a student choose the university or city in Canada?

Applicants should be flexible about placement. The programme arranges placements based on available participating institutions and other relevant considerations; a specific university or city is not guaranteed.

Does WUSC guarantee permanent residence?

No. WUSC facilitates the sponsorship process, but Canadian immigration authorities make the final immigration and admissibility decisions.

Can students receive support after the first year?

Students are expected to work towards financial independence after the first 12 months. They can explore institutional scholarships, bursaries, other assistance, and permitted employment options with their institution.

Can applicants with disabilities apply?

WUSC encourages eligible refugee youth with disabilities to apply. Applicants who need accommodations to complete the application should contact the relevant WUSC office or country partner.

University Preparation Programme

Elimisha Kakuma

University preparation, academic guidance, and application support for eligible refugee students in Kakuma.

Important Notice: This Is NOT a Scholarship

Elimisha Kakuma is not a scholarship provider. It does not directly award university scholarships or guarantee funding for university tuition.

It is a university preparation and college-access programme that helps eligible refugee students prepare for higher education and navigate university admission and external scholarship applications.

Students who want financial assistance to attend university must still identify and apply for suitable scholarships or other funding opportunities separately. Participation in Elimisha Kakuma does not guarantee admission to a university or receipt of a scholarship.

About the Programme

Elimisha Kakuma supports high-achieving refugee students who want to pursue university education but may need additional academic preparation, guidance, and support with the university application process.

The programme helps students strengthen their readiness for higher education, explore university pathways, and prepare applications for universities and external funding opportunities.

It is particularly relevant to students living in Kakuma who need structured guidance as they work towards accessing higher education.

Who Can Apply?

Eligibility depends on the programme's current recruitment announcement. In the 2026–2027 cohort announcement, applicants were expected to meet requirements including:

  • Applicants must hold official registered refugee status in Kakuma Refugee Camp or Kalobeyei Integrated Settlement and possess valid documentation.
  • Candidates must have achieved a minimum grade of B minus (B-) on the KCSE or hold an equivalent secondary school leaving qualification.
  • Applicants must commit to physically residing in Kakuma for the full 16-month duration of the intensive gap-year program.
  • Candidates must commit to attending mandatory weekday classes and workshops full-time at the Elimisha Kakuma center.
  • There are no strict age limits, though applicants must be high school graduates ready for immediate transition into university preparation.
  • Applicants must demonstrate strong academic promise, personal motivation, and active involvement in school or camp community leadership.
  • Women, persons living with disabilities, members of marginalized groups, and candidates who completed secondary education within the camp are strongly encouraged to apply.
  • Candidates must be prepared to submit all secondary school termly report cards alongside national examination results.

Important: These are based on a previous cohort announcement, not a guarantee of eligibility for a future intake. Applicants should check the latest official announcement before applying.

What Support Does It Provide?

Elimisha Kakuma provides programme-related support to eligible participants. Depending on the applicable programme arrangements, this has included:

  • Preparation and guidance for university applications.
  • Support in exploring higher education opportunities and external scholarships.
  • Academic and college-access preparation.
  • Limited participant support, which has included a monthly stipend, weekday breakfast and lunch, and transportation assistance where applicable.

The availability and conditions of participant support depend on the programme's arrangements. These benefits should not be interpreted as a promise to pay university tuition, accommodation, or all expenses associated with a university degree.

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official Elimisha Kakuma website and review the programme information.
  2. Look for an official announcement confirming that applications are open for a new cohort.
  3. Read the current eligibility criteria, application instructions, required documents, and deadline.
  4. Prepare the requested academic records and refugee registration documents.
  5. Submit your application using the method specified in the official announcement.

Do not assume applications are open just because the programme has a website. Check the official website for the latest intake announcement and deadline.

The deadline for the 2026–2027 cohort was 23 January 2026. That application period has passed; check with Elimisha Kakuma for information about a future cohort.

Before You Apply

  • Elimisha Kakuma is a preparation and application support programme, not a university scholarship.
  • Admission to the programme does not guarantee university admission.
  • Participation does not guarantee that you will receive an external scholarship.
  • You may need to apply separately to universities and scholarship providers.
  • Always confirm current eligibility, support offered, and application deadlines directly with the programme.

Official Links and Contact

International Vocational Training Opportunity

Malengo Ausbildung Programme

A vocational training pathway that helps eligible refugees living in Kenya prepare for professional training and future employment in Germany through German-language education, financial assistance, application guidance, and mentorship.

Important: Check the Application Status

The Malengo Ausbildung Programme is designed for eligible refugees and nationals living in Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda who want to pursue vocational training in Germany.

Malengo's official website indicates that applicants can register their interest while waiting for a new application round to open. Registering interest is not the same as submitting an application or being selected.

Before preparing your application, check the official programme page for the latest intake announcement, eligibility requirements, and instructions for applicants in Kenya.

This is a vocational training opportunity, not a conventional bachelor's degree scholarship.

About Malengo Ausbildung

Ausbildung is Germany's vocational training system. It combines classroom learning with practical, workplace-based training to prepare participants for a specific occupation.

Depending on the occupation, training usually lasts between one and four years. Trainees learn both the theoretical and practical aspects of their profession and work towards a recognised vocational qualification.

Malengo helps eligible young people from Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda prepare for this pathway by providing intensive German-language training and assistance with applications, relocation, and adjustment to life in Germany.

During vocational training, participants receive a salary from their training organisation under the applicable training arrangement.

Who Can Apply?

According to Malengo's published eligibility requirements, refugees living in Kenya may apply if they meet the programme's conditions.

Basic eligibility requirements include:

  • You are between 18 and 30 years old at the time of application.
  • You are a registered refugee currently living in Kenya. Refugee documentation is required.
  • You have completed secondary school and hold an accepted certificate, such as the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE), or an equivalent qualification from another country.
  • You have not completed a bachelor's or master's degree.
  • You can commit to a full-time, intensive German language course lasting up to one year, followed by one to four years of vocational training in Germany.
  • You are prepared to relocate for the language course and subsequent vocational training.
  • You demonstrate motivation, financial need, persistence, personal integrity, and a strong willingness to learn.

Important: Meeting the basic requirements does not guarantee selection. Malengo uses a competitive selection process, and additional conditions may apply.

Documents for Refugees in Kenya

Refugees applying from Kenya must provide acceptable proof of their refugee registration.

Malengo's published FAQs identify the following documentation routes for refugees from Kenya:

  • A valid refugee travel document; or
  • A refugee identity card together with family attestation; or
  • A refugee waiting card, which Malengo also identifies as acceptable for applicants from Kenya.

The exact documents required should be confirmed against the current application instructions. Do not assume that every type of identification is interchangeable.

Check Refugee Documentation Requirements

German Language Preparation

German is essential because vocational training involves classroom instruction and communication in the workplace.

Malengo's published FAQs state that applicants should have at least A2-level German when applying. Applicants who can demonstrate B1 or B2 proficiency and meet the other criteria may have stronger selection prospects.

Selected scholars receive intensive German-language training aimed at reaching B2 proficiency. This preparation can last up to one year and is intended to prepare them for vocational training in Germany.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their existing German proficiency through the programme's specified evidence and assessment process.

What Support Does Malengo Provide?

For selected scholars, the programme describes support that may include:

  • Intensive German-language classes up to B2 level.
  • Financial support for language classes and associated accommodation and living expenses during the language-training phase.
  • Guidance with applications for vocational training positions in Germany.
  • Assistance with vocational training visa applications and associated visa fees.
  • Support with travel arrangements, including the flight to Germany.
  • Pre-departure orientation to help prepare participants for life in Germany.
  • Assistance with finding accommodation.
  • Mentorship, community support, and access to professional psychosocial or legal assistance when needed.

These benefits apply to selected participants under the programme's arrangements. They should not be interpreted as a guarantee of selection or as a promise that every possible expense will be covered.

What Happens During and After Training?

If selected, you will first participate in the required German-language preparation. Towards the end of this phase, you will receive assistance applying for suitable vocational training positions.

If accepted by a training organisation and granted the required visa, you can travel to Germany and begin your vocational training.

Vocational training combines practical work with classroom instruction. Under the applicable arrangement, trainees receive a salary from their training organisation to help meet their living expenses.

After successfully completing training, graduates may pursue employment opportunities in their occupation. Further residence and employment options depend on German immigration rules and the individual's circumstances.

Employment, a particular salary, permanent residence, or citizenship is not guaranteed by participation in this programme.

Funding and Financial Obligations

Malengo states that its Ausbildung Programme is financed through an Income Share Agreement (ISA).

This means selected participants do not pay the programme's covered costs upfront. Under the published arrangement, participants who later earn a sufficiently high income may be required to contribute a share of their earnings back to Malengo for a limited period.

Malengo states that participants who do not secure a sufficiently high-paying job are exempt from these contributions.

Before accepting an offer:

  • Read the actual Income Share Agreement carefully.
  • Understand the income threshold, contribution percentage, payment duration, and any exemptions.
  • Confirm which costs are covered and whether any expenses remain your responsibility.
  • Ask Malengo to explain any terms you do not understand before signing.

The exact contractual terms provided to selected applicants should take precedence over general descriptions on an information page.

How to Apply

  1. Visit Malengo's official Ausbildung programme page.
  2. Read the eligibility criteria for refugees living in Kenya.
  3. Check whether a new application round is open. If applications are closed, look for the official Kenya interest-registration option.
  4. Prepare your secondary-school certificate, accepted refugee documentation, and evidence of your German-language level.
  5. If invited to proceed, complete the required language assessment and interview stages.
  6. If selected, review the programme conditions and Income Share Agreement before accepting.

Malengo states that applying and participating in its selection process are free of charge. Never pay an individual who claims they can guarantee your selection.

Visit the Official Ausbildung Programme Page

Read the Official Eligibility FAQs

Important Things to Know

  • This programme explicitly includes eligible registered refugees living in Kenya.
  • You must meet the age, education, documentation, German-language, and availability requirements.
  • You should be prepared for full-time language training and subsequent vocational training in Germany.
  • This is a vocational training pathway, not a bachelor's degree scholarship.
  • Selected trainees receive a salary during vocational training under the applicable training arrangement.
  • The programme uses an Income Share Agreement. Understand its terms before accepting an offer.
  • Registering interest does not guarantee that you can submit an application or be selected. Check the latest official intake announcement.
  • Applications and selection are free. Do not pay anyone who promises admission or selection.

Fully Funded Scholarship Opportunities

Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

Supporting talented young people facing financial and social barriers to access quality education, develop leadership skills, and contribute to their communities.

Important Information Before Applying

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a scholarship initiative implemented through selected universities and educational organisations. It is not a single scholarship with one central application form or one universal deadline.

You must apply through a participating institution that offers the degree or programme you want to study.

Each partner institution sets its own eligibility requirements, application process, available courses, selection procedure, and deadline. Some partners offer undergraduate scholarships, while others offer postgraduate scholarships.

Admission to a participating university does not automatically mean that you will receive a Mastercard Foundation scholarship. Applicants must satisfy the relevant academic admission and scholarship-selection requirements.

Always check the official partner directory to confirm whether the institution and programme you want are accepting applications.

About the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global education initiative that supports talented, service-oriented young people who face barriers to higher education.

The programme aims to help Scholars obtain relevant education, develop leadership potential, transition into meaningful work, and contribute to positive social and economic change.

Its partner network includes universities and educational organisations in Africa and other regions. Available opportunities vary by institution and may include undergraduate and master's degree programmes.

The programme places particular emphasis on expanding access for young women, refugees and forcibly displaced people, people with disabilities, and other young people whose circumstances have restricted their educational opportunities.

Official Programme Overview

Levels of Study

Scholarship levels depend on the participating institution. The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program supports the following types of education through its partner network:

1. Undergraduate Degrees

Some partners offer scholarships for students who want to begin a bachelor's degree after completing secondary school or an accepted equivalent qualification.

Eligible courses and entry requirements differ between universities. Applicants should confirm that their secondary school qualifications meet the chosen university's admission requirements.

2. Postgraduate Master's Degrees

Some partners offer scholarships for eligible applicants who have already completed a bachelor's degree and want to pursue a master's qualification.

Applicants may need a strong undergraduate academic record, relevant experience or interests, leadership evidence, and a clear connection between their proposed studies and future contribution to society.

3. Other Education Pathways

The wider Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program network has included secondary and other educational pathways through selected partners. However, not every partner offers these levels.

The Foundation's current general information states that the programme does not offer scholarships for PhD candidates.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program provides financial, academic, and personal support. The exact package depends on the institution and the scholarship offer made to an individual Scholar.

Depending on the partner's arrangements, support may include the following:

  • Tuition fees: Payment of eligible university tuition costs.
  • Accommodation: Assistance with housing or university residence costs where included in the scholarship package.
  • Living expenses: Financial assistance for eligible everyday expenses, according to the partner's terms.
  • Learning materials: Support for books, study supplies, and other academic resources.
  • Academic support: Guidance and resources to help Scholars succeed in their studies.
  • Mentorship and counselling: Personal guidance, wellbeing support, and assistance navigating university life.
  • Leadership development: Opportunities to develop leadership, service, and community-engagement skills.
  • Travel support: A return air ticket to the Scholar's country of origin where necessary and included in the applicable programme arrangements.

Important: This list describes possible forms of support across the programme. It does not mean that every partner provides every benefit or that every expense is automatically covered. Read the specific institution's scholarship terms before accepting an offer.

Official Scholarship Benefits and FAQs

Who Can Apply?

There is no single eligibility checklist that applies identically to every Mastercard Foundation partner. However, applicants are generally assessed on factors such as academic ability, financial circumstances, leadership potential, and their commitment to contributing to their communities.

Common Selection Considerations

  • Academic achievement: Applicants must meet the academic admission requirements of their chosen institution and degree programme.
  • Financial need: Applicants should be able to demonstrate that financial or socioeconomic barriers have restricted their access to education.
  • Leadership potential: Applicants may need to show initiative, responsibility, service, or leadership in their school or community.
  • Community contribution: Applicants should explain how their education and skills could benefit their communities or contribute to wider social development.
  • Programme-specific eligibility: Applicants must satisfy the institution's nationality or residency rules, age requirements where applicable, qualification requirements, and any other conditions.

The Foundation's general application guidance has described age guidelines of 29 years or younger for undergraduate applicants and 35 years or younger for graduate applicants. These should not be treated as universal rules: confirm the current age criteria published by the specific partner before applying.

Meeting the general considerations does not guarantee selection. The institution's official requirements take priority.

Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Students

Refugees and forcibly displaced people are explicitly encouraged to apply to suitable Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program partners.

The Foundation's guidance identifies forcibly displaced young people among the groups the programme seeks to support. Some partner institutions give particular consideration to applicants affected by displacement.

However, refugee eligibility is not identical at every university. A partner may require applicants to live in a particular country, hold specific immigration or refugee documents, or meet additional academic and admission conditions.

Documents Refugee Applicants May Need

Depending on the institution, applicants may be asked to provide some or all of the following:

  • Secondary school certificates and transcripts, or university certificates and transcripts for postgraduate applications.
  • Refugee identification or registration documents, if required by the partner.
  • Proof of nationality or residence where required.
  • A personal statement or scholarship essay.
  • Recommendation letters or academic references.
  • Evidence of leadership, volunteering, community service, or other relevant activities.
  • English-language test results or other evidence of language proficiency, if required.

These are examples, not a universal document checklist. Prepare documents according to the current application instructions of the partner you choose.

Official Guidance for Refugees and Displaced Applicants

Where Can You Apply?

Applications are managed by participating universities and organisations. The official directory provides information about each partner, the available level of study, personal circumstances prioritised, and application status.

Examples of partner institutions include:

  • African Leadership University (ALU), Rwanda: Undergraduate opportunities, with particular emphasis on young women, refugees, and young people with disabilities.
  • United States International University–Africa (USIU-A), Kenya: Undergraduate scholarship opportunities for eligible young Africans, including refugees and displaced people. Check the current status before applying.
  • Makerere University, Uganda: Undergraduate and master's scholarship pathways through its programme, subject to the current recruitment cycle and eligibility rules.
  • University of Cambridge, United Kingdom: Master's scholarships for eligible African applicants applying to qualifying courses.
  • McGill University, Canada: Selected postgraduate opportunities for eligible applicants from African countries, subject to the institution's programme requirements.
  • EARTH University, Costa Rica: Undergraduate opportunities for eligible young people from disadvantaged communities.

This is a selection of examples, not a complete list. The partners, programmes, and application statuses can change. Always use the official directory to find the latest information.

ALU — Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

USIU-A — Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

Makerere University — Scholarship Portal

How to Apply

Follow these steps to identify and apply for a suitable Mastercard Foundation scholarship.

  1. Choose your level of study. Decide whether you are seeking an undergraduate degree or a master's degree.
  2. Identify suitable institutions. Search the official partner directory and look for institutions offering your preferred course and level of study.
  3. Check eligibility carefully. Read the institution's requirements for academic qualifications, age, nationality or residence, refugee status where relevant, financial need, and leadership.
  4. Check the application status and deadline. Confirm that applications are open for the relevant intake. Do not rely on deadlines from previous years.
  5. Prepare your documents. Gather your academic records, identity or refugee documents where required, references, and any additional materials requested.
  6. Follow the partner's application process. Some institutions require an admission application, a separate scholarship form, or both. Others use a different process. Follow the official instructions.
  7. Complete every required section. Submit the application and documents before the deadline. Keep copies of your submission and any confirmation messages.
  8. Monitor your application. Follow the partner's instructions for interviews, additional documents, admission decisions, and scholarship selection.

Start with the Official Partner Directory

Application Fees and Other Costs

The Mastercard Foundation does not have one universal application fee for every partner. Universities may have their own admission application fees or testing requirements.

The Foundation states that where a partner requires an admission application fee, the fee will be reimbursed if the applicant is selected for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.

Do not assume that all costs incurred before selection will be paid in advance. If you cannot afford an application fee or a required test, contact the institution to ask whether a waiver or other assistance is available.

Scam warning: The Mastercard Foundation warns that social media posts or individuals claiming to recruit Scholars in exchange for payment are not affiliated with the Foundation. The Foundation does not solicit money from individuals to award scholarships.

Use official university websites and verified application portals. Never pay an agent who promises guaranteed selection.

Official Information on Fees and Fraud Prevention

Application Deadlines

There is no single deadline for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. Each participating institution determines its own application schedule.

Some partners may recruit several months before the academic year begins, while others publish their opportunities on a different timetable.

For each opportunity, confirm:

  • The application opening date.
  • The scholarship deadline.
  • Whether university admission must be completed before scholarship consideration.
  • Whether separate scholarship and admission applications are required.
  • Whether references, test results, or supporting documents must be submitted by an earlier date.

Check Current Deadlines Through Partner Institutions

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because the programme is competitive, applicants should prepare carefully and show more than an interest in receiving financial assistance.

  • Explain your educational goals. Identify the course you want to study and why it is relevant to your future.
  • Demonstrate leadership. Describe real examples of taking initiative, helping others, solving problems, or contributing to your school or community.
  • Explain your financial circumstances. Clearly describe the barriers that make it difficult to access higher education.
  • Show how you will contribute. Explain how your education and skills could benefit your community or help address a meaningful challenge.
  • Prepare accurate documents. Ensure your academic records, identity documents, references, and application information are complete and consistent.
  • Follow the institution's instructions. Do not submit a generic application without adapting it to the course and scholarship requirements of the partner.

Official Application Tips

Frequently Asked Questions

Can refugees apply?

Yes. The Foundation explicitly encourages applications from refugees and forcibly displaced people. However, applicants must meet the requirements of the specific partner institution.

Can I apply directly to the Mastercard Foundation?

No. Prospective Scholars should apply through a participating university or organisation. The partner manages the application and selection process.

Does admission to a partner university guarantee a scholarship?

No. University admission and scholarship selection are distinct decisions. You must meet the scholarship criteria and be selected for funding.

Can I apply to more than one partner institution?

Yes. Applicants may apply to multiple partners, subject to each institution's application rules. Check each partner's deadlines and requirements separately.

Does every scholarship cover all expenses?

No universal package applies to every partner. Financial support may include tuition, accommodation, learning materials, living expenses, travel, and additional support, but the precise benefits depend on the institution and scholarship offer.

Can I apply for a PhD?

The Foundation's current general programme guidance states that doctoral scholarships are not currently offered through the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. Confirm the available levels with the partner institution.

Where can I find the correct application deadline?

Visit the official partner directory and open the page for your chosen institution. Its official scholarship page should provide the relevant application instructions and deadline.

International Secondary Education Scholarship

United World Colleges (UWC)

A global education movement bringing together students from different countries, cultures, and backgrounds to study, collaborate, and contribute to a more peaceful and sustainable world.

Important Information Before Applying

UWC is primarily a two-year international secondary-school programme, not a university bachelor's degree scholarship.

Students generally attend a UWC school or college to complete the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) or, at selected institutions, the International Baccalaureate Career-related Programme (IBCP).

UWC offers scholarships through its national committees and other approved application routes. Financial support can be full, all-inclusive, up to fully funded, or partial.

Scholarship availability depends on the school, the places allocated to the relevant committee, available funding, and the applicant's assessed financial need.

Applicants should check the age and education requirements carefully. Meeting the general UWC criteria does not guarantee admission or a scholarship.

About United World Colleges

United World Colleges is a global movement that uses education to bring together young people from diverse national, cultural, social, and economic backgrounds.

UWC schools encourage students to learn alongside people whose experiences and perspectives may be different from their own. The educational experience combines academic study with community service, extracurricular activities, intercultural learning, and personal development.

UWC aims to help young people become active, responsible citizens who can contribute to positive change in their communities and beyond.

The movement includes schools and colleges in different countries. Each school has its own learning environment, location, and opportunities, while sharing the broader UWC mission and values.

Official UWC Website

Level of Study and Duration

International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme

The IBDP is a two-year pre-university qualification studied by students at UWC schools and colleges. It is internationally recognised and can be used when applying to universities, subject to each university's admission requirements.

International Baccalaureate Career-related Programme

Selected UWC institutions offer the IBCP, which combines academic study with career-related learning. Availability depends on the school.

UWC is therefore particularly relevant to eligible students who are at the appropriate secondary-school stage and want to continue their education in an international learning environment.

Important: UWC should not be confused with a scholarship for someone who has already completed secondary school and wants to begin a bachelor's degree. Its standard IBDP/IBCP route has specific age and educational-stage requirements.

Official Information on UWC Programmes

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

UWC scholarships vary in value and coverage. Financial support is assessed through the relevant application route, and the final package depends on the available scholarship and the student's financial circumstances.

Depending on the award, support may include:

  • Tuition fees: Full or partial payment of school tuition.
  • Accommodation: Room and board at the UWC school or college.
  • Books and learning materials: Support for educational resources required during the programme.
  • IB examination fees: Payment of International Baccalaureate examination registration costs where covered.
  • Educational activities: Support for eligible curricular trips, project weeks, and other school activities.
  • Travel and visa expenses: These may be included in all-inclusive awards or other packages that specifically cover them.
  • Pocket money and additional costs: Some all-inclusive scholarships provide pocket money and cover other reasonable expenses.

Not every scholarship covers all these expenses. Some awards cover tuition and accommodation but leave travel, visa costs, personal expenses, or other items to the family.

Before accepting an offer, read the scholarship conditions carefully and confirm exactly what is covered and what you would need to pay yourself.

Official UWC Fees and Scholarships Information

Types of Scholarships and Financial Support

1. All-inclusive scholarships

These awards can cover tuition, accommodation, meals, books, IB examination fees, eligible school activities, visa and travel expenses, pocket money, and other reasonable costs.

2. Full scholarships

Full scholarships usually cover tuition, room and board, books, IB examination fees, and curricular activities. Some expenses may still fall outside the package, so applicants should check the award conditions.

3. Up-to-fully-funded scholarships

These commonly cover tuition, accommodation, meals, books, IB examination fees, and curricular trips. The exact support varies by school and award.

4. Partial scholarships

Partial awards cover some of the costs of attending UWC. The student or family may need to contribute towards the remaining fees and expenses.

UWC encourages students to apply through the appropriate national committee even if their families cannot afford the full cost of attendance. Financial need is assessed during the selection process.

Who Can Apply?

Eligibility depends on the application route and the national committee or institution handling the application. Applicants should check the requirements for their country of residence or citizenship.

Common eligibility considerations

  • Age: UWC students typically begin the two-year programme at around 16, 17 or 18 years old. Individual application routes set their own age limits.
  • Education level: Applicants must be at the appropriate stage of secondary education and meet the relevant academic progression requirements.
  • Citizenship or residency: Applicants generally apply through the UWC national committee connected to their country of residence or citizenship, subject to that committee's rules.
  • Personal qualities: UWC looks for curiosity, integrity, compassion, responsibility, openness to different perspectives, and a commitment to service.
  • English-language readiness: English is the primary language of instruction at most UWC schools. Applicants should check the language expectations for their route.
  • Financial need: Applicants seeking financial support will generally be asked to provide financial information for a needs assessment.

Academic excellence matters, but UWC selection is not based on grades alone. Selection committees also consider the applicant's values, motivation, potential, and suitability for the UWC experience.

Official Application and Selection Guidance

Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Students

UWC's commitment to bringing together students from different backgrounds can make it an option for eligible refugees and displaced students. However, the correct application route and eligibility rules must be confirmed before applying.

Refugee applicants should contact the relevant national committee to confirm whether it accepts applicants with their particular residency and documentation status.

Documents that may be requested

  • Academic transcripts and school certificates.
  • A valid identification document or passport, where available and required.
  • Refugee registration or identification documents, where applicable.
  • Personal statements or responses to application questions.
  • Information about school activities, volunteering, leadership, and community involvement.
  • Financial information if the applicant is requesting a scholarship.

This is a general guide, not a fixed document list. Requirements vary between committees and application routes.

Do not assume that refugee status automatically qualifies an applicant for a UWC scholarship. The applicant must meet the age, education, residency, and other requirements of the relevant selection route.

Find the Appropriate UWC National Committee

Applying Through UWC Kenya

UWC Kenya is the national committee route for eligible applicants connected to Kenya. It selects candidates for placement at UWC schools and colleges.

Entry 2027: Application timeline

According to the official UWC Kenya website, the Entry 2027 application window runs from 1 July to 31 December 2026.

The committee specifies that application documents should be submitted during the period 1 December to 31 December 2026. Applicants should read the instructions carefully and should not submit documents outside the specified submission period.

Age requirements

For the Entry 2027 cycle, UWC Kenya states that applicants must be at least 16 and no more than 19 years old in the year they plan to attend. Applicants turning 19 in 2027 must turn 19 after 1 September 2027.

Citizenship and residency

UWC Kenya states that applicants must hold Kenyan citizenship or residency, including dual citizens. Applicants residing in Kenya must be studying and currently completing their high school education within the country.

If you are a refugee living in Kenya, contact UWC Kenya directly to confirm whether your documents and current education status meet its residency and application requirements.

Education requirements

For Entry 2027, UWC Kenya accepts applicants from recognised education backgrounds, including the Kenyan 8-4-4 curriculum, Competency-Based Education, Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel, the American curriculum, the International Baccalaureate, and homeschooling equivalents.

Applicants must meet the specific education-stage requirement stated for their curriculum and complete the required level by the specified date.

Interview-day fee

UWC Kenya lists a non-refundable fee of KSh 3,000 for attending its interview day. Fee waivers may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Applicants who cannot afford this fee should contact the committee and ask about a fee waiver before making payment.

UWC Kenya Eligibility Criteria

UWC Kenya Application Instructions and Timeline

How to Apply

  1. Check your eligibility. Review the age, education, citizenship or residency, and other requirements for the relevant application route.
  2. Choose the correct application route. Most applicants seeking financial support apply through a UWC national committee.
  3. Read the selection criteria. Understand the values, personal qualities, and educational readiness the committee is looking for.
  4. Prepare the required documents. Collect your academic records, identification, and any other documents listed in the committee's instructions.
  5. Complete the application. Follow the official instructions and submit your application during the permitted period.
  6. Participate in selection activities. Shortlisted applicants may be invited to interviews, group activities, or other assessments, depending on the committee.
  7. Complete financial information. If selected for further consideration, provide the information required for the financial needs assessment.
  8. Review the offer carefully. If nominated, confirm the school placement, scholarship coverage, and any remaining financial responsibilities before accepting.

Each national committee has its own deadlines and procedures. Do not use UWC Kenya's dates if you are applying through another committee.

Find Your National Committee

Official UWC Application Portal

Other Ways to Apply

UWC Global Selection Programme

The Global Selection Programme allows eligible students to apply for places at participating UWC schools and colleges. This route is intended for applicants who do not require financial assistance.

Applicants using the Global Selection Programme must pay the full cost of attendance and are not eligible for scholarships through that route.

Students who need financial support should normally explore the appropriate national committee route instead.

Apply Through a National Committee

Compare UWC Application Routes

What Does UWC Look For?

UWC considers the applicant as a whole. Grades are important, but the selection process also considers personal qualities, motivation, and potential to contribute to the community.

  • Intellectual curiosity: A genuine interest in learning, exploring ideas, and asking questions.
  • Commitment to UWC values: Respect for diversity, peace, sustainability, and intercultural understanding.
  • Social competence: The ability to work with people from different backgrounds and perspectives.
  • Resilience and independence: Readiness to adapt to a demanding academic and residential environment.
  • Personal responsibility: Integrity, accountability, and respect for others.
  • Service and engagement: An interest in contributing to the community and taking meaningful action.

Applicants should use genuine examples from their own experiences when describing their interests, values, leadership, and motivation.

Official UWC Selection Guidance

Important Things to Know

  • UWC is primarily a two-year secondary-school programme, not a bachelor's degree scholarship.
  • Age and educational-stage requirements are important and vary by application route.
  • Scholarships may be fully funded, all-inclusive, up to fully funded, or partial.
  • Applicants seeking financial support should use the appropriate national committee route.
  • A place at UWC and the amount of financial assistance are subject to selection and available funding.
  • Refugee applicants should confirm their eligibility and required documents with the relevant committee.
  • Applicants must check the current application timeline rather than relying on previous years' deadlines.

Refugee Scholarship and Education Pathway

UNICORE — University Corridors for Refugees

A programme coordinated by UNHCR and Italian universities that enables eligible refugees living in selected host countries to pursue master's degrees in Italy through scholarships and a safe, regular pathway to higher education.

Current Application Status

The UNICORE 8.0 application round for 2026 is closed.

Applications opened on 2 March 2026 and the general deadline was 17 April 2026 at noon Central European Summer Time. Some participating universities had different deadlines within the published application period.

The 2026 call offered scholarships for eligible refugees to begin two-year master's degree programmes in Italy in the 2026/2027 academic year.

If you missed this application round, monitor the official UNICORE website and UNHCR Kenya announcements for information about a future call. A new application round or deadline should not be assumed until it is officially announced.

Check the Official UNICORE Website

Check UNHCR Kenya Announcements

About UNICORE

UNICORE stands for University Corridors for Refugees. It is an initiative coordinated by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in partnership with Italian universities, the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, and other organisations.

The initiative aims to expand access to higher education for refugees living in countries of first asylum. It creates a safe and regular pathway for selected students to travel to Italy and continue their university education.

Participating universities offer master's scholarships and manage their own academic selection processes. UNHCR and programme partners support the wider initiative and refugee verification arrangements.

Unlike an ordinary international student admission route, UNICORE is specifically designed for eligible refugees who meet the requirements of the relevant call and participating university.

The programme does not automatically grant a place to every refugee applicant. Selection is competitive, and applicants are assessed according to academic merit, motivation, programme suitability, and the requirements published by the university.

Official UNICORE Programme Information

Level of Study and Duration

UNICORE primarily supports eligible refugees pursuing a second-cycle university qualification, which corresponds to a master's degree in the Italian higher education system.

  • Applicants must hold officially recognized refugee status (in collaboration with UNHCR) and reside in one of the designated host countries (e.g., Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, South Africa, Nigeria, Mozambique, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe).
  • Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree awarded by a recognized higher education institution (typically obtained within the last 5 years).
  • Applicants must demonstrate strong academic achievement with a Minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent to at least 24/30 under the Italian grading system).
  • Candidates must meet the specific entry and academic course requirements for their chosen Master's degree program at participating Italian host universities.
  • Applicants must have never before been enrolled in a degree program at any of the partner universities participating in the UNICORE project.
  • Candidates must demonstrate English language proficiency at CEFR Level B2 or higher through official test certificates or proof of an English-medium undergraduate degree.
  • Applicants may apply to a maximum of two participating Italian universities per call for applications cycle.
  • Candidates must successfully pass both the initial documentation evaluation and an online interview conducted by the university's expert selection committee.

Applicants must hold a qualification that is valid for admission to their chosen master's programme. A bachelor's degree alone does not guarantee eligibility: the degree, grades, subject background, and any additional admission requirements must satisfy the university's rules.

UNICORE is not a general undergraduate scholarship for students who have only completed secondary school.

Official Admission Criteria

Who Can Apply? Eligible Countries

Under the 2026 UNICORE 8.0 call, applicants had to be recognised refugees in one of the following countries:

  • Bangladesh
  • Burkina Faso
  • Cameroon
  • Ethiopia
  • India
  • Kenya
  • Mozambique
  • Niger
  • Nigeria
  • South Africa
  • Uganda
  • Zambia
  • Zimbabwe

Refugee status had to be recognised in an eligible country in accordance with the programme's verification arrangements.

Being a citizen of one of these countries is not the same as being a recognised refugee there. UNICORE is designed for refugees, not for all citizens or international students living in the listed countries.

The eligible-country list may change in future editions. Always consult the latest official call before applying.

Academic and General Eligibility

For the 2026 UNICORE 8.0 call, applicants generally had to meet the following requirements.

1. Recognised refugee status

Applicants had to be recognised as refugees in one of the countries included in the call and provide the required refugee identification or proof of registration.

2. A qualifying university degree

Applicants needed a qualification that allowed them to apply for their chosen second-cycle master's degree programme in Italy.

3. Minimum academic performance

The general 2026 criteria specified a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.0 under the grading system of the country where the applicant graduated, or the equivalent under the Italian Ministry of Education's comparison table.

Applicants should not assume that a GPA of 3.0 on one grading scale automatically equals the required result on another scale. Consult the official comparison table and the university's individual call.

4. Date of graduation

The general admission criteria for the 2026 call specified a degree obtained in or after 2021 and by the applicable application deadline. Some universities did not apply the same graduation-date limit, so individual calls must be checked carefully.

5. English proficiency

Applicants needed sufficient English proficiency for the chosen programme. A separate English language certificate was not universally required by the general UNICORE rules, but individual universities could require one or assess English during the interview.

6. Previous enrolment at partner universities

The general criteria stated that applicants must not previously have been enrolled in a degree programme at one of the partner universities. Check the individual call for the precise rule.

Important: These are requirements from the 2026 call, not a guarantee that a future edition will use exactly the same criteria.

Read the Official Eligibility Requirements

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

UNICORE scholarships combine tuition support, financial assistance, and services intended to help selected refugee students study and settle into university life in Italy.

Under the published programme information, benefits can include the following.

  • Tuition fees: Exemption from tuition fees at the participating university under the applicable scholarship.
  • Study grant: Financial support to help cover living expenses during the student's stay in Italy.
  • Air travel: Financial support for flight-ticket expenses associated with travelling to Italy.
  • Visa-related expenses: Financial assistance for eligible visa costs.
  • Accommodation: Accommodation support or arrangements according to the scholarship and local partner services.
  • Meals: Meal support as provided under the relevant university and local partner arrangements.
  • Residence permit costs: Assistance with expenses related to obtaining a study residence permit in Italy.
  • Health insurance: Support for health insurance under the programme's applicable arrangements.
  • Study materials: Assistance with learning resources, which may include books, laptops, and other academic materials.
  • Additional support services: Depending on the local arrangements, students may receive legal, social, or psychological support.

The exact scholarship package can vary by university and local partner. Applicants must read the individual university's call to understand the amount of the grant, which expenses are covered, and whether any personal costs remain.

Scholarship renewal and continued residence arrangements may depend on academic progress, including passing a minimum number of examinations under the applicable rules.

Official Scholarship Benefits and FAQs

Required Application Documents

The 2026 call listed the following mandatory documents. Requirements may differ slightly between universities and degree programmes.

  • Refugee identification: A refugee ID card or proof of refugee registration.
  • Degree certificate: Evidence of the qualification required for admission to the selected master's programme.
  • Academic transcripts: Records of examinations passed and the corresponding grades.
  • GPA documentation: Evidence of the applicant's academic average according to the relevant grading system.
  • Curriculum vitae (CV): A summary of education, relevant experience, skills, and other relevant activities.
  • Motivation letter: An explanation of the applicant's motivation and suitability for the selected programme.
  • Additional documents: Any other materials required by the selected university or master's programme.

Some documents that appear optional in the general guidance may be compulsory for a particular university. Always follow the individual call.

Documents should be genuine, readable, and consistent. The programme warns that fraudulent certificates can lead to disqualification and other consequences.

Participating Universities and Courses

UNICORE does not offer one common master's degree. Participating Italian universities publish their own calls and identify the eligible courses available under each edition.

Depending on the university and year, opportunities may span different academic disciplines. Applicants should choose a programme that matches their previous academic background and meets the university's admission requirements.

The 2026 UNICORE 8.0 edition included participating universities across Italy. The available courses, number of places, and scholarship arrangements differed between institutions.

How to choose a course

  • Check the official list of participating universities and their master's programmes.
  • Confirm that your previous degree qualifies you for the selected course.
  • Review any required subjects, grades, language skills, or other prerequisites.
  • Read the university's individual call for details about scholarship coverage and selection.

Applicants could generally submit applications to a maximum of two universities under the 2026 call. Some universities also limited the number of courses an applicant could select.

Explore Participating Universities and Courses

How to Apply

When a new call opens, applicants should follow the instructions published by UNICORE and the participating universities.

  1. Check the current call. Confirm that a new UNICORE application round has officially opened.
  2. Review eligibility. Check your refugee status, country of residence, degree, GPA, graduation date, English proficiency, and any additional university requirements.
  3. Choose your master's programmes. Compare the available courses and select programmes that match your previous studies.
  4. Read each university's call. Check the deadline, required documents, scholarship benefits, and any additional admission procedure.
  5. Create one account. Register on the official UNICORE application platform. The programme instructs applicants to use only one account.
  6. Upload your documents. Submit the required refugee documentation, academic records, GPA evidence, CV, motivation letter, and any additional materials.
  7. Submit applications to eligible universities. Follow the platform's instructions and observe the limit on the number of universities. Some institutions may also require an application through their own portal.
  8. Complete the selection process. Universities assess applications and may invite shortlisted candidates to an online interview.
  9. Monitor your account and email. Follow the status of your application and check your inbox, including the spam folder, for university communications.

This process describes the general procedure for the 2026 edition. Always follow the instructions issued for the next application round.

Official UNICORE Application Portal

Application Instructions and Admission Criteria

How Are Applicants Selected?

Each participating university is responsible for its own academic selection process. The general UNICORE 8.0 procedure included two stages.

Stage 1: Document evaluation

A university-appointed committee evaluates the application documents. The general 2026 criteria included:

  • Academic background and GPA.
  • CV, relevant experience, and personal skills.
  • The relationship between previous studies and the selected master's programme.

Under the general 2026 scoring system, candidates receiving fewer than 25 points in the document evaluation were not admitted to the next stage. Universities could have different scoring rules in their individual calls.

Stage 2: Online interview

Shortlisted applicants were invited to an online interview. The university committee could assess subject knowledge, technical skills, English proficiency, and other relevant factors.

Applicants should ensure that their application accurately reflects their qualifications and that they can discuss their previous studies and chosen programme.

Application Fees and Scam Prevention

Participation in UNICORE, including the application process, is free.

Applicants should not pay an agent, individual, or unofficial organisation to obtain a scholarship or guarantee selection.

If anyone requests money in connection with the UNICORE application process, consult UNHCR or the official programme contacts before taking any action.

Submit genuine documents only. The programme states that fraudulent academic certificates or university diplomas can result in disqualification and may lead to further consequences.

Official FAQs and Fraud Prevention Information

What Happens After Graduation?

UNICORE provides a pathway for eligible refugee students to enter Italy and pursue their master's degree. It is not, by itself, a permanent immigration or resettlement programme.

After completing the degree, graduates must consider their legal options under the rules applicable to their individual circumstances. The programme's official guidance explains that graduates may return to their country of first asylum or consider another residence permit if they meet the relevant requirements.

Selection for UNICORE should not be interpreted as a guarantee of permanent residence in Italy or permission to settle in another European country.

Students should read the programme guidance on residence permits and seek reliable advice about their individual circumstances.

Read Official Guidance on Life After Graduation

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a refugee living in Kenya apply?

Kenya was included in the eligible-country list for the 2026 UNICORE 8.0 call. Applicants still needed recognised refugee status and had to meet the academic and university-specific requirements. The 2026 call is now closed.

Can I apply if I have only completed secondary school?

No, not for the standard UNICORE master's route. Applicants need a qualifying higher education degree that meets the entry requirements of their chosen master's programme.

Can I apply if my bachelor's degree was earned outside Kenya?

The general FAQ allows some applicants with degrees from outside their country of asylum, but individual universities may restrict this. Read the relevant university's call before applying.

Do I need an IELTS or other English certificate?

A separate certificate was not a universal requirement under the general 2026 guidance. However, some universities or programmes may require one, and English proficiency may be assessed during an interview.

Can I apply to more than one university?

The 2026 call allowed applicants to apply to a maximum of two universities. Check the rules of any future edition before submitting applications.

Is the scholarship fully funded?

UNICORE provides substantial support, including tuition exemption, a study grant, and assistance with travel and visa-related expenses. The exact benefits and services depend on the individual university and scholarship arrangements, so applicants should confirm what is covered.

Is the application free?

Yes. The official programme states that participation and the application process are free. Be cautious of anyone asking for money to secure selection.

When can I apply again?

The 2026 call is closed. Check the official UNICORE website and UNHCR Kenya announcements for any future application round. Do not assume that a new deadline has been announced until it appears on an official source.

Use these official resources to confirm programme details, eligibility requirements, and future calls.
