SNHU Scholarship — JRS Kenya & Global Education Movement

An online U.S. university degree opportunity for eligible refugee learners in Kenya, delivered through a partnership involving Southern New Hampshire University (SNHU), the Global Education Movement (GEM), and Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS) Kenya.

Opportunity type: Undergraduate degree programme

Institution: Southern New Hampshire University (SNHU), USA

Programme partners: Global Education Movement (GEM) and JRS Kenya

Study mode: Online, competency-based learning with local support

Location: Kenya, through the programme's local learning support

Latest verified application deadline: 31 March 2026

Current status: 2026 application window closed; a new intake has not been confirmed here.

1. About the Programme

The SNHU programme offers eligible refugee learners an opportunity to pursue an accredited U.S. undergraduate degree through flexible online study. In Kenya, SNHU's Global Education Movement works with JRS Kenya to combine university learning with local academic guidance and career-development support.

The learning model is competency-based, meaning students demonstrate what they know through practical work and projects. Students can receive academic coaching and support as they progress through their studies.

This is a university degree opportunity, not merely a short online course or a general scholarship directory.

2. What Support Does It Offer?

According to the official 2026 call, the programme offered selected students support that included:

  • An opportunity to pursue an accredited SNHU bachelor's degree online.
  • A study laptop for use throughout the programme.
  • Internet or data support for online learning.
  • Access to a physical learning centre and study space.
  • Academic coaching and mentorship.
  • Student community activities and leadership opportunities.
  • Professional development, including work-readiness and communication skills.
  • Internship and networking opportunities through partner organisations.
  • Counselling and wellbeing support.
  • Exposure to career pathways and industry partners.

Important: The exact funding arrangement, eligible degree options, and support available should be confirmed in the next official call. Do not assume that every cost or expense is covered unless the current programme announcement explicitly says so.

3. Who Can Apply?

The programme is designed to expand access to higher education for refugee learners. However, the 2026 announcement linked above does not provide a complete list of eligibility requirements in its main text. In the previous criteria:

  • Applicants must hold officially recognized refugee status, asylum-seeker status, or belong to an economically vulnerable host community family.
  • Candidates must reside within geographic commuting distance of an active SNHU GEM partner in-person site (e.g., Kakuma, Nairobi, Kigali, Dzaleka, or Beirut).
  • Applicants must hold a completed secondary school completion certificate (such as KCSE, UACE, High School Diploma, or national equivalent).
  • Candidates must demonstrate basic oral and written English comprehension sufficient to complete project-based academic assignments.
  • Applicants must commit to a self-paced, project-based competency learning model rather than taking traditional exam-based academic courses.
  • There are no age limits or maximum age restrictions required to apply for or enroll in SNHU GEM degree programs.
  • Candidates must possess basic computer literacy skills and a commitment to completing mandatory on-site orientation sessions.
  • Applicants must commit to spending required weekly learning hours at local partner technology centers to maintain active academic progress.

Meeting general admission expectations does not automatically guarantee selection for the JRS-supported programme.

4. Subjects and Degree Options

SNHU offers a range of degree programmes, but applicants should not assume that every SNHU major is available through the JRS/GEM opportunity in Kenya. The degree options open to a particular cohort must be confirmed in the relevant call or with the programme team.

Students interested in information technology, software, business, communications, or other fields should verify the available programmes before applying.

Visit Southern New Hampshire University

5. Application Process

  1. Check the official UNHCR Kenya announcements page for a new SNHU/JRS application call.
  2. Read the entire announcement and confirm the eligibility requirements before starting an application.
  3. Prepare the academic, identity, refugee-registration, and other documents specifically requested in the new call.
  4. Submit the application through the official application link provided in that announcement.
  5. Follow any instructions for assessments, interviews, document verification, or subsequent selection stages.

Do not use an old application form as proof that applications are currently open. The form linked in the 2026 announcement belongs to the previous intake.

6. Application Status and Deadline

The latest verified call found for this listing was published on 16 March 2026, with a deadline of 31 March 2026. That deadline has passed.

As of the last verification for this page, a new application deadline had not been confirmed. Applicants should check the official announcements page rather than relying on social-media reposts or outdated forms.

Check UNHCR Kenya Announcements

7. Official Links

  • Official 2026 SNHU Scholarship Announcement — UNHCR Kenya
  • UNHCR Kenya Announcements
  • SNHU Global Education Movement — Locations and Partners
  • JRS — Education Beyond Borders, including the Kakuma programme

8. Important Reminder

The SNHU/JRS opportunity can provide a pathway to a U.S. university degree while allowing students to study online with local support. However, applications are not continuously open. Check the official announcement for the next intake, eligible applicants, degree choices, and funding details.

Be cautious of anyone asking you to pay a fee to secure selection or promising guaranteed admission. Use official programme announcements and application channels.

Online University & Financial Aid

University of the People (UoPeople)

Associate and Bachelor's Degrees

Institution: University of the People (UoPeople)

Institution Type: Non-profit, online university

Location: United States — online study

Study Level: Associate and Bachelor's degrees

Funding Type: Tuition-free education with separate financial aid opportunities for eligible students

Study Mode: Online

Application Status: Admission applications are available; scholarship funding depends on eligibility and availability.

Official Website: Visit University of the People

About University of the People

University of the People (UoPeople) is a non-profit, tuition-free online university offering degree programmes to students around the world.

Its online learning model allows students to study without relocating to a physical campus. This can be useful for students who cannot afford international travel or living expenses in another country.

However, tuition-free does not mean that every part of studying is free. Students may be responsible for an application fee and course assessment fees unless they receive financial assistance.

Is UoPeople a Scholarship?

No. University of the People is a university, not a single scholarship programme.

The university does not charge traditional tuition fees. It offers separate scholarships and financial assistance to eligible applicants and students who need help paying its application or course assessment fees.

Scholarship funding is not automatic. Students must first be accepted to the university before requesting scholarship support through the student portal.

Awards are subject to funding availability and the university's conditions. Students should not assume that every fee will be covered before receiving confirmation of their award.

Available Study Programmes

UoPeople offers online programmes in several academic fields. Undergraduate options include:

Technology

  • Associate of Science in Computer Science
  • Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

Business

  • Associate of Science in Business Administration
  • Bachelor of Science in Business Administration

Health

  • Bachelor of Science in Health Science

Programme availability and degree requirements can change. Check the current university catalogue for the latest programme list and admission requirements.

View the Official University Catalogue

Who Can Apply?

UoPeople accepts applications from qualified students internationally, subject to its admission policies. Applicants generally need to:

  • Meet the admission requirements for their chosen programme.
  • Provide the educational information and supporting documents requested during the application process.
  • Meet the applicable English-language requirements for an English-taught programme.
  • Have reliable access to a device and internet connection suitable for online study.
  • Be prepared to complete coursework and assessments within the university's academic schedule.

Applicants with refugee status can explore the university's admission and financial aid options. They should confirm which identity and education documents are accepted for their individual circumstances.

Admission to the university does not guarantee a scholarship.

What Does It Cost?

UoPeople does not charge tuition or fees for ordinary course instruction and learning materials. However, application and assessment fees apply.

According to the university's 2026/27 undergraduate catalogue, the listed fees include:

  • Application fee: US$60.
  • Undergraduate course assessment fee: US$180 per course.
  • Estimated Associate of Science in Computer Science total: US$3,660.
  • Estimated Bachelor of Science in Computer Science total: US$7,260.

These are estimated costs for students completing the programmes entirely at UoPeople. Transfer credits, additional courses, fee changes and financial aid may affect the final amount.

Important: These costs can still be significant for students with limited financial resources. Apply for available aid and confirm your actual fee obligations before committing to a programme.

Check Official Undergraduate Fees

Scholarships and Financial Assistance

UoPeople provides scholarship opportunities to help eligible students who cannot afford the university's fees. Assistance may cover some or all eligible course assessment fees, depending on the award.

The university states that scholarship requests are considered after a student has been accepted. Students can request assistance through the Funding page in their student portal.

Important conditions include:

  • Scholarship awards are subject to available funding.
  • Students may need to apply again for assistance in a later term.
  • Scholarship funds are applied to eligible university fees rather than paid directly to the student.
  • Some awards have limits on the number of assessment fees they cover.
  • Students must meet the relevant academic progress and scholarship conditions to retain assistance.

Do not assume that an award covers every course, all application costs or other personal expenses.

Explore Official UoPeople Scholarships

How to Apply

Students interested in UoPeople should follow these steps:

  1. Visit the official website and choose the programme you wish to study.
  2. Review the admission requirements, programme details and current fee schedule.
  3. Complete the online admission application and provide the requested educational and personal information.
  4. Follow the university's instructions for any required application fee or request for a fee grant.
  5. Complete the admission process and wait for the university's decision.
  6. After acceptance, access the student portal and look for the Funding page to request available scholarship assistance.
  7. Review the award decision and confirm which fees are covered before making financial commitments.

The university's admission process and scholarship application process are separate. Being admitted does not mean that financial aid has been approved.

Start at the Official UoPeople Website

What You Need for Online Study

Since programmes are delivered online, students should consider the practical requirements before applying.

  • A suitable computer or supported device.
  • A stable internet connection.
  • Enough data or connectivity to access learning materials.
  • A quiet place and regular time for independent study.
  • A plan for paying any fees not covered by an approved scholarship.

Students studying from refugee settlements or other underserved communities should consider internet availability, electricity and the cost of mobile data before committing to an online degree.

Application Deadlines and Current Status

UoPeople has its own admission periods and application procedures. The university's scholarship assistance is handled separately and depends on funding availability.

There is no single deadline that applies to every UoPeople scholarship. Applicants should check the current admission calendar and available financial aid options directly with the university.

Current listing status: Admission information is available online; the availability of a particular scholarship and the amount of assistance must be confirmed with UoPeople.

Check Current Scholarship Availability

Important Safety Information

  • Use the official UoPeople website for admission and financial aid information.
  • Be cautious of anyone promising guaranteed scholarship approval in exchange for money.
  • Do not assume that an admission offer includes a scholarship award.
  • Read the fee schedule carefully and verify any payment instructions directly with the university.
  • Keep copies of your application, admission decision and financial aid correspondence.

Columbia University Scholarship for Displaced Students

A university-wide scholarship initiative designed to help eligible refugee and displaced students access higher education at Columbia University in New York, USA.

Scholarship provider: Columbia University, administered by Columbia Global

Scholarship name: Columbia University Scholarship for Displaced Students (CUSDS)

Study levels: Undergraduate and graduate degrees, depending on the participating school and programme

Study location: Columbia University, New York, United States

Funding: Full tuition and assistance with non-tuition expenses for selected students

Intended applicants: Eligible refugee and displaced students

Latest verified status: Not accepting applications for the 2026–2027 academic year

1. Current Application Status

Applications are currently closed for the 2026–2027 academic year.

Columbia University's official scholarship page confirms that it is not accepting applications for this academic year. A new application period has not been confirmed here.

Students should check the official scholarship page for future announcements. Do not rely on old application forms, previous deadlines or third-party websites claiming that applications are open.

Check the Official Scholarship Status

2. About the Scholarship

The Columbia University Scholarship for Displaced Students was launched in 2019 to help address barriers to higher education faced by people whose education and lives have been disrupted by displacement.

Administered by Columbia Global in partnership with participating schools across the university, the programme has supported displaced students pursuing degrees in different academic fields.

The programme has historically supported students from different countries and backgrounds. However, its availability depends on the university's current selection arrangements and participating schools.

Read About Previous Scholarship Recipients

3. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

Columbia's official description states that accepted students receive full tuition and assistance with non-tuition expenses. Historical programme information describes support for accommodation and living expenses.

The exact financial package and covered costs must be confirmed in any future scholarship announcement and the student's award terms.

  • Full tuition for the supported degree programme.
  • Assistance with eligible expenses beyond tuition.
  • Potential support for housing and living costs, according to the applicable award arrangement.

Important: Do not assume that travel, visa expenses, health insurance, personal purchases or every other cost will automatically be covered. Check the official terms if a new selection round is announced.

4. Which Study Levels Are Supported?

The scholarship has supported students pursuing undergraduate and graduate degrees through participating Columbia schools. The available programmes can vary according to the school's participation and admission requirements.

Applicants interested in computer science, engineering, technology or another field should confirm whether their intended degree and school are included in any future scholarship round.

This opportunity is for university-level study. It is not a general short-course scholarship or an online-only degree programme.

Visit Columbia University's Official Website

5. Who May Be Eligible?

The scholarship was created for eligible displaced students. Historical programme information has included foreign nationals with refugee status, people who have received asylum or applied for asylum in the United States, and certain other displaced people covered by the programme's eligibility rules.

These historical categories should not be treated as a confirmed eligibility checklist for a future intake. Columbia must publish or confirm the applicable rules before a new application can be assessed.

  • Applicants must hold official recognized refugee status globally, have received US asylum, or have an active asylum application pending in the United States.
  • Candidates living under Temporary Protected Status (TPS), humanitarian parole, or Special Immigrant Visas (e.g., eligible Afghan or Ukrainian nationals) in the US are eligible to apply.
  • Applicants who are internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing outside their home region due to conflict or persecution qualify for consideration.
  • Candidates must apply to and secure admission to an eligible, participating undergraduate or graduate degree program at Columbia University.
  • US citizens and US permanent residents (green card holders) are strictly ineligible for this award.
  • There are no age restrictions or maximum age limits to apply for or receive the CUSDS scholarship.
  • Applicants must demonstrate strong academic merit and meet the competitive admission prerequisites of their target Columbia school.
  • Candidates must commit to enrolling as full-time, on-campus students across participating degree programs.

Living in a refugee-hosting country or holding refugee documentation does not by itself guarantee eligibility, admission or a scholarship.

6. How Does the Application Process Work?

Columbia's process for admitting displaced students involves university admissions timelines and the participating schools. The programme should not be treated as a scholarship with a permanently open application form.

If a new application round is announced, applicants should:

  1. Read the new announcement on Columbia Global's official website.
  2. Confirm that the scholarship is accepting applications for their intended academic year.
  3. Check the participating schools, degree options and eligibility requirements.
  4. Prepare academic records, identity or refugee-status evidence and other requested documents.
  5. Follow the published instructions for scholarship consideration and university admission.
  6. Observe the stated deadlines and any additional school-specific requirements.

Do not submit personal documents through unofficial forms or pay an individual who promises guaranteed selection.

7. Documents to Prepare for a Possible Future Round

The exact requirements for a future round are not confirmed. Depending on the degree and programme rules, applicants may need documents such as:

  • Refugee registration documents or other proof of qualifying status.
  • Secondary-school certificates and transcripts for undergraduate admission.
  • University transcripts and degree certificates for graduate admission.
  • English-language test results, if required.
  • A personal statement or application essays.
  • Academic references or recommendation letters, if required.
  • A résumé or curriculum vitae, where requested.
  • Any additional documents required by the relevant Columbia school.

This is a preparation guide, not an official application checklist. Follow the requirements of the specific degree and scholarship if applications reopen.

8. Official Links

  • Columbia University Scholarship for Displaced Students
  • Columbia Global — Displaced Students and Scholars Resources
  • Profiles of Previous Scholarship Recipients
  • Columbia University Main Website

9. Important Reminder for Applicants

The Columbia University Scholarship for Displaced Students is a significant higher-education funding initiative, but applications are not currently being accepted for the 2026–2027 academic year.

Keep your academic records organised and monitor the official Columbia Global page for changes. Do not make travel plans, pay application agents or assume that a future intake is guaranteed before Columbia publishes an official announcement.

Refugee and Displaced Persons Scholarship

University of London Refugee and Displaced Persons Scholarships

Undergraduate and Postgraduate Distance Learning

Programme Provider: University of London

Study Mode: Distance learning

Study Levels: Undergraduate and postgraduate

Funding: Scholarship applied towards eligible University of London course fees

Eligible Applicants: Refugees and displaced persons with valid supporting documentation

Current Status: Most scholarships for 2026/27 are exhausted. The next round is expected to be advertised in May or June 2027.

Official Website: Visit the Official Scholarship Page

About the Scholarship

The University of London Refugee and Displaced Persons Scholarships support eligible refugees and displaced people who wish to pursue selected university degrees through distance learning.

The scholarships are offered for a set number of places across selected programmes each academic year. Awards are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to eligibility and availability.

This opportunity can be particularly useful for people who cannot relocate to another country for university because of financial, legal or personal circumstances.

Important: This is a course-fee scholarship, not necessarily a comprehensive living-cost scholarship. It should not be assumed to cover internet access, a computer, accommodation, food, transport or other personal expenses.

Eligible Degree Programmes

The official scholarship page lists the following programmes as eligible for this scholarship:

Undergraduate Programmes

  • BSc Computer Science
  • BSc Business Administration
  • BSc Marketing
  • LLB Law

Postgraduate Programmes

  • MSc Accounting and Financial Management
  • MSc Professional Accountancy
  • MSc Data Science
  • MSc Cyber Security
  • MSc Project Management
  • Global MBA
  • Postgraduate Laws LLM
  • MA Human Rights
  • MA Global Diplomacy

The university sets a limited number of awards for each programme or group of programmes. Not every listed programme will necessarily have a scholarship available throughout the application period.

For students interested in technology: BSc Computer Science, MSc Data Science and MSc Cyber Security are particularly relevant. Check the entry requirements for each programme before applying.

Check the Official List of Eligible Programmes

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet the university's scholarship eligibility conditions. These include:

  • Having an offer of a place on one of the degree programmes listed as eligible for the scholarship.
  • Being a new student, or having become displaced while already studying with the University of London.
  • Having refugee or displaced person status supported by formal documentation.
  • Providing current status documentation that includes a valid start date and end date, as required by the university.

Priority is given to applicants who do not already hold a bachelor's or master's degree.

Applicants must also meet the academic and admission requirements of their chosen programme. Scholarship eligibility does not guarantee admission or an award.

For refugees in Kenya: Prepare the documentation accepted by the University of London to confirm your refugee or displaced status. Before applying, check whether your available document meets the university's current validity and date requirements.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The scholarship is applied against course fees payable directly to the University of London.

  • Eligible University of London course fees.
  • Support for the maximum period of registration allowed for the relevant programme, subject to the scholarship terms and continued eligibility.

The scholarship does not automatically cover every expense associated with online study. Applicants should budget separately for any computer, internet, electricity, examination-centre charges or personal living expenses not expressly included in their award.

The award may be reviewed annually. Recipients must continue to meet the scholarship's academic and other conditions.

Documents to Prepare

The university's published requirements include documentary evidence of refugee or displaced person status. Applicants should prepare the following as relevant to their course application:

  • Current formal refugee or displaced person documentation.
  • Documentation showing the required valid start and end dates.
  • Secondary school certificates and academic transcripts for undergraduate entry.
  • Degree certificates and transcripts for postgraduate entry.
  • Any additional documents required by the chosen degree programme.
  • Information requested on the programme and scholarship forms.

This is a preparation list, not a substitute for the official course-specific checklist. The university may require further evidence depending on the programme and applicant.

How to Apply

You must apply for an eligible academic programme and receive an offer before your scholarship application can be considered.

  1. Visit the official University of London website and choose an eligible distance-learning programme.
  2. Review the academic entry requirements, course fees and application deadlines.
  3. Submit the online application for your chosen programme.
  4. Wait until you receive an offer of a place.
  5. Complete the Refugee and Displaced Person scholarship application form when applications for your programme are available.
  6. Submit current documentary evidence of your refugee or displaced person status through the university's Enquiry Hub. Select the Admissions and Scholarship/Bursary Opportunities categories as directed.
  7. Check your email and the university's instructions for updates or additional requirements.

Scholarship applications are considered on a rolling basis. The university advises applicants to submit the programme application and scholarship application at least two weeks before the programme application deadline.

Submitting a scholarship form without first receiving an offer of a place will not meet the stated requirements.

Read the Official Application Instructions

Selection and Scholarship Conditions

Scholarships are limited in number and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis among eligible applicants. Availability can differ by programme.

Recipients must follow the university's academic regulations and scholarship terms. The published conditions include:

  • The scholarship cannot be transferred to another person.
  • It cannot be applied retrospectively to studies from previous academic years.
  • It may be held alongside some external funding, but cannot be combined with another University of London bursary or scholarship.
  • Recipients must make satisfactory academic progress. The published terms specify a minimum of two examinations passed in each year of registration.
  • Withdrawing from the programme or failing to comply with the scholarship terms may result in the award being withdrawn.

Read the full terms and conditions before accepting an award.

Application Deadline and Current Status

2026/27 academic year: The university states that no further scholarships are available for most of the listed programmes in this round. Three MSc Professional Accountancy scholarships are listed without the same exhausted notice, but their availability should be confirmed directly with the university.

Next expected round: Scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year, for programmes starting in or after September 2027, are expected to be advertised in May or June 2027.

These are expected announcement dates, not a confirmed application deadline. Check the official page for changes.

Check the Latest Scholarship Status

Important Safety Information

  • Use the official University of London website and Enquiry Hub to submit applications and documents.
  • Do not pay agents who promise guaranteed scholarship selection or special access to university officials.
  • Do not assume that receiving an admission offer means a scholarship has been awarded.
  • Confirm the exact course fees and scholarship coverage before accepting your place.
  • Keep copies of your programme application, offer letter, scholarship application and supporting documents.

Study in Romania — Government MFA Scholarship

A Romanian government scholarship programme that enables eligible international students from non-EU countries to pursue university studies in Romania with tuition support and other financial benefits.

Scholarship provider: Romanian Government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA)

Programme coordinator: Tempus Public Foundation is not the administrator; applications are handled through the official Study in Romania scholarship platform.

Study destination: Romania

Eligible applicants: Citizens of eligible non-EU countries, subject to programme exclusions

Study levels: Bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees

Fields: Most fields except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy

Funding: Tuition, eligible Romanian-language preparation, monthly stipend and student-dormitory accommodation support

2026–2027 application deadline: 31 March 2026

Current status: Applications for 2026–2027 are closed.

1. Current Application Status

The application period for the 2026–2027 academic year has closed.

Applications were accepted through the official online platform from 16 February to 31 March 2026. The published timetable initially indicated that selection results would be announced around 15 July 2026. Applicants should check the official portal for the latest results information and any updates from the scholarship authorities.

The next application period has not been confirmed in this listing. Do not assume that applications are open until a new official call is published.

Visit the Official Scholarship Portal

2. About the Scholarship

The Romanian Government, through its Ministry of Foreign Affairs, offers scholarships to eligible foreign citizens from non-EU countries. The programme is intended to support international education and strengthen academic and cultural relationships between Romania and participating countries.

Applications are assessed through a competitive evaluation of the submitted documents. Applicants must meet the programme's academic requirements, submit a complete application and comply with the applicable document authentication rules.

Scholarships are available at accredited Romanian higher education institutions, subject to the programme rules and available study options.

Read the Official Programme Information

3. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

According to the official programme information, scholarship recipients receive the following support under the applicable rules:

  • Tuition fees: Tuition for the approved study programme, within the normal duration of the relevant degree cycle.
  • Romanian-language preparatory year: Tuition for the preparatory year when it is required before beginning the degree.
  • Monthly stipend: A scholarship allowance during the preparatory year and eligible university studies.
  • Accommodation support: Funding for accommodation in student dormitories within the allocated government subsidy and subject to available places.
  • Application-related fees: Exemption from specified registration and application-processing fees covered by the programme rules.

Important financial warning: The scholarship does not automatically cover every expense. International transport, visa-related costs and personal expenses may need to be paid by the student. Dormitory accommodation depends on availability and the applicable subsidy.

Before accepting an award, applicants should confirm the current stipend amount and plan how to cover costs that are not included.

Check the Official Scholarship Benefits

4. Available Study Levels

  • Bachelor's degree: Undergraduate programmes generally lasting three to six years, depending on the field.
  • Master's degree: Postgraduate programmes generally lasting one to two years.
  • Doctoral degree: PhD programmes generally lasting four years under the published programme structure.

Applicants must have the academic qualification required for their intended study level. Doctoral applicants must obtain the written agreement of a doctoral supervisor belonging to the relevant doctoral school before submitting their application and must pass the required admission interview.

The scholarship does not cover Medicine, Dental Medicine or Pharmacy.

5. Language of Instruction

This is an important point for applicants who want to study in English.

  • Bachelor's programmes: Available through this scholarship in Romanian.
  • Master's programmes: Available through this scholarship in Romanian.
  • Doctoral programmes: May be available in Romanian or another language offered by the selected doctoral school, including English where permitted.

Applicants who do not know Romanian are generally provided with a Romanian-language preparatory year before beginning their bachelor's or master's programme.

Certain applicants may be exempt from the preparatory year if they satisfy the official language-proficiency or previous-study conditions.

If you need an English-taught bachelor's degree, check this language restriction carefully before considering this scholarship.

Explore Romanian Universities and Study Programmes

6. Who Can Apply?

The programme is generally open to citizens of non-EU countries, subject to the official exclusions and application rules.

Applicants must generally:

  • Be citizens of an eligible non-EU country.
  • Have good academic results, meeting the programme's minimum equivalent of 7 out of 10 in the Romanian grading system, or a "Good" result where applicable.
  • Hold the completed qualification required for the intended degree level.
  • Submit a complete application and the required documents.
  • Meet the deadline and document-authentication requirements.
  • Meet any additional requirements for the chosen programme.

The official rules exclude certain categories, including people who have requested or acquired a form of protection in Romania, specified diplomatic personnel and their families, certain international-organisation staff and people already receiving a Romanian state scholarship for the same study cycle.

Refugee status in another country is not, by itself, listed as a general exclusion in the programme rules. However, applicants must still satisfy the nationality, passport, academic and documentation requirements.

A valid passport is mandatory for the application. Applicants should not assume that a refugee ID alone can replace the required passport.

Read the Official Eligibility Conditions

Eligibility Criteria

  • Applicants must hold citizenship in a non-EU country, regardless of their current country of residence.
  • Candidates must have achieved a minimum cumulative grade point average of at least 7.0 out of 10.0 (or "Good" equivalent) in their most recent level of completed education.
  • Bachelor's and Master's degree programs funded under this award are taught exclusively in the Romanian language.
  • Applicants who do not speak Romanian are automatically granted a supplementary, fully funded 1-year preparatory Romanian language course prior to starting degree studies.
  • Candidates applying for Medicine, Dental Medicine, and Pharmacy programs are strictly excluded from receiving this scholarship award.
  • EU citizens, Romanian nationals, dual citizens holding Romanian citizenship, and diplomatic staff or employees of international organizations based in Romania are ineligible.
  • Doctoral (PhD) applicants may study in Romanian or an approved foreign language (such as English) provided they secure written agreement from an accredited university PhD supervisor prior to applying.
  • Candidates who have not reached 18 years of age by the course start date must submit notarized parental consent documentation alongside their application.

7. Required Documents

The official application instructions list documents including:

  • Copies of completed academic diplomas or certificates.
  • Academic transcripts for completed studies.
  • Birth certificate or an equivalent document.
  • A copy of the first three pages of a valid passport.
  • A curriculum vitae in English, French or Romanian.
  • Authorised translations of documents where required.
  • Proof of a name change, if applicable.
  • Additional documents required for the specific degree or applicant category.

Doctoral applicants must also provide the required letter of intent, information about their research and publications, and written agreement from the doctoral supervisor.

Academic documents must meet the applicable apostille or authentication requirements. The official rules specify that documents should be scanned individually in PDF format.

Because authentication requirements can depend on the issuing country, applicants should check the latest instructions before preparing their documents.

View the Official Document Checklist

8. How to Apply

  1. Check eligibility. Confirm that your nationality, academic qualifications and documents meet the official requirements.
  2. Choose a study field. Review eligible universities and programmes, remembering the Romanian-language requirement for bachelor's and master's degrees.
  3. Create an online account. Use the official Study in Romania scholarship platform.
  4. Complete the application. Enter your personal and academic details and upload all required documents.
  5. Review before submitting. The official FAQ warns that applications cannot be edited or updated after submission.
  6. Wait for the selection decision. Results are communicated through the official process. Selected applicants must then follow the instructions for acceptance, university enrolment and visa formalities.

Applications must be submitted through the official online platform. Applications sent directly by email or delivered to ministry offices are not accepted for this programme.

Open the Official Application Portal

9. Application Deadline and Selection

For the 2026–2027 academic year:

  • Applications opened: 16 February 2026.
  • Application deadline: 31 March 2026.
  • Initially announced result period: Around 15 July 2026.

The application window has closed. Applicants who submitted applications should monitor the official portal and their registered email addresses for results or updated instructions.

The next cycle's dates and conditions should be confirmed only when the Romanian authorities publish a new official call.

Check Official Study in Romania News

10. Frequently Asked Questions

Is this scholarship fully funded?

It provides tuition support, a monthly stipend and accommodation support under the programme's rules. However, it does not automatically cover international transport, visa costs or all personal expenses.

Can I study computer science?

Computer science and related fields may be available, depending on the university and programme options. Bachelor's and master's study under this MFA scholarship is in Romanian, so applicants who do not know Romanian generally need to complete the preparatory year.

Can I apply using only a refugee ID?

The official 2026–2027 requirements specify a valid passport. Do not assume that a refugee ID can replace it. Contact the official programme administrators if your passport situation makes it difficult to meet this requirement.

Can I apply directly to a Romanian university for this scholarship?

No. Applications for the MFA scholarship must be submitted through the official Study in Romania scholarship platform. University admission procedures may involve additional steps after selection.

Can I apply for Medicine, Dental Medicine or Pharmacy?

No. These fields are excluded from this particular MFA scholarship programme.

Are applications still open?

No. The 2026–2027 application period closed on 31 March 2026. Monitor the official portal for a future call.

About

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Edinburgh supports talented African students who have demonstrated academic ability, leadership potential, and a commitment to making a positive difference in their communities.

The programme focuses on postgraduate study and sustainability, with opportunities for eligible scholars to study on campus in Edinburgh or through selected online programmes.

Applicants should review the official programme website carefully because eligible courses, study modes, and application procedures vary.

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must meet the programme's eligibility requirements, which include:

  • Be a citizen and resident of, or hold refugee status in, an African country.
  • Have faced significant barriers to education or early-career opportunities, such as social, financial, personal, practical, or health-related barriers.
  • Demonstrate academic qualifications that meet the entry requirements for an eligible University of Edinburgh programme.
  • For Master's applicants, hold an undergraduate degree and provide the required official degree certificate and final transcript by the application deadline.
  • Demonstrate leadership potential and a record of service within their community.
  • Demonstrate experience or a clear ambition to contribute meaningfully to addressing the climate crisis.
  • Meet the programme's age requirements. For the 2027/28 intake, applicants must be 35 or younger in the year the programme begins.
  • Master's applicants must not have previously completed a postgraduate degree. Separate conditions apply to postgraduate diploma applicants.
  • Meet the requirements for the specific online or on-campus programme selected.

Applications from women, people with refugee or displaced backgrounds, and people with disabilities are particularly encouraged. Meeting these criteria does not guarantee selection.

Essential Documentation

Applicants should prepare the documents required for their selected programme and application stage. These may include:

  • Academic Documents: Official undergraduate degree certificate and final university transcript for postgraduate applicants.
  • Personal Information: Information needed to confirm citizenship, residence, or refugee status in an African country.
  • Academic and Programme Information: Details of the eligible course or study mode the applicant intends to pursue.
  • Leadership and Community Service: Information demonstrating leadership, community involvement, and potential to contribute to positive change.
  • Educational Barriers and Future Impact: Information explaining barriers the applicant has overcome and their commitment to addressing the climate crisis.

Consult the official application guidance for the complete requirements. Do not submit documents through unofficial websites or email addresses.

What It Covers

Scholarship benefits depend on the selected study route. The programme's published support includes:

  • On-campus Master's Scholarships: Approved tuition fees, accommodation, travel, a living-cost stipend, and study materials.
  • Online Master's Scholarships: Approved tuition fees and an academic stipend to support access to a laptop and reliable internet, alongside programme activities and support.
  • Online Postgraduate Diploma Scholarships: Approved tuition fees and support specified for the eligible online programme.
  • Climate Leadership Programme: Opportunities to participate in leadership development, workshops, and activities focused on sustainability and climate-related challenges.

The benefits available to each scholar depend on the study route and the official terms of the award. Review the programme website for the full details.

Application Process

  1. Review the official eligibility criteria and available on-campus or online programmes.
  2. Follow the required information-session and pre-screening process.
  3. If eligible and invited, complete the required application forms through the official application system.
  4. Submit the required academic documents and other information before the applicable deadline.
  5. Follow official communications regarding selection, interviews, and subsequent university admission.

Applicants should follow the current cycle's instructions. Attending an information session alone does not guarantee an invitation to apply or a scholarship award.

Application Deadline

For the 2027/28 cycle, the mandatory information sessions took place in September 2026. The Applicant Declaration Form deadline was 19 October 2026 at 5:00 p.m. UK time.

The main scholarship application deadline is 19 November 2026 at 5:00 p.m. UK time for eligible applicants who were invited to apply. The programme does not accept applications outside its stated process.

If you did not attend a required session or receive an invitation, check the official website for future opportunities rather than assuming you can enter the current application stage.

Refugee & Displacement Support Award

University of Toronto Scholars and Students at Risk Award Program

Undergraduate / Graduate
Country: Canada 🇨🇦
Study Level: Undergraduate and Graduate
Funding: Non-repayable financial assistance of up to CAD $10,000
Application Status: Open for the 2026 application round
Deadline: 30 November 2026, 5:00 p.m. EST

About the Award

The University of Toronto Scholars and Students at Risk Award Program provides financial assistance to undergraduate and graduate students whose education has been affected by conflict, war, displacement, or changing political circumstances.

The programme recognises that students may face serious financial and educational barriers because they have been forced to leave their home countries, seek asylum, or study in circumstances affected by political instability and changes in immigration law.

The award is administered by the University Registrar's Office and is available to eligible domestic and international students. Refugees and asylum-seekers may qualify regardless of their immigration status in Canada, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements.

Important: This is a university financial assistance award, not a separate admission programme or a guaranteed full scholarship. Applicants must satisfy the university's student or admission-status requirements before they can qualify.

Eligibility Criteria

The university identifies several qualifying circumstances. Applicants must meet an applicable circumstance, the relevant student-status requirement, and the financial-need requirement.

  • Refugees and asylum-seekers: You are, or have been within the last five years, a refugee or asylum-seeker anywhere in the world. The university states that Canadian immigration status does not determine eligibility under this criterion.
  • Students affected by political changes: Your current or proposed programme of study has been affected by changing political circumstances in your country of current or future study, including changes in immigration law.
  • Students temporarily studying at U of T: You are studying temporarily at the university, such as through an exchange, during conflict or political turmoil in the country where you are registered, and have the university's applicable special registration status.
  • University student or admission status: You must meet the university's applicable requirements. These include being a registered full-time student, a newly admitted student, or an undergraduate transfer student who has accepted an offer for full-time study in the upcoming academic year. Special rules apply to qualifying temporary exchange students.
  • Financial need: You must be able to demonstrate financial need.

For refugees living in Kenya: Refugee status in Kenya does not automatically prevent you from qualifying. However, you must also meet the University of Toronto's student or admission-status requirements and demonstrate financial need.

Being a refugee alone is not sufficient. If you have not applied to the university, received the required admission offer, or obtained the relevant student status, do not assume you can submit this award application independently.

The award is available to undergraduate and graduate students, but applicants should check the exact conditions that apply to their level and admission status.

What Does the Award Cover?

The award provides non-repayable financial assistance of up to CAD $10,000. Successful applicants do not have to repay the award as a loan.

The amount awarded may depend on the applicant's circumstances, financial need, and the university's assessment. Receiving the maximum amount is not guaranteed.

This award should not be treated as a full-ride scholarship. It does not promise to cover all tuition fees, accommodation, food, transport, health insurance, books, visa costs, or other living expenses.

Before relying on this funding, calculate the remaining cost of your programme and identify other funding sources you may need.

The official award page should be consulted for the current award-payment arrangements and any conditions attached to an offer.

Required Application Information

The university instructs applicants to complete the University of Toronto Student Awards Application and describe their circumstances. Prepare the following information so that you can complete the form accurately:

  • Refugee or asylum-seeker status: Explain your current or previous status within the last five years, if applying under this criterion.
  • Educational impact: Describe how conflict, displacement, political changes, or immigration-law changes have affected your current or proposed studies, as applicable to your circumstances.
  • Financial need: Provide clear information about your financial situation and your need for assistance.
  • University information: Have your University of Toronto student or admission details available.
  • Supporting evidence: Be prepared to provide relevant evidence of your status and financial circumstances if requested through the application process.

Follow the official application form for the exact information and supporting documents required. Do not assume that a refugee ID, passport, or other single document is sufficient for every applicant.

How to Apply

  1. Check your eligibility. Read the official award requirements and confirm that you meet both the qualifying-circumstance and university student-status conditions.
  2. Secure the required university status. If you are not already a qualifying University of Toronto student, review the admission process for your chosen programme. Admission applications have separate deadlines and requirements.
  3. Open the official award page. Use the link below to access the Scholars and Students at Risk Award Program information.
  4. Complete the Student Awards Application. Describe your refugee or asylum-seeker status, where applicable, explain how your education has been affected by the relevant circumstances, and demonstrate financial need.
  5. Review your answers. Make sure your explanation is accurate, consistent with your supporting information, and addresses the questions in the official form.
  6. Submit online before the deadline. The university states that paper applications and applications sent by email will not be accepted for this programme.
  7. Monitor your email. The university says applicants are usually informed of award decisions within one or two months after the application deadline.

Application Deadline

The published deadline for the current award round is:

30 November 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST).

This is the deadline for the award application, not a general extension of University of Toronto admission deadlines. Applicants must meet the applicable university student or admission-status requirements.

Because admission and award applications are separate processes, students who have not yet secured the required university status should check whether they can realistically meet all requirements before the award deadline.

Submit well before the deadline and check the official page for any updates.

Selection and Results

Applications are reviewed by the University Registrar's Office. Applicants are generally notified of decisions by email, usually within one or two months after the deadline.

Meeting the eligibility requirements does not guarantee an award. Applicants should not make travel arrangements or assume that all university costs will be covered before receiving an official award decision.

If selected, keep the award letter and follow the university's instructions regarding payment and any conditions attached to the funding.

Important Notes for Refugee Applicants

  • You do not have to be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident to qualify under the refugee or asylum-seeker criterion.
  • Refugees and asylum-seekers outside Canada may qualify, including eligible applicants living in Kenya.
  • You must still meet the university's student or admission-status requirements and demonstrate financial need.
  • This award is not a substitute for applying for admission to the University of Toronto.
  • The award provides up to CAD $10,000, not guaranteed full funding.
  • Applications must be submitted using the official online process. Paper and email submissions are not accepted for this award.
  • The university does not promise to arrange refugee status, visas, travel, or admission through this award.

About the Scholarship

The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the University of Toronto's flagship scholarship for exceptional international undergraduate students. It recognizes outstanding academic achievement, creativity, leadership, and the potential to make a positive contribution to the global community.

Approximately 37 students are selected each year. The scholarship is highly competitive and is available for eligible students entering their first undergraduate degree at the University of Toronto.

Applicants cannot apply independently without a school nomination. Their secondary school must nominate them through the university's official process.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Must be an international student who requires a Canadian study permit.
  • Must be in the final year of secondary school during the 2026–2027 academic year, or have graduated from secondary school no earlier than June 2026 for the September 2027 intake.
  • Must be beginning undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027.
  • Must demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, creativity, leadership, and involvement in school or community activities.
  • Must be nominated by their current secondary school.
  • Must apply for admission to an eligible undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto.

Students already attending post-secondary studies, or those beginning post-secondary studies in January 2027, are not eligible for the September 2027 Pearson Scholarship intake.

Required Documentation

Applicants should prepare the following as applicable:

  • Secondary school academic transcripts and certificates.
  • Documents required for the University of Toronto admission application.
  • The school's official nomination submitted through the university's nomination process.
  • The Pearson Scholarship application, accessible through the private link provided to nominated students.
  • Any additional information or supporting documents requested by the university.

Applicants should also check the university's instructions for English-language proficiency and any programme-specific admission requirements.

What the Scholarship Covers

The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship provides funding for four years of undergraduate study at the University of Toronto.

  • University tuition fees.
  • Books and required incidental fees.
  • Full residence support for the four-year scholarship period.

The award is intended to support scholars throughout their undergraduate studies, subject to the university's scholarship conditions.

Application Process

  1. Confirm eligibility: Check the official scholarship requirements and ensure that you qualify for the intended intake.
  2. Contact your school: Ask your current secondary school whether it participates in the Pearson Scholarship nomination process.
  3. Obtain a nomination: Your school must nominate you through the university's official process.
  4. Apply for university admission: Submit an application for an eligible undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto.
  5. Complete the scholarship application: Once nominated and after applying for admission, use the private application link provided by the university.
  6. Submit all required documents: Ensure all forms and supporting materials are submitted before the applicable deadlines.

Application Deadline

For the September 2027 intake:

  • School nomination deadline: October 9, 2026.
  • University admission application deadline for Pearson consideration: October 16, 2026.
  • Pearson Scholarship application and supporting documents deadline: November 6, 2026.

As of October 20, 2026, the school nomination and university admission deadlines for this intake have passed. The November 6 deadline applies to students who have already been nominated and completed the required admission application. Check the official website for any updates and information about future intakes.

About the Scholarship

The Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program at Stanford University develops a multidisciplinary community of graduate students who demonstrate independence of thought, purposeful leadership, and a civic mindset.

Scholars receive financial support for graduate studies and participate in leadership development activities alongside students from different academic disciplines and countries.

The programme selects scholars across Stanford's graduate schools. Applicants may come from any country and may pursue eligible graduate degrees in a range of fields.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Applicants from all countries are welcome to apply.
  • Applicants must apply to an eligible, full-time graduate degree programme at Stanford University.
  • Applicants must submit a separate application to Knight-Hennessy Scholars and to their chosen Stanford graduate programme.
  • For the 2027 cohort, applicants must have earned their first bachelor's degree in January 2020 or later, or expect to earn it by September 2027.
  • Applicants must demonstrate independence of thought, purposeful leadership, and a civic mindset.
  • Applicants must meet the admission and academic requirements of their chosen Stanford graduate programme.

The undergraduate-degree date requirement has specific exceptions for eligible military applicants. Applicants should review the official eligibility rules for full details.

Required Documentation

The Knight-Hennessy application generally includes the following components:

  • Online application form.
  • Résumé or curriculum vitae.
  • Academic transcripts and information about previous studies.
  • Standardized test scores, where required by the relevant process.
  • Recommendation letters.
  • Short answers and essays responding to the application prompts.

The Stanford graduate programme may require additional documents, such as a statement of purpose, writing samples, or programme-specific test results. Requirements vary by department.

What the Scholarship Covers

Knight-Hennessy Scholars provides financial support for up to three years of graduate study at Stanford University.

  • Tuition and associated fees, according to the programme's funding policy.
  • A stipend for living and educational expenses.
  • A travel stipend intended to support travel to and from Stanford.

Funding duration and arrangements depend on the scholar's degree programme and applicable award conditions. Some graduate degrees last longer than the standard three-year scholarship support period.

Application Process

  1. Choose a graduate programme: Identify an eligible full-time graduate degree at Stanford that matches your academic and career goals.
  2. Check eligibility: Confirm that your undergraduate-degree date and academic background meet the programme requirements.
  3. Prepare your documents: Gather transcripts, résumé, recommendation letters, and other required materials.
  4. Apply to Knight-Hennessy Scholars: Complete and submit the separate scholarship application.
  5. Apply to Stanford: Submit a separate application to your chosen graduate programme by its applicable deadline.
  6. Complete both applications on time: Check the official deadlines carefully because the two applications have separate submission requirements.

Application Deadline

The application for the 2027 Knight-Hennessy Scholars cohort closed on October 6, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

The application for the 2028 cohort is expected to open in summer 2027. Applicants must also follow the deadline for their selected Stanford graduate programme. Check the official website for updated dates and requirements.

About the Scholarship

The Elimu Scholarship Programme is administered by the Jomo Kenyatta Foundation (JKF) in partnership with Kenya's Ministry of Education. It supports learners from poor and vulnerable backgrounds who need financial assistance to continue their education.

The 2026 programme targeted learners transitioning to senior school after the 2025 Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA). It covers eligible learners across Kenya, including qualifying refugee learners in Kakuma, Kalobeyei and Dadaab.

This programme is intended for school-level education. Students seeking undergraduate or university scholarships should explore other opportunities listed on Portico Kakuma.

Eligibility Criteria

Under the official 2026 announcement, applicants were expected to meet the following requirements:

  • Be transitioning to senior school in 2026 after completing the relevant 2025 KJSEA assessment.
  • Have attended an eligible public junior school or an eligible camp-based refugee school.
  • Come from a poor or vulnerable background, such as an orphaned household, extreme poverty, neglect, or a family facing serious financial difficulties.
  • Meet the academic achievement requirements specified for the applicant's category.
  • Learners with special needs or disabilities were considered under the programme's affirmative-action provisions.

Refugee applicants: The 2026 announcement specifically included eligible refugee learners in Kakuma, Kalobeyei and Dadaab who studied in UNHCR-supported camp schools or qualifying nearby public junior schools. The stated achievement thresholds differed for boys and girls.

Eligibility rules may change for future intakes. Applicants should consult the latest official announcement before applying.

Required Documentation

Applicants should follow the current official application instructions. Documents may include:

  • The completed official Elimu Scholarship application form.
  • Academic assessment or school records requested by the programme.
  • Documents confirming the learner's identity and school details.
  • Supporting information about financial hardship or vulnerability, where required.
  • Any additional documents specified by the relevant education office, camp management office or application portal.

This is a general preparation list, not a confirmed exhaustive checklist. Use the official form for the requirements applicable to the relevant intake.

What the Scholarship Covers

According to the 2026 announcement, successful beneficiaries receive support for the three-year senior-school education period, including:

  • School fees.
  • Transport to and from school.
  • A school kit or shopping allowance.
  • Pocket money.
  • Mentorship and psychosocial support.

The exact support available under a future intake should be confirmed through the official programme announcement.

How to Apply

  1. Read the latest Elimu Scholarship announcement from the Ministry of Education or Jomo Kenyatta Foundation.
  2. Confirm that the learner meets the age, school, academic and vulnerability requirements for the relevant intake.
  3. Obtain the application form from the designated education office or the relevant camp management office, where applicable.
  4. Complete the form and attach all supporting documents requested in the official instructions.
  5. Submit the application through the officially designated online portal or physical submission point before the announced deadline.
  6. If shortlisted, attend any interview or verification process required by the programme.

Application Deadline

About Kiron Campus

Kiron Campus is an online learning platform operated by Kiron Education, a nonprofit organization that supports refugees, migrants and underserved communities through accessible education and professional development.

Learners can explore self-paced courses in areas such as digital skills, languages, business, technology and career development. Some courses and programmes provide certificates that can help learners demonstrate their skills when applying for jobs or further learning opportunities.

Basic courses are available to everyone who registers. Refugees, asylum seekers and eligible people under international protection can request verification to access additional offers, which may include Coursera for Refugees, mentoring and other professional development programmes.

Important: Kiron is not an accredited university and does not award bachelor's or master's degrees. It also does not provide university scholarships or direct financial support.

Who Can Use Kiron?

  • Anyone can register for access to Kiron's basic learning courses.
  • Learners need access to a smartphone, tablet or computer.
  • A stable internet connection is recommended.
  • A good level of English is useful because many courses are offered in English.
  • Applicants seeking expanded access must provide an accepted document proving refugee, asylum-seeker or other eligible international-protection status.
  • Some specialised programmes have additional requirements based on age, location, language, experience or professional interests.

Verification does not guarantee access to every specialised programme. Some opportunities have limited places and are available only during announced verification periods.

Documents Required

To register for basic courses, create an account and confirm your email address.

To request verification for additional refugee-focused offers, prepare an accepted legal document that proves your eligible protection status, such as a recognised refugee or asylum-seeker document.

Kiron publishes guidance on accepted documents and verification periods. Check the latest requirements before uploading your documents.

What Is Available for Free?

  • Self-paced online courses.
  • Selected digital and language learning resources.
  • Access to additional learning offers after verification.
  • Free certificates for eligible courses available through the Coursera for Refugees programme.
  • Selected mentoring, webinars and career-development opportunities.

Not every course provides a certificate, and access to partner programmes may depend on eligibility and available places. Never pay for a course that Kiron identifies as free for you.

How to Get Started

  1. Visit the official Kiron Campus website.
  2. Create an account and confirm your email address.
  3. Explore the courses available to your account and choose subjects that match your learning goals.
  4. If you qualify for expanded access, check whether the verification window is open and upload an accepted document according to Kiron's instructions.
  5. Once eligible for additional offers, follow the instructions provided for partner courses, certificates or mentoring programmes.
  6. Complete courses and keep records of any certificates or skills you earn.

Application Deadline

Kiron's basic learning platform does not use a single annual scholarship deadline. You can register and explore basic courses throughout the year.

Verification for expanded access takes place during specific announced periods. Specialised training and mentoring programmes may have their own deadlines and eligibility criteria.

Berea welcomes international students from many countries and provides substantial financial aid to those admitted. Its funding model is designed to make an undergraduate education accessible to students who could not otherwise afford it.

Students participate in the college's Labor Program, through which they work in approved campus positions while gaining practical experience and contributing to the college community.

Berea offers bachelor's degrees in a range of academic fields. Applicants should check the available majors to confirm that their intended area of study is offered.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Applicants must be international students applying under Berea College's international admissions process.
  • Applicants should demonstrate strong academic ability and readiness for college-level study.
  • Applicants must demonstrate significant financial need.
  • Applicants must meet the college's English-language proficiency requirements.
  • Applicants must meet the admission requirements for international first-year students.
  • Applicants who have already earned a bachelor's degree are not eligible for a new undergraduate degree at Berea.
  • Applicants must submit all required application materials by the international admissions deadline.

Admission is highly competitive. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission or a particular financial aid offer.

Required Documentation

International applicants should prepare the documents listed in Berea's official application checklist, including:

  • Completed international application for admission.
  • Personal essay written by the applicant.
  • Academic transcripts and secondary school certificates.
  • Letters of recommendation and other supporting materials required by the application.
  • Financial Resource Recommendation Form completed by an appropriate person who is not a close relative.
  • Official English-language proficiency test report, such as Duolingo English Test, IELTS or TOEFL, meeting the college's requirements.
  • Completed Berea College International Financial Questionnaire.

Additional documents may be requested during application review. Follow the current checklist in the applicant portal, especially for documents that need to be submitted directly by a school or recommender.

What the Funding Covers

Berea provides admitted international students with financial aid and scholarships intended to cover the major costs of undergraduate study.

  • Tuition.
  • Housing.
  • Food and meals.
  • Required college fees covered by the financial aid programme.
  • Access to the college's Labor Program, which provides work experience and earnings for personal expenses.

Beginning in Fall 2027, Berea's Financial Freedom framework states that tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies will be covered without loans for enrolled students.

Important financial note: International students may be required to pay an enrollment deposit to confirm their place. Berea states that additional financial assistance may be available to students who cannot pay all or part of the required deposit. Read the current admission offer carefully and contact the college if the deposit creates a financial barrier.

Application Process

  1. Visit Berea College's official international admissions page.
  2. Review the eligibility criteria, application checklist and deadline for the intended entry year.
  3. Complete the international application for admission.
  4. Prepare your personal essay and arrange the required recommendations.
  5. Submit your academic records, English-language test report, financial information and all other required documents.
  6. Monitor your applicant portal and email for requests for additional information.
  7. If admitted, review your financial aid offer, deposit instructions and immigration-document requirements.

Application Deadline

International applicants: November 30.

Berea lists November 30 as the international application deadline. Applicants should confirm the deadline for their intended entry year and ensure that every required document is received on time.

Admission decisions and enrollment instructions are communicated by Berea College. Submitting an application does not guarantee admission or a particular financial aid award.
