Need-Based Financial Aid

Bowdoin College Financial Aid for International Students

Bachelor's
Country: United States 🇺🇸
Study Level: Undergraduate
Funding: Full Demonstrated Financial Need
Institution: Bowdoin College, Maine

About the Opportunity

Bowdoin College is a private liberal arts college in Brunswick, Maine, United States. It welcomes students from around the world and provides financial assistance to admitted students who need support to afford their education.

Bowdoin practises need-blind admission for international applicants. This means that, in its standard first-year admissions process, a family's ability to pay does not determine whether an applicant is admitted.

The college meets the full calculated financial need of every admitted student, including international students, through financial aid packages that use grants and other resources rather than student loans.

Important: This is need-based financial aid, not a separate merit scholarship. Admission is highly competitive, and funding is based on the college's assessment of the family's financial circumstances.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Applicants from any country may apply as international students if they require a visa to study in the United States.
  • Applicants must meet Bowdoin's undergraduate admission requirements.
  • Applicants should demonstrate academic readiness for demanding college-level study.
  • Applicants seeking financial assistance must have their financial circumstances assessed by Bowdoin's Student Aid Office after admission, according to the current process.
  • Applicants must submit the required academic records, recommendations and application materials.
  • English-language proficiency must be sufficient for college-level study. English proficiency test scores are optional for international applicants, although submitted scores may be reviewed.

International transfer applicants are not eligible for Bowdoin's institutional financial aid packages. Applicants who have already earned a bachelor's degree are not eligible for undergraduate admission.

Required Documentation

First-year applicants should prepare the following materials, as applicable:

  • Completed application through the Common Application, Coalition on Scoir, or an eligible QuestBridge process.
  • Secondary school transcripts and official examination results.
  • School report and recommendation from a counsellor, principal or appropriate school official.
  • Teacher recommendations required by the application.
  • Bowdoin-specific application questions and any required supplementary materials.
  • English-language test results, if the applicant chooses to submit them.
  • Additional documents requested through the applicant portal.

Applicants educated in Kenya should arrange to submit their official KCSE results as required. Transcripts should be in English; if translation is needed, Bowdoin prefers it to be prepared by a school official or certified organisation.

International applicants who are not Canadian citizens do not need to submit financial aid materials until they receive an admission offer. If admitted, they should follow the Student Aid Office's instructions and submit the required materials within the stated timeframe.

What the Financial Aid Covers

Bowdoin assesses each admitted student's financial circumstances and builds a package to meet the student's full calculated need. The exact package depends on the college's assessment.

  • Tuition costs.
  • Housing and food costs included in the college budget.
  • Other eligible educational expenses included in the aid calculation.
  • Grant assistance and other institutional resources.
  • A small on-campus work expectation as part of the financial aid package.

Bowdoin's financial aid packages do not include student loans. However, full calculated need is determined by the college's financial aid assessment; it does not automatically mean that every personal expense or travel cost will be covered.

Application Process

  1. Choose your application route: Apply through the Common Application, Coalition on Scoir, or an eligible QuestBridge route.
  2. Complete the application: Provide your academic history, activities, recommendations and required Bowdoin-specific responses.
  3. Submit your academic documents: Arrange for your school records and official examination results to reach Bowdoin.
  4. Indicate your need for financial assistance: Follow the financial aid questions and instructions provided during the application process.
  5. Monitor your applicant portal: Check for missing documents, admissions updates and any additional instructions.
  6. If admitted, apply for financial aid: International applicants who are not Canadian citizens receive instructions for submitting financial documents after admission.
  7. Review your financial aid decision: Check the offer carefully and contact the Student Aid Office if you have questions about the award or required contribution.

Application Deadlines

Bowdoin's published deadlines for first-year applicants include:

  • Early Decision I: November 15, 2026.
  • Early Decision II: January 5, 2027.
  • Regular Decision: January 5, 2027.

International applicants who are not Canadian citizens submit their financial aid materials after admission under Bowdoin's current process. If admitted, applicants should expect to submit the requested financial documents within seven days of the offer.

Check Bowdoin's official deadline page for the latest dates, supporting-document instructions and any changes for the intended entry year.

EARTH University Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

Undergraduate

Programme Provider: EARTH University and the Mastercard Foundation

Country of Study: Costa Rica

Study Level: Undergraduate / Bachelor's Degree

Field of Study: Agricultural Sciences

Funding Type: Scholarship funding and living support

Application Status: Check the official website for the current application cycle.

About the Scholarship

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at EARTH University supports eligible young people who have the potential to become leaders and contribute to positive change in their communities. It provides an opportunity to pursue undergraduate studies in Agricultural Sciences at EARTH University in Costa Rica.

The programme focuses on academic learning, practical agricultural experience, leadership, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development. It is intended to help students develop the skills needed to address challenges in their communities and beyond.

Young people affected by displacement and other barriers to higher education may be relevant applicants, subject to the programme's current eligibility requirements.

About EARTH University

EARTH University is an international university in Costa Rica that specialises in Agricultural Sciences. Its approach combines classroom learning with practical experience, leadership development, environmental responsibility, and community engagement.

Students should be prepared for a demanding, practical programme that includes agricultural and sustainability-related learning. This is not a general Computer Science or Information Technology scholarship.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet EARTH University's admission requirements and the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program's requirements for the relevant application cycle.

Before applying, check whether you meet the following requirements:

  • You are applying for undergraduate study in Agricultural Sciences at EARTH University.
  • You meet the university's academic and language requirements.
  • You can provide the required academic records and identity documents.
  • You meet the programme's financial-need and other scholarship selection criteria, where applicable.
  • You meet the current rules concerning nationality, residence, displacement status, and eligible countries.
  • You can meet the programme's study, participation, and relocation requirements.

Important for refugees: If you are a refugee living in Kenya, contact EARTH University to confirm whether your refugee documentation and country of residence meet the current requirements. Do not assume that refugee status alone guarantees eligibility.

Academic Requirements

Applicants should have the required secondary-school qualifications for admission to EARTH University's undergraduate programme. Exact grade requirements, accepted school-leaving certificates, and any additional academic conditions must be confirmed through the university's current admissions guidance.

If your academic records were issued outside Costa Rica, ask whether they need official translations, certification, or additional evaluation.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The programme provides scholarship funding and support for eligible scholars. The exact benefits and conditions should be checked in the official scholarship information for the relevant intake.

Before accepting an offer, confirm whether the award covers:

  • University tuition and compulsory academic fees.
  • Accommodation and meals.
  • Learning materials and other academic expenses.
  • Travel to and from Costa Rica.
  • Visa, immigration, insurance, and other required costs.
  • Personal expenses not covered by the scholarship.

Do not assume every item above is covered. Obtain confirmation from the university about the exact funding package and any costs the student must pay independently.

Documents to Prepare

The final document list depends on the current application instructions. Applicants may need to prepare:

  • Secondary-school certificates and academic transcripts.
  • A valid passport or other accepted identity documentation.
  • Proof of refugee or displacement status, if applicable.
  • Evidence of financial circumstances, if requested.
  • Personal statements or application essays, if required.
  • Academic or other references, if requested.
  • Any required translations or certified copies.

This is a preparation checklist, not a confirmed official document list. Follow the instructions for the current intake.

How to Apply

  1. Visit EARTH University's official website and locate the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program information.
  2. Check whether applications for the relevant undergraduate intake are currently open.
  3. Read the eligibility criteria carefully, including the rules for international applicants and refugees.
  4. Prepare the required academic, identity, and supporting documents.
  5. Follow the university's official application instructions and submit the required information before the deadline.
  6. Monitor your email and application account for any requests for additional documents or updates.

Application Deadline and Current Status

Application dates may change between intakes. Portico Kakuma has not independently confirmed a current deadline for this scholarship.

Check the official EARTH University website before applying. If no current call is published, contact the university to ask when applications will reopen.

Important Safety Advice

  • Use official EARTH University channels to verify the application process.
  • Be cautious of individuals who promise guaranteed admission or scholarship awards in exchange for payment.
  • Do not send identity documents or sensitive personal information to unverified contacts.
  • Confirm any application charges directly with the university before making a payment.

For current eligibility rules, application dates, funding details, and application instructions, use the official sources below.

Sanctuary Scholarship

Imperial College London Undergraduate Sanctuary Scholarship

Undergraduate

Programme Provider: Imperial College London

Country of Study: United Kingdom

Study Level: Undergraduate degree

Funding Type: Full tuition fees and living-cost support

2026/27 Funding: Full tuition fees, £16,500 per year towards living costs, and a one-off £1,500 equipment grant, according to the published scholarship information.

Eligible Applicants: Applicants affected by forced displacement who meet Imperial's specific immigration, residency, academic, and financial eligibility requirements.

Application Status: Closed for 2026/27. Check the official website for future application rounds.

Last Published Deadline: 24 April 2026.

About the Sanctuary Scholarship

Imperial College London's Undergraduate Sanctuary Scholarship is intended to help eligible students affected by forced displacement access higher education. The scholarship aims to reduce financial barriers that can prevent students with the ability and potential to succeed from pursuing an undergraduate degree.

Imperial is a university in London, United Kingdom, with strengths in science, engineering, medicine, and business. Its undergraduate programmes are academically demanding and have subject-specific admission requirements.

The Sanctuary Scholarship provides substantial financial support to eligible students who meet the university's admission and scholarship conditions.

Important for refugees in Kenya: Imperial's published eligibility information includes people who have been granted refugee status in the UK or in another country. This makes the scholarship potentially relevant to some recognised refugees living in Kenya. However, refugee status alone does not guarantee eligibility, and the other requirements must also be met.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

For the published 2026/27 award, the scholarship information lists the following support:

  • Full tuition fees: Coverage of the applicable tuition fees for the eligible undergraduate programme.
  • Living-cost support: £16,500 per year towards living expenses.
  • Equipment grant: A one-off grant of £1,500 to help with eligible equipment-related costs.

These amounts refer to the published 2026/27 award and should not automatically be assumed to apply to future intakes. Funding amounts and conditions may change.

Before accepting an award, applicants should confirm how the living-cost support is paid, how many years it covers, whether it continues for the full duration of the degree, and which additional expenses are not covered.

Do not assume that separate costs such as international travel, visa-related expenses, immigration health charges, or all personal expenses are automatically covered unless Imperial confirms this.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must satisfy Imperial College London's published Sanctuary Scholarship criteria for the relevant academic year. These may include specific requirements relating to immigration status, residence, financial circumstances, and undergraduate admission.

The university's published eligibility information recognises certain applicants who have been granted refugee status in the UK or another country. Nevertheless, this should not be interpreted as an unrestricted scholarship available to every refugee worldwide.

Before applying, confirm all of the following:

  • Whether your current immigration or protection status falls within the scholarship's accepted categories.
  • Whether refugee status granted by the Kenyan authorities is accepted for the relevant intake.
  • Whether applicants must meet any additional residence, immigration, or application-timing conditions.
  • Whether you must have applied for admission to an eligible undergraduate programme at Imperial.
  • Whether you must hold an offer of admission before submitting a scholarship application.
  • Whether you must demonstrate that you cannot access mainstream student funding.
  • Whether there are additional household-income or financial-need requirements.
  • Whether your chosen degree programme is included in the scholarship.
  • Whether you meet the academic and English-language entry requirements for that programme.

For applicants living in Kakuma: Contact Imperial before investing time or money in an application. Ask specifically whether a recognised refugee currently residing in Kenya can apply while remaining outside the UK, and whether any additional immigration or residence conditions apply.

Can Refugees Living in Kenya Apply?

Imperial's published information includes refugee status granted in another country among the relevant circumstances. Therefore, a refugee who has been formally recognised in Kenya may be worth enquiring about.

However, recognition of refugee status in another country is not necessarily the only eligibility condition. The university may apply additional rules concerning residence, immigration status, access to other funding, course admission, or the timing of the application.

Refugees living in Kenya should obtain written confirmation from Imperial that they can apply from Kenya before treating the scholarship as an available option.

A refugee ID or proof of registration should not automatically be assumed to satisfy every document or immigration-status requirement.

Academic Requirements

Scholarship applicants must meet the admission requirements for their intended undergraduate degree. Imperial's courses have different academic prerequisites, and some require particular subjects or exceptionally strong grades.

Applicants should check:

  • The minimum grades and qualifications required for their chosen course.
  • Whether their national secondary-school certificate is accepted for direct undergraduate entry.
  • Whether additional qualifications or a foundation programme are required.
  • Whether specific subjects, such as Mathematics or relevant sciences, are compulsory.
  • The English-language requirements for their course.
  • Whether any admissions tests, interviews, or other course-specific assessments apply.

Meeting the Sanctuary Scholarship's eligibility criteria does not guarantee admission to Imperial College London. Applicants must satisfy the academic requirements of their chosen course as well.

Which Undergraduate Courses Are Available?

The scholarship should not be treated as an offer to study any course without restrictions. Applicants must check the scholarship rules and the eligible-course information for the relevant intake.

Imperial offers undergraduate programmes across areas including engineering, computing, mathematics, physical sciences, medicine, and business. Each programme has its own admissions requirements.

If you are interested in Computer Science, Computing, Mathematics, or a related field, check the specific course entry requirements and ask Imperial whether the course is eligible for Sanctuary Scholarship funding.

Documents to Prepare

The precise document checklist must be confirmed using the official instructions for the relevant application year. Applicants may be asked for documents such as:

  • Secondary-school certificates and academic transcripts.
  • A passport or other accepted identity documentation.
  • Official proof of refugee status or other accepted evidence of forced displacement.
  • Evidence of current residence, if required.
  • Evidence of household income or financial circumstances, if requested.
  • English-language test results, where required.
  • An Imperial undergraduate application or offer reference, if applicable.
  • Personal statements or supporting explanations, if required by the application process.
  • Certified copies or official translations where requested by the university.

This is a preparation list, not a definitive official checklist. Follow the current instructions and do not pay for additional documents or tests until you know they are required.

How to Apply

The 2026/27 scholarship round is closed. The steps below explain how prospective applicants can prepare for a future round; they do not mean that applications are currently being accepted.

  1. Visit Imperial College London's official Sanctuary Scholarship page.
  2. Read the eligibility requirements for the relevant academic year.
  3. Contact the university to confirm whether recognised refugees living in Kenya can apply from outside the UK.
  4. Identify an eligible undergraduate course and review its academic requirements.
  5. Follow Imperial's official undergraduate admissions instructions.
  6. Check whether a course offer or another admissions milestone is required before submitting the scholarship application.
  7. Prepare the required academic, identity, refugee-status, and financial documents.
  8. Submit the scholarship application through the official process when the next round opens.
  9. Monitor your email and application account for requests for additional information.

Application Deadline and Current Status

The published deadline for the 2026/27 Undergraduate Sanctuary Scholarship was 24 April 2026 at 9:00 a.m. British Summer Time.

That deadline has passed. Applications for the 2026/27 round are closed.

Current listing status: Closed — check the official website for a future round.

Do not assume that the next application cycle will use the same deadline, funding amounts, eligible immigration categories, or application process.

Questions to Ask Imperial

If you are a refugee living in Kenya, contact Imperial and request written clarification on the following:

  • Can a person granted refugee status in Kenya apply while continuing to reside in Kenya?
  • Must applicants already be residing in the UK at any point in the process?
  • What proof of refugee status is accepted?
  • Must applicants have a university offer before applying for the scholarship?
  • Which undergraduate programmes are eligible?
  • When is the next application round expected to open?
  • Will the funding package remain the same for the next academic year?

Use the contact information published on Imperial's official website to ensure your enquiry reaches the appropriate team.

Important Safety Advice

  • Use the official Imperial College London website to confirm eligibility and deadlines.
  • Be cautious of anyone promising guaranteed admission or scholarship funding in exchange for payment.
  • Do not send your passport or refugee documents to unverified agents or social media accounts.
  • Confirm any charges directly with Imperial before paying.
  • Keep copies of official application instructions and correspondence.

Official Website and Further Information

Always check the official sources for the latest eligibility criteria, course requirements, funding information, and future application dates.

Rowan Williams Cambridge Studentship

Postgraduate — Master's and PhD

Programme Provider: Cambridge Trust and the University of Cambridge

Study Destination: United Kingdom

Study Level: Master's and PhD under the current central funding listing

Funding Type: Full-cost studentship

Eligible Applicants: Overseas applicants and eligible applicants already in the UK, including refugees and asylum seekers

Application Status: Check the official funding listing and your chosen course's deadline

Official Funding Listing: Cambridge Trust — Rowan Williams Studentship

About the Studentship

The Rowan Williams Cambridge Studentship is a funding programme established by the Cambridge Trust to help students who face severe barriers to accessing higher education at the University of Cambridge.

It is intended for people affected by conflict, instability, persecution, discrimination, violence, or other serious violations of human rights. Eligible applicants may include refugees, asylum seekers, and people from areas affected by conflict.

The award can cover the cost of studying at Cambridge, including tuition fees and maintenance support. Additional allowances, such as eligible travel and immigration-related costs, may be considered according to need and the award's terms.

Important level-of-study note: Cambridge's general sanctuary funding page describes the studentship as available at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. However, the current central 2027/28 Cambridge Trust funding listing specifically lists Master's and PhD study. Undergraduate applicants should contact Cambridge or check the relevant college's current instructions before relying on this award for a bachelor's degree.

Official overview: Financial Support for Sanctuary Seekers at Cambridge

Who Can Apply?

Applicants should meet the award's criteria concerning barriers to higher education. The official listing identifies people who:

  • Come from an area of instability or a zone of conflict.
  • Have been at risk of discrimination, persecution, violence, or other abuse of their human rights.
  • Are refugees or asylum seekers and meet the programme's other eligibility requirements.
  • Are applying for a course and study level covered by the relevant funding call.
  • Meet Cambridge's academic, course-specific, and funding application requirements.

The programme's published information allows applications from overseas applicants as well as eligible applicants already in the United Kingdom. Therefore, being a refugee living outside the UK does not automatically exclude someone from consideration.

Eligibility is not a guarantee of an award. Applicants should confirm the precise criteria for their intended course and funding year on the official website.

Academic Requirements

There is no single academic grade requirement that applies to every Cambridge course. Applicants must satisfy the academic entry requirements for their chosen Master's or PhD programme.

  • For a Master's degree, applicants generally need an appropriate previous university qualification and the academic preparation required by the course.
  • For a PhD, applicants must meet the department's research and academic requirements, which may include a relevant prior degree and a research proposal.
  • Applicants must meet any applicable English-language requirements.
  • Some courses have additional prerequisites, assessments, portfolios, interviews, or research requirements.

Check the specific course page before applying. Meeting the studentship's background criteria does not replace Cambridge's academic admissions requirements.

Course information: University of Cambridge Postgraduate Study

What Does the Funding Cover?

The award may include the following, subject to the official terms and the successful applicant's circumstances:

  • University tuition fees: support for the applicable course fees.
  • Maintenance allowance: living-cost support intended to be sufficient for one person.
  • Travel costs: eligible travel expenses may be considered according to need.
  • Visa costs: eligible student visa expenses may be considered.
  • Immigration Health Surcharge: eligible costs may be considered.
  • Other allowances: additional support may be considered where permitted by the award.

This is described as a full-cost award, but applicants should check the funding offer carefully. Do not assume that every possible expense, dependent's costs, or personal expense will automatically be covered.

Documents to Prepare

The exact documents depend on the course and the current application instructions. Applicants may need to prepare:

  • Academic certificates and transcripts.
  • A CV or academic résumé.
  • A personal statement or statement of purpose, where required.
  • Academic or professional references, as specified by the course.
  • Evidence of English-language proficiency, if required.
  • A research proposal or other course-specific documents, particularly for research degrees.
  • Evidence of refugee, asylum-seeker, displacement, or other relevant circumstances, if requested.
  • Any additional information required by the Cambridge Trust funding application.

This is a preparation checklist, not a definitive list of mandatory documents. Follow the current course and scholarship instructions and submit sensitive documents only through official channels.

How to Apply

  1. Choose an eligible course. Find a suitable Master's or PhD programme and review its entry requirements, funding eligibility, and application deadline.
  2. Check the studentship's current listing. Confirm that the award is available for your intended course and entry year.
  3. Prepare your supporting documents. Gather the academic records, references, statements, and other evidence requested for your course and funding application.
  4. Apply for admission to Cambridge. Submit the university application by the deadline applicable to your course.
  5. Complete the studentship funding requirements. Follow the current Cambridge Trust instructions, including the relevant funding questions in the application portal and any additional application steps specified for the award.
  6. Monitor official communications. Check your application portal and email for updates, requests for further information, and funding decisions.

Deadline warning: For the 2027/28 funding year, the current central listing states that the deadline is the same as the funding deadline for the chosen course. Different courses may have different deadlines. Check your course and the studentship listing before applying.

View the current 2027/28 funding listing

Undergraduate Applicants

Although Cambridge's general sanctuary funding information refers to undergraduate and postgraduate students, the current central funding search entry is specifically listed for Master's and PhD study.

Students seeking a bachelor's degree should not assume that the current postgraduate application route applies to them. Contact Cambridge's sanctuary team or the relevant college to confirm whether an undergraduate route is available for the intended entry year.

Cambridge — Sanctuary Support

Important Information for Refugee Applicants

  • Applicants living outside the UK should confirm the applicable course requirements and immigration arrangements.
  • Refugee status or a history of displacement may be relevant to eligibility, but it does not guarantee admission or funding.
  • Cambridge admission and scholarship decisions are separate considerations; applicants must satisfy both sets of requirements.
  • Check whether your previous qualifications meet the requirements for your chosen course.
  • Use only official University of Cambridge and Cambridge Trust websites for applications and funding instructions.

Refugee Education and Complementary Pathways

Habesha Protection Scholarship

Technical Higher Education — TSU / Associate Degree

Programme Provider: U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI), Latin America and the Caribbean

Partner: The Shapiro Foundation and participating universities in Mexico

Study Destination: Aguascalientes, Mexico

Eligible Location for the 2026 Call: Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya

Study Level: Higher Technical University Degree (TSU), comparable in broad terms to an associate degree

Funding Type: Academic scholarship plus living and relocation support, subject to programme conditions

2026 Application Status: Closed

Next Intake: Not yet confirmed

Official Website: USCRI

About the Habesha Protection Scholarship

The Habesha Protection Scholarship is part of the Habesha Project, managed by the U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI). Through its Complementary Pathways initiative, the programme provides selected refugees with an opportunity to continue their education in Mexico while pursuing a safer and more stable future.

The 2026 Kenya call invited eligible refugees and asylum seekers living in Kakuma Refugee Camp to apply for technical higher education at participating universities in Aguascalientes, Mexico. Two scholarship places were allocated to applicants from Kenya under that call.

This is not a conventional four-year bachelor's scholarship. The advertised qualification was a Higher Technical University Degree (TSU), a technical qualification designed to provide practical and theoretical skills for employment.

The 2026 opportunity included programmes related to Information Technology, software development, data science and artificial intelligence, alongside business and engineering fields.

Official announcement: USCRI — 2026 Habesha Project Call

Eligibility Requirements

The following requirements come from the published 2026 Kenya call. They should be checked again if USCRI announces another intake, because future requirements may change.

  • Age: Between 18 and 23 years old for the TSU programme.
  • Marital and family status: Single and without children.
  • Protection status: Recognised as a refugee in Kenya under the 2026 call.
  • Place of residence: Currently residing in Kakuma Refugee Camp.
  • Academic performance: Minimum C+ in previous academic performance, or the equivalent specified in the call.
  • English proficiency: Minimum B1 level in English for the published call.
  • Academic interest: A clear interest in an available field, such as Information Technology, business or engineering.
  • Financial and educational barriers: Facing significant barriers to accessing university education.
  • Protection needs: Lacking effective protection in the country of asylum, as assessed under the programme's criteria.
  • Documentation: Able to provide the required identity, refugee-registration and academic documents.

Meeting the minimum criteria does not guarantee selection. The programme also evaluates academic preparation, motivation, adaptability, independence, language and cognitive competencies, and the applicant's need for international protection.

Applicants must follow the exact criteria in the next official call. Do not assume the 2026 requirements will remain unchanged.

Available Fields of Study

The 2026 call listed technical programmes at participating universities in Aguascalientes, Mexico. Listed academic areas included:

  • Information Technology: Multiplatform Software Development.
  • Data Science, including an Artificial Intelligence area.
  • Mechatronics and automation.
  • Business and administration-related fields.
  • Marketing and human capital management.
  • Other technical programmes listed by the participating universities.

Programme availability differs between institutions. Applicants should check the specific courses and university options in the official call before choosing a field.

Participating Universities

The 2026 Kenya call listed the following institutions in Aguascalientes, Mexico:

  • Universidad Tecnológica del Norte de Aguascalientes (UTNA).
  • Universidad Tecnológica El Retoño (UTR).

Applicants should use the official USCRI application materials to confirm the programmes offered at each institution and the course available for any future intake.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The published 2026 programme described the following benefits:

  • Academic tuition: A 100% academic scholarship covering monthly tuition for the eligible TSU programme.
  • Monthly living allowance: Up to MXN 9,000 per month for one year, intended to help cover rent, food and transportation.
  • Air travel: The cost of the plane ticket to Mexico was covered under the published programme terms.
  • Local travel: Local travel expenses were to be covered or reimbursed according to the programme conditions.
  • Student visa support: Assistance with the visa application process and logistical coordination.
  • Health insurance: Annual incorporation into Mexico's Mexican Institute of Social Security (IMSS) during studies.
  • Laptop: A laptop loan for study purposes.
  • Spanish language training: An intensive Spanish language and culture course intended to help students reach B2 level.
  • Legal and migration support: Guidance with the relevant Mexican immigration and protection procedures.

Important funding limitations: The 2026 call stated that the academic scholarship did not cover registration fees, books or degree costs. The monthly allowance was described for one year, with a second year subject to funding availability. Applicants should confirm whether these terms change in a future call and should not assume that every expense will be paid.

Important Immigration Information

This opportunity is a complementary education pathway, not simply a scholarship that allows a student to study abroad and then automatically return to their previous status.

The 2026 programme materials explained that selected students would receive support for lawful stay in Mexico and would be required to apply for refugee status and international protection there as part of the process for obtaining permanent residency.

The programme documents also clearly state that recognition as a refugee in Mexico is not guaranteed. Final immigration decisions are made by the relevant Mexican authorities.

Applicants should carefully read the programme's immigration conditions and understand the implications for their personal circumstances before accepting an offer.

Documents Required

The 2026 application instructions requested legible documents uploaded in PDF format, including:

  • Birth certificate.
  • UNHCR proof of registration or manifest, as specified in the call.
  • Valid Kenyan government refugee identification.
  • KCSE or equivalent secondary-school certificate.
  • KCPE or equivalent primary-school certificate.
  • High-school grades or academic transcript.
  • Recent passport-style face photograph with a white background.
  • Cover letter of motivation.
  • Academic and personal essay.
  • Letter of recommendation, optional under the 2026 call.
  • Other academic certificates, if available and relevant.

Selected candidates were also advised to retain the required original documents for validation. A future application may require different documents, so use the latest official checklist.

How Applicants Were Selected

The 2026 selection process included several stages:

  1. Initial document screening: Applications and supporting documents were checked against the basic eligibility criteria.
  2. Academic assessment: The submitted academic records, essay and cover letter were reviewed.
  3. Competency and motivation interview: Shortlisted applicants were assessed for motivation, academic commitment, adaptability, independence, and language and cognitive skills.
  4. Protection and vulnerability assessment: Applicants' need for international protection and support was assessed.
  5. Final selection and acceptance: Selected candidates were notified and completed the programme's acceptance procedures.

Selection considered both academic and humanitarian factors. Meeting the academic minimum alone was not sufficient to guarantee a place.

Application Status and Future Intakes

The 2026 Kenya application window ran from 1 May to 31 May 2026. That round is now closed.

UNHCR Kenya explains that opportunities such as Habesha/DIME are announced through channels serving Kakuma and Kalobeyei, including education partners, schools, community communication networks, notice boards, local radio and official announcements.

The programme has operated through multiple calls, but that does not guarantee a new Habesha Protection Scholarship intake every year. As of this listing, the next application window has not been confirmed.

Refugees interested in a future call should monitor USCRI's official website and announcements shared through trusted education and refugee-support partners in Kakuma.

UNHCR Kenya — Education Opportunities Abroad

Fraud Prevention and Important Warnings

  • The 2026 call stated that all stages of the application process were free of charge.
  • Do not pay an agent or individual who promises to secure a scholarship place.
  • Do not submit false information or altered documents. Misrepresentation can result in disqualification.
  • Do not assume that a future intake is open until USCRI publishes an official announcement.
  • Read the funding and immigration terms carefully before accepting an offer.
  • Use official programme contacts to verify application links and instructions.

University of Barcelona Refugee Support Programme

Transition Course, Undergraduate Continuation and Master's Study

Programme Provider: University of Barcelona (UB), through the UB Solidarity Foundation

Study Location: Barcelona, Spain

Programme Name: UB Refugi — Support Programme for Refugees and People from Conflict Areas

Target Applicants: Eligible refugees and people in refugee-like situations, including applicants residing in countries outside the European Union

Funding Type: Comprehensive support under previous international calls

Application Status: The previous international call closed in June 2024. A new international call has not been confirmed in the information available for this listing.

About the Programme

The University of Barcelona Refugee Support Programme, known as UB Refugi, helps refugees and people affected by armed conflict or human-rights violations access higher education and rebuild their academic and professional lives.

The programme is coordinated by the UB Solidarity Foundation. One of its initiatives has been to create a safe educational pathway for eligible displaced students who live outside the European Union and need support to continue their university studies in Spain.

Unlike programmes intended only for refugees who have already reached Spain, the previous international pathway specifically included applicants living in non-EU countries of first asylum or transit. This makes it relevant for refugees researching opportunities from countries such as Kenya.

Who Could Apply?

The 2024 international call established eligibility criteria for students affected by displacement, conflict or serious human-rights violations. Applicants generally needed to:

  • Be a non-EU applicant in a refugee or refugee-like situation, as defined by the programme's published rules.
  • Be living outside the European Union in a country of first asylum, transit or another qualifying situation.
  • Demonstrate vulnerability in the effective exercise of human, economic and social rights in their place of residence.
  • Meet the age limit and documentary requirements specified in the relevant call.
  • Have a university education or academic background suitable for the intended continuation of studies.
  • Provide evidence of displacement, vulnerability and academic qualifications.

Age requirement: The published 2024 rules required applicants to be 26 years old or younger at the application deadline. This must be checked again if another call opens.

For refugees in Kakuma: Living in Kenya does not automatically disqualify an applicant under the previous international pathway. However, applicants must satisfy the new call's eligibility rules if the programme reopens. The previous call's criteria should not be treated as permanent rules.

What Level of Study Does It Support?

The previous international scholarship pathway was designed for students continuing an existing university education. It was not a general scholarship for beginning a bachelor's degree from the first year.

The previous pathway included:

  • A transition course to prepare students for university study in Barcelona.
  • Progression to a master's degree at the University of Barcelona, subject to the relevant requirements.
  • Progression to the final two years of an eligible undergraduate degree, subject to admission requirements.

The transition course included Spanish and Catalan language learning and study related to human rights. Students needed to meet the academic and administrative requirements for progression to their chosen university programme.

The previous call excluded degrees in Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy and Psychology. Applicants should consult any future call for the list of eligible courses.

What Did the Previous Scholarship Cover?

The 2024 international call offered 10 grants with the following support:

  • Tuition fees for the transition course and eligible study stages, subject to the programme's renewal and progression conditions.
  • Accommodation.
  • A monthly allowance of €200 under the 2024 call.
  • Private health insurance.
  • Academic guidance and support.
  • Psychological and emotional support.
  • Legal assistance and guidance.
  • Support with language learning and practical aspects of settling into university life.

Important: These benefits describe the previous international call. They are not a guarantee that a future call will offer the same funding, number of places or conditions. Applicants should also confirm how travel, visa and other relocation expenses would be handled.

Documents to Prepare

The exact document list will depend on the next call. Applicants can begin organising the following materials, but should not submit them until the official instructions are published:

  • Valid refugee identification or other official evidence of displacement or refugee-like circumstances.
  • Academic certificates and university transcripts, where applicable.
  • Passport or other identity documents, if available and required.
  • Evidence of financial, social or human-rights vulnerability.
  • A curriculum vitae or academic history, if requested.
  • A motivation statement and other supporting documents specified in the call.

Do not assume that every document listed here was mandatory in the previous call. Always follow the official application instructions for the relevant intake.

How to Apply

The previous international call is closed. If a new international pathway is announced, applicants should:

  1. Read the official call and confirm that applicants residing in Kenya are eligible.
  2. Check the age limit, prior university-study requirements and eligible degree programmes.
  3. Prepare evidence of refugee status or displacement, academic records and vulnerability.
  4. Follow the published submission instructions and deadline.
  5. Check the conditions for progression from the transition course to a degree programme.

Admission, selection for funding and permission to travel to Spain are separate requirements. A scholarship offer does not remove the need to meet applicable visa conditions.

Current Application Status

The last international call described in this listing was for the 2024–2025 transition course and subsequent eligible university studies. Applications closed on 12 June 2024.

The University of Barcelona also has other refugee-support initiatives, including support for applicants already in Spain. Those initiatives have different eligibility rules and should not be confused with the international pathway.

Refugees living in Kakuma should monitor the official UB Refugi programme pages and confirm that any future announcement accepts applicants currently residing outside the European Union.

For enquiries, use the contact information published on the official programme website to ask whether a new international call is planned and whether applicants residing in Kenya will be eligible.

University of Manchester Humanitarian Scholarship

Undergraduate Bachelor's Degrees

Programme Provider: The University of Manchester

Study Location: Manchester, United Kingdom

Scholarship Type: Humanitarian scholarship for eligible international applicants affected by conflict or persecution

Target Applicants: People facing serious barriers to higher education because of armed conflict, persecution or violence

Funding: Previous awards covered tuition fees, living expenses and visa costs

Application Status: Closed. A future application round has not been confirmed.

About the Scholarship

The University of Manchester Humanitarian Scholarship was established to help people whose education has been disrupted by armed conflict, persecution or other serious humanitarian circumstances.

The programme has supported eligible international applicants who face significant barriers to starting or continuing undergraduate higher education. It is particularly relevant to people who cannot safely or realistically access university education because of the circumstances in their home country or place of displacement.

Unlike sanctuary scholarships that require applicants to already live in the United Kingdom, the previous humanitarian scholarship route considered international applicants. However, applicants living outside the UK must meet the specific eligibility conditions of any future call.

Who Can Apply?

Eligibility must be confirmed from the official guidance for the relevant application round. Previous programme criteria focused on applicants who:

  • Had experienced displacement, armed conflict, persecution or serious violence.
  • Faced substantial barriers to accessing undergraduate higher education.
  • Had not been able to start or complete an undergraduate degree because of their circumstances.
  • Met the academic entry requirements for an eligible undergraduate course at the University of Manchester.
  • Met the scholarship's nationality, residency, documentation and other requirements.

For refugees in Kakuma: Refugee status alone should not be assumed to guarantee eligibility. Applicants would need to demonstrate that they meet the scholarship's humanitarian criteria and satisfy the academic requirements. The next call may change the eligible groups or conditions.

Eligible Study Level

The Humanitarian Scholarship has been associated with undergraduate bachelor's study at the University of Manchester. It should not be treated as a general scholarship for every postgraduate or short-course programme.

Applicants must check whether their chosen bachelor's degree is eligible under the next scholarship call and whether they must first apply for university admission.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

Previous awards have been described as covering major costs associated with studying in the United Kingdom, including:

  • University tuition fees.
  • Living expenses or maintenance support.
  • Visa-related costs, subject to the published award terms.

Important funding note: These details refer to previous awards. They are not a promise that a future scholarship will provide the same benefits or cover every expense, such as flights, accommodation deposits, equipment or personal costs. Confirm the exact package before applying.

Academic Requirements

Applicants must meet the university's entry requirements for their chosen course, including the required secondary school qualifications, subject prerequisites and English language proficiency.

The required qualifications vary by degree. Applicants educated outside the United Kingdom should check the university's country-specific entry requirements and confirm whether their school-leaving certificate is accepted for direct entry or whether a foundation route is required.

Documents to Prepare

The next application call will determine the exact documentation required. Applicants can begin organising:

  • Proof of identity and refugee or displacement status, where applicable.
  • Secondary school certificates and academic transcripts.
  • Evidence explaining how conflict, persecution or humanitarian circumstances affected access to education.
  • Proof of English language proficiency, if required.
  • A personal statement or supporting statement, if requested.
  • Any additional documents required for university admission and scholarship assessment.

Do not assume that preparing these documents guarantees eligibility or that all will be required in the next round. Follow the official instructions when applications reopen.

How to Apply

The scholarship is currently closed. If the University of Manchester announces another round, applicants should:

  1. Read the new official scholarship guidance carefully.
  2. Confirm that applicants living outside the United Kingdom can apply.
  3. Check the eligible courses and academic entry requirements.
  4. Follow the stated process for university admission and scholarship application.
  5. Submit all required supporting documents before the published deadline.

Do not use an old application form or assume that the previous deadline applies to a future intake.

Current Application Status

The Humanitarian Scholarship is not currently open for applications. The University of Manchester has indicated that information about a possible 2027/2028 round will be published if available.

Applicants should monitor the official scholarship page for an announcement rather than relying on unofficial social media posts or previous deadlines.

FilmAid Kenya Media Training is not a conventional academic scholarship that pays university tuition fees for a diploma or bachelor's degree. Depending on the specific programme offered, participants may receive practical training, mentorship or opportunities to work on creative projects. The exact activities and benefits depend on the particular intake and should be confirmed directly with FilmAid Kenya.

About the Opportunity

FilmAid Kenya uses film, media and storytelling to engage refugee communities and host communities. Its work has included educational communication, community storytelling and activities that help participants develop media-related skills.

This opportunity may be useful for young people interested in creative work, communication, filmmaking or digital content production. It is separate from a university scholarship and should be considered a potential route for gaining practical experience rather than a replacement for formal higher education.

  • Photography and visual storytelling
  • Journalism and community reporting

  • Creative project development

These are potential areas of relevance, not a confirmed list of courses available in every FilmAid Kenya intake. Check the current programme announcement for the actual training offered.

Young people from refugee and host communities who are interested in media, communication and creative skills may wish to enquire about eligibility.

However, eligibility requirements, age limits, education requirements, selection criteria and whether applicants must live in a particular location can vary. Refugees living in Kakuma should confirm that a specific intake accepts applicants from their location before applying.

Funding and Costs

This is a training opportunity, not a confirmed fully funded scholarship. The availability of free training, equipment, transport assistance, meals, accommodation or other participant support has not been verified for a current intake.

Before committing to a programme, ask FilmAid Kenya whether there are any participation fees and whether any costs are covered.

Application Status

About the Scholarship

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Ashesi University supports academically talented young Africans who face financial barriers to higher education and demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to contributing to their communities.

Ashesi University is a private university located in Berekuso, Ghana. Its educational approach emphasizes ethical leadership, critical thinking, entrepreneurship and practical problem-solving.

This programme may be particularly interesting to students seeking an undergraduate degree in technology, engineering, business or management while receiving substantial financial support.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

Ashesi describes the Mastercard Foundation Scholars award as one of its most comprehensive scholarship packages. Published programme information describes support for:

  • Books, supplies and learning resources
  • Transportation to and from the scholar's home country
  • Stipends and additional socioeconomic support
  • Transition support to help students adjust to university life

Who Should Consider Applying?

For refugees living in Kakuma, Kenya: Ashesi has documented support for students from diverse backgrounds, including refugees. African Leadership University Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

Bachelor's Degree

University: African Leadership University (ALU)

Scholarship Provider: Mastercard Foundation in partnership with ALU

Country: Rwanda

Campus: Kigali, Rwanda

Study Level: Undergraduate

Study Mode: Full-time, on campus

Funding Type: Full-ride scholarship for selected scholars

Target Applicants: Academically strong African students facing financial hardship, including refugees and displaced young people

January 2027 Intake Deadline: 30 November 2026, according to ALU's published admissions page

Official Scholarship Page: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ALU

Official Application Portal: Apply to ALU

1. About the Scholarship

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at African Leadership University supports promising young Africans who have the academic ability and leadership potential to contribute to their communities but face financial barriers to higher education.

The programme places particular emphasis on young women, refugees, displaced young people and students with disabilities. It aims to make university education accessible to talented students whose circumstances might otherwise prevent them from studying.

ALU uses a learning model that emphasizes practical projects, problem-solving, leadership, entrepreneurship and learning through real-world challenges. Students are expected to take responsibility for their learning and develop solutions to problems affecting their communities and the wider world.

ALU's published programme information reports that its Mastercard Foundation Scholars community includes students from across Africa, including refugees and displaced young people.

This is a university scholarship, not a short training course, education grant or loan. Selected scholars undertake an undergraduate degree and receive financial support according to the terms of their scholarship award.

2. Why This Opportunity Matters for Refugees

Refugees often face additional barriers to university education, including limited household income, interrupted schooling, difficulty obtaining documents and the high cost of studying outside their country of residence.

ALU's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program specifically identifies refugees and displaced individuals among the groups it encourages to apply. This makes the programme relevant to eligible refugees living in Kenya, including young people in Kakuma who wish to pursue undergraduate education.

Refugee applicants must still meet the university's admission requirements, demonstrate financial need, provide supporting documents and compete for a limited number of scholarship places. Refugee status is an important consideration, but it does not guarantee selection.

3. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

ALU describes its Mastercard Foundation Scholars awards as full-ride scholarships. The university states that scholarships cover full tuition and provide additional financial support throughout the scholar's university journey.

Depending on the terms of the particular award, the package may include support for:

  • Full university tuition fees.
  • Additional costs associated with studying at ALU.
  • Accommodation and essential living expenses, where included in the award.
  • Learning resources and academic support, where covered by the scholarship.
  • Other support specified in the scholar's funding agreement.

Important: The precise coverage depends on the scholarship contract and funding partner. Applicants should read the actual award terms to establish which costs are covered. Do not assume that airfare, passport fees, visa fees, personal spending or every other expense is automatically covered.

ALU also offers tuition grants. These are different from the full-ride Mastercard Foundation scholarship: a tuition grant reduces tuition fees but does not cover all other costs of attending university.

Official financial-aid information: ALU Scholarships and Grants

4. Who Is Eligible to Apply?

According to ALU's published financial-aid eligibility criteria, applicants seeking scholarship consideration must demonstrate the following:

  • Financial need: The applicant must be unable to afford ALU tuition through other available financial assistance and must provide acceptable supporting evidence.
  • Academic ability: The applicant must meet ALU's admission requirements and demonstrate strong academic performance. ALU's published scholarship criteria specify strong national examination results, including at least a B average.
  • Age: ALU's current financial-aid page lists applicants aged 26 and below.
  • Leadership potential: Applicants should demonstrate the potential to lead, solve problems and contribute positively to their communities.
  • Community contribution: Applicants should show a commitment to using their education and opportunities to create positive change.

ALU particularly encourages applications from young women, refugees and displaced individuals, and people with physical or learning disabilities.

These are the published scholarship criteria. Applicants must also satisfy the separate admission requirements for their chosen degree programme.

Official eligibility information: ALU Financial Aid Eligibility

5. Eligibility for Refugees Living in Kakuma, Kenya

Refugees living in Kakuma are part of the audience this scholarship seeks to reach. ALU's programme has enrolled refugees and displaced young people from different African countries, and the university explicitly identifies refugee applicants as a priority group.

Applicants living in Kenya should prepare to provide their academic records and valid refugee documentation. ALU's financial-aid instructions accept humanitarian-status evidence such as a valid refugee or internally displaced person document issued by UNHCR, a local government or another relevant entity.

Refugee applicants should make their circumstances clear in the application and accurately describe their financial situation, educational history and community involvement.

Being a refugee does not remove the need to meet the academic, age, financial-need and leadership criteria. It also does not guarantee a scholarship, because the number of awards available at each intake is limited.

6. Available Degree Programmes

ALU Rwanda offers undergraduate degree programmes, including the following:

  • Software Engineering: Relevant to students interested in software development, programming and building technology products.
  • Entrepreneurial Leadership: For students interested in developing ventures, leading projects and solving business or social problems.
  • International Business and Trade: For students interested in international business, trade and related fields.

Degree availability can change. Applicants should use ALU's official website to check the programme list for their intended intake.

Official website: African Leadership University

7. Academic Documents and Qualifications

Applicants should prepare authentic academic documents that demonstrate their secondary school education and results. ALU assesses academic qualifications as part of its admission process.

Documents commonly requested during the application process include:

  • Secondary school certificate or equivalent qualification.
  • Academic transcripts or official examination results.
  • Identification documents accepted by ALU.
  • Any additional academic documents requested by admissions.

Applicants who studied in Kenya should provide the KCSE certificate and any other documents requested by ALU. If a certificate is pending, contact admissions for instructions rather than submitting an altered or unofficial replacement.

Applicants whose academic records and refugee documents use different name orders should explain the discrepancy truthfully and follow ALU's instructions for supporting documentation.

The university determines whether an applicant's qualifications meet its admission requirements. Do not assume that every certificate is automatically accepted without assessment.

8. How to Apply

ALU uses a multi-stage admissions process. Scholarship applicants first complete the university admission process and then follow the financial-aid instructions provided through the application system.

  1. Open the official application portal. Visit ALU's admissions website and select the appropriate undergraduate intake.
  2. Complete the introduction stage. Provide the requested basic personal information and begin the application.
  3. Complete the additional information stage. Provide the required academic details and upload the documents requested by ALU.
  4. Indicate your need for financial aid. Follow the application instructions to access the financial-aid process if eligible.
  5. Complete the financial-aid application. ALU may request household financial information, an explanation of your circumstances and evidence supporting the information you provide.
  6. Upload supporting evidence. Submit the requested financial documents and humanitarian-status documentation where applicable.
  7. Complete any required scholarship assessments. Follow the instructions in the financial-aid portal, including any essays or challenges assigned to applicants.
  8. Submit all required applications. Make sure the main admissions application and the financial-aid application are both completed as instructed.
  9. Monitor your application. Check your email and application portal for requests, decisions or additional instructions.

Eligibility to apply for financial aid does not guarantee an award. Scholarship decisions depend on the applicant's qualifications, financial circumstances, leadership potential and the number of available scholarships.

Start Your ALU Application

9. Financial Documents to Prepare

ALU may require evidence to verify the household's financial circumstances and the information given in the financial-aid application.

Examples listed in ALU's financial-aid instructions include:

  • Recent official bank statements, where available.
  • Mobile-money statements, where applicable.
  • Evidence of household income or lack of employment.
  • A signed declaration from a parent or guardian where requested.
  • Evidence of previous education funding or sponsorship, if applicable.
  • Other documents requested to verify financial need.

ALU's instructions specify that certain financial documents should be no older than three months. Follow the current portal instructions for the exact documents, formats and dates required for your application.

Applicants should not invent income figures or obtain false documents. If a document is unavailable because of displacement, poverty or other circumstances, explain the situation and ask ALU what alternative evidence it accepts.

Official financial-aid guidance: How to Apply for Financial Aid at ALU

10. Age Limit and Competition

ALU's published financial-aid page currently lists an age requirement of 26 or below for its scholarships. Applicants should check the current intake's conditions before submitting an application.

The programme is competitive, and only a limited number of scholarships are available for each intake. Meeting the age, academic and financial-need requirements makes an applicant eligible for consideration; it does not guarantee selection.

Applicants should submit complete and accurate applications and clearly demonstrate their academic preparation, leadership potential, financial circumstances and commitment to contributing to their communities.

11. Application Deadline

ALU's official admissions page lists 30 November 2026 as the closing date for the January 2027 intake.

This is the published university intake deadline. Applicants seeking Mastercard Foundation funding must also complete the required financial-aid process and meet any related instructions and deadlines.

Submit early rather than waiting until the final day. ALU states that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and that availability of places may affect consideration for a preferred intake.

Check the Current Deadline and Apply

12. Travel, Immigration and Other Costs

Selected scholars study at ALU in Rwanda. Applicants living in Kenya should plan for the possibility of needing travel documents and permission to enter Rwanda.

Before accepting an offer, read the scholarship agreement carefully to establish whether it covers travel, immigration costs and other expenses associated with moving to Rwanda. Do not assume that every expense is covered unless it is specified in writing.

Applicants should not pay an unofficial agent to submit an ALU application. ALU states that it does not authorize agents or individuals to charge applicants for application assistance.

13. What Happens After You Apply?

After submitting the application, applicants should monitor their email and admissions portal for updates. ALU may request additional documents or information during its review.

Admission and scholarship decisions are separate considerations. An offer of admission does not automatically mean that the applicant has received the Mastercard Foundation scholarship.

If a scholarship is offered, review the award letter for its coverage, conditions, duration and any responsibilities attached to the funding before accepting.

Applicants who do not receive a full scholarship should not assume that a partial tuition grant will cover accommodation, meals, travel or other costs. Any alternative funding offer should be assessed according to its actual terms.

14. Avoid Application Scams

  • Use ALU's official website and application portal.
  • Do not pay anyone who promises guaranteed admission or a scholarship.
  • Do not share passwords or application-account access with an agent.
  • Provide genuine academic, financial and refugee documents.
  • Rely on the written scholarship offer to understand funding coverage.

ALU explicitly warns applicants that it does not charge fees for application services or authorize agents to submit applications on applicants' behalf.

Official application page: ALU Admissions

15. Portico Kakuma: Important Information

The ALU Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a relevant opportunity for eligible refugees and displaced young Africans seeking undergraduate education. It is particularly worth exploring for students interested in Software Engineering and other programmes offered by ALU.

Applicants need to meet the university's academic requirements, demonstrate financial need, satisfy the scholarship conditions and complete both the admissions and financial-aid procedures.

The January 2027 intake deadline published by ALU is 30 November 2026. Scholarship places are limited, and an application does not guarantee funding.

Remember: Apply through official ALU channels, provide authentic documents and read the scholarship offer carefully before making travel or financial commitments.

Fully Funded Scholarship

University of Tomorrow Scholarship

Undergraduate

Scholarship Provider: International Christian University (ICU)

Country: Japan

Study Level: Undergraduate / Bachelor's Degree

Official Website: ICU Scholarships and Financial Aid

1. About the Scholarship

The University of Tomorrow Scholarship is a funding programme offered by International Christian University (ICU), a private university located in Tokyo, Japan.

It is intended for highly motivated students from countries classified by the United Nations as Least Developed Countries (LDCs). The programme supports students who want to use their education to make a positive difference in their communities and the wider world but face economic or social barriers to accessing higher education.

This is a university scholarship, not a separate university and not a refugee-specific scholarship. Applicants must satisfy the official nationality, educational background, admission and scholarship requirements.

2. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

ICU lists the following benefits for the University of Tomorrow Scholarship, normally for four years of undergraduate study, provided the recipient continues to meet the scholarship requirements.

  • Matriculation fee.
  • Annual tuition fees.
  • University facilities fees.
  • On-campus dormitory admission and accommodation fees, including July and August.
  • A monthly living allowance of ¥110,000.

The scholarship's tuition and dormitory fees are generally exempted rather than paid directly to the student. The living allowance is transferred to the recipient's Japanese bank account after the required arrangements have been completed.

Important: The published benefits do not automatically guarantee payment for every expense associated with studying abroad. Applicants should budget separately for any costs not explicitly covered by the award, including application-related expenses, travel to Japan, passport or visa-related expenses and other personal costs where applicable.

Scholarship continuation is conditional on meeting ICU's academic and other ongoing requirements.

3. Who Is Eligible?

The University of Tomorrow Scholarship has specific eligibility requirements. Meeting the nationality requirement alone is not sufficient.

  • Nationality: Applicants must be nationals of a country classified as a Least Developed Country by the United Nations.
  • Secondary education: The current published guidelines require applicants to have graduated, or expect to graduate by the time of enrolment, from a high school or secondary educational school in an eligible Least Developed Country. The guideline excludes international schools.
  • Admission route: For the LDC scholarship quota described in ICU's current guideline, applicants must use English Language Based Admissions (ELBA) for September entry, second application period.
  • Financial need: Applicants must need financial support to study at ICU and provide the required supporting documents.
  • Academic and personal qualities: ICU considers academic achievement, character, motivation and the overall strength of the admission and scholarship applications.
  • Student status: Recipients must enrol at ICU as regular undergraduate students and meet the applicable student-visa and enrolment requirements.

ICU's current guidelines should be read in full before applying. Eligibility requirements may differ for other admissions routes and future scholarship cycles.

4. Important Information for Refugees in Kenya

This scholarship is not specifically designed for refugees. Refugees may only be able to benefit if they meet all the programme's standard eligibility requirements.

For example, a South Sudanese applicant who completed secondary school in Kenya may meet the nationality condition because South Sudan is classified as a Least Developed Country, but may not meet the published secondary-school-location condition.

Refugee status or a refugee identification document does not, by itself, waive the scholarship's academic-background requirements. Applicants educated outside an eligible LDC should obtain a clear answer from ICU before spending money on application documents or courier services.

Official admissions contact: ICU English-Language Undergraduate Admissions

5. When Can You Apply?

ICU's current published guidelines specify the following application period for the University of Tomorrow Scholarship LDC quota associated with September 2027 entry:

  • Opens: February 15, 2027, at 10:00 Japan Standard Time.
  • Deadline: February 25, 2027, at 23:59 Japan Standard Time.

The scholarship application deadline follows the applicable university admissions schedule. Applicants must complete both the admissions application and the separate scholarship application process.

The University of Tomorrow Scholarship LDC quota is not available through every ICU admissions route. Applicants must use the correct route specified in the current guidelines.

Always read the latest official guideline before submitting an application, as future dates and requirements may change.

View ICU's official application schedule

6. How to Apply

Eligible applicants should follow ICU's official instructions. The general process for the relevant English-language admission route includes the following steps:

  1. Read the current undergraduate admissions guide and confirm that your nationality, secondary education and academic background meet the requirements.
  2. Prepare the required school certificates, official transcripts, English-language test results and other admissions documents.
  3. Apply to ICU through its Online Application System during the correct application period.
  4. Complete the separate scholarship application through the system specified in ICU's current scholarship guidelines.
  5. Submit the required scholarship essay, recommendation letter and financial documents in the prescribed format.
  6. Submit all documents by their respective deadlines and monitor your application for any further instructions.

The scholarship application is separate from the university admissions application. Applying for admission alone does not automatically complete the scholarship application.

Start with ICU's official admissions information

7. Documents You May Need

The exact document list is set out in the current scholarship guideline. It includes documents such as:

  • Official high-school certificates and academic transcripts.
  • Required university admissions documents.
  • The prescribed scholarship application essay.
  • A recommendation letter using ICU's designated form.
  • Original documents or certificates relating to parental income or earnings, as required by the guideline.
  • Other supporting documents requested by ICU.

Follow the official instructions on document format, translation, certification, submission method and deadlines. Incomplete scholarship applications may be disqualified.

Applicants who live outside Japan should plan ahead if any original documents must be sent by post or courier.

8. How Competitive Is It?

The University of Tomorrow Scholarship is highly competitive. ICU's published guideline lists an expected award of only one scholarship recipient under the LDC quota.

Selection considers the overall application, including the quality of the application materials, admission results and relevant financial circumstances.

Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission or a scholarship. Students should keep exploring other suitable funding opportunities while preparing their applications.

9. Relationship With the ICU Peace Bell Scholarship

The University of Tomorrow Scholarship and the ICU Peace Bell Scholarship are two distinct scholarships offered by the same institution: International Christian University (ICU) in Japan. They are not two different universities.

Eligible applicants may apply for both scholarships when ICU's current rules permit it. However, applicants selected under the combined scholarship process receive only one of the applicable awards. The two scholarships cannot be combined to receive both sets of benefits.

You may choose to apply for one scholarship or seek consideration for both if you satisfy the eligibility requirements. Applying for both does not guarantee selection or automatically increase your chances of receiving an award.

The University of Tomorrow Scholarship has a specific LDC nationality and secondary-education requirement, while the Peace Bell Scholarship has its own eligibility criteria. Therefore, eligibility for one does not automatically mean eligibility for the other.
