Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları)

Associate Degree, Bachelor's, Master's and PhD

Programme Provider: Government of Türkiye

Administered by: Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB)

Study Destination: Türkiye (Turkey)

Funding Type: Government-funded, competitive scholarship

Application Method: Online application through the official Türkiye Scholarships application system

2026 Application Status: Closed

Expected Next Cycle: January–February 2027, subject to official confirmation

About Türkiye Scholarships

Türkiye Scholarships, also known as Türkiye Bursları, is a competitive scholarship programme funded by the Government of Türkiye. It supports eligible international students who want to pursue higher education at participating universities in Türkiye.

The programme combines financial assistance with university placement. It is intended to help academically qualified students access higher education while building international academic, cultural and professional connections.

Scholarships are offered at different study levels, including undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. The courses, universities and scholarship options available to an applicant depend on the official programme catalogue and the applicant's educational background.

Important: This is a competitive scholarship, not an automatic grant. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee selection.

Scholarship Benefits and Financial Coverage

The full-time Türkiye Scholarships programme lists the following benefits for successful scholars, subject to the applicable award terms:

  • University and programme placement: Support with placement at an eligible Turkish university and department through the scholarship system.
  • Tuition fees: Coverage of the university tuition fees included in the scholarship terms.
  • Monthly stipend: A regular allowance to help meet living expenses. The amount depends on the study level and the applicable official award terms.
  • Accommodation: Accommodation support as specified by the programme.
  • Health insurance: Health insurance support under the scholarship terms.
  • Turkish-language course: A one-year Turkish-language course is included in the full-time scholarship programme.
  • Flight tickets: The official programme lists a one-time flight ticket at the beginning of education and another at graduation, according to its applicable terms.

Read carefully: Do not assume that every additional personal expense will be paid. Before accepting an award, read the official scholarship agreement to understand the accommodation arrangements, stipend conditions, travel rules and any expenses that remain your responsibility.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

Türkiye Scholarships is generally open to eligible international applicants from countries around the world. Applicants must meet the requirements for the particular study level and programme they select.

Eligible applicants can include:

  • Students who have already graduated from the previous education level required for their intended programme.
  • Students who are expected to graduate before the official graduation cut-off stated for the application cycle.
  • Applicants who satisfy the relevant academic, age, nationality and documentation requirements.

The programme's general eligibility information identifies Turkish citizens and people who have lost Turkish citizenship as ineligible. Applicants already enrolled at a Turkish university at the same level for which they are applying are also generally ineligible under the published criteria.

Always check the latest official call because individual scholarship programmes can have additional conditions.

Academic Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet the minimum academic achievement requirement for their intended level of study. The official general criteria currently list the following minimum percentages:

  • Associate degree and Bachelor's degree: At least 70% academic achievement.
  • Master's degree and PhD: At least 75% academic achievement.
  • Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy: At least 90% academic achievement.

These are minimum thresholds, not guaranteed winning scores. Competitive applicants may need stronger academic records depending on the programme, university and applicant pool.

How should applicants understand the percentage? The scholarship provider must determine how a particular country's grades, examination results or cumulative average correspond to its eligibility requirements. Do not assume that a letter grade automatically equals a particular percentage.

Applicants should provide accurate certificates and transcripts so that their academic background can be assessed. If their school uses a grading scale other than percentages, they should follow the application system's instructions and provide the official results requested.

Age Eligibility Requirements

Age is one of the most important eligibility conditions. The official general criteria currently state that applicants must be below the relevant age limit for their intended programme.

  • Associate degree and Bachelor's degree: Must be under 21 years old.
  • Master's degree: Must be under 30 years old.
  • PhD: Must be under 35 years old.

These are strict screening criteria in the published general eligibility rules. An applicant should not assume that strong grades, refugee status, financial hardship or a long period without schooling automatically creates an age-limit exemption.

Which date determines the applicant's age? The exact age-calculation date must be confirmed in the instructions for the relevant application cycle. Check the current official call rather than calculating eligibility using the date you submit the application alone.

If an applicant is at or above the published age limit, they should carefully verify their eligibility before investing time in an undergraduate application.

Can Refugees and Displaced Students Apply?

The general Türkiye Scholarships eligibility information states that applicants from all countries may apply, subject to the programme's rules. The general criteria do not list refugee status itself as a universal disqualification.

This means a refugee or displaced student living outside their country of origin may explore the opportunity if they satisfy the scholarship's nationality, academic, age and documentation requirements.

However, this is not a guarantee of special consideration, selection or an exception to the standard eligibility rules. The general programme should not be described as a refugee-only scholarship.

For refugees living in Kenya: Check which identity and travel documents the application system accepts, and whether the successful applicant must provide a valid passport or other specific documents for university registration and travel. A refugee ID should not automatically be assumed to replace a passport or every document required by Turkish authorities.

Applicants should provide truthful information about their nationality, residence and legal status. If a document is unavailable because of displacement, contact the official scholarship administrator for clarification before submitting substitute documents.

Previous Education Requirements

Applicants must have the educational qualifications required for the programme they select. Undergraduate applicants generally need to have completed secondary education or be on track to graduate within the official deadline stated for that application cycle.

Applicants who are still completing secondary school should check the exact graduation cut-off and submit the provisional or current school documents permitted by the official application instructions.

Applicants who have already graduated should prepare their final school-leaving certificate and academic transcript. If certificates or transcripts are unavailable, incomplete, damaged or contain spelling differences, they should seek guidance from the scholarship administrator about acceptable supporting documentation.

Important: Meeting the graduation requirement does not remove the age or minimum academic achievement requirements.

Available Courses and University Choices

Türkiye Scholarships supports several study fields, including engineering, basic sciences, social sciences and other disciplines offered through its participating institutions. The exact list varies by programme and application cycle.

Applicants interested in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology or related fields should search the official programme catalogue before applying. They should check the language of instruction and the entry requirements of each available course.

Candidates can choose only from the universities and departments made available to them in the official application system. The choices shown may depend on the applicant's education history and other programme conditions.

Some programmes are taught in Turkish, while others may be taught in English or another language. The one-year Turkish language course does not mean that every degree is taught in English.

Before selecting a course, verify that the degree's language, entry requirements and qualification recognition are suitable for your future plans.

Language Requirements

Language requirements depend on the university and degree programme selected. Some programmes may require proof of proficiency in English or another language of instruction. Turkish-taught programmes may have additional language requirements.

Applicants should not assume that an English-language test result automatically satisfies every university's requirements. Check the accepted tests, minimum scores and any exemptions stated for the chosen programme.

The full-time scholarship programme lists a one-year Turkish-language course. Applicants should nevertheless confirm the language conditions attached to their specific award and university placement.

Who May Be Ineligible?

Under the published general criteria, the following circumstances can make an applicant ineligible:

  • Being a Turkish citizen or having lost Turkish citizenship.
  • Already studying at a Turkish university at the same education level for which the applicant is applying.
  • Falling outside the applicable age limit.
  • Failing to meet the minimum academic achievement requirement.
  • Not having the educational qualification required for the chosen programme by the stated deadline.
  • Failing to provide the required documents or providing false, misleading or inconsistent information.

These are general screening points. Individual programmes may have further restrictions, so the current official application guide remains the final reference.

Documents Applicants Should Prepare

The exact document checklist can vary by education level and programme. Applicants should use the current official application system to confirm what must be uploaded.

Documents commonly requested for an application may include:

  • A valid identity document or passport, as required by the application instructions.
  • A recent photograph that meets the system's requirements.
  • Academic certificates or graduation documents.
  • Academic transcripts showing subjects and grades.
  • Any permitted provisional school results for applicants who have not yet graduated.
  • Examination results or language certificates, where required by the selected programme.
  • A statement of purpose or motivation statement, where requested.
  • Recommendation letters or other supporting documents, if required by the relevant application.

Applicants should upload clear, readable copies and ensure that names and dates are consistent across their documents. If names appear in different orders or spellings, they should follow the official instructions for explaining the discrepancy.

Do not pay someone to create false documents or alter academic results. Inaccurate information can jeopardise an application.

How Are Applicants Selected?

Türkiye Scholarships is competitive. Applicants who meet the basic eligibility criteria may proceed to further evaluation, but not everyone who qualifies will receive an award.

The official selection process considers factors that include:

  • Academic performance and previous qualifications.
  • Consistency between the applicant's background and chosen study preferences.
  • Academic interests and future career goals.
  • The content and quality of the motivation statement.
  • Participation in social, cultural or other activities.

Undergraduate applicants may also be required to take a quantitative test covering areas such as mathematics, geometry and logic before the interview stage, according to the official selection process.

Applicants should prepare to explain why they chose their field, what they hope to achieve through the degree and how their previous experiences connect to their plans.

Application Dates and Current Status

The official 2026 general application period ran from 10 January to 20 February 2026. That application period has closed.

The official application calendar lists 10 January to 20 February as the general application period. The exact dates for the 2027 cycle have not yet been officially confirmed as of this page's last review.

Students interested in the next cycle should prepare their documents in advance and check the official website for the announcement of the next application period.

Do not treat January–February 2027 as a confirmed deadline. It is an expected period based on the usual calendar. The official announcement takes precedence.

How to Apply

  1. Read the current eligibility rules on the official Türkiye Scholarships website.
  2. Confirm that you meet the age, academic, nationality and graduation requirements for your intended level.
  3. Search for available universities and programmes, including the language of instruction.
  4. Prepare the required identity, academic and supporting documents.
  5. Create an account in the official Türkiye Scholarships application system when the application period opens.
  6. Complete the application carefully and select only eligible programmes available in the system.
  7. Review the entire application and submit it before the official deadline.
  8. Monitor the official system and your contact details for selection updates or requests for further steps.

Apply through the official portal only. Be cautious of individuals or agencies claiming they can guarantee a scholarship in exchange for payment.

Advice for Refugees and Students Facing Financial Hardship

Applicants who have experienced displacement or financial hardship should focus first on meeting the formal eligibility conditions. Refugee status and financial need do not, by themselves, waive the programme's minimum age or academic requirements.

If you are eligible, prepare a clear record of your education and achievements. Explain any genuine interruption in your education if the application provides an appropriate place to do so.

If you have a refugee identity document but do not have a passport, do not assume either that you are automatically excluded or that your refugee document will be accepted for every stage. Ask the official administrator which documents are accepted at application, award and travel stages.

Use the official guidance for your particular circumstances before spending money on document processing, translations or other services.

Important Things to Remember

  • The 2026 general application period is closed.
  • The next general application period is expected around January–February 2027, but the official dates are not yet confirmed.
  • Undergraduate applicants generally must be under 21 and meet the 70% minimum academic requirement.
  • Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy applicants generally need at least 90% academic achievement.
  • Meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee selection.
  • Available courses and language requirements differ by university and programme.
  • Refugee status does not automatically provide an exception to the published eligibility criteria.
  • Always confirm the latest rules using official sources before applying.

Official Websites and Further Information

Use these official sources to confirm eligibility, application dates, benefits and available programmes.

  • Official Türkiye Scholarships Website
  • Official Eligibility Criteria and Scholarship Programmes
  • Full-Time Scholarship Benefits and Study Levels
  • Official Application Calendar
  • Official 2026 Application Announcement
  • Evaluation and Selection Process

Before You Apply

Türkiye Scholarships can provide extensive financial support for eligible international students, but its age and academic requirements are important screening conditions. Check these first, then verify the available courses and documents using the official website.

About the Chinese Government Scholarship

The Chinese Government Scholarship, commonly called the CSC Scholarship, supports eligible international students who want to study at participating universities in China. It is administered by the China Scholarship Council on behalf of the Chinese government.

Scholarships may be available for undergraduate degrees, master's degrees, doctoral degrees, Chinese-language study and certain visiting or non-degree programmes.

The programme is not one single application with identical rules for everyone. Applications may be handled through Chinese diplomatic missions, designated government authorities or participating universities, depending on the scholarship category.

As a result, applicants must confirm the eligibility conditions, agency details, funding package and deadline for the particular route they intend to use.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

A full Chinese Government Scholarship commonly includes several of the following benefits, subject to the applicable scholarship category and award terms:

  • Tuition fees: A tuition waiver for the approved study programme.
  • Accommodation: University accommodation or an accommodation subsidy, depending on the applicable scholarship arrangements.
  • Monthly stipend: A living allowance according to the study level and official scholarship terms.
  • Medical insurance: Medical insurance or comprehensive medical coverage specified by the scholarship.
  • Preparatory language study: Some students may receive Chinese-language preparation before beginning their academic programme, if required and included in their award.

Important about travel: Do not assume that international flights are covered. Some official CSC calls explicitly require students to pay their own international airfare. Check the specific award terms before accepting an offer.

The exact stipend, accommodation arrangement and other benefits must be confirmed in the current official scholarship announcement. Not every programme administered by CSC has the same funding package.

Application Routes: Which One Should You Use?

Before preparing an application, identify the correct application route. This is particularly important for international applicants and refugees living outside their country of origin.

Route A: Embassy or Government-Nominated Scholarship

Some CSC scholarships are administered through a Chinese embassy or a designated government authority in a country. The authority may set its own eligibility conditions, documents, agency number, nomination process and deadline.

An embassy-nominated opportunity may be restricted to citizens of the country concerned. If an announcement says it is for Kenyan citizens or Kenyan students applying through Kenya's Ministry of Education, a Somali refugee living in Kenya must not assume that they qualify.

Route B: University-Based Application

Some participating universities accept applications for CSC scholarships through their own designated processes. Applicants must identify universities that offer their intended course and confirm whether international applicants of their nationality and residence status can use that route.

A university-based route may still require a CSC online application, a pre-admission document, academic documents and separate university admission steps.

Route C: Special Government Scholarship Programmes

China also offers specialised scholarship schemes for particular groups, professional fields or postgraduate applicants. Some are intended for public servants, experienced professionals or candidates with specific qualifications.

These special programmes are not interchangeable with the general undergraduate scholarship. Check the exact eligibility requirements before choosing one.

General Eligibility Requirements

General CSC calls commonly require applicants to:

  • Be a citizen of a country other than the People's Republic of China.
  • Meet the academic qualifications required for the intended study level.
  • Meet the applicable age limit.
  • Be in good physical and mental health as required by the relevant call.
  • Meet the chosen university's academic and language requirements.
  • Submit the required documents in the requested format.
  • Follow the rules of the particular application authority or university.

These are general requirements, not a guarantee that every applicant qualifies for every CSC category. Individual calls can add further conditions.

Eligibility for Undergraduate Applicants

Applicants seeking a bachelor's degree generally need to have completed high school or an equivalent secondary qualification and meet the age and academic conditions specified by the application route and university.

Age Requirement

General CSC scholarship calls commonly set an undergraduate age limit of under 25 years at the time specified in the relevant announcement. The exact wording and age-calculation date must be checked in the current call.

Academic Qualification

Applicants generally need a recognised high-school qualification and sufficiently strong academic results. The CSC's general eligibility rules do not establish one universal secondary-school percentage that applies to every university and every country.

Universities may set their own minimum grades, required subjects or additional admission tests. Applicants must check the requirements for their intended degree.

China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA)

Beginning with the 2026/2027 academic year, the published CSC application guidance requires applicants for bachelor's programmes to take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) and provide a valid score report.

Applicants should confirm the required CSCA subjects with their target university and major, and check the official CSCA website for current test dates and registration details. Do not rely on test dates from a previous admission cycle.

Language Requirements

Language requirements depend on the programme's teaching language. Chinese-taught courses may require Chinese proficiency, while English-taught courses may require accepted English-language evidence according to the university's rules.

Other Undergraduate Requirements

  • Completion of secondary education or an accepted equivalent qualification.
  • Academic transcripts and certificates.
  • A valid CSCA score report where required.
  • A study plan or personal statement if requested.
  • Any pre-admission document required by the chosen university or scholarship authority.

Note: A university may impose additional requirements for engineering, medicine, science or other specialised degrees.

Eligibility for Master's Applicants

Applicants for master's programmes generally need to hold a recognised bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification. General CSC calls commonly specify that master's applicants should be under 35 years old, although the precise wording in the applicable call must be followed.

Applicants should also:

  • Meet the university's academic entry requirements.
  • Provide bachelor's degree certificates and transcripts.
  • Meet the language requirements of the selected programme.
  • Submit a study plan or research proposal where required.
  • Provide recommendation letters where required by the university or scholarship category.

Some specialised scholarships may require professional experience, employment in a particular sector or nomination by a government authority. These requirements do not automatically apply to every general CSC master's route.

Eligibility for PhD Applicants

Doctoral applicants generally need a recognised master's degree or an equivalent qualification in a relevant field. General CSC calls commonly set a doctoral age limit of under 40 years, subject to the applicable call.

PhD applicants may need to provide:

  • Master's degree certificate and academic transcripts.
  • A detailed research proposal.
  • Recommendation letters from academic referees.
  • Evidence of language proficiency.
  • A pre-admission document or acceptance from a suitable academic department or supervisor, where required.

Research areas, supervisor availability and additional admission conditions vary between universities. Applicants should verify that their proposed research can be supported by the institution they select.

Language Requirements

Applicants must meet the language requirements of their chosen course. These requirements are not identical across all universities or scholarship categories.

Published general CSC calls commonly specify the following minimum Chinese-language levels for certain Chinese-taught programmes:

  • Chinese-taught undergraduate programmes: HSK Level 3 is commonly specified in general guidance, subject to the applicable programme rules.
  • Chinese-taught master's and doctoral programmes: HSK Level 4 is commonly specified in general guidance.

Some programmes may require a higher level. Applicants should not assume that these general levels are sufficient for every course.

For programmes taught in English, the university may request IELTS, TOEFL or another accepted proof of English proficiency, or may specify its own exemption rules.

A language test is not necessarily required in the same form by every university. Check the current admission instructions for the course and language of instruction you choose.

Can refugees Living in Kenya Apply?

Refugees living in Kenya should distinguish between scholarship eligibility and the rules of the authority that receives applications.

Kenya's embassy-nominated route: The published 2026/2027 call distributed through Kenya's Ministry of Education specified Kenyan KCSE requirements for undergraduate applicants and described the places as scholarships for Kenyan students. It also required a preliminary selection process through the Ministry.

A refugee living in Kenya should therefore not assume that this particular nomination route is open to them. Contact the Ministry or the relevant scholarship authority to confirm whether non-Kenyan citizens are permitted to apply before investing time in that route.

University-based route: A refugee may investigate participating universities that accept applications from international students of their nationality. However, the applicant must confirm that the university offers a CSC-funded place and that the particular route accepts their citizenship and circumstances.

Identity and travel documents: Applicants may need a valid ordinary passport, academic certificates, transcripts and other documents. Do not assume that a refugee ID automatically replaces a passport for every stage of the process. Ask the relevant authority which documents it accepts if a passport is unavailable.

Refugee status does not automatically waive age limits, academic requirements, CSCA requirements or university admission conditions.

Documents Applicants May Need

The final checklist depends on the scholarship route, university and intended study level. Commonly requested documents include:

  • Passport: A clear copy of the passport information page, with the validity required by the current call.
  • Academic certificates: The highest completed qualification required for the intended study level.
  • Academic transcripts: Official records showing subjects and grades.
  • Language evidence: HSK results or accepted English-language evidence where required.
  • CSCA score report: Required for undergraduate applications under the published 2026/2027 guidance.
  • Study plan or research proposal: Prepared according to the required length and format.
  • Recommendation letters: Often requested for graduate programmes.
  • Pre-admission document: Required by many calls and application routes.
  • Physical examination form: May be required for applicants planning to stay in China for an extended period.
  • Police clearance or non-criminal record: Required where specified by the current call.
  • Additional supporting documents: Any documents requested by the university, embassy or designated government authority.

Documents that are not in Chinese or English may require certified or notarised translations, depending on the application instructions.

Upload clear, authentic and readable documents. Follow the exact instructions for file format, translation, certification and document validity.

How to Apply

  1. Choose the correct route. Determine whether the application is through an embassy, a government authority or a participating university.
  2. Check eligibility. Confirm nationality, age, academic qualifications, language requirements and any additional restrictions.
  3. Find suitable universities. Use the official Study in China website to identify universities and programmes relevant to your goals.
  4. Check the university's requirements. Confirm course availability, teaching language, admission documents and whether the university offers CSC funding for that programme.
  5. Prepare the required documents. Arrange academic records, identity documents, language evidence, study plans and any required CSCA results.
  6. Obtain pre-admission documents if required. Follow the target university's process for obtaining a pre-admission notice or other accepted document.
  7. Complete the official online application. Use the application portal and agency details stated in the current announcement.
  8. Complete any additional steps. This may include a university application, nomination, interview or submission of documents to the responsible authority.
  9. Submit before the deadline. Each route may have a different deadline. Submitting to a university does not necessarily complete every CSC application step.

Application Dates and Current Status

The 2026/2027 application period for the published Kenya-nominated CSC call closed in November 2025. Other CSC routes had different deadlines.

The Kenya Ministry of Education also published a separate CSC-administered MOFCOM programme in 2026 for eligible public servants applying for postgraduate study. That programme had a 25 May 2026 submission deadline and was not a general undergraduate scholarship.

As of October 2026, applicants should not assume that the next general CSC deadline or Kenya nomination requirements have been announced.

Check the official portal and the relevant embassy, ministry or university for the next call. Dates and agency numbers from previous years must not be reused without confirmation.

Important Things to Remember

  • The CSC Scholarship is a group of scholarship routes, not a single award with identical rules everywhere.
  • Undergraduate applicants generally need to be under 25 and hold a suitable high-school qualification, subject to the current call.
  • Undergraduate applicants must check the CSCA requirement for the relevant admission year.
  • Language requirements depend on the chosen course and university.
  • Some country-specific nomination routes may be restricted to citizens of that country.
  • Full scholarship benefits do not necessarily include international airfare.
  • A pre-admission document or university admission process may be required in addition to the CSC form.
  • Never assume that meeting the minimum requirements guarantees a scholarship.

Beware of Scholarship Scams

The China Scholarship Council warns applicants against using unauthorised intermediaries to process Chinese Government Scholarship applications.

Use the official scholarship portal and the application authority named in the relevant call. Do not pay an individual who promises guaranteed admission or a guaranteed scholarship.

Be especially cautious of requests for money sent to personal mobile-money accounts or private bank accounts. Verify any application fee or payment request directly with the official university or authority.

Official Websites and Resources

  • Study in China — Official CSC Scholarship Information
  • Search Participating Chinese Universities
  • China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA)
  • Kenya Ministry of Education — Scholarship Announcements
  • Embassy of China in Kenya — Official Website

Before You Apply

First confirm that the scholarship route accepts your nationality and circumstances. Then check the age, academic, language and document requirements before preparing the application.

Portico Kakuma provides this information for guidance. Final eligibility, admission, nomination and funding decisions belong to the official scholarship authorities and participating universities.

Macalester College International Student Financial Aid

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | Fall 2027 Entry

What this opportunity is: Institutional need-based financial aid and automatic merit scholarships offered by Macalester College to admitted international first-year undergraduate applicants who demonstrate financial need.

Host institution: Macalester College

Destination: Saint Paul, Minnesota, United States of America

Application platform: Common Application (no application fee)

Study level: First-year undergraduate / Bachelor's degree (4-year programme)

Target applicants: International applicants (non-US citizens and non-permanent residents), including refugee and displaced students who demonstrate strong academic readiness and financial need.

Funding policy: Need-aware admission; meets 100% of institutionally calculated demonstrated financial need for admitted students through a combination of grants, merit awards, campus employment, and institutional loans.

Application rounds & deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry): Early Decision II: 1 January 2027 (Aid forms due 8 January 2027) | Regular Decision: 15 January 2027 (Aid forms due 22 January 2027).

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

Before You Apply: Understanding Macalester's Need-Aware Aid Reality

Macalester College is a private liberal arts and sciences college in Saint Paul, Minnesota, known for its strong commitment to internationalism and substantial financial aid funding for international students.

However, applicants must understand two critical facts before adding Macalester to their Common App list:

1. Macalester is need-aware for international admissions: Unlike need-blind institutions, Macalester evaluates your family's ability to pay as part of the admissions decision. Because the international financial aid budget is finite, applicants who require almost full funding face significantly higher competition for admission. Macalester has noted that international applicants whose families can contribute less than $40,000 per year compete within the most selective tier of its international applicant pool.

2. Macalester meets 100% of demonstrated need if admitted: Once Macalester decides to admit an international student who applied for aid on time, the college commits to meeting 100% of that student's calculated financial need across all four years of study.

Cost of Attendance and How Financial Aid Packages Work

To evaluate whether Macalester is financially realistic for your situation, look at the official comprehensive charges (2026–2027 baseline, which adjust slightly each year for 2027–2028):

  • Tuition: $74,394 per year
  • Residence Hall (On-campus housing): $9,268 per year
  • Meal Plan: $8,162 per year
  • Student Activity Fee: $230 per year
  • Total Direct Billed Comprehensive Fee: $92,154 per year

In addition to billed charges, Macalester estimates indirect expenses (such as books, personal supplies, health insurance, and travel), bringing the total estimated I-20 Cost of Attendance to approximately $97,883 per year.

Components of a Macalester International Financial Aid Package

Macalester does not meet need solely through free grants. Instead, an international aid offer combines up to four components:

  • Need-Based Institutional Grants: Gift aid awarded by Macalester that does not need to be repaid.
  • Automatic Merit Scholarships (DeWitt Wallace & Turck Scholarships): Every international applicant is automatically considered for merit awards (such as the Charles J. Turck Presidential Honor Scholarship and the DeWitt Wallace Distinguished Scholarship, which can range up to $40,000 per year). No separate merit application is required. Note: If you qualify for need-based aid, merit awards are integrated into your overall need-based package rather than stacked on top to reduce your expected family contribution.
  • On-Campus Student Employment: International aid recipients are offered part-time on-campus jobs (typically 10 to 12 hours per week during the academic year) to earn funds for personal and incidental expenses. Important: You must work to earn this allotment; if you choose not to work, Macalester will not replace the work allotment with extra grant money.
  • Macalester College International Student Loan (MCISL): Some packages include a modest institutional loan component to help finance a portion of educational expenses.

Critical Visa & I-20 Certification of Finances Rule

After admission, to receive your Form I-20 (required to apply for a US F-1 Student Visa), you must submit Macalester's Certification of Finances (COF) and official bank statements proving that your family or external sponsors can pay the remaining gap between the total Cost of Attendance (~$97,883) and your total Macalester Financial Aid Award.

Costs you must still plan for independently: Even with a high aid package, students must carefully verify coverage for passport processing, US visa application fees, SEVIS I-901 fees, travel to the US Embassy, initial flight tickets, and mandatory health insurance charges.

Strict Financial Aid Rules You Cannot Afford to Miss

1. You CANNOT apply for financial aid after enrolling

Macalester strictly prohibits international students who enrol without financial aid from applying for institutional need-based aid in later years. Do not claim you can pay full fees just to improve your chances of admission—if admitted without aid, you will receive zero institutional financial assistance for all four years.

2. Mandatory Macalester Financial Declaration Form

Every international applicant—whether requesting financial aid or not—must complete the Macalester Financial Declaration Form inside the Macalester Applicant Portal after submitting their Common App. Your admissions application will not be reviewed until this form and your financial aid documents are received.

3. Free Alternative to the CSS Profile (ISAFA)

Macalester does not distribute CSS Profile fee waiver codes to international applicants. However, if paying the College Board's CSS Profile fee is a financial burden, Macalester officially allows you to submit the free 2027–2028 International Student Application for Financial Assistance (ISAFA) instead.

4. Four-Year Package Guarantee & Outside Scholarships

International students who qualify for need-based aid are provided a four-year financial aid commitment at the time of admission, though you must submit updated financial verification forms each year. If you win external scholarships from foundations or NGOs, you are legally required to report them to Macalester's Financial Aid Office.

Eligibility Criteria

  • First-Year Undergraduate Entry: Must be completing or have completed secondary school and applying as a first-time degree-seeking undergraduate student (fall entry only; Macalester does not offer spring intake for first-year students).
  • Citizenship Classification: Open to all non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents (dual US citizens must apply through the domestic financial aid process using FAFSA and CSS Profile).
  • Academic Preparation: Strong secondary school academic record across core subjects (Mathematics, Sciences, English, Humanities/Social Sciences).
  • Timely Aid Request: Must indicate intent to apply for financial aid on the Common App and submit all required financial forms by the stated round deadline.

Guidance for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Macalester welcomes applications from refugee and displaced students worldwide. If you live in a refugee camp or host country (such as Kenya) and hold citizenship from another country (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia):

  • Citizenship entry on Common App: Select your country of legal citizenship under the non-US citizen section. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," as that category applies only to individuals holding US domestic immigration status.
  • Documenting informal or zero family income: If your parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal income without tax returns, do not fabricate income numbers. Use the special circumstances section of the ISAFA or CSS Profile—and attach an official UNHCR/government refugee attestation letter or signed family financial statement—to explain your household's exact living situation.
  • Testing & interview costs: Because Macalester is test-optional for SAT/ACT and does not require paid third-party interviews (such as InitialView or Vericant), applicants from low-resource settings are not penalized for skipping optional paid services.

Academic Programmes and STEM Opportunities

Macalester offers over 60 areas of study within a flexible liberal arts and sciences curriculum. Popular programmes for quantitative and technology-focused students include:

  • Computer Science
  • Applied Mathematics and Statistics
  • Data Science (interdisciplinary concentration)
  • Economics and Quantitative Economics
  • Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Environmental Studies
  • Pre-Engineering Dual-Degree Pathways (3-2 or 4-2 combined engineering programmes with partner universities)

Note on Engineering: Like most US liberal arts colleges, Macalester does not award a standalone Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) degree directly; students interested in engineering pursue Computer Science, Physics, or Applied Mathematics at Macalester or apply for a cooperative dual-degree engineering transfer pathway.

Application Rounds and Deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry)

Note that Early Decision I and Early Action deadlines (1 November 2026) have already passed. Two admission rounds remain open for Fall 2027 entry:

  • Early Decision II (Binding):
    Common App Admission Deadline: 1 January 2027
    Financial Aid Documents Deadline (CSS Profile/ISAFA & Declaration Form): 8 January 2027
  • Regular Decision (Non-Binding):
    Common App Admission Deadline: 15 January 2027
    Financial Aid Documents Deadline (CSS Profile/ISAFA & Declaration Form): 22 January 2027
    Mid-Year / Updated Senior Grades Deadline: 15 February 2027
Portico Recommendation on Admission Round:

Unless you have confirmed directly with Macalester's financial aid office that your family's expected contribution is affordable, Regular Decision (15 January 2027) is safer than binding Early Decision II because Regular Decision allows you to compare financial aid offers across multiple universities before committing.

Complete Checklist of Required Documents

1. Academic & Admissions Documents

  • Common Application & Personal Essay: Submitted online (Macalester charges $0 application fee for all first-year applicants).
  • Official Secondary School Transcripts & National Exam Results: Certified copies of all high school academic records (e.g., KCSE certificate/result slip and Form 1–4 transcripts) submitted by your school counsellor or official.
  • Two Recommendation Letters: One recommendation from your school counsellor/principal and one recommendation from a teacher in a core academic subject.
  • English Proficiency Proof (Recommended if applicable): Optional if your secondary school curriculum was taught primarily in English for at least two years (such as Kenyan secondary schools). If your schooling was not in English, submit TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores (self-reporting is accepted during initial review).
  • SAT or ACT Scores (Optional): Macalester is strictly test-optional; submitting scores is not required and will not disadvantage your admission or scholarship review.

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Documents

  • CSS Profile (School Code: 6390) OR Free 2027–2028 ISAFA: Submit one of these forms detailing your household income, assets, family size, and dependants.
  • Macalester Financial Declaration Form: Completed directly inside your Macalester Applicant Portal checklist once your Common App is processed.
  • Supporting Income / Refugee Documentation: Parent wage statements, tax documents (if applicable), employer letters, or official statements explaining unemployment, informal livelihoods, or refugee status.

Step-by-Step Application Process

  1. Add Macalester College to your Common App list. Verify it fits within your 20-college Common App limit and note that Macalester requires no application fee.
  2. Indicate your intent to apply for financial aid. In the Macalester-specific questions on Common App, select "Yes" for need-based financial aid.
  3. Invite your school counsellor and academic teacher. Assign your recommender roles early in Common App so they can upload your transcripts, school report, and recommendation letters before January 2027.
  4. Submit your Common App by 15 January 2027 (Regular Decision). Complete your personal essay and Macalester's supplemental questions carefully.
  5. Activate your Macalester Applicant Portal immediately. Within a few days of submitting Common App, you will receive login credentials for your portal. Log in and complete the mandatory Macalester Financial Declaration Form.
  6. Submit either the CSS Profile or the free 2027–2028 ISAFA by 22 January 2027. If paying for the CSS Profile ($25+) is a hardship, download and upload the free ISAFA through your portal along with supporting financial statements.
  7. Monitor your portal checklist for missing items. Check regularly until every admissions and financial aid requirement shows as received, and submit updated senior/national exam results by 15 February 2027 if applicable.

Wesleyan University International Student Financial Aid

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | Fall 2027 Entry

What this opportunity is: Institutional need-based financial aid offered by Wesleyan University to admitted international first-year undergraduate applicants who demonstrate financial need, including automatic consideration for the Wesleyan African Scholars Program for eligible African citizens and permanent residents.

Host institution: Wesleyan University

Destination: Middletown, Connecticut, United States of America

Application platforms: Common Application or Coalition Application via Scoir

Study level: First-year undergraduate / Bachelor's degree (4-year programme)

Target applicants: International first-year applicants (non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents) from any country, including refugee and displaced students who demonstrate strong academic ability and financial need.

Funding policy: Need-aware admission for international students; meets 100% of Wesleyan-calculated demonstrated financial need for admitted students without student loans (grant aid + work-study).

Regular Decision deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry): Admission Application: 1 January 2027 | Financial Aid Application (CSS Profile or ISFAA): 15 January 2027 | Certification of Finances: 15 February 2027.

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

Before You Apply: Understand How Wesleyan Financial Aid Works

Wesleyan University is a selective private liberal arts university in Middletown, Connecticut, offering full need-based financial assistance to a limited cohort of admitted international students each year.

Before adding Wesleyan to your college list, make sure you understand four defining features of its financial aid system:

1. Need-aware admission with extreme selectivity: Wesleyan is need-aware for international applicants. Your family's financial need is factored into the admissions decision, and competition for international financial aid is intense across all countries.

2. 100% of demonstrated need met — with ZERO student loans: If you are admitted with financial aid, Wesleyan commits to meeting 100% of your institutionally calculated need across all four years through grant aid and campus work-study only—Wesleyan does not include student loans in undergraduate financial aid packages.

3. Purely need-based (no merit or athletic scholarships): Wesleyan awards financial aid strictly based on demonstrated family financial need. It does not offer academic merit scholarships or athletic scholarships.

4. Wesleyan African Scholars Program pathway: Citizens or permanent residents of any of Africa's 54 countries who apply for financial aid are automatically considered for the Wesleyan African Scholars Program (which awards full cost-of-attendance packages to roughly 11 African scholars each year). There is no separate scholarship form—selection happens through the standard admission and need-based aid review.

Cost of Attendance and What Financial Aid Covers

Wesleyan publishes multi-year projected annual costs for international student visa certification. The expected annual Cost of Attendance (covering tuition, fees, housing, dining, books, personal expenses, and health insurance) is:

  • 2027–2028 Academic Year (Year 1): $109,400
  • 2028–2029 Academic Year (Year 2): $114,300
  • 2029–2030 Academic Year (Year 3): $119,400
  • 2030–2031 Academic Year (Year 4): $124,800

Components of a Wesleyan International Aid Package

  • Wesleyan University Grants: Direct institutional gift aid covering the gap between your Cost of Attendance and your expected family/student contribution. Grants never have to be repaid.
  • Student Work-Study Expectation: Most aid packages include a reasonable campus employment expectation during the academic year so students can earn money toward books and personal expenses.
  • No Loans: Wesleyan eliminates student loans from its undergraduate financial aid awards, allowing students to graduate debt-free.

Costs You Must Verify Carefully

  • Expected Family Contribution (EFC): Even under a 100% demonstrated-need policy, Wesleyan determines what your family can contribute using its own financial formula. If your family has zero ability to pay, you must document this clearly.
  • Travel, Visa & Arrival Expenses: Confirm in writing with Wesleyan's Financial Aid Office whether your specific package includes an international travel allowance, health insurance coverage, or start-up assistance—and plan separately for passport fees, US F-1 visa fees, SEVIS I-901 fees, and embassy travel.

Mandatory International Student Certification of Finances (COF)

Every international applicant—whether requesting financial aid or not—must submit Wesleyan's International Student Certification of Finances (COF) form, along with official bank statements or financial documentation verifying any expected family/sponsor contribution.

For Regular Decision, the Certification of Finances is due by 15 February 2027 (Early Decision II due 1 February 2027). Missing or inaccurate financial information can delay your application review or even result in an admission offer being rescinded.

Critical Financial Aid Rules and Policies

1. Apply for aid at the time of admission—not later

To receive institutional financial aid at Wesleyan, international students must apply for financial aid and be found eligible when applying for first-year admission. If you indicate on your admission application that you will not seek financial assistance, you cannot apply for institutional aid upon enrolling (and will not be eligible until after completing at least two full semesters, with no guarantee of funds).

2. Free Alternative to the CSS Profile (ISFAA)

Wesleyan uses the College Board CSS Profile (School Code: 3959) and does not issue CSS Profile fee waiver codes to international students. However, if paying the CSS Profile fee is a financial hardship, Wesleyan explicitly allows you to submit the free International Student Financial Aid Application (ISFAA) instead by emailing the completed form directly to internationalaid@wesleyan.edu.

3. Noncustodial Parent Requirement

If your biological or adoptive parents are divorced, separated, or were never married, Wesleyan requires financial information from both parents: either the CSS Noncustodial Parent Profile or a separate ISFAA completed by the noncustodial parent for their household. If you have zero contact with a noncustodial parent or cannot obtain their information due to displacement/safety reasons, contact Wesleyan's Financial Aid Office to ask about a Noncustodial Parent Waiver request.

4. No Aid for International Transfer Students

Wesleyan provides zero institutional financial aid to international transfer students. You must apply as a first-time, first-year undergraduate applicant with no prior full-time university enrolment.

Eligibility Criteria

  • First-Year Status Only: Must be completing or have completed secondary school and applying for first-year undergraduate entry with no prior full-time college or university enrolment.
  • Citizenship: Open to international applicants from all countries (non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents). To be considered for the Wesleyan African Scholars Program, you must be a citizen or permanent resident of one of Africa's 54 countries.
  • Demonstrated Financial Need: Must submit complete, verifiable family financial documentation by the stated deadline.
  • Academic Excellence: Strong secondary school transcripts, rigorous coursework, compelling essays, and strong teacher/counsellor recommendations.

Guidance for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya or other host countries can apply to Wesleyan as international first-year applicants:

  • Citizenship classification on Common App: Select your country of legal citizenship (for example, South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia) under the non-US citizen option—do not choose "US Refugee/Asylee," which applies only to US domestic immigration status.
  • Documenting informal livelihoods or zero income: Because the CSS Profile has limited character space, Wesleyan encourages international applicants with special circumstances to submit dollar-specific explanations and supporting documentation (such as UNHCR refugee attestation, proof of unemployment, or a signed household income statement) directly to internationalaid@wesleyan.edu.
  • Application fee waiver: Wesleyan's $65 application fee is automatically waived for international applicants who indicate financial need and request an admission fee waiver on the Common App or Coalition Application.

Academic Programmes and STEM Pathways

Wesleyan offers more than 45 major fields of study across the natural sciences, mathematics, arts, humanities, and social sciences, allowing students to double-major or design interdisciplinary concentrations:

  • Computer Science
  • Mathematics and Data Analysis (Quantitative Analysis Center)
  • Physics, Astronomy, Chemistry, and Molecular Biology & Biochemistry
  • Economics and Quantitative Economics
  • Environmental Studies and Earth & Environmental Sciences
  • Dual-Degree Engineering Options (3-2 or 4-2 combined engineering programmes with Columbia University, Caltech, or Dartmouth)

Note on Engineering: Wesleyan awards Bachelor of Arts (BA) degrees across its majors and does not offer a standalone 4-year Bachelor of Engineering degree; students seeking accredited engineering degrees pursue physics/computer science at Wesleyan alongside a dual-degree engineering transfer pathway.

Application Rounds and Deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry)

Note that Early Decision I (15 November 2026) has passed. For Fall 2027 entry, pay close attention to Wesleyan's separated admission and financial aid deadlines:

  • Early Decision II (Binding):
    Admission Application Deadline: 1 January 2027
    Financial Aid Application Deadline (CSS Profile/ISFAA): 1 January 2027
    Certification of Finances Deadline: 1 February 2027
  • Regular Decision (Non-Binding):
    Admission Application Deadline: 1 January 2027
    Financial Aid Application Deadline (CSS Profile/ISFAA): 15 January 2027
    Certification of Finances Deadline: 15 February 2027
Portico Recommendation on Admission Round:

Notice that Wesleyan's Regular Decision admission deadline is 1 January 2027—two weeks earlier than many other US universities whose deadlines fall on 15 January. Apply under Regular Decision rather than binding Early Decision II so you can compare financial aid offers from multiple institutions before making a final decision.

Complete Checklist of Required Documents

1. Academic & Admissions Documents (Due 1 January 2027 for RD)

  • Common Application or Coalition Application via Scoir: Includes Wesleyan member questions and your personal essay.
  • Official Secondary School Transcript & School Report: Complete high school academic records (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts and KCSE certificate/result slip) submitted by your school counsellor, with certified English translations if any documents are not in English.
  • Counsellor Recommendation & Mid-Year Grade Report: Submitted through your application platform as grades become available.
  • Two Academic Teacher Evaluations: Wesleyan encourages one evaluation from a humanities, social sciences, or language teacher and a second from a mathematics or science teacher.
  • Standardised & English Proficiency Tests (Optional): SAT/ACT scores are optional for all applicants. English proficiency tests are optional, though strongly recommended if English is not your first language or primary language of instruction (self-reported scores accepted during review; minimum benchmarks: Duolingo 130, TOEFL iBT 100, IELTS 7.5).

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Documents

  • CSS Profile (School Code: 3959) OR Free ISFAA: Submitted by 15 January 2027 (Regular Decision). Note that electronic CSS Profile processing takes 3–5 business days, so submit early.
  • Noncustodial Parent CSS Profile or Separate Noncustodial ISFAA: Required if your parents are divorced, separated, or never married.
  • Income Verification Documents: Certified English translations of parent tax returns, employer income letters, or formal statements documenting unemployment, informal income, or displacement circumstances.
  • International Student Certification of Finances (COF): Submitted by 15 February 2027 (Regular Decision) together with bank statements or sponsor verification for any expected family contribution.

Step-by-Step Application Process

  1. Add Wesleyan University to your Common App (or Scoir) list. Ensure it fits within your 20-college Common App limit.
  2. Request need-based financial aid and an admission fee waiver. Select "Yes" to applying for financial aid on the application and indicate eligibility for the $65 application fee waiver.
  3. Submit your admission application by 1 January 2027. Ensure your counsellor and two core academic teachers submit your transcripts, school report, and evaluations on time.
  4. Activate your WesCheck Applicant Portal. Once Wesleyan receives your application, log into WesCheck to track missing admissions and financial aid items.
  5. Submit the CSS Profile (Code 3959) or email the free ISFAA by 15 January 2027. If paying for the CSS Profile causes financial hardship, download the ISFAA, complete all sections accurately (plus a separate ISFAA for a noncustodial parent if applicable), and email it with income documentation to internationalaid@wesleyan.edu.
  6. Submit the Certification of Finances by 15 February 2027. Complete the COF form and upload supporting financial documentation through your WesCheck portal before the February deadline.
  7. Monitor WesCheck regularly through decision release. Respond promptly if the Financial Aid Office requests additional income verification or translations.

About Grinnell College and Its International Aid Programme

Grinnell College is a highly selective, private liberal arts and sciences college located in Grinnell, Iowa. It is widely recognised for its self-governed, open curriculum (with no general-education core requirements beyond a first-year tutorial) and its commitment to funding international students from diverse socioeconomic backgrounds.

Before applying, understand how Grinnell's admissions and financial aid process works:

1. Need-aware admission for international students: Grinnell is need-aware when evaluating non-US citizens. Your family's financial need is considered alongside your academic record during the admissions decision, making admission highly competitive for applicants requiring almost full funding.

2. 100% of demonstrated need met — with NO student loans: If you are admitted and submitted your financial aid application on time, Grinnell commits to meeting 100% of your institutionally calculated financial need without including student loans in your aid package.

3. Automatic Merit Scholarship Consideration: Outstanding international applicants are automatically evaluated for merit scholarships based on their Common App admission file—no separate scholarship application or early priority deadline is required for international applicants.

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in Grinnell need-based aid packages

  • Need-Based Institutional Grants: Gift aid awarded by Grinnell to cover the gap between the annual Cost of Attendance and your expected family contribution. Grants do not need to be repaid.
  • Merit Scholarships (where awarded): Competitive merit awards granted to top-performing international applicants regardless of need profile. (Note: if you also qualify for need-based aid, merit awards are integrated into your overall need-based calculation.)
  • Loan-Free Need Packaging: Grinnell states that it meets full institutional demonstrated need without requiring student loans.

Expenses and conditions to verify independently

  • Expected Family Contribution (EFC): Grinnell calculates how much your family can contribute based on its own formula. Even when 100% of calculated need is met, your family is expected to pay any assessed contribution.
  • Pre-Arrival & Immigration Expenses: Confirm directly with Grinnell's Financial Aid Office what your package covers regarding mandatory health insurance, international flights, passport fees, US F-1 visa fees, SEVIS I-901 fees, and travel to the US Embassy.

Critical Rule: You CANNOT Apply for Aid After Admission

Grinnell will not consider financial aid applications after you are admitted to the College. If you indicate on your Common App that you do not intend to apply for need-based financial aid, you are permanently ineligible to request institutional financial aid in your first year or in any future years at Grinnell.

In addition, your admissions file is considered incomplete and will not be reviewed for admission until your required financial aid form is submitted by the deadline.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for admission and international need-based financial aid at Grinnell College for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • First-Year Undergraduate Status: Must be completing or have completed secondary school and applying for first-year undergraduate admission (fall intake only).
  • Secondary Curriculum Completion: Applicants must complete the full secondary education cycle required for university entry in their country (for example, completing KCSE in Kenya, or continuing through A-Levels if studying under an O-Level/A-Level system; O-Levels alone are not sufficient).
  • Citizenship Status: Must be an international applicant (non-US citizen and non-US permanent resident). Dual US citizens must apply under domestic need-blind rules using the FAFSA and CSS Profile.
  • English Proficiency: Must demonstrate strong English proficiency through accepted testing (Duolingo English Test, IELTS, or TOEFL) unless exempt under Grinnell's language policy.
  • Timely Financial Aid Submission: Must select "Yes" to applying for need-based aid on the Common App and submit either the 2027–28 CSS Profile or Grinnell's online ISFAA by the exact admission round deadline.

Guidance for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya or other host countries can apply to Grinnell as international first-year applicants:

  • Citizenship classification on Common App: Select your country of legal citizenship (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia) under the non-US citizenship section. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," which applies only to US domestic immigration status.
  • Zero-cost application & free financial aid form: Grinnell charges $0 application fee on the Common App and offers a free online International Student Application for Financial Assistance (ISAFA) inside your Grinnell applicant portal so you do not have to pay for the CSS Profile.
  • Reporting displaced or informal household finances: Convert all currency amounts into US dollars ($) as instructed on the form. If parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal income without formal tax records, provide honest estimates and explain your household's exact situation clearly in the form's special circumstances section.

Academic Programmes and STEM Pathways

Grinnell offers over 40 majors and concentrations within a liberal arts and sciences framework, including strong quantitative and STEM fields:

  • Computer Science
  • Mathematics and Statistics
  • Data Science / Quantitative Analysis
  • Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Biological Chemistry
  • Economics and Policy Studies
  • Cooperative 3-2 Engineering Pathways (with Columbia University, Caltech, Washington University in St. Louis, or Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute)

Note on Engineering: Grinnell awards Bachelor of Arts (BA) degrees and does not offer a standalone 4-year Bachelor of Engineering degree on campus; students interested in engineering combine sciences/mathematics at Grinnell with a cooperative dual-degree engineering transfer programme.

Application Rounds and Deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry)

At Grinnell College, the financial aid deadline is identical to the admission application deadline for each round:

  • Early Decision I (Binding):
    Admission & Financial Aid Deadline: 15 November 2026
    Decision Release: Mid-to-late December 2026
  • Early Decision II (Binding):
    Admission & Financial Aid Deadline: 5 January 2027
    Decision Release: Early February 2027
  • Regular Decision (Non-Binding):
    Admission & Financial Aid Deadline: 15 January 2027
    Decision Release: Late March / Early April 2027 | Student Reply Date: 1 May 2027

Note that Early Decision I (15 November 2026) closes immediately. For most applicants needing near-full financial aid, Regular Decision (15 January 2027) is the safest option because it is non-binding and lets you compare financial aid packages across multiple universities before making a commitment.

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Academic & Admissions Documents

  • Common Application & Personal Essay: Submitted online ($0 application fee; no supplemental essay required by Grinnell).
  • Official High School Transcripts (Mark Sheets / Report Cards): Showing all subjects studied and marks earned across every year of secondary school (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts in Kenya), sent directly by your high school counsellor/principal via Common App (preferred), official school email, or stamped postal/fax submission.
  • Official External / National Exam Results: Certified copies of national examination certificates or result slips (such as KCSE, WAEC, NECO, IGCSE/A-Level, or IB), submitted by your school official.
  • Secondary School Report & Counsellor Recommendation: Completed and uploaded by your school counsellor/principal via Common App.
  • Teacher Recommendation Letter(s): At least one recommendation from a core academic subject teacher (uploaded via Common App).
  • English Proficiency Test Score Report: Official score report from Duolingo English Test, IELTS (via IELTS E-Delivery to Grinnell College Admission Office), or TOEFL iBT / Essentials (TOEFL Code: 6252).
  • SAT or ACT Scores (Optional): Grinnell is test-optional; SAT/ACT scores are not required for admission or merit scholarship consideration.

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Form (Choose Option A OR Option B)

  • Option A — 2027–28 CSS Profile (School Code: 6252): Submitted online through the College Board website (paper copies not accepted). Note: Grinnell does not provide CSS Profile fee waiver codes to international applicants.
  • Option B — Grinnell's Online International Student Application for Financial Assistance (ISAFA): A free online form accessed directly inside your Grinnell Applicant Portal after submitting your Common App.

Important Submission Rules for Financial Documents

1. Portal-only submission for ISAFA: Grinnell explicitly states that the online form inside your Grinnell Applicant Portal is the only accepted method for submitting the ISAFA. Do not submit PDF copies or email financial forms to the Financial Aid Office.

2. Do NOT send extra unrequested documents: Grinnell instructs international applicants not to upload bank statements, tax files, or a Certification of Finances unless specifically requested by the Office of Financial Aid.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Add Grinnell College to your Common App list. Verify it fits within your 20-college Common App limit. Applying to Grinnell is completely free ($0 fee).
  2. Indicate your intent to apply for need-based financial aid. In the Grinnell member questions on Common App, select "Yes" to indicate that you are applying for need-based financial assistance.
  3. Invite your school counsellor and academic teacher early. Enter your counsellor and teacher details in Common App so they can upload your high school transcripts, KCSE/national exam results, school report, and recommendation letters before the deadline.
  4. Arrange your official English proficiency test scores. Send official Duolingo, IELTS, or TOEFL scores (Code: 6252) directly to Grinnell College if required for your curriculum background.
  5. Submit your Common App well before 15 January 2027 (Regular Decision). Submit your Common App several days early—especially if you plan to use Grinnell's free online ISAFA—because you can only access the ISAFA after your Common App is submitted and your Grinnell Applicant Portal account is activated.
  6. Log into your Grinnell Applicant Portal and complete your financial aid form by 15 January 2027. Either submit the 2027–28 CSS Profile (Code: 6252) via College Board or complete Grinnell's free online ISAFA inside your portal before the deadline.
  7. Check your portal checklist until every item is marked complete. Remember that Grinnell will not review your application for admission until both your academic records and your financial aid form are received.
