About Amherst College and Its International Financial Aid Policy

Amherst College is a top-ranked, highly selective private liberal arts college in Amherst, Massachusetts, and one of the very few institutions in the United States that is 100% need-blind for international students.

Before adding Amherst to your Common App list, understand four critical features of how its admissions and financial aid system operates:

1. Truly need-blind international admission: Amherst evaluates your application without looking at your family's ability to pay or how much financial aid you request. Requesting a full financial aid package does not hurt your chances of being admitted. However, because Amherst is one of the most selective colleges in the world (with an international acceptance rate around 3%), admission itself is extraordinarily competitive.

2. 100% of calculated financial need met — with NO loans: Once admitted, Amherst commits to meeting 100% of your institutionally calculated demonstrated financial need across all four years using grant scholarships and a reasonable campus work-study expectation—with zero student loans required. Over 82% of Amherst's international students receive need-based financial aid, with an average annual international aid package exceeding $84,000.

3. Strictly need-based (no merit or athletic scholarships): Amherst does not award academic merit scholarships, talent awards, or athletic scholarships. All institutional financial aid is awarded exclusively on the basis of demonstrated family financial need.

4. Open Curriculum with Five-College Consortium Access: Amherst features an open curriculum (allowing students to design their course of study without rigid distribution requirements) and belongs to the Five-College Consortium alongside Smith College, Mount Holyoke College, Hampshire College, and UMass Amherst—allowing Amherst students to take courses across all five campuses at no extra tuition cost.

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in Amherst need-based financial aid packages

  • Amherst Scholarship Grants: Institutional gift aid covering the gap between Amherst's total Cost of Attendance (tuition, mandatory fees, on-campus housing, and dining plan) and your calculated family/student contribution. Grants never have to be repaid.
  • Campus Student Employment (Work-Study): Aid packages typically include a modest on-campus job expectation during the academic year so students can earn money for books, supplies, and personal expenses.
  • Zero Loan Packaging: Amherst does not include loans in any undergraduate financial aid package.
  • Exchange-Rate Protection Policy: Amherst actively monitors foreign currency fluctuations; if your home currency shifts by 10% or more relative to the US dollar, Amherst reviews and adjusts aid packages for students from that country.

Expenses and conditions to verify independently

  • Expected Family & Student Contribution: Even under a 100% demonstrated-need policy, Amherst uses its own Institutional Methodology to assess what your family can pay. If your family has zero ability to pay, you must document this accurately.
  • Health Insurance, Travel & Pre-Arrival Costs: Verify directly with Amherst's Office of Financial Aid how mandatory student health insurance, international flights, winter clothing allowances, passport fees, US F-1 visa fees, and SEVIS I-901 fees are handled for high-need international recipients.

Critical Rule: Apply for Financial Aid at the Time of Admission

Amherst strictly enforces its international aid entry policy: if you enter Amherst as an international student without applying for financial aid at the time of admission, you are not eligible to apply for institutional financial aid in subsequent years unless your family experiences an unforeseen, documented catastrophic change in financial circumstances. Always request aid during your initial application if you will need funding at any point during your degree.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya (such as in Kakuma or Dadaab camps or urban areas) or other host countries are eligible to apply to Amherst College under its need-blind, full-need international admissions policy. Pay careful attention to these specific procedures:

  • 1. Citizenship selection on Common App: If you are a refugee living in Kenya and hold citizenship from another country (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia), select your country of legal citizenship under the non-US citizen option on Common App. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," as that classification applies solely to individuals holding US domestic immigration status.
  • 2. Explaining displacement & interrupted schooling in your application: Amherst practises holistic admissions. Use the Common App Additional Information section (and ask your school counsellor or teacher recommenders to note in their letters) any educational disruptions, camp/host-country school conditions, limited access to laboratories or textbooks, or family displacement circumstances so admissions officers evaluate your achievements in full context.
  • 3. Requesting the $75 Application Fee Waiver: If paying Amherst's $75 application fee causes financial hardship, request a Common App fee waiver inside your Common App profile (which your school counsellor approves online), or contact Amherst's Office of Admission directly before submitting if you cannot secure an online counsellor approval.
  • 4. Requesting a CSS Profile Fee Payment Code: Amherst requires the 2027–2028 CSS Profile (School Code: 3003) for all international financial aid applicants. If the CSS Profile fee presents a financial hardship, contact Amherst's Office of Financial Aid early to inquire about an international CSS Profile fee payment code—do not wait until the January 15 deadline, as codes are limited and take time to process.
  • 5. Documenting zero income, informal work, or missing tax returns: If your parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal income without government tax returns, do not invent numbers. Report exact figures in your home currency on the CSS Profile, upload a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement plus any UNHCR/government refugee attestation or signed household income explanation directly to Amherst's Financial Aid Portal, and provide your own clear English translation (Amherst explicitly states you do not need to pay for a certified translation service—your own accurate English translation is accepted for financial documents).
  • 6. Noncustodial Parent Waiver (if separated due to conflict/displacement): Amherst normally requires a separate CSS Profile from both biological/adoptive parents if they are divorced, separated, or never married. If you have lost contact with a parent due to conflict, displacement, or abandonment and cannot obtain their financial records, submit Amherst's Noncustodial Parent Waiver Petition with supporting documentation from a counsellor, UNHCR officer, or community leader.
  • 7. Valid Passport / Travel Document Planning: While you do not need a valid passport to submit your Common App, admitted refugee students will need a recognised passport or UNHCR/government Convention Travel Document (CTD) to obtain an F-1 US Student Visa after admission. Begin exploring your travel document options early.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for admission and need-based financial aid at Amherst College for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must meet the following criteria:

  • Academic Standing & Secondary Completion: Must be completing or have completed secondary school (such as KCSE in Kenya or equivalent national/international secondary qualifications) and applying for a first undergraduate degree (Bachelor of Arts). (Note: International transfer students who have already completed some university coursework are also eligible for need-blind, full-need aid at Amherst under separate transfer deadlines.)
  • Citizenship: Open to applicants of all nationalities worldwide. Non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents apply through the international financial aid process.
  • English Language Proficiency: Applicants whose first language is not English and whose most recent two years of secondary school instruction were not taught in English must submit official TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, or Duolingo English Test scores. (Students who completed their most recent two years of secondary school in an English-medium curriculum, such as Kenyan secondary schools, are exempt from English proficiency testing.)
  • Demonstrated Financial Need & Timely Aid Filing: Must indicate intent to apply for financial aid on the admission application and submit the 2027–28 CSS Profile and required family income documentation.

Academic Programmes and STEM Opportunities

Amherst College offers more than 40 majors leading to a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree across the sciences, mathematics, humanities, and social sciences, including:

  • Computer Science
  • Mathematics and Statistics
  • Data Science (interdisciplinary pathway)
  • Physics, Astronomy, Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry & Biophysics, and Neuroscience
  • Economics and Political Economy
  • Environmental Studies and Geology
  • Five-College Engineering & Applied Science Courses (via cross-registration at UMass Amherst, Smith College, and Mount Holyoke College)

Note on Engineering: Amherst awards Bachelor of Arts (BA) degrees and does not offer a standalone ABET-accredited Bachelor of Engineering degree on its own campus; students interested in engineering typically major in Physics, Computer Science, or Mathematics while taking engineering courses through the Five-College Consortium or pursuing a graduate engineering degree after graduation.

Application Rounds and Deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry)

Note that the binding Early Decision deadline (9 November 2026) has already passed. Amherst does not offer Early Decision II or Early Action. Only Regular Decision remains open for Fall 2027 first-year entry:

  • Regular Decision Admission Application Deadline: 5 January 2027 (via Common App or Coalition Application via Scoir)
  • Regular Decision Financial Aid Priority Deadline: 15 January 2027 (2027–28 CSS Profile and 2025 parent/student income documentation)
  • Regular Decision Notification Date: On or around 20 March 2027
  • Admitted Student Reply Date: 1 May 2027
Portico Deadline Alert:

Amherst's Regular Decision admission deadline is 5 January 2027—ten days earlier than the 15 January deadline used by many other US colleges. Submit your Common App by 5 January 2027 and complete your CSS Profile and financial uploads by 15 January 2027. (Amherst notes that financial aid documents submitted slightly after the priority date are still reviewed without penalty, though submitting by 15 January ensures your aid award is ready when admission decisions are released in March.)

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Academic & Admissions Documents (Due 5 January 2027)

  • Common Application (or Coalition Application via Scoir): Includes your main personal essay and the Amherst Writing Supplement.
  • $75 Application Fee or Approved Fee Waiver: Requested inside Common App and confirmed by your school counsellor.
  • Official Secondary School Transcript & School Report: Complete high school academic records (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts and certified KCSE certificate/result slip) uploaded by your school counsellor/principal via Common App.
  • Mid-Year Report / Updated Grades: Submitted by your school counsellor once final or mid-year grades become available.
  • Two Academic Teacher Recommendations: Recommendations from two teachers in core academic subjects (such as Mathematics, Science, English, History, or Foreign Language).
  • English Proficiency Test Scores (Only if not exempt): Recommended minimum scores for non-exempt applicants: Duolingo English Test 130+, IELTS Academic 7.5+, or TOEFL iBT (Amherst Code: 3003). Self-reported scores are accepted for initial review.
  • SAT or ACT Scores (Optional): Amherst is test-optional; you are not required to submit SAT/ACT scores, and applicants without scores are not disadvantaged.

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Documents (Priority Date: 15 January 2027)

  • 2027–2028 CSS Profile (Amherst School Code: 3003): Completed online through the College Board in your home currency. (International students do not complete the US FAFSA.)
  • Separate Noncustodial Parent CSS Profile (if applicable): Required if your parents are divorced, separated, or never married (unless a Noncustodial Parent Waiver is approved).
  • 2025 Parent & Student Income Documentation (PDF format): Signed and dated copies of your and your parents' 2025 tax returns, employer salary certificates/wage statements, or a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement accompanied by refugee attestation or household livelihood explanations.

Important Upload Rule for International Income Documents

Amherst explicitly instructs international applicants to upload signed and dated copies of their 2025 income documentation (in .PDF format—image files like JPG/PNG are not accepted) directly to Amherst College's Financial Aid Portal—and NOT to College Board IDOC. All documents must show original currency amounts and include an English translation (your own translation is acceptable).

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Add Amherst College to your Common App (or Scoir) list. Verify it fits within your 20-college Common App limit.
  2. Indicate your intent to apply for need-based financial aid and a fee waiver. Select "Yes" to applying for financial aid in Amherst's member questions, and request a Common App fee waiver if paying $75 is a financial hardship.
  3. Complete the Amherst Writing Supplement and Common App essays. Prepare thoughtful essays that reflect your intellectual curiosity, values, and lived experiences.
  4. Invite your school counsellor and two academic teachers early. Assign your counsellor and two core subject teachers in Common App so they can upload your transcripts, KCSE results, school report, and recommendations before 5 January 2027.
  5. Submit your Regular Decision admission application by 5 January 2027. Submit early to avoid technical delays and unlock your Amherst Applicant Portal.
  6. Submit the 2027–2028 CSS Profile (Code: 3003) by 15 January 2027. Complete the CSS Profile online via College Board in your home currency (contact Amherst's Financial Aid Office early if you need to request a CSS Profile fee payment code).
  7. Upload your 2025 income/non-tax PDFs directly to Amherst's Financial Aid Portal by 15 January 2027. Log into your Amherst Financial Aid Portal and upload your signed PDF income statements, Non-Tax Filer Statement, or refugee financial explanations directly to the portal (not IDOC).
  8. Monitor your Amherst Applicant & Financial Aid Portals regularly. Check both portals until every admission and financial aid item is marked complete, and respond promptly to any follow-up verification requests.

About the University of Notre Dame and Its International Financial Aid

The University of Notre Dame is a private, Catholic research university located in Notre Dame, Indiana, near South Bend. It is one of a small group of US universities that maintains a need-blind admissions policy for all international undergraduate applicants while committing to meet 100% of admitted students' demonstrated financial need.

Before adding Notre Dame to your Common App list, make sure you understand four essential features of its admissions and financial aid system:

1. Need-blind international admission: Notre Dame evaluates your undergraduate admission application without considering your family's ability to pay. Requesting full financial assistance does not reduce your chances of admission, though overall international acceptance remains highly selective (around 7%).

2. 100% of demonstrated need met — without student loans: Once admitted, Notre Dame meets 100% of your institutionally calculated demonstrated financial need through need-based scholarships and grants that do not depend on taking student loans.

3. Automatic Merit Scholarship Consideration (Notre Dame Scholars' Program): Every first-year applicant is automatically considered for selective, renewable merit scholarships (such as the flagship Stamps Scholarship and named merit awards typically worth $25,000/year)—no separate application is needed. Note: if you qualify for need-based aid, merit awards are integrated into your overall need-based package rather than reducing your calculated family contribution.

4. First-Year Studies & Academic Structure: All incoming first-year students enter through the First Year of Studies advising structure and must indicate an intended college or school on their application (Arts & Letters, Science, Engineering, Mendoza College of Business, or School of Architecture). Note that applicants to the Mendoza College of Business must select Mendoza on their initial first-year application, as internal transfer into Mendoza later is severely restricted.

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in Notre Dame financial aid packages

  • Need-Based University Scholarships & Grants: Gift aid awarded by Notre Dame to cover the gap between the annual Cost of Attendance (tuition, mandatory fees, on-campus housing, and dining) and your expected family contribution. Grants never have to be repaid.
  • Loan-Free Need Packaging: Notre Dame's need-based financial aid packages for international undergraduates do not require students to take out student loans to meet calculated need.
  • Student Employment Opportunities: Admitted international students on F-1 visas are eligible for on-campus part-time employment to help cover books, supplies, and incidental personal costs.

Expenses and conditions to verify independently

  • Expected Family Contribution (EFC): Notre Dame uses its own institutional formula (via the CSS Profile) to calculate how much your family can contribute. Even when 100% of calculated need is met, your family is expected to pay any assessed contribution.
  • Pre-Arrival, Health Insurance & Travel Costs: Verify directly with Notre Dame's Office of Financial Aid how mandatory student health insurance, international flights, passport processing, US F-1 visa fees, SEVIS I-901 fees, and embassy travel are budgeted and supported for high-need international students.

Critical Rule: Request Financial Aid at the Time of Admission

International applicants who wish to be considered for institutional need-based financial aid must indicate their intent to apply for aid and submit the required CSS Profile during the initial admission process. Do not state that you can pay full fees with the hope of requesting institutional aid after arriving on campus.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya (such as in Kakuma or Dadaab camps or urban centres) or other host countries are eligible to apply to the University of Notre Dame under its need-blind, full-need international admissions policy. Keep these crucial points in mind:

  • 1. Citizenship selection on Common App: If you are a refugee residing in Kenya and hold citizenship from another country (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia), select your country of legal citizenship under the non-US citizen option on Common App. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," as that category applies only to individuals with US domestic immigration status.
  • 2. Contextualising displacement & schooling challenges: Notre Dame practises holistic admissions and explicitly evaluates applicants within their educational, cultural, and social context. Use the Common App Additional Information section—and ask your teacher or counsellor recommender to mention—any interrupted education, camp or host-country school constraints, or family displacement circumstances.
  • 3. $85 Application Fee Waiver (Automatic via Common App / Scoir): Notre Dame accepts automatic fee waivers directly through the Common Application and Coalition Application. In Common App, go to your Profile section, select Common App Fee Waiver, check the financial-need indicator that applies to you, and sign to have the $85 fee waived automatically upon submission.
  • 4. No CSS Profile Fee Waivers — Contact Admissions Early if Stuck: Notre Dame requires the 2027–28 CSS Profile (School Code: 1841) for all non-US citizens applying for need-based aid. However, Notre Dame explicitly notes that it is unable to provide CSS Profile fee waiver codes to international applicants. If paying the CSS Profile fee is an insurmountable barrier due to refugee status or extreme financial hardship, email admissions@nd.edu and finaid@nd.edu well ahead of January 15, 2027 to explain your situation and ask for guidance.
  • 5. Documenting zero income, informal livelihoods, or missing tax returns: If your parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal income without tax returns, do not invent figures. Report exact household figures accurately on the CSS Profile and upload a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement alongside UNHCR/government refugee documentation or a signed household income statement via College Board IDOC / Notre Dame's financial aid portal when requested.
  • 6. Noncustodial Parent Requirement (and Waiver Option): If your biological or adoptive parents are divorced, separated, or never married, Notre Dame requires a separate CSS Profile from the noncustodial parent. If you have lost contact with a parent due to conflict, displacement, or abandonment, contact Notre Dame's Office of Financial Aid to submit a Noncustodial Parent Waiver Request supported by documentation from a counsellor, UNHCR officer, or community leader.
  • 7. English Proficiency Testing Access: If English was not your primary language of instruction and no testing centre for TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, or PTE Academic is accessible in your area, Notre Dame instructs applicants to contact admissions@nd.edu directly to review alternative options.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for undergraduate admission and need-based financial aid at the University of Notre Dame for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must satisfy the following criteria:

  • Secondary School Completion & Academic Preparation: Must be completing or have completed secondary school (e.g., KCSE in Kenya or equivalent national/international secondary credentials) and applying for a first bachelor's degree. Notre Dame expects strong preparation across core academic units: 4 units of English, at least 3–4 units of Mathematics (4 units required for Science, Engineering, Business, and Architecture applicants), 2–4 units of Science (Chemistry and Physics required for Engineering/Science), 2–4 units of Foreign Language, and 2–4 units of History/Social Science.
  • Citizenship: Open to international applicants of all nationalities worldwide. Non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents apply through the international financial aid process.
  • English Language Proficiency: Required if your primary first language is not English or your secondary education was not taught primarily in English. (Students educated primarily in English-medium secondary schools, such as in Kenya, generally meet the English-instruction criteria, though submitting strong scores is welcome; SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing 650+ or ACT English/Reading 26+ also waives the English exam.)
  • Timely Financial Aid Filing: Must indicate intent to apply for need-based financial aid on the admission application and complete the 2027–28 CSS Profile (School Code: 1841).

Academic Programmes and Colleges

Notre Dame offers more than 75 undergraduate degree programmes across five undergraduate colleges and schools:

  • College of Engineering: Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Civil Engineering, Environmental Earth Sciences
  • College of Science: Mathematics, Applied and Computational Mathematics & Statistics (ACMS), Data Science, Physics, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, Neuroscience and Behavior
  • College of Arts and Letters: Economics, Political Science, Global Affairs, Psychology, Philosophy, Theology, Sociology, Film/Television/Theatre, Design
  • Mendoza College of Business: Accountancy, Finance, Business Analytics, Management & Organization, Marketing (must be selected at the time of initial first-year application)
  • School of Architecture: Five-year professional Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.)

Note that Restrictive Early Action (1 November 2026) has already passed. Only Regular Decision remains open for Fall 2027 first-year entry:

  • Regular Decision Admission Application Deadline: 1 January 2027 (note: some Notre Dame admissions pages list 4 January 2027; aim to submit by 1 January 2027 to be completely safe)
  • Regular Decision Financial Aid Priority Date: 15 January 2027 (Complete 2027–28 CSS Profile — School Code: 1841 — plus requested IDOC financial documents)
  • Regular Decision Notification Date: Late March 2027
  • Admitted Student Confirmation Deadline: 1 May 2027
Portico Deadline & Testing Alert:

1. Early January Deadline: Notre Dame's Regular Decision admission deadline falls right at the start of January (1 January 2027), followed closely by the 15 January 2027 CSS Profile priority date. Do not wait until mid-January.

2. Test-Optional Window (2026–2027 Cycle Only): Notre Dame remains test-optional for SAT/ACT for Fall 2027 entry (the 2026–2027 application cycle), though it has announced that SAT/ACT scores will become mandatory again starting with Fall 2028 entry.

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Academic & Admissions Documents (Due 1 January 2027)

  • Common Application or Coalition Application via Scoir: Includes your main personal essay and the Notre Dame Writing Supplement.
  • $85 Application Fee or Automatic Fee Waiver: Selected directly inside your Common App Profile or Scoir fee waiver section.
  • Official Secondary School Transcripts & National Exam Results: Complete high school academic records (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts and certified KCSE certificate/result slip) with certified English translations if issued in another language.
  • Teacher Evaluation Letter: One evaluation letter from a high school teacher in a core academic subject who knows you well (counsellor evaluation is recommended, though not strictly required).
  • Official English Proficiency Test Scores (If applicable): Sent directly from the testing agency (TOEFL/CSS Code: 1841) — do not upload self-reported PDFs to your status portal. Minimum benchmarks: Duolingo English Test 125, IELTS Academic 7.5, or TOEFL iBT 100 (or 5.5 average / 5.0 section minimum on the post-February 2026 TOEFL scale).
  • SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2027 Entry): Not required for the 2026–2027 cycle.

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Documents (Priority Date: 15 January 2027)

  • 2027–2028 CSS Profile (Notre Dame School Code: 1841): Completed online through College Board for the custodial parent (and a separate Noncustodial Parent CSS Profile if parents are divorced, separated, or never married). (International applicants do not complete the US FAFSA.)
  • Supporting Tax / Income Documentation via IDOC: After submitting your CSS Profile, College Board's Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC) will notify you which supporting tax returns, wage statements, or Non-Tax Filer statements to upload.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Add University of Notre Dame to your Common App (or Scoir) list. Verify it fits within your 20-college Common App limit and select your intended undergraduate college/school (especially if applying to Business, Engineering, or Architecture).
  2. Request your automatic application fee waiver and indicate need-based aid. Activate the Common App Fee Waiver in your Profile section to waive the $85 fee, and select "Yes" to applying for need-based financial aid.
  3. Complete the Notre Dame Writing Supplement and personal essay. Reflect thoughtfully on your academic goals, community leadership, service, and personal values.
  4. Invite your core academic teacher (and counsellor) early. Ensure your teacher uploads your letter of evaluation and your school submits official secondary transcripts and KCSE/national exam results before 1 January 2027.
  5. Arrange official English proficiency scores (if required). Have Duolingo, IELTS, or TOEFL send official scores directly to Notre Dame (Code: 1841) well ahead of the deadline.
  6. Submit your Regular Decision admission application by 1 January 2027. Submit early to avoid technical bottlenecks and unlock your Notre Dame Applicant Status Portal.
  7. Complete the 2027–28 CSS Profile (School Code: 1841) by 15 January 2027. Submit your CSS Profile via College Board (plus any noncustodial parent profile or waiver request) and upload requested income or Non-Tax Filer documentation through IDOC.
  8. Monitor your Notre Dame Applicant Status Portal regularly. Check both your admission checklist and financial aid checklist to ensure every item is received.

About Kenyon College and Its International Financial Aid

Kenyon College is a selective private liberal arts and sciences college located in Gambier, Ohio, renowned for its strength in writing, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences, as well as its close-knit residential campus community.

Before adding Kenyon to your Common App list, make sure you understand four key features of its international admissions and financial aid process:

1. Need-aware international admission: Kenyon is need-aware for non-US citizens. Your family's financial circumstances and the amount of aid you request are evaluated alongside your academic profile during the admissions decision. Because institutional funding for international students is limited, admission is highly competitive for applicants requiring almost full financial aid.

2. 100% of demonstrated need met if admitted: Once Kenyon admits an international student who submitted their financial aid application on time, the college commits to meeting 100% of that student's institutionally calculated financial need across all four years.

3. Automatic Merit Scholarship Consideration: Every international applicant is automatically considered for Kenyon's merit scholarships (such as the Kenyon Honors Scholarship, Trustee Opportunity Scholarship, and Science Scholarship, which can range up to $25,000+ per year)—no separate merit application is required. Note: if you also qualify for need-based aid, merit awards are integrated into your overall need-based package rather than stacked to lower your expected family contribution.

4. Demonstrated Interest & Optional Interviews: Kenyon considers demonstrated interest in its holistic review. Attending virtual admissions webinars, engaging with Kenyon's international admissions team, or scheduling an optional virtual interview can help strengthen your application.

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in Kenyon international aid packages

  • Kenyon Need-Based Grants & Merit Scholarships: Gift aid awarded by the college that does not need to be repaid, covering the primary gap between the Cost of Attendance (tuition, mandatory fees, on-campus housing, and meal plan) and your family's assessed contribution.
  • On-Campus Student Employment: International aid packages typically include a campus work-study expectation during the academic year to help cover books, supplies, and personal expenses.
  • Modest Loan Component (Verify Exact Terms): Unlike loan-free institutions, Kenyon's standard need-based financial aid packaging can include a modest student loan component alongside grants and campus employment. Review your award letter carefully if admitted.

Expenses and conditions to verify independently

  • Expected Family Contribution (EFC): Kenyon calculates your expected contribution from parental and student income and assets. Even when 100% of calculated need is met, your family is responsible for paying any assessed contribution.
  • Pre-Arrival, Health Insurance & Travel Costs: Confirm directly with Kenyon's Office of Financial Aid whether your specific award covers mandatory student health insurance, winter clothing/settling-in costs, international flights, passport processing, US F-1 visa fees, and SEVIS I-901 fees.

Critical Rule: Apply for Financial Aid at the Time of Admission

International students must request financial aid and submit their financial aid application at the time they apply for first-year admission. If you enrol at Kenyon without applying for financial aid, you are not eligible to apply for institutional need-based aid in subsequent years.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya (such as in Kakuma or Dadaab camps or urban centres) or other host countries are eligible to apply to Kenyon College as international first-year applicants. Keep these practical points in mind:

  • 1. Citizenship selection on Common App: If you are a refugee living in Kenya and hold citizenship from another country (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia), select your country of legal citizenship under the non-US citizen option on Common App. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," which applies only to individuals holding US domestic immigration status.
  • 2. Zero Application Fee ($0) & Free Online Aid Form Option: Kenyon charges $0 application fee for all domestic and international first-year applicants. Furthermore, while Kenyon accepts the CSS Profile (Code: 1370), international applicants may alternatively use Kenyon's free online International Student Financial Aid Application inside the admissions portal if paying for the CSS Profile is a hardship.
  • 3. Contextualising displacement & interrupted schooling: Use the Common App Additional Information section—and ask your school counsellor or teacher recommenders to note in their letters—any interrupted schooling, camp/host-country school conditions, limited access to science labs or textbooks, or displacement circumstances so admissions officers understand your achievements in full context.
  • 4. Documenting zero income, informal work, or missing tax returns: If your parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal livelihoods without government tax returns, do not fabricate income numbers. Report exact household figures honestly and submit a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement alongside any UNHCR/government refugee attestation or signed household financial explanation.
  • 5. Noncustodial Parent Requirement & Waiver Option: If your biological or adoptive parents are divorced, separated, or never married, Kenyon normally requires financial forms from both parents. If you have lost contact with a parent due to conflict, displacement, or abandonment, contact Kenyon's Office of Financial Aid (finaid@kenyon.edu) to submit a Noncustodial Parent Waiver Request supported by documentation from a counsellor, UNHCR officer, or community leader.
  • 6. Optional Interviews (Skip Paid Third-Party Services): Although Kenyon lists paid third-party interview vendors (InitialView and Vericant) for international applicants, interviews are not required. Low-income and refugee applicants can request a free virtual interview directly with a Kenyon admissions officer or alumni interviewer—or skip the interview entirely without penalty.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for undergraduate admission and international financial aid at Kenyon College for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must satisfy the following requirements:

  • Secondary School Completion & Academic Preparation: Must be completing or have completed secondary school (such as KCSE in Kenya or equivalent national/international secondary qualifications) and applying for a first Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree. Kenyon expects a rigorous college-preparatory secondary curriculum across English, mathematics, laboratory sciences, social studies/history, and foreign language.
  • Citizenship: Open to international applicants of all nationalities worldwide. Non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents apply through the international financial aid process.
  • English Language Proficiency: Required unless your primary language of instruction in secondary school is English (such as in Kenyan secondary schools). Applicants from non-English-medium schools must submit Duolingo English Test (130+ encouraged), IELTS Academic (7.0+ encouraged), or TOEFL iBT (100+ encouraged).
  • Timely Financial Aid Filing: Must indicate intent to apply for financial aid on the admission application and submit either the 2027–28 CSS Profile (Code: 1370) or Kenyon's online international financial aid form by the deadline.

Academic Programmes and STEM Opportunities

Kenyon College offers more than 50 majors, minors, and interdisciplinary concentrations leading to a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree, including:

  • Mathematics and Statistics (including Scientific Computing concentration)
  • Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry, and Molecular Biology
  • Neuroscience and Environmental Studies
  • Economics and Quantitative Economics
  • English & Creative Writing, International Studies, Political Science, Psychology, and Philosophy
  • Dual-Degree Engineering Pathways (3-2 or 4-2 combined engineering programmes with Case Western Reserve University, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, or Washington University in St. Louis)

Note on Computer Science & Engineering: Kenyon offers a Scientific Computing concentration and strong Mathematics, Physics, and Economics majors, but does not offer a standalone Computer Science major or a standalone 4-year Bachelor of Engineering degree on campus. Students seeking pure Computer Science or Engineering should confirm curriculum fit carefully before applying.

  • Secondary School Report & Official High School Transcripts: Complete academic records across all years of secondary school (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts and certified KCSE certificate/result slip) uploaded by your school counsellor/principal.

Complete the CSS Profile via College Board (and upload requested income/non-tax files to College Board IDOC) or complete Kenyon's free online international financial aid application inside your admissions portal.

About Lafayette College and Its International Financial Aid

Lafayette College is a selective private liberal arts and engineering college located in Easton, Pennsylvania. Unlike many small liberal arts colleges that only offer science or pre-engineering pathways, Lafayette offers accredited 4-year Bachelor of Science (BS) engineering degrees alongside liberal arts, computer science, mathematics, and social science majors.

Before adding Lafayette to your Common App list, make sure you understand four essential features of its international admissions and financial aid process:

1. Need-aware international admission with high competition: Lafayette is need-aware for international applicants—meaning the Admissions Committee considers your family's ability to pay when making an admission decision. Because international financial aid resources are limited, admission is extremely competitive for students who require near-full funding.

2. 100% of demonstrated need met if admitted: Once Lafayette admits an international student who applied for aid on time, the college commits to meeting 100% of that student's demonstrated financial need based on the CSS Profile across all four years of study (provided you maintain satisfactory academic progress and renew your CSS Profile annually).

3. Packages include grants, work-study, AND institutional loans: Unlike loan-free universities, a Lafayette need-based financial aid package typically combines institutional grant/scholarship gift aid, an on-campus student employment allotment, and an institutional student loan component.

4. Automatic Merit Scholarship Consideration (Marquis & Cur Non Scholarships): All international first-year applicants are automatically considered for Lafayette's merit awards (such as the prestigious Marquis Fellowship/Scholarship and Cur Non Scholarship)—no separate merit scholarship application or financial aid form is required for merit consideration. (Note: if you also qualify for need-based aid, merit scholarships are incorporated into your overall need-based package.)

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

To put Lafayette's costs into perspective, the published 2026–2027 direct baseline charges are approximately $70,486 for tuition, $13,474 for on-campus housing, and $8,320 for meals (exceeding $92,000 per year before books, fees, health insurance, and personal expenses).

Included in Lafayette need-based financial aid packages

  • Institutional Grants & Merit Scholarships: Gift aid awarded by Lafayette that does not need to be repaid, covering the primary portion of tuition, housing, and dining costs.
  • Campus Student Employment (Work-Study): Part-time on-campus job opportunities during the academic year to help cover books, supplies, and incidental personal expenses.
  • Institutional Student Loans: Lafayette offers institutional student loans as part of its international financial aid packages to help bridge remaining calculated need.

Expenses explicitly NOT covered by standard aid

  • Summer and Interim Break Expenses: Lafayette explicitly states that meeting 100% of demonstrated need does not cover summer living costs or winter/interim break expenses—those costs remain the responsibility of the student and family.
  • Expected Family Contribution & Pre-Arrival Costs: Even with a strong financial aid offer, your family is responsible for any assessed family contribution, as well as passport fees, US F-1 visa fees, SEVIS I-901 fees, embassy travel, and initial arrival/flight costs unless specifically included in your award letter.

Important Notice on Loans and Enrollment Deposit ($750)

1. Review loan terms carefully: Because Lafayette's need-based packages can include an institutional student loan, carefully inspect the exact grant-to-loan ratio in your financial aid offer before committing.

2. Enrollment deposit: Accepted students who choose to enrol at Lafayette must submit an electronic enrolment form and a $750 nonrefundable enrolment deposit by May 1 (Regular Decision) or March 1 (Early Decision II). If you receive a full or near-full financial aid package and cannot afford the $750 deposit upfront, contact Lafayette's Admissions and Financial Aid offices immediately upon admission to ask about a deposit deferral or waiver.

  • 2. Contextualising displacement & schooling challenges: Lafayette conducts a holistic admissions review that considers your educational environment, personal responsibilities, and community involvement. Use the Common App Additional Information section—and ask your school counsellor or teacher recommender to highlight—any interrupted education, camp or host-country school constraints, or displacement circumstances.
  • 3. $65 Application Fee Waiver: If paying the $65 USD application fee causes financial hardship, select the appropriate fee waiver dropdown response directly on your Common Application or Coalition Application (supported by your school counsellor).

Noncustodial Parent CSS Profile (and Waiver Option): Lafayette requires any noncustodial parent (if parents are divorced, separated, or never married) to submit a separate CSS Profile for Noncustodial Parents. Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for undergraduate admission and international financial aid at Lafayette College for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must meet the following criteria:

  • Secondary School Completion & Academic Readiness: Must be completing or have completed secondary school (e.g., KCSE in Kenya or equivalent national/international secondary qualifications) and applying for a first bachelor's degree. (International transfer students who have enrolled in a degree-seeking university programme are also eligible to apply for competitive need-based and merit aid under separate transfer deadlines.)
  • Citizenship: Open to international applicants of all nationalities worldwide. Non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents apply through the international financial aid process.
  • English Language Proficiency: Required unless you qualify for an approved waiver (3+ years of English-medium academic instruction or native English proficiency). Typical competitive benchmarks: TOEFL iBT 100 (new TOEFL scale: 5), IELTS Academic 7.0, or Duolingo English Test 130.
  • Timely Financial Aid Filing: Must indicate intent to apply for need-based financial aid on the admission application and submit the 2027–28 CSS Profile (Code: 2361) and IDOC documents by the exact admission deadline.

Academic Programmes and Engineering / STEM Pathways

Lafayette College offers 36+ undergraduate degree programmes across four academic divisions, awarding both Bachelor of Arts (AB) and Bachelor of Science (BS) degrees:

  • Accredited 4-Year Engineering (BS) Programmes: Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, plus Integrative Engineering and Engineering Studies
  • Computing & Quantitative Sciences: Computer Science (AB or BS), Mathematics (AB or BS), Mathematics–Economics, Data Science (minor/interdisciplinary)
  • Natural & Life Sciences: Biology, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Physics, Neuroscience, Environmental Science and Environmental Studies, Geology
  • Social Sciences & Humanities: Economics, International Affairs, Government & Law, Psychology, Philosophy, Film & Media Studies, Art & Architecture

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Academic & Admissions Documents (Due 15 January 2027)

  • Common Application or Coalition Application via Scoir: Includes your personal essay and Lafayette's supplemental short-answer essay question.
  • $65 USD Application Fee or Approved Fee Waiver: Selected directly on your Common App or Coalition Application.
  • Official Secondary School Transcript & School Report: Complete high school academic records (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts and certified KCSE certificate/result slip) uploaded by your school counsellor/principal.
  • Mid-Year / First-Trimester Grades: Submitted by your school counsellor as soon as updated grades become available.
  • Two Recommendation Letters: One recommendation from your guidance counsellor/principal and at least one recommendation from an academic teacher.
  • English Proficiency Test Score Report (Unless waived): Official TOEFL (Code: 2361), IELTS, or Duolingo English Test score report (minimums: TOEFL 100 / 5, IELTS 7.0, Duolingo 130).
  • SAT or ACT Scores (Optional): Lafayette is strictly test-optional for Fall 2027 and Fall 2028 entry; submitting SAT/ACT scores is not required.

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Documents (Due 15 January 2027)

  • Supporting Income / Non-Tax Documents via College Board IDOC: Tax returns, employer wage statements, or a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement and household financial explanation uploaded through College Board's Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC).

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  4. Invite your school counsellor and academic teacher early. Ensure your counsellor and at least one teacher upload your recommendation letters, school report, secondary transcripts, and KCSE/national exam certificates before 15 January 2027.
  5. Confirm your English proficiency waiver or send official scores. If you attended an English-medium secondary school for at least three years, email admissions@lafayette.edu to confirm your waiver; otherwise send official TOEFL (Code: 2361), IELTS, or Duolingo scores.
  6. Submit your Regular Decision application by 15 January 2027. Submit several days ahead of the deadline to activate your Lafayette Applicant Portal.
  7. Complete the 2027–28 CSS Profile (Code: 2361) and IDOC uploads by 15 January 2027. Submit your CSS Profile via College Board (plus any noncustodial parent profile or waiver request) and upload supporting income or Non-Tax Filer statements via IDOC.
  8. Monitor your Lafayette Applicant Portal and IDOC checklists regularly. Confirm that both admissions and financial aid items are marked complete, and watch for virtual interview opportunities.

United States Need-Blind Undergraduate Admissions & 100% Grant-Based Financial Aid

Princeton University International Student Financial Aid

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | Fall 2027 Entry

What this opportunity is: Need-blind undergraduate admission paired with one of the most generous need-based financial aid programmes in the world—meeting 100% of Princeton-calculated demonstrated financial need through grants and modest campus employment, with zero student loans and using Princeton's own free financial aid form (PFAA) rather than the paid CSS Profile.

Host institution: Princeton University

Destination: Princeton, New Jersey, United States of America

Application platform: Common Application ($75 application fee, or approved fee waiver)

Study level: First-year undergraduate / Bachelor's degree (Bachelor of Arts [AB] or Bachelor of Science in Engineering [BSE], 4-year programme; international transfer students are also evaluated under the need-blind, full-need policy)

Target applicants: International applicants (non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents) from any country, including refugee, displaced, and low-income students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement and financial need.

Funding policy: Need-blind admission for all domestic and international applicants; meets 100% of Princeton-calculated demonstrated financial need through grant aid and modest campus work-study—with no student loans and no merit or athletic scholarships.

Regular Decision deadlines (Fall 2027 Entry): Admission Application: 1 January 2027 | Optional Arts Supplement: 8 January 2027 | Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA) & Supporting Documents: 1 February 2027.

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

About Princeton University and Its International Financial Aid

Princeton University is a world-renowned Ivy League research university in Princeton, New Jersey. It was the first university in the United States to replace student loans with grants in its financial aid packages, and it treats international and domestic applicants identically in both admissions and financial aid.

Before adding Princeton to your Common App list, understand four defining features of its admissions and financial aid system:

1. Truly need-blind international admission: Princeton does not limit its financial aid budget for international students and evaluates your application without considering your family's ability to pay. Requesting full financial assistance does not reduce your chances of admission, though overall international admission is extraordinarily selective (around 2%).

2. 100% of demonstrated need met — with ZERO student loans: If admitted, Princeton covers the entire difference between its Cost of Attendance and your calculated family contribution through Princeton Grants (which never have to be repaid) and a modest campus job. Students from low-income families typically qualify for packages that cover full tuition, housing, meals, books, and personal expenses with zero expected parental contribution.

3. NO CSS Profile or IDOC required — Princeton uses its own FREE form: Unlike almost every other Ivy League and selective US university, Princeton does not use the CSS Profile or College Board IDOC. Instead, after you submit your Common App, you complete the free Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA) directly through your Princeton Applicant Portal.

4. Purely need-based (no merit or athletic scholarships): Princeton does not award academic merit scholarships or athletic scholarships. All institutional funding is distributed strictly according to demonstrated financial need.

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in Princeton financial aid packages

  • Princeton University Grants: Direct institutional gift aid covering tuition, mandatory fees, residential college housing, and dining plans—and for high-need students, allowances for books, personal expenses, mandatory health insurance, and international travel. Grants never have to be repaid.
  • Campus Student Employment: Most financial aid packages include a modest on-campus job expectation (typically 8–10 hours per week) during the academic year to earn spending money.
  • Zero Student Loans: Princeton never requires students to borrow loans to meet their calculated financial need.

Expenses and conditions to verify independently

  • Parental Contribution Assessment: Princeton determines how much your family can contribute based on its review of your PFAA and supporting financial records. Families with very low income and minimal assets are typically assessed a $0 parental contribution.
  • Pre-Arrival & Immigration Costs: While Princeton offers generous support for admitted low-income students, verify directly with Princeton's Undergraduate Financial Aid Office how passport fees, US F-1 visa fees, SEVIS I-901 fees, and initial arrival flights are reimbursed or covered.

Important Rule: Submit Your Common App BEFORE Accessing the PFAA

You cannot fill out the Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA) until after you submit your Common Application and activate your Princeton Applicant Portal. Submit your Regular Decision Common App on or before 1 January 2027 so you have plenty of time to complete the PFAA and upload supporting financial PDFs before the 1 February 2027 financial aid deadline.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya (such as in Kakuma or Dadaab camps or urban centres) or other host countries are eligible to apply to Princeton University under its need-blind, full-need international admissions policy. Keep these essential details in mind:

  • 1. Citizenship selection on Common App: If you are a refugee living in Kenya and hold citizenship from another country (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia), select your country of legal citizenship under the non-US citizen option on Common App. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," which applies only to individuals holding US domestic immigration status.
  • 2. Zero Financial Aid Form Cost (No CSS Profile Needed): Because Princeton uses its own free PFAA and does not accept the CSS Profile, refugee and low-income applicants do not need to pay College Board fees or hunt for CSS Profile fee waiver codes.
  • 3. $75 Application Fee Waiver: If paying Princeton's $75 application fee is a financial hardship, request a Common App Fee Waiver inside your Common App Profile (or select the Princeton-specific fee waiver option inside Princeton's Common App questions).
  • 4. Documenting zero income, informal work, or missing tax returns: If your parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal livelihoods without government tax returns, do not invent income figures. Enter accurate household figures on the PFAA, and upload a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement along with UNHCR/government refugee attestation or a signed household income explanation in .pdf format directly into your PFAA portal (combine multiple PDFs into one file where needed).
  • 5. Noncustodial Parent Form or Waiver Request: If your biological or adoptive parents are divorced, separated, or unmarried and living in separate households, Princeton requires a Non-custodial Parent Form. If you have lost contact with a parent due to conflict, displacement, or abandonment, submit Princeton's Non-custodial Parent Waiver Request Form (available in the Princeton Financial Aid Form Library) supported by documentation from a counsellor, UNHCR officer, or community leader.
  • 6. Contextualising displacement & schooling challenges: Use the Common App Additional Information section—and ask your school counsellor or teacher recommenders to note in their letters—any interrupted schooling, camp/host-country school conditions, limited access to laboratories, or family displacement circumstances so admissions officers evaluate your achievements in full context.
  • 7. Graded Written Paper Requirement (Must Be in English): Princeton requires every applicant to submit a Graded Written Paper from an academic course (preferably English, history, or social studies) completed during the last three years of secondary school. Princeton explicitly states that the paper and teacher comments must have been originally written in English and cannot be translated from another language.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for undergraduate admission and financial aid at Princeton University for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must satisfy the following requirements:

  • Secondary School Completion & Academic Preparation: Must be completing or have completed secondary school (e.g., KCSE in Kenya or equivalent national/international secondary qualifications) and applying for a first bachelor's degree. Princeton expects strong preparation across core academic subjects (4 years of English, 4 years of mathematics including calculus for engineering applicants, 4 years of one foreign language, at least 2 years of laboratory science including physics and chemistry for engineering applicants, and at least 2 years of history).
  • Citizenship: Open to international applicants of all nationalities worldwide. Non-US citizens and non-US permanent residents are evaluated under the exact same need-blind, full-need policy as US students.
  • English Language Proficiency: Applicants whose native language is not English and who have spent fewer than three years at a secondary school where English is the primary language of instruction must submit official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, or PTE Academic scores. (Students who attended an English-medium secondary school for at least three years, such as in Kenya, are exempt from English proficiency testing.)
  • Timely PFAA Filing: Must indicate intent to apply for financial aid on Common App and complete the 2027–28 Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA) by 1 February 2027.

Academic Programmes and Degrees

Princeton offers 37 academic concentrations (majors) and over 55 interdisciplinary minors across two undergraduate degree tracks:

  • Bachelor of Science in Engineering (BSE): Computer Science (BSE track), Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Chemical and Biological Engineering, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Operations Research and Financial Engineering (ORFE)
  • Bachelor of Arts (AB): Computer Science (AB track), Mathematics, Applied and Computational Mathematics, Physics, Astrophysical Sciences, Chemistry, Molecular Biology, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Economics, Public and International Affairs (Princeton School of Public and International Affairs), Politics, History, Philosophy, Architecture

Note: When applying to Princeton, you indicate whether you intend to pursue the AB or BSE degree, and you do not formally declare your major until the end of your first year (for BSE) or second year (for AB).

  • Regular Decision Admission Application Deadline: 1 January 2027 (via Common App)
  • Optional Arts Supplement Deadline: 8 January 2027
  • Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA) & Supporting Documents Deadline: 1 February 2027
  • Regular Decision Notification Date: Late March 2027
  • Admitted Student Reply Date: 1 May 2027

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Academic & Admissions Documents (Due 1 January 2027)

  • Common Application & Princeton Writing Supplement: Includes your main personal essay plus Princeton's short-answer and supplemental essay prompts.
  • $75 Application Fee or Approved Fee Waiver: Requested inside Common App.
  • Graded Written Paper (Mandatory): A 1–2 page (or longer) graded essay/paper from an academic course (preferably English, history, or social studies) written in English during your last three years of secondary school, showing your teacher's grade and comments.
  • Official Secondary School Transcript & School Report: Complete secondary school records (e.g., Form 1–4 transcripts and certified KCSE certificate/result slip) uploaded by your school counsellor or principal via Common App. (If your school does not calculate a GPA, Princeton does not expect you to convert or invent one.)
  • Mid-Year Report (If applicable): Submitted by your school official if new internal or predicted final-year grades are issued (not needed if you have already graduated).
  • Two Academic Teacher Recommendations: Recommendations from two teachers in different core academic subjects (e.g., one Humanities/Social Science teacher and one Math/Science teacher) who taught you in higher-level courses.
  • English Proficiency Test Scores (Only if not exempt): Official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, or PTE Academic scores if you have attended an English-medium secondary school for fewer than three years.
  • SAT or ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2027 Entry): Not required for the 2026–2027 cycle.

2. Mandatory Financial Aid Documents (Due 1 February 2027)

  • 2027–2028 Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA): Completed online for free using your Princeton Applicant Portal credentials after submitting Common App. (International students do not file the FAFSA, CSS Profile, or IDOC.)
  • 2025 Parent Income / Tax Documentation (in .PDF format): Signed copies of 2025 tax returns and wage statements, or a signed Non-Tax Filer Statement alongside UNHCR/refugee attestation or household livelihood explanations uploaded directly in the PFAA portal.
  • Non-custodial Parent Form or Waiver Request (If applicable): Required if your parents are divorced, separated, or unmarried and living in separate households.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Add Princeton University to your Common App list. Verify it fits within your 20-college Common App limit and choose your intended degree track (AB or BSE).
  2. Indicate your intent to apply for financial aid and request a fee waiver. Select "Yes" to applying for need-based financial aid in Princeton's member questions, and activate your Common App Fee Waiver if paying $75 is a financial hardship.
  3. Prepare your Graded Written Paper and Princeton supplemental essays. Select a strong graded paper written in English with visible teacher comments/grade, and craft thoughtful essays for Princeton's writing supplement.
  4. Invite your school official and two core academic teachers early. Assign your principal/counsellor and two teachers from different core subjects in Common App so they can upload your transcripts, KCSE results, School Report, and teacher recommendations before 1 January 2027.
  5. Submit your Regular Decision Common App by 1 January 2027. Submit early to receive your Princeton Applicant Portal login details.
  6. Log into your Princeton Applicant Portal and complete the free 2027–28 PFAA by 1 February 2027. Use the account credentials created for your admissions application to fill out the PFAA online.
  7. Upload your supporting 2025 income or Non-Tax Filer PDFs in the PFAA portal by 1 February 2027. Combine multi-page PDF documents into a single file where appropriate and submit any Non-custodial Parent Form or Waiver Request before the deadline.
  8. Monitor your Princeton Applicant Portal regularly. Confirm that every admission and financial aid item is marked received, and respond promptly to any follow-up verification requests.

About NYU Abu Dhabi and Its International Financial Aid

New York University Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) is a highly selective liberal arts and research campus located in Abu Dhabi, UAE, operated in partnership with New York University. It is renowned for its global student body representing over 120 countries and its extensive institutional financial support for international undergraduates.

Before adding NYU Abu Dhabi to your Common App list, make sure you understand four key operational features of its admissions and aid system:

1. Need-aware international admission: NYUAD is need-aware when evaluating international undergraduate applicants. Your family's financial circumstances and the amount of aid requested are considered during the admissions review. Because financial aid resources are finite, admission is extremely competitive for students requiring near-full funding.

2. Comprehensive Cost of Attendance coverage: The estimated annual Cost of Attendance at NYUAD is approximately $90,434 per year (including direct charges of ~$84,520 for tuition [$68,574], housing, meals, health insurance, and books/supplies, plus indirect estimated expenses for personal items and annual travel). Admitted students who qualify for financial aid receive need-based grants deducted directly from these billed expenses.

3. Four-year aid renewal consistency: Institutional financial aid awarded at admission is generally renewed at the exact same level for all four years, provided you maintain satisfactory academic progress and meet university renewal requirements. NYUAD does not reassess financial need upward later.

4. Integrated portal tracking (STARS & Applicant Profile): Applying to NYUAD requires more than just the Common App; you must complete the supplemental STARS academic record self-reporting form and the NYUAD Applicant Profile inside your NYU Applicant Portal.

What Financial Aid Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in successful NYUAD financial aid packages

  • Need-Based Institutional Grants: Gift aid that does not need to be repaid, applied directly to offset direct university charges (tuition, housing, meal plan, health insurance, and books).
  • Travel & Personal Allowances (Where Awarded): Some award letters include travel support (such as estimated annual round-trip flights home) and personal support allocations disbursed each semester.

Expenses and conditions to verify independently

  • Expected Family Contribution (EFC): NYUAD calculates what your family can contribute based on your CSS Profile data. Even when financial aid is granted, your family remains responsible for any calculated family share.
  • External Scholarships Cap: Your combined total awards from NYUAD and external scholarships cannot exceed the total estimated annual Cost of Attendance (~$90,434). If you win external funding, NYUAD's institutional grant may be adjusted accordingly.

Critical Rule: Apply for Financial Aid During the Admission Cycle

NYUAD strictly requires international students to apply for financial aid during the initial application cycle. If you do not apply for institutional aid when submitting your admission application, you cannot request institutional aid later while enrolled at NYUAD.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced students living in Kenya (such as in Kakuma or Dadaab camps or urban centres) or other host countries are eligible to apply to NYU Abu Dhabi as international undergraduate applicants. Keep these essential points in mind:

  • 1. Citizenship selection on Common App: If you are a refugee residing in Kenya and hold citizenship from another country (such as South Sudan, Somalia, DRC, Burundi, or Ethiopia), select your country of legal citizenship under the non-US citizen option on Common App. Do not select "US Refugee/Asylee," which applies only to individuals holding US domestic immigration status.
  • 2. Contextualising displacement & schooling challenges: NYUAD evaluates applicants holistically within their regional, educational, and socioeconomic context. Use the Common App Additional Information section—and ask your school counsellor or teacher recommenders to highlight—any interrupted education, camp or host-school constraints, or family displacement circumstances.
  • 3. $85 Application Fee Waiver: If paying the $85 Common App fee causes financial hardship, select the fee waiver option in your Common App Profile (which your school counsellor approves online), or request a fee waiver inside your NYU Applicant Portal after submission.
  • 4. Requesting a CSS Profile Fee Payment Code: NYUAD requires the 2027–28 CSS Profile (NYU School Code: 2785) for all international financial aid applicants (covering both custodial and noncustodial parents). Because the CSS Profile fee can be a barrier, NYUAD provides limited CSS Profile Fee Payment Codes on a first-come, first-served basis. Crucial rule: You cannot request a fee code until after you submit your Common App and activate your NYU Applicant Portal (requests open starting October 1).
  • 5. Documenting zero income, informal livelihoods, or missing tax returns: If your parents or guardians are unemployed, displaced, or earn informal income without tax records, do not invent numbers. Report accurate figures on the CSS Profile and upload signed Non-Tax Filer Statements, UNHCR/government refugee attestation, or a signed household income explanation via College Board IDOC in English and US dollars ($).
  • 6. Noncustodial Parent Requirement (and Waiver Option): If your parents are divorced, separated, or never married, NYUAD requires a separate CSS Profile from the noncustodial parent by the deadline (10 January for ED II, 1 February for RD). If you have lost contact with a parent due to conflict, displacement, or abandonment, you may submit a CSS Profile Waiver Request for the Noncustodial Parent form along with supporting documentation to ncpwaiver@nyu.edu.
  • 7. UAE Student Visa & Mandatory Health Insurance: Admitted international students studying in Abu Dhabi require a UAE student entry visa and must be covered by health insurance that originates in the UAE. Mandatory health insurance is factored into billed direct costs and handled through NYUAD's student mobility and finance offices.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for undergraduate admission and need-based financial aid at NYU Abu Dhabi for Fall 2027 entry, applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • Secondary School Completion & Academic Readiness: Must be completing or have completed secondary school (e.g., KCSE in Kenya or equivalent national/international secondary credentials) and applying for a first undergraduate degree.
  • Citizenship: Open to international applicants of all nationalities worldwide (non-Emirati citizens).
  • English Language Proficiency: Required if English is not your native language and you have not studied for at least three consecutive years exclusively in an English-medium secondary school. Accepted tests include TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, or the Duolingo English Test.
  • Timely Financial Aid Filing: Must submit the 2027–28 CSS Profile (NYU School Code: 2785) for both custodial and noncustodial parents by the matching round deadline.

Academic Programmes and Divisions

NYU Abu Dhabi offers undergraduate majors across four academic divisions leading to a Bachelor of Arts (BA) or Bachelor of Science (BS) degree:

  • Arts and Humanities: Literature and Creative Writing, History, Art and Art History, Music, Philosophy, Theater
  • Science: Computer Science, Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, General Engineering
  • Social Science: Economics, Political Science, Social Research and Public Policy, Psychology
  • Engineering: Civil Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, General Engineering, Mechanical Engineering

  • Noncustodial Parent Waiver Request (If applicable): Submitted to ncpwaiver@nyu.edu by the same deadline if you cannot obtain noncustodial parent financial records.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Add NYU Abu Dhabi to your Common App list. Select New York University and choose the Abu Dhabi campus as your preferred location, ensuring it fits within your 20-college limit.
  2. Request an application fee waiver and indicate financial aid interest. Indicate financial need on your application to waive the $85 Common App fee, and confirm you are applying for institutional financial aid.
  3. Submit your Common App by the deadline (1 January for ED II, 5 January 2027 for RD). Submit early to receive your NYU Applicant Portal login credentials.
  4. Complete STARS and the NYUAD Applicant Profile in your NYU portal. Log into your portal to self-report your grades in STARS and complete all campus-specific profile questions.
  5. Request a CSS Profile Fee Payment Code (if needed). If paying the CSS Profile fee is a hardship, submit the NYUAD CSS Profile Fee Payment Code Request Form through your portal as early as possible (codes are limited).
  6. Submit the 2027–28 CSS Profile (School Code: 2785) by the aid deadline (10 Jan for ED II, 1 Feb 2027 for RD). Ensure both custodial and noncustodial parents complete their respective CSS Profile applications online via College Board.
  7. Upload supporting financial documents via IDOC. Submit all requested parent tax returns, income statements, or Non-Tax Filer statements in English and US dollars through College Board IDOC.
  8. Monitor your NYU Applicant Portal regularly. Verify that all admission and financial aid checklist items show as received before decision release.
