Kenya-Based Fully Funded Undergraduate Scholarship for Young Africans

USIU-Africa Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | Nairobi, Kenya

What this opportunity is: A full-cost undergraduate scholarship for academically talented young Africans who face financial, displacement, gender or disability barriers. It is funded through the partnership between the Mastercard Foundation and United States International University–Africa (USIU-Africa), and it combines tuition and living support with leadership training, entrepreneurial training, psychosocial support, career counselling and mentorship.

Host institution: United States International University–Africa (USIU-Africa)

Funder: Mastercard Foundation (Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program)

Destination: Nairobi, Kenya

Programme running since: July 2020. USIU-Africa reports that it is educating over 1,000 students through the programme.

Application method: Scholarship application form for the specific call, sent by email as PDF files, delivered to the Scholars Program Office, or posted. The official programme page does not describe an online application portal.

Application fee: None. Applying is free.

Study level: First-time undergraduate degree (Bachelor's) in one of the 13 approved programmes

Target applicants: Young Africans facing socioeconomic barriers, including young women, young men, refugee and displaced youth, and youth with disabilities. Each call states which group it is focusing on.

Age limit: 29 years at the time of application. The limit is 32 years for refugee and displaced youth and for youth with disabilities.

Funding policy: Full-cost scholarship covering tuition and functional fees, laptop, books and learning materials, accommodation, meals, medical insurance, stipend and transport to and from home, plus leadership and entrepreneurial training and psychosocial support.

Intakes and calls: Two intakes per year, May (Summer) and September (Fall). USIU-Africa says calls are usually released around October/November for the May intake and February/March for the September intake.

Current status (14 November 2026): USIU-Africa's official programme page states that there is no open call for applications at the moment.

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

About the USIU-Africa Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

USIU-Africa has partnered with the Mastercard Foundation in the Scholars Program since July 2020. The programme aims to prepare young people to become ethical, community-focused leaders who contribute to change across Africa. By the end of their studies, scholars are expected to lead change in their communities, using internationally recognised and locally applicable qualifications.

USIU-Africa is a private university in Nairobi that serves students from more than 70 nationalities. It reports that, since the partnership began, it has supported more than 5,000 students through the various initiatives under the programme. Before you plan your application, make sure you understand five key features of how this scholarship works:

1. Applications open only when a call is advertised: The programme runs a specific call for each intake. At the time of this research, no call was open. Applications sent outside a call, to a different email address, or on an old form are not valid, so you should wait for the next announcement and prepare your documents in advance.

2. Selection happens before formal university admission: According to the official selection process, scholars are chosen through the programme's own application, shortlisting and interview stages. Selected scholars are then guided through the formal USIU-Africa admission process. You must still meet the university's entry requirements for your chosen programme.

3. Only 13 degree programmes are covered: The scholarship is valid only for the programmes sponsored by the Mastercard Foundation at USIU-Africa. Applications for any other programme, including engineering, are disqualified.

4. Open to Africans from across the continent: You do not have to be Kenyan. The scholarship is open to applicants from across Africa who meet the eligibility criteria, and it is not open to non-African nationalities.

5. Support goes beyond fees: Scholars receive living support and a stipend, and are also offered leadership training, entrepreneurial training, psychosocial support, career counselling and mentorship. In return, the programme expects scholars to give back to their communities and lead positive change after graduation.

What the Scholarship Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in the scholars' support package

  • Tuition and functional fees: Your degree fees at USIU-Africa.
  • Laptop, books and other learning materials: Resources you need for your coursework.
  • Reasonable accommodation and meals: Living costs while you study.
  • Medical insurance: Health cover while you are a scholar.
  • Stipend: A living allowance described as reasonable for a comfortable stay on campus.
  • Transport to and from home: Travel support between your home and the university.
  • Leadership training and entrepreneurial training: Skills development alongside your degree.
  • Psychosocial support, career counselling and mentorship: Support for your wellbeing and your transition to work or further study.
  • Disability support: Disability needs are reasonably catered for.

Additional opportunities for enrolled scholars

  • Scholars Entrepreneurship Fund (SEF 2.0): For the 2025–2026 round, USIU-Africa advertised grants of up to US$5,000 for business-related expenses to eligible Mastercard Foundation Scholars. This is a separate application for enrolled scholars who meet specific conditions, such as having completed entrepreneurial training, and it is not guaranteed as part of the scholarship. Do not count on it when planning your finances.

Limits and conditions to verify independently

  • Stipend amount: No figure is published, so ask the Scholars Program Office or check your award letter.
  • Only valid at USIU-Africa: You cannot take this scholarship to another university. The Mastercard Foundation has other partner universities around the world, each with its own separate application process.
  • Undergraduate only: The scholarship does not cover Master's or other postgraduate studies.
  • No credit transfer: You cannot transfer into the scholarship if you are already a scholar at another university or at USIU-Africa.
  • Application costs are yours: Applicants pay their own application-related costs, including printing and transport to interviews.
  • Duration and renewal: Confirm the exact length of support and any academic renewal conditions in your award letter.

Critical Rule: Use Only the Form and Email Address in the Current Call

USIU-Africa disqualifies applications that use a form from a different cycle, are sent to an email address other than the one in the call, arrive after the deadline, are incomplete, or are sent in a format the recruitment team cannot open (such as password-protected files). Earlier calls also asked applicants to send only one complete application, since duplicates can be rejected.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

Refugee and displaced youth, including those living in Kakuma, Dadaab or urban areas in Kenya, are one of the programme's named target groups. Keep these essential points in mind:

  • 1. Higher age limit: The general age limit is 29, but for refugee and displaced youth it is 32 years at the time of application.
  • 2. You must be an African national: The scholarship is open to African nationalities. Africans who studied in countries other than their own, including outside Africa, can still apply if they meet the criteria.
  • 3. Include your refugee identity document: Earlier calls asked refugee applicants to include a copy of their refugee identity document, alongside the other required papers. Check the current call for the exact list.
  • 4. Priority and targeting can change by call: Some earlier calls gave priority to registered refugees and displaced youth and to persons with disabilities, and UNHCR offices in Kenya and in other host countries such as Rwanda have shared past calls on their help sites. Each call states its target group, so read it carefully.
  • 5. Other education systems are accepted: You do not need to have sat KCSE. Applicants who followed other curricula can apply if they meet the other minimum criteria and are vetted in the same way as everyone else. International applicants must meet the equivalent of the Kenyan entry grade.
  • 6. Your final certificate is required: You must already hold your final secondary school certificate or result slip to apply. If you have not finished secondary school yet, wait for the next cycle after you receive it. If you lost your documents because of displacement, contact your school or examination body, and the Scholars Program team, as early as possible.
  • 7. Explain interrupted education honestly: Describe any gaps, school changes, camp or host-community school conditions and family displacement truthfully, in your own words, in your application letter. Do not invent or exaggerate details.
  • 8. Plan for the costs of applying: Applicants pay for their own printing and transport to interviews. If you live far from Nairobi, contact the programme early to ask how interviews will be held for your cycle, since some interviews have been held virtually.
  • 9. Submit digitally if you can: Applications can be emailed as PDF files, so a clear phone scan can save printing and posting costs. Make sure every page is readable and the files open without a password.
  • 10. Check your phone and email: Shortlisted applicants are contacted by phone and email. Use a phone number and email address you can reliably access, because applicants who hear nothing by the dates in the call should treat their application as unsuccessful.
  • 11. No fees, no agents: Applying is free. Nobody can sell you a place, speed up your application or guarantee selection.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for the USIU-Africa Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, applicants must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Facing Socioeconomic Barriers: Financial, displacement, gender or disability constraints that would make university study difficult without support.
  • Academic Talent: You must value learning and be motivated to complete your education. The official minimum is the university entry grade of C+ or above, or its equivalent, as set by the Kenya Commission for University Education. International applicants must meet the equivalent.
  • Extra Requirement for Pharmacy and Health Sciences: Applicants for the School of Pharmacy and Health Sciences need a higher mean grade (stated on the official page as 8- or equivalent) and at least C+ (8-) in the cluster subjects English, Mathematics, Biology and Chemistry. Confirm the exact grade in the current call.
  • Leadership Potential: A commitment to becoming a change maker, role model and mentor who practises ethical and transformative leadership.
  • Commitment to Giving Back: Evidence of past or current involvement in community outreach or activities that improve your community.
  • Age: 29 years or younger at the time of application, or 32 years or younger for refugee and displaced youth and for youth with disabilities.
  • First-Time Undergraduate Applicant: You must be seeking your first undergraduate degree. The programme is intended for applicants who have not previously had the opportunity to join a tertiary institution, so holders of a diploma are not eligible.
  • Previous University Study: If you dropped out of another university, the recruitment panel reviews your case individually to decide whether your reason fits the criteria.
  • Completed Secondary Education: Your final secondary school certificate or result slip must be attached. You cannot apply while still waiting to finish secondary school.
  • African Nationality: Open to applicants from across Africa. Non-African nationalities are not eligible.
  • Interest in an Approved Programme: You must apply for one of the 13 sponsored programmes and meet USIU-Africa's admission requirements for it.
  • Target Group Named in the Call: Each call says which group it focuses on (for example, young women, young men, refugee and displaced youth, or youth with disabilities). Make sure you fit the group for your cycle.

Is this scholarship right for you?

It is likely a good fit if you have finished secondary school, meet the entry grade, have not studied at a tertiary institution before, face real financial or displacement barriers, can show community involvement, and are interested in one of the 13 sponsored programmes.

It is not the right route if you already hold a diploma or degree, want to study engineering or another programme outside the list, want to study outside USIU-Africa, or are applying for postgraduate study. Other Mastercard Foundation partner universities run their own separate programmes.

Approved Academic Programmes

The scholarship covers the following 13 undergraduate degree programmes at USIU-Africa. Programmes outside this list are not covered, and applications for them are disqualified.

  • School of Science and Technology (SST): Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Technology, Information Systems and Technology, Data Science and Analytics, Software Engineering
  • School of Pharmacy and Health Sciences (SPHS): Bachelor of Pharmacy, Bachelor of Science in Epidemiology and Biostatistics
  • School of Communication, Cinematic and Creative Arts (SCCCA): Bachelor of Arts in Animation, Bachelor of Arts in Film Production and Directing
  • Chandaria School of Business Administration (CSOB): Bachelor of Science in Finance, International Business Administration, Accounting
  • School of Humanities and Social Sciences (SHSS): Bachelor of Arts in International Relations, Bachelor of Arts in Psychology

Note on engineering: Engineering is not on the approved list. USIU-Africa states that applications for programmes not offered under the scholarship are disqualified.

Application Timeline and Current Status

There are two intakes each year, and a separate call is published for each one. As of 14 November 2026, USIU-Africa's official page says no call is currently open.

  • May (Summer) intake:
    Call usually released around October/November.
  • September (Fall) intake:
    Call usually released around February/March.

USIU-Africa also says calls are advertised at least six months before the semester of intake. Exact opening and closing dates are set in each call and are strictly enforced. Calls are posted on the USIU-Africa website and its social media pages.

Portico Deadline Alert:

1. No call is open right now. Do not send an application until USIU-Africa publishes a call. Some websites repeat old or unofficial deadlines, so rely only on the official USIU-Africa pages.

2. Prepare early. Collect your certificates, identity documents and recommendation letter now, and start drafting your application letter, so that you can submit well before the deadline once the call opens.

3. Late applications are not shortlisted. USIU-Africa lists submitting past the deadline as a reason for not being shortlisted.

4. Use the right call for the right intake. Make sure the form, email address and deadline you use belong to the same call.

Common Documents Needed to Apply

The exact list is published in each call, so always follow the call for your cycle. Based on recent calls, applicants have generally been asked for:

1. Core Application Documents

  • Completed scholarship application form: The form for the specific cycle you are applying to. Forms from other cycles are invalid. Forms are free, can be downloaded from the call, or collected in print from the USIU-Africa admissions office.
  • Application letter: About your personal background, why you chose USIU-Africa, and your goals after graduation.
  • Academic documents: Copies of your academic certificates and transcripts, including your final secondary school certificate or result slip.
  • Recommendation letter: A current letter from a teacher, counsellor, community leader or another person who knows you well. The programme has published guidelines for writing a good recommendation letter.
  • Passport-size photograph
  • Identification: A copy of your birth certificate, national ID or passport.

2. Additional Documents (Where Applicable)

  • Refugee identity document: A copy of your refugee ID, where applicable.
  • Disability documentation: Supporting documents for applicants with disabilities, as the call requires.

3. Format Rules

  • Scan the application form and all documents in PDF format.
  • Do not password-protect any file.
  • Make sure every scan is clear and readable.
  • Name your email subject with your name and nationality.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Watch for the next call for applications. Check the USIU-Africa Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program page and the university's social media pages regularly. UNHCR offices have also shared past calls.
  2. Read the call carefully. Check the target group, age limit, approved programmes, deadline, required documents and the exact email address for that cycle.
  3. Get the right application form. Download the form posted with the call, or collect a printed copy at the USIU-Africa admissions office. Use only the form for that cycle.
  4. Fill in every section and gather your documents. Complete all required areas, write your application letter, and attach all required documents, including your final secondary certificate or result slip.
  5. Scan everything as PDF files. Make sure the files are clear and not password-protected.
  6. Send one complete application before the deadline. Email it to mcfsp-applications@usiu.ac.ke (unless the call gives a different address), with your name and nationality as the email subject. You can also deliver it to the Scholars Program Office (School of Graduate Studies, Research and Extension building, USIU-Africa) or post it to: Program Director, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, United States International University–Africa, P.O. Box 14634–00800, Nairobi, Kenya.
  7. Wait for communication on the dates in the call. USIU-Africa does not give individual feedback to every applicant. If you receive no communication by the dates in the call, treat your application as unsuccessful.
  8. Attend the interview if shortlisted. Shortlisted applicants are called and invited to a face-to-face or virtual interview. Prepare to speak about your background, leadership and community involvement.
  9. Receive your award letter and complete admission. Successful applicants are told by phone and sent a scholarship award letter, then guided through the formal USIU-Africa admission process.

Tips for a Strong Application

These tips follow the selection criteria USIU-Africa publishes. They are general guidance from Portico Kakuma, not official rules.

  • Show each criterion with real examples. The panel looks at socioeconomic barriers, academic talent, leadership potential and commitment to giving back. Give a specific example of each from your own life instead of general statements.
  • Describe your community involvement clearly. Mention what you did, who it helped, how long you did it and what changed. Small, consistent efforts count, such as tutoring younger students, volunteering, or helping organise a community activity.
  • Explain why you chose your programme and USIU-Africa. The application letter asks why you chose USIU-Africa and what you plan to do after graduating. Link your chosen programme to a problem you want to help solve in your community.
  • Choose a recommender who knows you well. A teacher, counsellor or community leader who can describe your character, effort and leadership is more useful than a famous name. Give them the programme's recommendation letter guidelines and enough time.
  • Write in your own words. Your letter should sound like you. Keep it honest and specific, and have a trusted teacher check spelling and clarity.
  • Check everything before you send. Confirm that the form is complete, every required document is attached, the files open, the email address is correct and your subject line has your name and nationality.

Preparing for the interview

  • Be ready to explain your personal background and the barriers you have faced.
  • Prepare examples of times you led, helped others or solved a problem.
  • Know your chosen programme and what you hope to do with it.
  • Answer honestly. The interview assesses character, leadership ability and personal circumstances.
  • If the interview is virtual, test your phone or computer, internet and a quiet place beforehand.

Selection Process

USIU-Africa describes a six-stage selection process:

  1. Application: You submit a comprehensive application covering your academic achievements, financial need, leadership qualities and community service.
  2. Review of applications: Applications are checked for eligibility, academic merit and fit with the programme's goals.
  3. Shortlisting: Applicants who meet the criteria are shortlisted based on how competitive they are and their demonstrated potential.
  4. Interviews: Shortlisted candidates are interviewed, in person or virtually.
  5. Selection: Final selection considers interview results, academic background, financial need and overall fit.
  6. University admission: Selected scholars are guided through formal admission to USIU-Africa.

Common reasons applicants are not shortlisted

  • Not meeting the minimum eligibility criteria (this leads to automatic disqualification)
  • An incomplete application form
  • Missing required documents
  • Submitting after the deadline
  • Sending the application to the wrong email address
  • Using an invalid form, meaning a form from a different cycle
  • Sending files that cannot be opened easily, such as password-protected files

If you are unsuccessful

Whether you can reapply depends on the reason. If you did not meet the minimum university entry qualifications, the situation does not change and a new application will not help. If the problem was a missed deadline or missing documents, you can correct the mistake and apply again in a later cycle.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the scholarship only for women?
No. It is also open to men. Each call states the target group it is focusing on, and young women are strongly encouraged to apply.

Can I apply if I am not Kenyan?
Yes, if you are an African national who meets the criteria. Non-African nationalities are not eligible.

Can I apply if I did not sit KCSE?
Yes. Applicants from other curricula can apply if they meet the other minimum criteria. They go through the same vetting process as everyone else.

Can I apply with a diploma?
No. The scholarship is for applicants who have not previously had the opportunity to join a tertiary institution.

Can I apply before I finish secondary school?
No. Your final secondary school certificate or result slip must be attached, so you must wait for the next cycle after you receive it.

I dropped out of another university. Can I apply?
The recruitment panel reviews each case individually to see whether your reason for dropping out fits the criteria.

Can I study engineering with this scholarship?
No. The scholarship is valid only for the 13 sponsored programmes.

Does the scholarship cover a Master's degree?
No. It is only for undergraduate programmes.

Can I use the scholarship at another university?
No. This scholarship is valid only at USIU-Africa. Other partner universities have their own independent processes, listed on the Mastercard Foundation website.

How much is the stipend?
USIU-Africa does not publish an amount. It says the stipend is reasonable for a comfortable stay on campus.

How will I know if I qualified?
Shortlisted applicants are called and invited for interviews. Successful applicants are informed and sent award letters, and unsuccessful interviewees are emailed. If you hear nothing by the dates in the call, consider your application unsuccessful.

Who pays the cost of applying and travelling to interviews?
The applicant pays application and recruitment costs, including printing and transport to interviews.

Fees and Fraud Prevention

Applying is free. Never pay anyone to apply for this scholarship.

USIU-Africa and the Mastercard Foundation do not charge fees to apply for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. The university warns the public to be vigilant and to report suspicious activity to local law enforcement.

Earlier calls also warned that canvassing, using agents or paying fees can lead to disqualification. Apply yourself, using only official channels.

Do not send your documents to unofficial email addresses or social media accounts. Use only the email address and postal address in the official call.

Report suspected fraud to USIU-Africa at mcfsp-enquiries@usiu.ac.ke or by phone on +254 730 116 218 / 500 / 581 / 148 / 552 / 536.

Kenya-Based Need-Based Scholarship for Business, Finance and Accounting Students

Tuendelee Foundation Scholarship

College / Undergraduate | Diploma, Bachelor's and Professional Courses | Study in Kenya

What this opportunity is: A need-based scholarship from the Tuendelee Foundation for bright students who cannot afford tertiary education in Kenya. It supports students who want to study accounting, finance, commerce or another business-related course at a reputable university or college. Awards are based on each student's assessed needs.

Organisation: Tuendelee Foundation, a not-for-profit organisation based in Hurlingham, Nairobi, Kenya. "Tuendelee" is a Swahili word for "Let's Progress".

Destination: Reputable universities and colleges in Kenya

Application platform: Online application on the Tuendelee Foundation portal (app.tuendelee.org). You register first, then complete the application form.

Study level: Tertiary education: college and university study, including professional certificate courses such as CPA and ACCA

Fields of study: Accounting, finance, commerce and business-related courses

Target applicants: Bright, underprivileged students who cannot meet the costs of tertiary education. The foundation's focus includes students from rural areas, urban slums, and arid and semi-arid areas.

Age limit: 18 to 30 years

Funding policy: May cover tuition, exam fees (for example CPA and ACCA), accommodation, an allowance for upkeep, or a combination of these, based on assessed needs. The award is not the same for every student.

Application period (2026 call): 23 October 2026 to 30 November 2026

Current status (14 November 2026): Open, with about two weeks left.

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

About the Tuendelee Foundation Scholarship

The Tuendelee Foundation is a not-for-profit organisation that supports students to complete quality tertiary education. It believes that education changes a person's life and their surrounding community. Alongside the scholarship, the foundation runs a mentorship programme and an internship and job placement programme, and it works toward the United Nations goal of inclusive and equitable quality education.

Before you apply, make sure you understand four key features of this scholarship:

1. It is focused on business, finance and accounting: The foundation asks applicants to be interested in accounting, finance, commerce or a business-related course. Students studying other subjects should not expect to qualify.

2. You must already have a place to study in Kenya: You need an admission letter, or you must already be enrolled, at a reputable university or college in Kenya. The scholarship does not help you find a place.

3. Awards depend on your assessed need: The foundation selects students and offers support based on assessed needs. Your award might cover tuition only, or tuition together with accommodation, upkeep or exam fees. Ask the foundation exactly what your offer includes.

4. One call each year, with interviews: The foundation opens applications once a year, interviews applicants and selects deserving students. Successful scholars may also benefit from mentorship and from internship and job placement support linked to the foundation.

What the Scholarship Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Support the foundation says it can provide

  • Tuition: Fees for your college or university course.
  • Exam fees: Fees for professional certificate exams, for example CPA and ACCA.
  • Accommodation: Housing support while you study.
  • Allowance for upkeep: Living support, which one scholar describes as a monthly stipend.
  • A combination of the above: Your award can be one of these items or several of them, depending on your assessed needs.
  • Mentorship and career support: The foundation runs a mentorship programme, and its sister consulting company supports foundation students with internship and job placements.

Limits and conditions to verify independently

  • The package is not fixed: The foundation does not publish a set amount. Ask exactly what is covered, how much, and for how many years.
  • Duration and renewal: The public pages do not explain how long support lasts or what is needed to keep it. Confirm this in writing if you are offered an award.
  • Other funding: If you already receive another scholarship, tell the foundation honestly and ask how it affects your award.
  • Kenya only: The scholarship is for study at reputable universities and colleges in Kenya.
  • Application costs: The public pages mention no application fee, but you will still need to pay for your own internet, phone and travel to any interview.

Critical Rule: Check That You Meet Every Basic Requirement First

You must be a Kenyan citizen or resident, aged 18 to 30, interested in a business-related course, and hold an admission letter or already be enrolled at a reputable institution in Kenya. If you miss any of these, do not spend your time on this application. Refugee applicants should confirm residence rules with the foundation before applying (see the next section).

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

The foundation's public pages do not mention refugees, so it is not clear whether refugee students qualify. The scholarship is open to Kenyan citizens or residents. Keep these essential points in mind:

  • 1. Confirm that you count as a "resident" before you apply: The foundation does not define the word "resident" on its public pages. Contact the foundation by email or phone and ask whether refugees and asylum seekers living in Kenya, with a valid refugee ID or proof of registration, are eligible. Keep their answer in writing.
  • 2. You need admission or enrolment first: You must have an admission letter or be enrolled in a reputable university or college in Kenya. If you are still waiting for a place, you cannot apply yet.
  • 3. Your course must be business-related: The scholarship is for accounting, finance, commerce and business-related courses.
  • 4. Age 18 to 30: Check your age against the limit before you start.
  • 5. Arid and rural backgrounds are part of the focus: The foundation says its focus includes students from rural areas, urban slums and arid and semi-arid areas. Describe your own background honestly, including where you grew up and the barriers to your education.
  • 6. Prepare identity and status documents: Keep clear copies of your refugee ID or registration papers, and any other identity documents you have, ready to upload in case the form asks for them.
  • 7. Plan for online access: The application is completed online, and you must register on the portal first. If your internet access is limited, plan where and when you will complete it, and avoid waiting until the final day. For technical problems, the 2024 application page listed a support phone number (see contacts below).
  • 8. Explain interrupted schooling honestly: Selection looks at your financial need, educational and career plans, interests and achievements. If displacement affected your schooling, explain it truthfully in your own words and do not exaggerate.
  • 9. Ask about interviews early: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed. Ask the foundation whether interviews are held in person or online, so that you can plan for travel or a good internet connection.
  • 10. No payments and no agents: Never pay anyone to apply, to improve your chances or to speed up your application.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for the Tuendelee Foundation Scholarship, applicants must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Kenyan Citizen or Resident: You must be a Kenyan citizen or a resident of Kenya. Refugee applicants should confirm with the foundation that their status counts.
  • Age: Between 18 and 30 years old.
  • Interest in a Business-Related Course: You must be interested in accounting, finance, commerce or a business-related course, including professional courses such as CPA and ACCA.
  • Admission or Enrolment in Kenya: You must hold an admission letter, or already be enrolled at a reputable university or college in Kenya.
  • Genuine Financial Need: You must be a bright student from a disadvantaged background who cannot afford tertiary education costs.
  • Thoughtful Educational and Career Plans: The foundation looks for clear, realistic plans for your studies and future career.
  • Interests, Achievements and Potential: Your achievements and your potential to reach your goals are part of the assessment.

Is this scholarship right for you?

It is likely a good fit if you already have a place at a Kenyan university or college, you are studying (or planning to study) a business, finance or accounting course, you are between 18 and 30, and you have real financial need.

It is not the right route if you are studying outside Kenya, your course is not business-related, you do not yet have admission, or you are outside the age range.

Courses and Study Areas

The foundation supports students pursuing business-related courses at reputable colleges and universities in Kenya, including:

  • Accounting: Degree and diploma courses, and professional certificates such as CPA and ACCA
  • Finance: Finance and related business programmes
  • Commerce: Commerce and business studies
  • Other business-related courses: Confirm with the foundation whether your specific course qualifies

Note: The foundation's public pages do not list approved institutions or courses. It only asks for a "reputable" university or college in Kenya, so confirm your institution and course with the foundation before applying.

Application Timeline and Current Status

The foundation runs one call each year. The 2026 application period runs from 23 October 2026 to 30 November 2026.

  • Application period opens: 23 October 2026
  • Application deadline: 30 November 2026 (in the 2024 round the deadline was 11:59 pm, so confirm the closing time on the portal)
  • Review and shortlisting: In the 2024 round, applications were reviewed and candidates shortlisted in December
  • Interviews: In the 2024 round, shortlisted applicants were interviewed in January
  • Award and onboarding: In the 2024 round, scholarships were awarded and successful candidates onboarded in February

The review, interview and award dates above are from the 2024 round and are given only as a guide. The foundation has not published a 2026 timetable on its public pages, so check the portal for current dates.

Portico Deadline Alert:

1. The deadline is 30 November 2026. Do not wait until the final day. Portals can be slow when many applicants submit at once.

2. Register now. You must register on the portal before you can reach the form. You can then browse all sections of the form to gather what you need before you submit.

3. Confirm your eligibility today. If you are a refugee or are unsure about the residence requirement, contact the foundation immediately, since replies can take time.

4. Confirm the dates on the portal. Always check the application portal for the exact opening and closing times before you rely on this page.

Common Documents Needed to Apply

The foundation does not publish a document list on its public pages. The application form asks for the required information and documents, and the portal lets you look through all sections before you submit. Based on the eligibility rules, it is sensible to have these items ready:

1. Documents to Prepare in Advance

  • Admission letter or proof of enrolment: From your university or college in Kenya.
  • Identification: National ID, or for refugee applicants your refugee ID or registration document, together with proof of your age.
  • Academic records: Your KCSE certificate or result slip, or equivalent secondary school results, and any college transcripts.
  • Evidence of financial need: Any documents that show your family's circumstances, for example letters from a school, community leader, or humanitarian organisation, if relevant.
  • Your education and career plans: Be ready to describe your chosen course, why you chose it and what you plan to do after graduating.
  • Evidence of achievements and activities: Certificates, awards, or leadership and volunteering roles, if you have them.

Important: This is a preparation list from Portico Kakuma, not the foundation's official list. Submit exactly what the application form asks for.

2. Contact Details

  • A working email address and phone number that you check often
  • An alternative contact, if the form allows one

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Read the eligibility rules carefully. Check that you meet the residence, age, course and admission requirements.
  2. Contact the foundation if you are unsure. Refugee applicants should ask by email or phone whether their status qualifies, and keep the reply.
  3. Open the application page. Go to the Scholarship Program page on the Tuendelee Foundation website and select "Apply for Scholarship", which takes you to the application portal.
  4. Register on the portal. Fill in your registration details. You are then taken to the application form.
  5. Browse all sections of the form. Look through every section first so that you know which information and documents you need to gather.
  6. Complete the form honestly and fully. Describe your financial need, education and career plans, interests and achievements clearly and truthfully, and upload the documents the form requests.
  7. Check and submit before 30 November 2026. Review everything, submit early, and keep any confirmation message or email.
  8. Get help if you have a technical problem. Use the foundation's contact details rather than waiting until the deadline passes.
  9. Wait for shortlisting and attend the interview. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed. Prepare to talk about your background, need, goals and achievements.
  10. Accept your award and complete onboarding. Successful candidates are awarded the scholarship and onboarded. Make sure you understand exactly what your award covers.

Tips for a Strong Application

These tips follow the selection factors the foundation publishes. They are general guidance from Portico Kakuma, not official rules.

  • Be specific about your financial need. Genuine financial need is the first factor the foundation lists. Explain your situation clearly and honestly, including who supports you and what you cannot afford.
  • Make your plans clear and connected. The foundation looks for thoughtful and coherent educational and career plans. Link your chosen course to the career you want and to how you will use it.
  • Show what you have done. Mention your achievements, interests and responsibilities, even small ones, such as helping with a family business, tutoring, or volunteering.
  • Show your potential. Give an example of a time when you worked hard, solved a problem or improved your results despite difficulty.
  • Write in your own words. Keep your answers honest and clear, and ask a teacher or mentor to check spelling and clarity.
  • Submit early. Early submission leaves time to fix problems with the portal or your documents.

Preparing for the interview

  • Be ready to explain your background and why you need support.
  • Know your course and be able to describe your career plans.
  • Prepare examples of your achievements and activities.
  • Answer honestly and clearly, and ask questions about the award if you are unsure.
  • If the interview is online, test your phone or computer, internet and a quiet place beforehand.

Selection Process

The foundation calls for applications once a year, interviews applicants and selects bright, talented and deserving students for support based on assessed needs. It considers:

  • Genuine financial need
  • Thoughtful and coherent educational and career plans
  • Your interests and achievements
  • Your potential to achieve your goals

In the 2024 round the stages were: application, review and shortlisting, interviews of shortlisted applicants, and then the award of scholarships and onboarding of successful candidates.

If you are unsuccessful

The foundation opens applications every year. The public pages do not say whether unsuccessful applicants can reapply, so ask the foundation. In the meantime, keep looking for other scholarships.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can apply?
Kenyan citizens or residents aged 18 to 30 who are interested in accounting, finance, commerce or a business-related course, and who hold an admission letter or are already enrolled at a reputable university or college in Kenya.

Can refugees apply?
The foundation's public pages do not say. The requirement is "Kenyan citizen or resident", so contact the foundation to confirm whether your refugee status qualifies before you apply.

Do I need to be admitted before I apply?
Yes. You need an admission letter, or you must already be enrolled.

Is it only for university students?
No. It supports tertiary education, which includes college and university study, and it can cover exam fees for professional certificates such as CPA and ACCA.

Does it pay everything?
Not necessarily. Support can cover tuition, exam fees, accommodation, upkeep allowance or a combination, based on your assessed needs.

Is there an application fee?
No fee is mentioned on the foundation's public pages. Never pay anyone to apply.

When will I hear back?
The foundation has not published a 2026 timetable. In the 2024 round, shortlisting took place in December, interviews in January and awards in February.

Where can I get help with a problem on the portal?
Use the contact details below. The 2024 application page also listed a separate number for technical help.

Fees and Fraud Prevention

Never pay anyone to apply for this scholarship.

The foundation's public pages do not mention any application fee. Nobody can sell you a scholarship, speed up your application or guarantee that you will be selected.

Apply only through the official Tuendelee Foundation website and portal. Do not send your documents to unofficial email addresses, social media accounts or WhatsApp numbers that you cannot verify with the foundation.

If anyone asks you for money, contact the foundation directly using the official details below.

University of Oxford Scholarship for Undergraduates from Low-Income Countries

Reach Oxford Scholarship

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | 2027 Entry | Oxford, United Kingdom

What this opportunity is: A scholarship from the University of Oxford and its colleges for new undergraduate students from low-income countries who, for financial or political reasons, cannot study for a degree in their own country. It covers the course fee, an annual grant towards living costs and one return air fare per year. It was formerly called the Oxford Student Scholarship.

Host institution: University of Oxford (with its colleges)

Destination: Oxford, United Kingdom

Application route: A two-step process. First you apply for undergraduate admission to Oxford through UCAS. Only if you receive an offer of a place can you submit a separate Reach Oxford Scholarship application.

Study level: First undergraduate (Bachelor's) degree, usually 3 or 4 years depending on the course

Eligible courses: Most Oxford undergraduate courses, except Medicine

Target applicants: Nationals of eligible low-income countries (countries on the OECD list of official development assistance recipients) who have excellent academic ability and demonstrate financial need. The list includes many countries across Africa, such as Kenya and South Sudan, but you must check your own country on the current official list.

Funding policy: Course fee, an annual grant towards living costs and one return air fare per year, for the duration of the course.

Number of awards: Very few. Recent guidance lists around 2 to 3 awards each year.

Key dates (2027 entry): Oxford admission (UCAS) deadline: 15 October 2026 (already passed) | Scholarship application opens: January 2027 | Scholarship deadline: 12 noon UK time on 26 January 2027

Current status (14 November 2026): Upcoming, but only for students who have already applied to Oxford for 2027 entry and hold an offer.

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

About the Reach Oxford Scholarship

The University of Oxford is one of the oldest and most selective universities in the world. The Reach Oxford Scholarship is one of very few scholarships that pays the full cost of an undergraduate degree there for students from low-income countries. Before you plan your application, make sure you understand five key features of how it works:

1. You cannot apply without an Oxford offer: Oxford cannot consider scholarship applications from students who have not been offered a place. This means you must first apply for admission, and win a place, and only then apply for the scholarship.

2. The admission deadline comes first, and it is much earlier: For 2027 entry, the UCAS deadline for Oxford was 15 October 2026, which has already passed. The scholarship deadline of 26 January 2027 is only for students who met the October deadline and received an offer. If you did not apply to Oxford this year, you cannot use this cycle.

3. Admission to Oxford is extremely competitive: You must meet Oxford's academic entry requirements for your course. Depending on the course, this can also include admissions tests, written work and interviews. The scholarship is awarded on top of this, and only a few students receive it.

4. It is for first-time undergraduates: The scholarship supports a first undergraduate degree, and applicants who have not already studied at undergraduate level are given priority. Oxford can consider an individual's undergraduate scholarship application only once.

5. The scholarship is tied to nationality, not just income: Eligibility depends on whether you are a national of a country on the OECD's list of official development assistance recipients (the DAC list), and on your financial need. Check the current official list for your country, since the list is reviewed from time to time.

What the Scholarship Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in the Reach Oxford award

  • Course fee: Your full undergraduate course fee at Oxford.
  • Annual grant towards living costs: A yearly grant to help with the cost of living in the UK.
  • One return air fare per year: A flight between your home country and the UK once each year.
  • Duration of the course: The award runs for the length of your degree, usually 3 or 4 years depending on your course.

Limits and conditions to verify independently

  • Living grant amount: The exact amount and how it is adjusted can change each year. Check Oxford's page when the application details are published in January 2027.
  • Visa and other costs: Oxford's public summary does not list visa fees, the Immigration Health Surcharge, or application costs such as the UCAS fee. Ask Oxford which costs, if any, the award helps with.
  • Medicine is excluded: The scholarship is available for most courses except Medicine.
  • Renewal conditions: Confirm in your award letter whether you must meet any academic or other conditions to keep the award each year.
  • No backup funding: Oxford has said that no additional funding is available for applicants who are not awarded the scholarship, so you must be realistic about how you would pay if you are not selected.

Critical Rule: No Oxford Offer Means No Scholarship Application

You cannot submit a Reach Oxford Scholarship application until you hold an offer from Oxford. For 2027 entry, the deadline to apply to Oxford through UCAS was 15 October 2026. If you did not apply by then, do not wait for the January scholarship call. Plan instead for a later entry year and mark the next UCAS deadline in your calendar.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

The scholarship exists for students who, for financial or political reasons, cannot study for a degree in their own country, which can include displaced students. Oxford's public information does not give separate rules for refugees, so keep these essential points in mind:

  • 1. Eligibility is based on nationality: You must be a national of a country on the OECD DAC list. If you are a refugee in Kenya who holds the nationality of another country, such as South Sudan, Somalia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi or Ethiopia, check that country on the current official list. Do not assume that your country of asylum is the one that counts.
  • 2. Confirm how Oxford treats your situation: If you are stateless, or your nationality or documents are unclear, contact Oxford's Undergraduate Admissions Office before you apply and ask how your status affects your fee status and scholarship eligibility. Keep the reply in writing.
  • 3. Admission comes first and has early deadlines: Plan very early. The UCAS deadline for Oxford falls in mid-October of the year before you would start, so applicants who want to enter in 2028 should prepare during 2027.
  • 4. Academic documents matter: Oxford checks that your qualifications meet its entry requirements. Check Oxford's guidance for your qualification (for example KCSE or another national or international qualification) and for the subjects you need for your chosen course. If you lost documents because of displacement, ask your school or examination body for replacements early.
  • 5. English-language evidence: If English is not your first language, or you were not taught in English, Oxford may ask for an English-language test. Check whether your secondary schooling is accepted and whether a test is required.
  • 6. Interviews and admissions tests: Many courses require an admissions test or an interview, and some ask for written work. Check your course's requirements and plan for reliable internet access.
  • 7. Explain your circumstances honestly: Describe interrupted schooling, camp or host-community school conditions and family circumstances truthfully in your own words, and ask your referee to describe the context of your education. Do not exaggerate.
  • 8. Be ready to show financial need: The scholarship is for students who cannot fund their studies. Details of the financial information required will be published when the application opens in January. If you cannot provide standard financial documents, keep any letters or records that explain your family's situation.
  • 9. Plan for visa and travel documents early: If you receive an award, you will need a valid passport or acceptable travel document and a UK student visa. Start checking your document options early.
  • 10. Apply to the right cycle: If you have not applied to Oxford for 2027 entry, begin preparing for the next admission cycle rather than waiting for the January 2027 scholarship application.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for the Reach Oxford Scholarship, applicants must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Oxford Offer: You must have applied to Oxford through UCAS by the October deadline and received an offer for an undergraduate course. You cannot apply for the scholarship before you hold an offer.
  • Nationality: You must be a national of a low-income country on the OECD DAC list of official development assistance recipients.
  • Cannot Study at Degree Level in Your Own Country: The scholarship is for students who, for financial or political reasons, cannot study for a degree in their own country.
  • Financial Need: You must show that you cannot afford to study at Oxford without the scholarship.
  • Academic Excellence: You must have an excellent academic record that meets Oxford's entry requirements for your course.
  • First Undergraduate Degree: The award is for new undergraduate students. Applicants who have not previously studied at undergraduate level are given priority.
  • Eligible Course: Any Oxford undergraduate course except Medicine.
  • English-Language Requirements: You must meet Oxford's English-language requirements for your course, where they apply.
  • One Application Only: Oxford can consider an individual's undergraduate scholarship application only once.

Is this scholarship right for you?

It is likely a good fit if you are a national of an eligible country, have outstanding grades, have already applied to Oxford for the current entry year and hold an offer, cannot afford your studies, and are applying for a first undergraduate degree.

It is not the right route if you did not apply to Oxford by the October deadline, want to study Medicine, already hold a degree, or are looking for a scholarship at a different university.

Courses and Study Areas

The scholarship can be held for most undergraduate courses at Oxford, across its academic areas, including the sciences, mathematics and computer science, engineering, humanities, languages and social sciences.

  • Eligible: Most undergraduate courses offered by the University of Oxford
  • Not eligible: Medicine
  • Course length: Usually 3 or 4 years depending on the course

Note: Each course has its own entry requirements, subject requirements and admissions tests. Read your chosen course page on Oxford's website carefully before applying.

Application Timeline and Deadlines (2027 Entry)

The Reach Oxford process has two stages. The first deadline has already passed for 2027 entry.

  • Stage 1: Apply to Oxford through UCAS
    Deadline: 15 October 2026 (6 pm UK time). This deadline has passed.
  • Admissions tests and interviews:
    Autumn 2026, depending on your course
  • Admission decisions and offers:
    Expected in January 2027
  • Stage 2: Reach Oxford Scholarship application
    Opens: January 2027. Oxford is expected to publish the full application details at that time.
    Deadline: 12 noon (UK time) on 26 January 2027
  • Selection:
    Expected in spring 2027
  • Results:
    Expected by the end of May 2027

The selection and results dates come from published guidance and may change, so check Oxford's official page.

Portico Deadline Alert:

1. The UCAS deadline for 2027 entry has passed. If you did not apply to Oxford by 15 October 2026, you cannot apply for this scholarship for 2027 entry.

2. If you hold an Oxford offer, the deadline is noon on 26 January 2027. Note that noon is UK time, which is earlier in the day than many applicants expect. Submit at least a few days early.

3. Deferred entry and foundation years: Guidance for earlier cycles says that if you hold an offer for deferred entry you should apply for the scholarship in January of the year you will actually start your course. Confirm this with Oxford if it applies to you.

4. Planning ahead: If you are aiming for a later entry year, the UCAS deadline for Oxford is usually in mid-October of the year before you start. Check the exact date on the UCAS website.

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Oxford Admission Documents (via UCAS)

  • UCAS application: Including your personal statement, course choice, and the Oxford college choice or open application.
  • Academic reference: A reference from your school or teacher.
  • Academic qualifications: Your secondary school results and transcripts, including national examination certificates (for example KCSE).
  • Admissions test results or written work: If your course requires them.
  • English-language evidence: If Oxford requires it for your situation.

2. Reach Oxford Scholarship Documents (Application Opens January 2027)

  • Scholarship application form: Available only to students who hold an Oxford offer. Oxford says it will publish the details in January 2027.
  • Evidence of nationality: A passport or other identity document showing your nationality.
  • Information about your financial situation: The exact documents have not been published yet. Prepare any records of your family's income or circumstances, and letters that explain them.

Important: The scholarship document list may change. Follow exactly what Oxford publishes in January 2027.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Check that you are eligible. Confirm that your nationality is on the current OECD DAC list, that you are applying for a first undergraduate degree, and that your course is not Medicine.
  2. Choose your Oxford course. Read the course page, check the subject and grade requirements, and find out whether your course needs an admissions test, written work or an interview.
  3. Apply to Oxford through UCAS by the October deadline. For 2027 entry this was 15 October 2026. For later years, check the new date on UCAS and Oxford's websites.
  4. Complete any admissions tests and interviews. Prepare carefully and make sure your internet and device work if the interview is online.
  5. Receive your Oxford offer. Only students who are offered a place can apply for the Reach Oxford Scholarship.
  6. Watch for the scholarship application in January. Check Oxford's undergraduate scholarships page when it opens (January 2027 for 2027 entry).
  7. Submit your scholarship application before the deadline. For 2027 entry the deadline is 12 noon UK time on 26 January 2027.
  8. Wait for the decision. Selection takes place in spring, and results are expected by the end of May.
  9. If you are awarded the scholarship, confirm your place, and begin your visa and travel preparations early.

Tips for a Strong Application

These tips are general guidance from Portico Kakuma, not official rules.

  • Focus on getting the Oxford offer first. Without an offer there is no scholarship, so most of your effort should go into a strong UCAS application and, where required, your admissions test and interview.
  • Show real depth in your subject. Oxford looks for academic ability and genuine interest in the subject. Read, study and explore beyond your school syllabus, and write about it in your personal statement.
  • Explain why you cannot study at degree level at home. The scholarship is for students who cannot study for a degree in their own country for financial or political reasons, so be clear and honest about your situation.
  • Get a referee who knows the context. Ask a teacher or counsellor who can describe your ability and also the conditions in which you studied.
  • Prepare for the admissions test and interview. Practise with past papers or sample questions published by Oxford, and practise explaining your thinking aloud.
  • Plan backup options. Because Oxford has few scholarships and offers no extra funding if you are not selected, apply to other universities and scholarships as well.

Selection Process

Oxford looks for students with excellent academic ability and demonstrated financial need. The process has these stages:

  1. Admission to Oxford: You must meet Oxford's entry requirements and receive an offer.
  2. Eligibility check: Oxford checks your nationality, first-degree status and course.
  3. Scholarship application: Offer holders submit the separate scholarship application by the January deadline.
  4. Selection: Applications are assessed in spring, based on financial need and academic ability.
  5. Results: Applicants are told the outcome, expected by the end of May.

Competition is very high, and the number of awards is small. Applying does not guarantee that you will receive funding.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I apply for Reach Oxford before I have an Oxford offer?
No. You must first apply through UCAS and receive an offer of a place.

I did not apply to Oxford by 15 October 2026. Can I still apply for 2027 entry?
No. The admission deadline for 2027 entry has passed, and without an offer you cannot apply for the scholarship. You can prepare for a later entry year.

Does it cover the whole degree?
Yes, it covers the duration of your course, usually 3 or 4 years, although you should confirm any conditions in your award letter.

Can I apply for Medicine?
No. Medicine is excluded.

Can I apply if I already have a degree?
The scholarship is for a first undergraduate degree, and applicants who have not studied at undergraduate level are given priority.

Is there a separate application if I hold a deferred offer?
Guidance for earlier cycles says to apply in January of the year you will actually start your course. Confirm with Oxford.

Can I apply more than once?
Oxford can consider an individual's undergraduate scholarship application only once.

Is my country eligible?
Eligibility depends on nationality and the OECD DAC list. Check the current official list for your country.

How many scholarships are awarded?
Very few. Recent guidance lists around 2 to 3 awards each year.

Is there a school nomination?
No school nomination requirement is stated.

Fees and Fraud Prevention

Never pay anyone to apply for this scholarship or to get an Oxford offer.

UCAS charges its own fee to apply for university, but nobody can sell you an offer, a scholarship or a faster decision. Agents cannot guarantee selection.

Apply only through UCAS and the official University of Oxford website. Do not send your documents or personal details to unofficial email addresses, social media accounts or WhatsApp numbers.

If anyone asks you for money in connection with the Reach Oxford Scholarship, contact Oxford's Undergraduate Admissions Office directly.
