Merit-Based Tuition Fee Discount for Self-Funded International Undergraduates

Cardiff University Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | Autumn 2027 Entry | Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom

What this opportunity is: A £10,000 tuition fee discount for the first year of study, awarded by Cardiff University to a small number of international undergraduate students who show strong academic potential. It is a partial award. It does not cover the full tuition fee, accommodation or living costs.

Host institution: Cardiff University

Destination: Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom

Number of awards: Nine scholarships for 2027 entry

Application route: A two-step process. First you apply for an eligible undergraduate course through UCAS and receive an offer. Eligible offer holders are then invited by email to complete a separate scholarship application form.

Study level: First-year entry to a full-time, Cardiff campus-based undergraduate taught programme starting in autumn (September) 2027

Target applicants: New international students who are classed as fee-paying international students, who are self-financed, and who hold an offer for an eligible course.

Funding policy: £10,000 off the first-year tuition fee only. The award is a fee discount, not cash. It cannot be used in place of a required deposit and cannot be used for any other year of entry or to pay for repeat years.

Scholarship application deadline (2027 entry): 23:59 UK time on Friday 2 April 2027

Current status (14 November 2026): Upcoming. The scholarship is for 2027 entry, and you need an offer from Cardiff before you can apply.

Last researched: 14 November 2026.

About the Cardiff Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship

Cardiff University is a Russell Group university in the capital city of Wales. This scholarship rewards international students who can demonstrate their academic potential. Before you plan your application, make sure you understand five key features of how it works:

1. It is a small, competitive award: Only nine scholarships are available for 2027 entry. Applications are assessed on the quality of your scholarship application and your academic application, together with your predicted and final grades.

2. It covers only part of the cost: The scholarship is £10,000 off your first-year tuition fee. International tuition fees, accommodation and living costs in the UK are much higher than this, so you must have a realistic plan for paying the rest.

3. You must be self-financed: The scholarship is only for self-funded students. You cannot hold non-repayable funding from other sources such as local governments, charities or private organisations, and Cardiff's terms state that applicants in receipt of any other scholarship, bursary, funding or discount are not eligible. Students who receive educational loans are still eligible.

4. You need an offer first, and an email invitation: You cannot apply before you hold an offer. Eligible offer holders are invited by email to complete the application form. If you believe you are eligible but have not received an email, you can contact the International Scholarships team.

5. Cardiff must be your firm choice and you must meet your conditions: You must confirm Cardiff as your firm choice on UCAS (not your insurance choice) and meet all offer conditions, including any English-language conditions, by 31 August 2027. If you do not meet the original published admission criteria, the scholarship will be withdrawn.

What the Scholarship Covers (and What You Must Verify)

Included in the award

  • £10,000 tuition fee discount: Deducted from your first-year tuition fee.

Not included

  • Years two onward: The award applies to the first year of study only.
  • Cash: There is no cash alternative.
  • Deposit: The discount cannot be used in place of any deposit that Cardiff requires.
  • Accommodation, living costs, flights, visa and health surcharge: None of these are covered.

Limits and conditions to verify independently

  • Total cost of your course: Check the international tuition fee for your specific course on Cardiff's website, and add accommodation and living costs.
  • UK student visa funds: A UK student visa normally requires you to show that you can pay your fees and living costs. Check the current UK government requirements before you apply.
  • Other funding makes you ineligible: If you hold or win another scholarship, bursary, discount or non-repayable funding, you may not be able to hold this award. Read the current terms carefully and ask Cardiff.
  • Acceptance window: If you are offered a scholarship, you must accept within two weeks of the award being allocated, or it may be offered to another student.
  • Deferred entry: The award is for the entry year stated and does not transfer to a later year. Applicants may be able to apply for the scholarships available for the later entry year instead.

Critical Rule: Check Whether You Are Truly "Self-Financed"

This scholarship is not open to students who receive non-repayable funding from other bodies. If you already depend on, or plan to apply for, a full scholarship or another bursary, this award may not be available to you. Read Cardiff's terms and conditions carefully and contact the International Scholarships team if you are unsure.

Important Notes for Refugee and Displaced Applicants

This scholarship is a partial award for self-funded students, so it will suit only some refugee and displaced applicants. Keep these essential points in mind:

  • 1. Be realistic about the total cost: The £10,000 discount covers part of the first year only. Before applying, make sure you understand the full tuition fee, living costs and visa requirements, and have a way to pay the rest. If you need a fully funded scholarship, look at other opportunities on Portico Kakuma alongside this one.
  • 2. Other scholarships can make you ineligible: Cardiff requires applicants to be self-financed and not in receipt of non-repayable funding from other sources. If you win a full scholarship elsewhere, you would normally not hold this one as well. Ask Cardiff how your situation is treated.
  • 3. Fee status must be "international": You must be classed as an international student for fee-paying purposes. Cardiff decides your fee status from your admission details. If your immigration or residence status is unusual, contact Cardiff's admissions team early and ask how your fee status will be assessed.
  • 4. Academic documents matter: Cardiff assesses your academic application, predicted grades and final grades. Check Cardiff's entry requirements for your qualification (for example KCSE or another national or international qualification). If you lost documents because of displacement, ask your school or examination body for replacements early.
  • 5. English-language requirement: You must meet any English-language conditions by 31 August 2027. Check whether your secondary education is accepted or whether you need an English test.
  • 6. Explain your circumstances honestly: In your UCAS application, ask your referee to describe the context of your education, including interrupted schooling or conditions in camp or host-community schools. Do not exaggerate.
  • 7. Check email regularly: The scholarship invitation is sent by email, and the acceptance window is only two weeks. Use an email address you can reach reliably, and check your spam folder.
  • 8. Plan for travel documents and visa: If you are admitted, you will need a valid passport or acceptable travel document and a UK student visa. Start checking your options early.
  • 9. No payments and no agents: Do not pay anyone to get an offer, a scholarship or an invitation.

Eligibility Criteria

To be considered for the Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship for 2027 entry, applicants must meet all of the following requirements:

  • International Fee Status: You must be classed as an international student for fee-paying purposes.
  • Self-Financed: You must be self-financed and not in receipt of non-repayable funding from alternative sources. Educational loans do not make you ineligible.
  • An Offer for an Eligible Course: You must hold an offer for an eligible undergraduate degree starting in September 2027 at the point of submitting your scholarship application.
  • Eligible Programme Type: The course must be full-time and Cardiff campus-based, and taught.
  • Firm Choice: You must confirm Cardiff University as your firm choice on UCAS. If Cardiff is your insurance choice, you are not eligible.
  • Meeting Your Offer Conditions: You must meet all conditions of your offer, including English-language conditions, by 31 August 2027, and meet the original published admission criteria for your course.
  • First-Year Entry: The scholarship is for year-one entry in autumn 2027 only.
  • Not a Visiting Student: The scholarship is not available to students who come to Cardiff for a semester or a year as part of a degree at another institution.
  • Application by the Deadline: You must submit the scholarship application by 23:59 UK time on 2 April 2027.

Is this scholarship right for you?

It is likely a good fit if you have strong grades, hold or expect to hold an offer for an eligible Cardiff course, can fund the rest of your costs through family, savings, loans or other repayable means, and do not rely on another scholarship.

It is not the right route if you need full funding, you already hold another scholarship or bursary, you are applying for Medicine, Dentistry or healthcare courses, or you are applying to study outside the Cardiff campus.

Eligible and Excluded Programmes

The scholarship is available to students on most full-time, campus-based undergraduate degree programmes at Cardiff University, across its academic schools.

Not included

All undergraduate programmes in the schools of Dentistry, Medicine and Healthcare are excluded. The list published for the previous cycle included:

  • Dental Hygiene (DipHE), Dental Surgery (BDS), Dental Therapy and Dental Hygiene (BSc)
  • Medicine (MBBCh) and Medicine: Graduate Entry (MBBCh)
  • Bachelor of Nursing (Adult, Child and Mental Health)
  • Diagnostic Radiography and Imaging (BSc), Midwifery (BMid)
  • Occupational Therapy (BSc), Physiotherapy (BSc), Radiotherapy and Oncology (BSc)

Note: Check Cardiff's current terms and conditions to see whether your course is eligible for 2027 entry.

Application Timeline and Deadlines (2027 Entry)

  • Apply for your course through UCAS:
    Follow the UCAS deadlines for 2027 entry (the main deadline falls in January 2027). Check the exact date on the UCAS website.
  • Receive an offer from Cardiff:
    Offers are made after Cardiff assesses your application.
  • Invitation to apply for the scholarship:
    Eligible offer holders are invited by email.
  • Scholarship application deadline:
    23:59 UK time on Friday 2 April 2027
  • Scholarship acceptance deadline:
    Two weeks after the award is allocated
  • Meet all offer conditions (including English language):
    31 August 2027
Portico Deadline Alert:

1. Apply to Cardiff on time. You cannot apply for the scholarship without an offer, so complete your UCAS application first.

2. The scholarship deadline is 2 April 2027 at 23:59 UK time. Do not leave it to the last day.

3. Watch your email. Invitations are sent to eligible offer holders. If you believe you qualify but get no email, contact the International Scholarships team.

4. Remember the acceptance window. If you win, you have only two weeks to accept.

Common Documents Needed to Apply

1. Admission Documents (via UCAS)

  • UCAS application: Including your personal statement and course choices.
  • Academic reference: A reference from your school or teacher.
  • Academic qualifications: Your secondary school results and transcripts, including national examination certificates (for example KCSE), and predicted grades if applicable.
  • English-language evidence: If Cardiff requires it for your course and your background.
  • Passport or identity document

2. Scholarship Application

  • Scholarship application form: Sent by email to eligible offer holders.
  • A short written statement: The form for the previous cycle asked applicants to answer one question in 300 words or fewer: what specific achievements, actions or evidence show that you should receive the scholarship. Text above the limit was not considered. Expect something similar, and follow the form you receive.

Important: Follow exactly what Cardiff asks for in your invitation, since requirements can change each cycle.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Check that you are eligible. Confirm that you are self-financed, an international fee-paying student, and applying for an eligible full-time course on the Cardiff campus.
  2. Apply to Cardiff through UCAS. Choose your course, write your personal statement, and make sure your referee submits your reference.
  3. Receive your offer and confirm Cardiff as your firm choice. Cardiff must be your firm choice, not your insurance choice.
  4. Watch for your scholarship invitation. Eligible offer holders are invited by email. If you believe you are eligible but have not received an email, contact the International Scholarships team.
  5. Complete and submit the scholarship form before 2 April 2027. Give specific, honest evidence of your achievements, and keep within the word limit.
  6. Wait for the decision. Applications are assessed on the scholarship application, your academic application, and your predicted and final grades.
  7. Accept the award within two weeks if you are successful. Awards that are not accepted in time may be offered to other students.
  8. Meet all your offer conditions by 31 August 2027. This includes your final grades and any English-language conditions.

Tips for a Strong Application

These tips are general guidance from Portico Kakuma, not official rules.

  • Focus first on your grades and UCAS application. The scholarship is assessed partly on your academic application and your predicted and final grades, so strong results are essential.
  • Use evidence, not general statements. The question asks for specific achievements, actions or evidence. Give concrete examples with details such as what you did, when, and what the result was.
  • Stay within the word limit. Text above the limit may not be read, so put your strongest points first.
  • Plan how you will pay the rest. Prepare a realistic plan for tuition after the discount, accommodation, living costs and visa requirements before you commit to Cardiff.
  • Keep your email accessible. Check regularly for the invitation and for the acceptance deadline.
  • Apply for other opportunities as well. This is a small partial award, so also apply for other scholarships. Remember that other non-repayable funding may affect your eligibility for this one.

Selection Process

  1. Admission: You apply through UCAS and receive an offer for an eligible course.
  2. Invitation: Eligible offer holders are invited by email to apply for the scholarship.
  3. Scholarship application: You submit the form by 2 April 2027.
  4. Assessment: Cardiff assesses the quality of your scholarship application and your academic application, together with your predicted and final grades.
  5. Award and acceptance: Successful applicants have two weeks to accept.
  6. Conditions: You must meet your original published admission criteria and offer conditions by 31 August 2027, or the scholarship is withdrawn.

Only nine awards are available, so applying does not guarantee that you will receive one.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is the scholarship?
£10,000 off your first-year tuition fee. It is not cash.

How many scholarships are there?
Nine for 2027 entry.

Does it cover all years of my degree?
No. It applies to the first year only.

Does it cover accommodation or living costs?
No. It is a tuition fee discount only.

Can I apply before I have an offer?
No. You must hold an offer for an eligible course when you submit your scholarship application.

How do I apply?
Eligible offer holders are invited by email to complete a form. If you think you are eligible but did not receive an email, contact the International Scholarships team.

Can I apply if I have another scholarship?
Not normally. You must be self-financed and not in receipt of non-repayable funding from other sources.

Can I apply if I have an educational loan?
Yes. Students who receive educational loans are eligible.

Can I apply for Medicine, Dentistry or healthcare courses?
No. Programmes in the schools of Dentistry, Medicine and Healthcare are excluded.

Can I make Cardiff my insurance choice?
No. Cardiff must be your firm choice.

Can I defer my entry?
The award applies to the entry year stated and does not transfer to a later year. Check Cardiff's terms if you plan to defer.

Is there a separate application fee?
Cardiff's public pages mention no separate fee for the scholarship application. UCAS charges its own application fee.

Fees and Fraud Prevention

Never pay anyone to get an offer, an invitation or a scholarship.

Nobody can sell you a place at Cardiff or a scholarship, or guarantee selection. Agents cannot speed up the scholarship decision.

Apply only through UCAS and the official Cardiff University website. Do not send your documents or personal details to unofficial email addresses, social media accounts or WhatsApp numbers.

If you receive a scholarship email you are unsure about, contact Cardiff's International Scholarships team through the official website.

Verify every requirement directly with Cardiff University before applying.

Deadlines, eligible courses, the number of awards and the application form can change each cycle. Portico Kakuma provides this guide as a detailed starting point, not as a substitute for your own independent research.

Before applying, visit Cardiff University's official scholarship page and read the full terms and conditions, check the tuition fee for your course, check the UK government's visa funding rules, and contact Cardiff's admissions or International Scholarships team if you have questions about your fee status or documents.

AfDB–Shanghai Ocean University Undergraduate Scholarship 2027

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | 2027 Intake | Shanghai, China

The African Development Bank Group (AfDB), in partnership with Shanghai Ocean University (SHOU), is offering fully funded undergraduate scholarship opportunities for qualified African students to pursue four-year bachelor's degree programmes in China. The initiative aims to develop African expertise in sustainable fisheries, aquaculture, marine science, engineering, food systems, economics and other fields that contribute to Africa's economic and technological development.

The scholarship is part of the African Development Bank's efforts to strengthen Africa's institutional and technical capacity in sustainable fisheries, aquaculture, marine science and resource management, in line with its Ten-Year Strategy (2024–2033).

Shanghai Ocean University is a research-oriented Chinese university specialising in marine science, aquaculture and ocean governance. The university collaborates with more than 40 international institutions and organisations.

1. Scholarship Overview

Scholarship name: African Development Bank Group – Shanghai Ocean University Scholarship

Academic year: 2027

Host institution: Shanghai Ocean University (SHOU)

Location: Shanghai, People's Republic of China

Scholarship level: Undergraduate / Bachelor's degree

Duration: Four years

Study mode: Full-time, on-campus study

Funding type: Fully funded

Eligible applicants: Nationals of African Development Bank regional member countries

Age limit: No older than 25 years as of 1 September 2027

Teaching language: Chinese

Chinese language preparation: Up to two years may be available for applicants who do not meet the required Chinese-language proficiency, subject to the programme conditions.

2. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

Successful candidates will receive financial and academic support throughout their scholarship studies. The official announcement confirms the following benefits:

  • Full tuition fees: The scholarship covers the full tuition fees for the approved undergraduate programme.
  • Accommodation: Accommodation costs are covered by the scholarship.
  • Meals: The scholarship provides meal support for successful students.
  • Monthly stipend: Students receive a monthly financial allowance during their scholarship studies. The official announcement does not specify the stipend amount.
  • Academic and research facilities: Students gain access to experienced university faculty, academic facilities and research resources.
  • Specialised professional training: The programme includes practical and professional training in relevant academic areas, particularly marine and aquatic sciences.

Expenses Not Covered

Applicants should make financial preparations for expenses that are not included in the scholarship package.

  • International flight tickets to China.
  • Visa application fees.

Important: The official announcement explicitly states that successful candidates are responsible for their own flight tickets and visa fees. It does not provide a detailed breakdown of other possible personal or incidental expenses. Applicants should seek clarification from the university before making financial arrangements.

3. Available Undergraduate Programmes

The scholarship supports four-year bachelor's degree studies across several academic colleges at Shanghai Ocean University. The available programmes include science, marine studies, engineering, economics and foreign languages.

A. College of Fisheries and Life Science

  • Aquaculture: Focuses on the breeding, cultivation and management of aquatic organisms, including fish and other aquatic species.
  • Biological Science: Covers the study of living organisms, biological systems, genetics, ecology and related scientific disciplines.

B. College of Marine Living Resource Science and Management

  • Marine Fishery Science and Technology: Focuses on fisheries science, fishing technologies, marine biological resources and sustainable fisheries management.
  • Marine Resources and Environment: Examines marine ecosystems, ocean resources, environmental protection and the sustainable management of marine environments.

C. College of Oceanography and Ecological Science

  • Marine Science: Covers ocean systems, marine ecosystems, oceanographic processes and scientific research related to the marine environment.

D. College of Food Science and Technology

  • Food Science and Engineering: Focuses on food production, processing, preservation, quality control and food safety technologies.
  • Biopharmaceuticals: Covers the application of biological processes and scientific technologies in pharmaceutical development and related industries.

E. College of Economics and Management

  • International Economics and Trade: Focuses on international business, global trade, economic systems, international markets and trade relations.

F. College of Engineering Science and Technology

  • Mechanical Design Manufacturing and Automation: Covers mechanical engineering, product design, manufacturing technologies and industrial automation.
  • Electrical Engineering and Automation: Focuses on electrical systems, automation technologies, electrical equipment and engineering applications.
  • Robotics Engineering: Covers robotics, intelligent machines, automation systems and the engineering technologies used to design and operate robotic systems.

G. College of Foreign Languages

  • English: An undergraduate programme offered through the College of Foreign Languages.

Important language clarification: Although the programme list includes English as a degree option, the official 2027 undergraduate scholarship brochure states that all listed programmes are taught in Chinese. Applicants should therefore not assume that choosing the English major means the degree is delivered entirely in English.

4. Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy the scholarship's nationality, age and language requirements to be considered.

A. Nationality Requirements

  • Applicants must be nationals of an African Development Bank Regional Member Country.
  • The opportunity is intended for eligible African nationals, rather than all international students residing in Africa.
  • Applicants should be prepared to provide government-issued documentation supporting their nationality.

Note for refugees and displaced applicants: Refugee status or residence in an African country does not automatically establish eligibility under a nationality-based scholarship. Refugees should confirm whether their nationality and available identity documents satisfy the programme's requirements before applying. A refugee identification card should not automatically be assumed to replace proof of nationality.

B. Age Requirements

  • Applicants must be no older than 25 years by 1 September 2027.
  • The programme also allows certain applicants to undertake a Chinese-language preparatory programme of up to two years.
  • Applicants using the language-preparation route must meet the applicable age requirements when they begin their undergraduate study programme.

C. Chinese Language Requirements

The stated Chinese-language requirement for undergraduate applicants is:

  • HSK Level 4.
  • A score above 180.
  • The HSK result must have been obtained within the previous two years.

HSK is the official Chinese language proficiency examination used to assess the Chinese-language abilities of non-native speakers.

D. Chinese Language Preparatory Programme

Applicants who do not yet meet the required Chinese-language proficiency may be eligible to undertake a Chinese-language preparatory programme lasting up to two years before commencing their undergraduate degree.

This provision is particularly important for African applicants who have completed their secondary education in English, French or another language and have not previously studied Chinese.

However, the preparatory route is conditional. Applicants should confirm the admission requirements, age conditions, language progression requirements and financial arrangements with the programme administrators.

E. China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA)

Undergraduate applicants are also required to take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA).

CSCA is an academic assessment used in the admission process for international undergraduate applicants to Chinese universities. Applicants should check the examination arrangements, available subjects, registration dates and any programme-specific requirements before applying.

The scholarship announcement requires applicants to take the assessment but does not provide a specific minimum CSCA score in the published eligibility criteria.

5. Academic Requirements

The official AfDB undergraduate scholarship announcement identifies the CSCA and Chinese-language requirements but does not publish a specific minimum KCSE grade, GPA, number of secondary-school passes or minimum examination percentage.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a particular national examination grade automatically guarantees eligibility or admission.

Candidates should prepare evidence of their completed secondary education and confirm the university's academic admission requirements for their chosen degree programme.

  • Applicants should have completed secondary education or hold an equivalent qualification suitable for entry into undergraduate study.
  • Academic certificates and transcripts should be available for assessment.
  • Applicants should confirm whether their national secondary-school qualification requires verification, authentication or translation.
  • Applicants should check whether additional academic subjects or examination results are required for their selected major.

Important: The above are documents and academic matters applicants should prepare and verify. They should not be interpreted as additional published AfDB scholarship eligibility conditions.

6. Required Documents

Applicants should prepare the following documents in anticipation of the online application and subsequent university assessment.

  • Valid passport or other government-issued identity documentation accepted by the programme.
  • Secondary-school completion certificate or equivalent academic qualification.
  • Official secondary-school academic transcripts.
  • HSK Level 4 certificate and examination result, where applicable.
  • CSCA examination result or evidence of taking the assessment, according to the application instructions.
  • Recent passport-sized photograph, if requested by the application portal.
  • Any additional academic or supporting documents requested by Shanghai Ocean University.

The list above is a preparation checklist, not a confirmed exhaustive list of mandatory uploads. Applicants should follow the actual document requirements displayed in the official application portal.

Documents that are not in the required application language may need certified translations. Applicants should verify the university's translation and authentication rules before paying for these services.

7. Programme Structure and Learning Experience

The undergraduate scholarship combines academic instruction with practical training, research activities and exposure to relevant industries.

The official programme brochure identifies the following learning activities:

  • Lectures and seminars: Academic instruction and seminars led by Shanghai Ocean University professors.
  • Laboratory practice: Practical laboratory sessions and technical training relevant to the selected academic discipline.
  • Research activities: Research-based discussions, academic presentations and group projects.
  • Field visits: Experiential learning through visits to major aquaculture sites.
  • Cultural activities: Opportunities to participate in cultural activities and city tours while studying in China.

Expected Learning Outcomes

By the end of the programme, students are expected to develop:

  • A stronger understanding of modern Chinese aquaculture systems.
  • Practical skills in aquatic organism observation.
  • Experience in environmental sampling and hatchery operations.
  • Cross-cultural communication and teamwork abilities.
  • Academic and technical knowledge relevant to their selected degree programme.

8. Application Process

Applications are submitted online through the official African Development Bank recruitment and scholarship announcement.

  1. Review the official announcement: Read the AfDB undergraduate scholarship vacancy and download the 2027 Shanghai Ocean University undergraduate scholarship brochure.
  2. Check your eligibility: Confirm that your nationality, age and academic background meet the requirements. Pay particular attention to the Chinese-language and CSCA requirements.
  3. Select your preferred programme: Review the available undergraduate majors and identify the programme that best matches your academic interests and future career plans.
  4. Prepare your supporting documents: Organise your identity documents, academic certificates, transcripts and relevant examination results.
  5. Complete the online application: Access the official application portal through the AfDB vacancy announcement and complete the required application form.
  6. Submit your application: Review all information and supporting documents before submitting your application within the applicable deadline.
  7. Wait for shortlisting: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted regarding the next stages of the selection process.
  8. Attend an interview if invited: Shortlisted applicants may be invited to participate in an online interview with Shanghai Ocean University.
  9. Follow further admission instructions: Successful candidates must follow the university's admission instructions, applicable language conditions and institutional regulations.

Submission of an application does not guarantee shortlisting, admission or receipt of a scholarship.

9. Selection Process

The official announcement confirms that applicants must complete the online application and that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment.

The next stages may include an online interview with Shanghai Ocean University.

Applicants should monitor their email accounts and any contact details supplied during the application process for updates and requests for additional information.

The official announcement does not publish a detailed scoring breakdown, number of available scholarships or a guaranteed selection timeline.

10. Application Deadline

Important deadline discrepancy: The official African Development Bank vacancy announcement and the undergraduate scholarship brochure display different closing dates.

  • AfDB official vacancy announcement: 17 November 2026.
  • 2027 undergraduate scholarship brochure: 12 November 2026.

As of 14 November 2026, the deadline stated on the AfDB vacancy page has not yet passed, but the date printed in the brochure has passed.

Applicants should immediately check whether the official online application portal remains open and contact the programme administrators if they encounter conflicting deadline information.

Do not wait until the final day to submit your application. The online portal may close according to its own deadline settings.

11. Important Information for Applicants

  • The scholarship is intended for nationals of African Development Bank regional member countries.
  • All the listed undergraduate programmes are taught in Chinese, according to the official brochure.
  • The required HSK result must be above 180 at Level 4 and obtained within the previous two years, unless the applicant qualifies for the stated preparatory language route.
  • Applicants must take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA).
  • The scholarship covers tuition, accommodation, meals and monthly stipends, but not international flight tickets or visa fees.
  • The exact monthly stipend amount and detailed accommodation arrangements are not stated in the published announcement.
  • Applicants should ensure that they can satisfy the nationality documentation requirements.
  • Successful candidates must comply with Shanghai Ocean University's rules, regulations and codes of conduct.
  • Receiving this scholarship does not create an employment relationship with the African Development Bank Group and does not guarantee future employment at the Bank.
  • The African Development Bank does not charge applicants fees for its recruitment and application processes. Applicants should be cautious of anyone requesting payment in exchange for a scholarship or guaranteed selection.

12. Official Application and Information Links

Applicants should use the following official sources to review the scholarship conditions and access the application process.

Official AfDB application announcement: 2027 AfDB–Shanghai Ocean University Bachelor's Scholarship

Official undergraduate scholarship brochure: Download the 2027 Undergraduate Scholarship Brochure (PDF)

AfDB Virtual Capacity Development Academy: View the 2027 Shanghai Ocean University Scholarship Opportunities

Shanghai Ocean University: Visit the official university website

13. Portico Kakuma Applicant Guidance

This scholarship is a potentially valuable opportunity for young African students interested in science, engineering, marine resources, food technology and related disciplines. However, applicants should carefully evaluate the language requirements before applying.

Students who have completed secondary education in English or French and have never studied Chinese should pay particular attention to the HSK requirement and the possibility of undertaking the preparatory Chinese-language programme.

Refugees and displaced students should pay special attention to the nationality requirement. Eligibility is based on nationality, not simply on being a refugee or living in an African country. If your identity documents do not clearly establish your nationality, contact the scholarship administrators before submitting an application.

Portico Kakuma encourages applicants to rely on the official AfDB and university announcements when making final decisions. Always verify application deadlines, document requirements and scholarship conditions before submitting your application.

Last researched: 14 November 2026. Scholarship information may change. Applicants should consult the official sources for the latest updates.

University of Stirling Undergraduate Africa Scholarship 2027

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | 2027 Entry | Stirling, Scotland, United Kingdom

The University of Stirling Undergraduate Africa Scholarship is a tuition fee reduction programme designed to support eligible international students living in African countries who wish to pursue undergraduate studies in Scotland, United Kingdom.

The scholarship provides eligible students with a £5,000 reduction in their annual tuition fees, with a potential total value of £20,000 over a four-year undergraduate degree.

Unlike competitive scholarships that require a separate application, the University of Stirling automatically identifies eligible students during the admissions process. Applicants must first apply for an eligible undergraduate degree and receive a conditional or unconditional offer.

The award is intended to make undergraduate education more accessible to students from across Africa. However, it is a partial tuition scholarship and does not provide full financial support for accommodation, meals, travel or other living expenses.

1. Scholarship Overview

Scholarship name: University of Stirling Undergraduate Africa Scholarship

Academic cycle: 2027 entry

Host institution: University of Stirling

Location: Stirling, Scotland, United Kingdom

Study level: Undergraduate / Bachelor's degree

Study mode: Full-time, on-campus study

Eligible intakes: January 2027, September 2027 and January 2028

Funding type: Partial tuition fee scholarship

Annual scholarship value: £5,000

Maximum stated value: £20,000 over four years

Number of awards: Multiple

Eligible region: All African countries

Fee classification: International students, including eligible EU students

Application method: Automatic consideration during the admissions process

Separate scholarship application: Not required

Separate scholarship deadline: None published

2. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The University of Stirling Undergraduate Africa Scholarship provides a tuition fee reduction of £5,000 for every eligible year of study.

A. Annual Tuition Fee Reduction

  • £5,000 per academic year: The university automatically deducts £5,000 from the eligible student's annual tuition fee.
  • Up to £20,000 over four years: Students undertaking an eligible four-year undergraduate degree may receive a total tuition reduction of £20,000, provided they remain eligible throughout the applicable period.
  • Automatic fee adjustment: Eligible students do not need to submit a separate scholarship application to receive the discount. Their annual tuition fee payments are reduced accordingly.

B. How Much Financial Support Will You Receive?

The following table illustrates the scholarship's advertised value over a four-year degree.

Study periodAnnual reductionCumulative reduction
Year 1£5,000£5,000
Year 2£5,000£10,000
Year 3£5,000£15,000
Year 4£5,000£20,000

Important: The £20,000 figure represents the maximum advertised tuition fee reduction over four years. It is not a cash payment made directly to students. The actual financial benefit depends on the eligible programme's tuition fees and the student's study duration.

C. What Is Not Covered?

This scholarship is not a fully funded award. It does not advertise financial support for the following expenses:

  • Remaining tuition fees: Students must pay the difference between their full international tuition fee and the £5,000 annual scholarship reduction.
  • Accommodation: University accommodation and private rental costs are not covered by this scholarship.
  • Food and meals: Students must finance their own food and daily living expenses.
  • International travel: Flights from African countries to the United Kingdom are not included.
  • Visa expenses: UK Student visa application fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge are not included.
  • Personal expenses: Transportation, books, clothing, telephone, internet and other personal costs are not covered.
  • Living allowance: The scholarship does not provide a monthly stipend.

D. International Tuition Fee Deposit

Applicants who require a UK Student visa must still pay the International Tuition Fee Deposit as part of the university's standard admissions process.

Receiving the Africa Scholarship does not automatically remove this deposit requirement. Applicants should contact the university to confirm the applicable deposit amount, payment deadline and any available arrangements.

3. Eligible Countries and Nationality Requirements

The Undergraduate Africa Scholarship is available to eligible international students from across Africa. The university identifies the eligible region as All Africa.

The published scholarship conditions focus on the applicant's country of residence at the point of application and international tuition fee status. They do not state a separate requirement that an applicant must hold African citizenship.

Examples of African Countries

Eligible applicants may include students living in countries such as:

  • Kenya
  • South Sudan
  • Uganda
  • Rwanda
  • Tanzania
  • Ethiopia
  • Somalia
  • Democratic Republic of the Congo
  • Nigeria
  • Ghana
  • South Africa
  • Other African countries

This list is illustrative rather than an exhaustive list of separately approved nationalities.

Important Information for Refugees and Displaced Students

The university's published scholarship eligibility requirements refer to living in Africa at the point of application, rather than explicitly requiring African citizenship.

Therefore, refugees and displaced students living in African countries may potentially satisfy the regional residence condition.

However, meeting the regional residence condition does not automatically establish eligibility for international tuition fee status or admission. Refugees should contact the university to clarify how their nationality, immigration documentation, refugee status and intended UK student visa application will be assessed.

Applicants should not assume that holding a refugee identification document automatically guarantees scholarship eligibility or a particular tuition fee classification.

4. Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy all the university's published scholarship conditions to receive the Undergraduate Africa Scholarship.

A. International Student Status

  • Applicants must be classified as international students for tuition fee purposes.
  • Applicants who qualify for UK home fee status may not meet this scholarship condition.
  • The university determines fee classification according to its applicable rules and the applicant's individual circumstances.

B. African Residence Requirement

  • Applicants must be living in an African country at the point of application.
  • The university identifies the eligible region as All Africa.
  • Applicants should provide accurate residential and contact information during the admissions process.

C. Admission Offer Requirement

  • Applicants must receive a conditional or unconditional offer of admission from the University of Stirling.
  • The offer must be for an eligible full-time undergraduate degree programme.
  • The programme must be delivered at the university's Stirling campus.

A conditional offer means that the university has offered admission subject to the applicant satisfying specified outstanding requirements, such as academic qualifications or English-language conditions.

An unconditional offer means that the university has confirmed that the applicant has satisfied the academic and other conditions attached to the offer.

D. New Student Requirement

The scholarship is available to eligible new students starting at the University of Stirling in one of the following intakes:

  • January 2027.
  • September 2027.
  • January 2028.

Eligible students progressing from the University of Stirling International Study Centre may also qualify under the university's stated conditions.

E. International Study Centre Progression

Students progressing from the University of Stirling International Study Centre may qualify for the award if they meet the relevant scholarship conditions.

Students progressing from a Foundation or International Year Two programme must have been domiciled in Africa at the point of application to the International Study Centre.

F. Scholarship Combination Restrictions

The Undergraduate Africa Scholarship cannot normally be combined with another University of Stirling scholarship.

The stated exception is the University of Stirling Sports Scholarships.

Applicants who qualify for multiple university awards should contact the admissions team to clarify which scholarship can be applied to their tuition fees.

G. Age Requirements

The published Undergraduate Africa Scholarship eligibility conditions do not specify a maximum applicant age.

Applicants should still satisfy the university's admission, immigration and other applicable requirements.

5. Academic Requirements and Entry Qualifications

Receiving the Africa Scholarship is dependent on securing admission to an eligible undergraduate programme. Applicants must therefore satisfy the University of Stirling's academic entry requirements for their selected course.

Academic requirements vary according to the applicant's country of education and the degree programme selected. Some courses also require specific subjects or higher grades in particular examination areas.

A. Requirements for Kenyan Applicants

According to the university's published country-specific entry requirements, applicants presenting the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) are expected to have:

  • KCSE overall Grade B or above.
  • Grade B+ or above in any subjects specifically required for the selected degree programme.
  • Any additional course-specific academic requirements stipulated by the university.

Applicants should understand that the general KCSE entry requirement does not guarantee admission to every undergraduate course. Competitive or specialised programmes may require higher grades or particular subjects.

B. Requirements for Other African Countries

The university publishes country-specific academic qualification guidance for international applicants. Requirements differ depending on the national education system.

Examples include:

  • Uganda: Uganda Advanced Certificate of Education (UACE), generally with an average grade of B.
  • Tanzania: Three principal passes in the Advanced Certificate of Secondary Education, with grades assessed according to the university's course requirements.
  • Rwanda: Applicants holding the Baccalauréat or Diplôme de Bachelier may be considered for direct undergraduate entry.
  • South Africa: An average of Grade 5 (60%) across five subject areas within the National Senior Certificate.
  • Nigeria: The university generally requires five WAEC/WASSCE grades of B or above, with no grade below C and additional requirements for essential subjects.

These are examples of country-specific requirements. Applicants should consult the official country information page for their own qualifications and the entry requirements of their intended degree.

C. English Language Requirements

International applicants must demonstrate that they have sufficient English-language proficiency to undertake their selected degree programme.

The university accepts several English-language qualifications, subject to the requirements of the individual course.

Depending on the programme and applicant's educational background, accepted evidence may include:

  • IELTS Academic.
  • Other recognised English-language examinations.
  • Eligible English-language qualifications from previous education.
  • Other evidence accepted under the university's English-language policy.

The exact minimum English score should be checked against the selected course. Applicants should not assume that all programmes have identical language requirements.

If an applicant does not meet the academic or English language requirements for direct entry, the university also provides pathway options through its International Study Centre.

6. Available Undergraduate Courses

The Undergraduate Africa Scholarship is not advertised as a scholarship restricted to a particular academic subject. Eligible full-time undergraduate programmes delivered at the university's Stirling campus may qualify.

The University of Stirling offers undergraduate programmes across several academic areas, including:

A. Computing and Technology

  • Computing Science.
  • Computer Science-related degree options.
  • Data Science-related study options.

B. Business and Management

  • Business Studies.
  • Accounting and Finance.
  • Business Management.
  • Marketing.
  • International Business.

C. Science and Environmental Studies

  • Biological Sciences.
  • Environmental Science.
  • Ecology and Conservation.
  • Marine and environmental-related study areas.

D. Social Sciences and Humanities

  • Psychology.
  • Politics and International Relations.
  • Criminology.
  • History.
  • English Studies.

E. Other Academic Areas

Additional undergraduate subjects are available across the university's academic schools, including sport, health, education, media and communication.

Important: The programmes above are examples of academic areas offered by the university, not a confirmed exhaustive list of scholarship-eligible courses. Applicants must check that their exact programme is full-time and delivered at the Stirling campus before relying on the scholarship.

7. Application Process

There is no separate application form for the Undergraduate Africa Scholarship. Applicants must first apply for admission to an eligible undergraduate programme at the University of Stirling.

Step 1: Choose an Undergraduate Programme

Visit the official university website and explore the undergraduate degree programmes available for the intended 2027 intake.

Select a programme that matches your academic qualifications, interests and career plans.

Step 2: Check the Admission Requirements

Review the academic and English-language requirements for your chosen course.

International applicants should also review the country-specific qualification guidance to determine whether their secondary-school certificates meet the university's entry requirements.

Step 3: Prepare Your Documents

Prepare the documents required for the university admissions application.

These may include:

  • Academic certificates.
  • Official academic transcripts or examination results.
  • Proof of English-language proficiency, where required.
  • Passport or other accepted identity documentation.
  • Personal statement, if required for the selected course.
  • Reference or supporting documents, where requested.

The exact documents depend on the degree programme and the applicant's circumstances.

Step 4: Submit an Undergraduate Admission Application

Complete the university's official application process for your selected programme and intended intake.

Follow the instructions on the relevant course application page. Depending on the programme and application route, applicants may apply through UCAS or directly through the university.

Step 5: Receive an Admission Offer

Wait for the admissions team to assess your application.

You must receive either a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time undergraduate degree delivered at the Stirling campus.

Step 6: Automatic Scholarship Consideration

Once you have an eligible admission application, the university automatically identifies students who satisfy the Undergraduate Africa Scholarship requirements.

There is no separate scholarship essay, scholarship application form or additional scholarship submission required.

Step 7: Check Your Offer and Tuition Fee Information

Eligible applicants should review their admission correspondence and fee information to confirm that the £5,000 annual scholarship reduction has been applied.

If the scholarship is not reflected in the offer or tuition fee information, contact the admissions team at admissions@stir.ac.uk.

Step 8: Arrange Remaining Funding and Immigration Requirements

Students must arrange sufficient funds for the remaining tuition fees, accommodation, living expenses, travel and applicable immigration costs.

Applicants who require a UK Student visa should also follow the university's instructions concerning the International Tuition Fee Deposit and visa documentation.

8. Scholarship Selection and Awarding Process

Unlike scholarships that select a small number of candidates through a competitive essay or interview process, the Undergraduate Africa Scholarship is automatically awarded to eligible applicants identified through the university's admissions process.

The university advertises multiple awards and does not publish a separate scholarship selection examination or interview requirement.

The main considerations are:

  • International tuition fee classification.
  • Living in an African country at the point of application.
  • Holding an eligible conditional or unconditional admission offer.
  • Starting an eligible full-time undergraduate course at the Stirling campus during an approved intake.
  • Meeting the restrictions concerning other university scholarships.

Applicants should remember that automatic scholarship consideration does not mean automatic university admission. They must still satisfy the academic and other entry conditions of their chosen programme.

9. Application Deadlines and Intakes

The university does not publish a separate closing date for the Undergraduate Africa Scholarship. Eligible students are identified automatically through the admissions process.

The published eligible starting dates for the 2027 scholarship cycle are:

  • January 2027 intake.
  • September 2027 intake.
  • January 2028 intake.

Although there is no separate scholarship deadline, applicants must still meet the application and admissions deadlines for their chosen degree programme.

International students should apply early enough to allow time for:

  • University application assessment.
  • Receiving and satisfying any conditional offer.
  • Confirming the scholarship reduction.
  • Arranging the required tuition fee deposit.
  • Obtaining a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS), where applicable.
  • Completing the UK Student visa application.
  • Making travel and accommodation arrangements.

Important: The absence of a scholarship deadline does not mean that admission applications remain open indefinitely. Course availability, intake capacity and immigration processing times may affect the practical application timeline.

10. Important Information for Applicants

  • The award is worth £5,000 per year, with a maximum advertised value of £20,000 over four years.
  • The scholarship is a tuition fee reduction, not a cash grant or monthly stipend.
  • Applicants must be living in Africa at the point of application.
  • Applicants must be classified as international students for tuition fee purposes.
  • A conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time undergraduate programme is required.
  • There is no separate scholarship application. Eligible applicants are automatically identified during admissions.
  • Students who require a UK Student visa must still pay the International Tuition Fee Deposit as part of the standard admissions process.
  • The scholarship cannot normally be combined with other University of Stirling scholarships, except the university's Sports Scholarships.
  • Accommodation, food, flights, visa fees and living expenses are not covered by this award.
  • Applicants should confirm their remaining financial obligations before accepting an admission offer.

11. Official Application and Information Links

Use the official university sources below to explore eligible undergraduate courses, review admission requirements and apply.

Undergraduate courses: Explore Undergraduate Degree Programmes

African country-specific requirements: International Students – Africa

English-language requirements: English Language Entry Requirements

Undergraduate scholarships: View Other Undergraduate Scholarships

International admissions enquiries: admissions@stir.ac.uk

International recruitment enquiries: international@stir.ac.uk

12. Portico Kakuma Applicant Guidance

The University of Stirling Undergraduate Africa Scholarship is an accessible funding opportunity for eligible African students because it does not require a separate scholarship application. Students who meet the conditions are automatically considered during the university admissions process.

However, applicants should carefully assess the financial implications before applying. A £5,000 annual tuition reduction can significantly lower the cost of studying, but students remain responsible for the remaining tuition fees and their living expenses in Scotland.

Students who require complete financial support should not treat this scholarship as a fully funded opportunity. They should first establish whether they have a realistic source of funding for the outstanding costs.

Guidance for Kenyan Students

Kenyan applicants should pay particular attention to the university's published KCSE entry requirement of Grade B or above, including Grade B+ in any required subjects.

Meeting the general academic requirement does not automatically guarantee admission. The selected course may have additional subject requirements.

Guidance for Refugees and Displaced Students

Students living in Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan or other African countries who hold refugee or displacement documentation should contact the university before applying if they are uncertain about their international tuition fee classification or immigration circumstances.

The published scholarship conditions do not expressly exclude refugees. However, applicants must still meet the residence, fee-status and admission requirements.

Portico Kakuma recommends that applicants obtain written clarification from the university before making financial commitments.

Partial tuition fee reduction

Lancaster University Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship 2027

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | 2027 Entry | Lancaster, England, United Kingdom

Lancaster University offers the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship to eligible international students from 12 selected countries and regions who are beginning undergraduate studies in 2027.

The scholarship provides a £3,000 tuition fee reduction for each eligible year of undergraduate study. It is designed to make university education more accessible to international students from countries identified by Lancaster University as underrepresented in its international student community.

Kenya is among the eligible countries. Applicants who are Kenyan nationals or whose permanent home address is in Kenya may qualify, provided they are classified as international fee-paying students and satisfy the other scholarship conditions.

There is no separate scholarship application. Eligible applicants are automatically considered when they apply for an undergraduate course at Lancaster University.

However, this is a partial tuition scholarship rather than a fully funded award. It does not cover accommodation, food, travel, visa expenses or other living costs.

1. Scholarship Overview

Scholarship name: Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship

Academic cycle: 2027 entry

Host institution: Lancaster University

Location: Lancaster, England, United Kingdom

Study level: Undergraduate / Bachelor's degree

Study mode: Full-time, on-campus study

Eligible entry year: 2027

Annual award: £3,000

Funding type: Partial tuition fee reduction

Eligible countries: 12 countries and regions, including Kenya

Fee classification: International fee-paying students

Application method: Automatic consideration through the university application

Separate scholarship application: Not required

Separate scholarship deadline: None published

Eligible campus: Lancaster University Bailrigg campus

2. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The scholarship provides a £3,000 reduction in the student's annual undergraduate tuition fees for each eligible year of study.

A. Annual Tuition Fee Reduction

  • £3,000 per year: Eligible students receive a £3,000 reduction in their annual tuition fees.
  • Multi-year support: The reduction is available for each eligible year of undergraduate study, subject to the scholarship conditions.
  • Automatic consideration: Students do not need to complete an additional scholarship application.
  • Tuition fee adjustment: The award is applied as a tuition fee reduction, rather than being paid as unrestricted cash directly to students.

B. Illustrative Scholarship Value

The following table illustrates the cumulative value for a student undertaking four eligible years of study.

Study periodAnnual reductionCumulative reduction
Year 1£3,000£3,000
Year 2£3,000£6,000
Year 3£3,000£9,000
Year 4£3,000£12,000

Important: The £12,000 figure is an illustration for four eligible years, not a separately advertised fixed total award. The actual value depends on the programme's eligible study periods. Years spent studying away from the university, including placement years and study-abroad periods, are excluded.

C. What Is Not Covered?

The Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship is a tuition fee reduction. It does not provide a complete financial package for international students.

The following expenses are not covered by this award:

  • Remaining tuition fees: Students must pay the balance of their international tuition fees after the £3,000 reduction.
  • Accommodation: University accommodation and private rental expenses are not included.
  • Food and meals: Students must finance their own food and daily living costs.
  • International travel: Flights to the United Kingdom are not included.
  • Visa expenses: UK Student visa application fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge are not covered.
  • Local transportation: Travel between accommodation, campus and other destinations is not covered.
  • Personal expenses: Books, clothing, telephone, internet and other personal costs are not included.
  • Monthly stipend: The scholarship does not advertise a monthly living allowance.

Applicants should calculate their remaining tuition and living costs before accepting an offer of admission.

3. Eligible Countries and Regions

The 2027 Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship is available to international applicants who are nationals of, or have a permanent home address in, one of the following 12 countries and regions:

  1. Canada
  2. Egypt
  3. Ghana
  4. Indonesia
  5. Kenya
  6. Malaysia
  7. Nigeria
  8. Pakistan
  9. Taiwan
  10. Thailand
  11. Turkey
  12. Vietnam

Special Information for Kenyan Applicants

Kenya is explicitly included in the university's 2027 list of eligible countries.

A Kenyan applicant may qualify through either of the following routes:

  • Being a Kenyan national.
  • Having a permanent home address in Kenya.

Applicants must also satisfy the international tuition fee classification requirement.

Important Information for Refugees and Displaced Students

The nationality-or-permanent-home-address wording is important for refugees and displaced students living in eligible countries.

For example, a South Sudanese refugee permanently residing in Kenya may potentially qualify through the permanent home address condition, even though South Sudan is not separately listed among the eligible countries.

However, refugee residence does not automatically establish that a person has a permanent home address under the university's scholarship rules. The university must confirm whether the applicant's particular circumstances and documentation satisfy this requirement.

Applicants should also remember that scholarship eligibility and UK immigration eligibility are separate matters. Refugee status in Kenya does not automatically provide permission to study in the United Kingdom.

Refugees and displaced students should contact Lancaster University's admissions team before applying if they are uncertain about their eligibility.

4. Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet the university's published eligibility conditions to receive the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship.

A. Nationality or Permanent Home Address

  • Applicants must be nationals of one of the 12 eligible countries or regions, or have a permanent home address in one of them.
  • Kenya is an eligible country.
  • Applicants should provide accurate nationality and residential information during admission.

B. International Tuition Fee Status

  • Applicants must be classified as international fee-paying students.
  • Applicants classified as UK home-fee students do not meet this scholarship condition.
  • The university determines the applicant's fee classification under its applicable regulations.

C. Eligible Undergraduate Programme

Applicants must apply for a full-time undergraduate degree programme that is delivered fully on campus at Lancaster University's Bailrigg campus.

The scholarship is not available for programmes or periods of study that do not satisfy these campus and study-mode requirements.

D. Admission Offer and Academic Conditions

  • Applicants must receive an offer of admission to an eligible undergraduate programme.
  • Students must meet or exceed the academic and other conditions attached to their admission offer.
  • Applicants who already have their examination results when applying must meet the published entry requirements for their selected course.

A conditional offer means that the university has offered admission subject to outstanding requirements. An unconditional offer means the applicant has satisfied the conditions attached to admission.

E. New Undergraduate Students

The scholarship is intended for eligible students starting an undergraduate course in the 2027 entry cycle.

F. Repeated Years of Study

Students are not eligible to receive the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship for repeated years of study.

Applicants should therefore understand that repeating an academic year does not automatically extend the scholarship entitlement.

G. Deferral Restrictions

The scholarship cannot be deferred to a future year of entry.

If an applicant chooses to defer their admission offer, the university will reassess the application against the scholarship opportunities and conditions applicable to the new entry year.

5. Academic Requirements and Entry Qualifications

The Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship does not publish one universal minimum examination grade for all eligible countries.

Applicants must satisfy Lancaster University's academic entry requirements for their selected undergraduate degree.

These requirements vary according to:

  • The country in which the applicant completed secondary education.
  • The national qualification presented.
  • The selected undergraduate programme.
  • Any essential subjects required by the course.
  • Any additional conditions stated in the admission offer.

A. Kenyan Academic Qualifications

Kenyan applicants presenting KCSE certificates should consult Lancaster University's country-specific entry requirements to establish whether their examination results qualify for direct undergraduate admission.

Applicants should not assume that the scholarship itself guarantees admission based on a particular KCSE grade.

Some programmes may have additional mathematics, science or other subject requirements.

B. Academic Documents

Applicants should prepare the following academic documents, as required by the university:

  • Secondary-school completion certificate.
  • Official secondary-school examination results.
  • Academic transcripts, where applicable.
  • Evidence of any additional qualifications required for the selected course.
  • Certified translations where documents are not in an accepted language.

C. English Language Requirements

Lancaster University requires international applicants to demonstrate sufficient English-language proficiency for their selected undergraduate course.

The university accepts various English-language qualifications and tests, subject to its admission policies and course-specific requirements.

Applicants should check the required English proficiency level for their intended programme before submitting their application.

The scholarship itself does not publish a separate English-language examination score. The applicable requirement comes from the university's admission conditions.

6. Available Undergraduate Programmes

The Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship is not restricted to a single academic discipline. It is available across eligible full-time undergraduate degree courses delivered fully on campus at Lancaster University's Bailrigg campus.

Lancaster University offers undergraduate programmes across several academic areas.

Additional undergraduate opportunities are available in areas such as health, medicine, education, languages, media, arts and communication.

Important: The subjects above are examples of academic areas available at Lancaster University. Applicants must check the exact course and campus arrangements for 2027 entry before assuming that a particular programme qualifies.

Courses involving periods away from the university, such as study abroad, industrial placements and years in industry, do not receive this scholarship for the periods spent away.

7. Application Process

There is no separate application for the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship. Applicants must first apply for an eligible undergraduate degree at Lancaster University.

Step 1: Explore Available Undergraduate Courses

Visit Lancaster University's official undergraduate course directory and identify a suitable degree programme for the 2027 academic year.

Check the course's duration, campus, entry requirements, tuition fees and available starting dates.

Step 2: Confirm Scholarship Eligibility

Before applying, confirm that:

  • You are a national of, or have a permanent home address in, one of the 12 eligible countries or regions.
  • You qualify for international tuition fee status.
  • Your selected programme is a full-time undergraduate course delivered fully on campus at Bailrigg.
  • You are applying for the 2027 entry cycle.

Step 3: Review Academic Entry Requirements

Check the academic requirements for your chosen degree using the university's country-specific qualification guidance and course information.

Make sure you have the required secondary-school qualifications and any essential subject grades.

Step 4: Prepare Your Application Documents

Organise the documents required for admission. These may include:

  • Academic certificates.
  • Academic transcripts or examination results.
  • Passport or other accepted identity documents.
  • English-language test results, where required.
  • Personal statement, where applicable.
  • Academic references, where requested.

Step 5: Apply for Admission

Submit an undergraduate application through the appropriate university application route.

Applicants should follow the instructions on Lancaster University's course pages and admissions website. Depending on the course and application circumstances, applications may be submitted through UCAS or another university-approved route.

Step 6: Receive an Admission Offer

Wait for Lancaster University to assess your application and issue an admission decision.

Applicants may receive a conditional or unconditional offer depending on whether all admission requirements have been satisfied.

Step 7: Automatic Scholarship Consideration

Eligible applicants are automatically identified through their university application.

There is no additional scholarship form, separate essay or scholarship interview required for this award.

Step 8: Meet Your Admission Conditions

The university awards the scholarship when the applicant meets the conditions of their offer or accepts an unconditional offer.

Applicants who already have their academic results when applying must meet the published academic entry requirements for their selected course.

Step 9: Confirm Your Tuition Fee Reduction

Review the scholarship information in your admission correspondence and tuition fee details.

If the £3,000 reduction is not reflected in your information despite meeting the eligibility conditions, contact Lancaster University's admissions team for clarification.

Step 10: Arrange Remaining Funding

Before accepting the offer, make sure you have a realistic plan for financing the remaining tuition fees, accommodation, food, travel, immigration costs and other expenses.

8. Combining Scholarships and Other Awards

Lancaster University allows the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship to be combined with certain other university awards, but restrictions apply.

A. Scholarships That May Be Combined

Eligible students may combine the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship with:

  • Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship: A separate tuition fee reduction for eligible high-achieving international undergraduate students who meet the academic conditions and make Lancaster their firm choice.
  • Undergraduate International Study Centre Progression Scholarship: A scholarship available to eligible students progressing from the Lancaster University International Study Centre, subject to the applicable progression conditions.

These combinations are subject to the individual award conditions. Applicants should confirm their eligibility for both awards before relying on a combined funding amount.

B. Other Scholarship Restrictions

  • The Regional Scholarship cannot be combined with any other Lancaster University scholarships, except the specifically permitted awards listed above.
  • If an applicant qualifies for both the Regional Scholarship and a scholarship or tuition fee discount from an international teaching partnership, only the award with the highest value will be made.

Applicants should not assume that every scholarship listed on Lancaster University's website can be combined with this award.

9. Important Restrictions and Conditions

A. Study Abroad and Placement Years

The scholarship is available only for eligible study undertaken fully on campus at Lancaster University's Bailrigg campus.

The award will not be provided for periods of study undertaken away from the university, including:

  • Study-abroad programmes.
  • Industrial placements.
  • Placement years.
  • Years in industry.

B. Repeated Academic Years

Students cannot receive the scholarship for repeated years of study.

C. Deferring Admission

The scholarship cannot be transferred automatically to a later entry year.

If an applicant defers their admission, the university will reassess the application under the scholarship opportunities and conditions applicable to the new year of entry.

D. Withdrawal of Scholarship

Lancaster University reserves the right to withdraw the scholarship if an award holder is subsequently found to be ineligible or does not comply with the scholarship's terms and conditions.

10. Application Deadlines

The university has not published a separate closing date for the Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship.

Eligible students are automatically considered through their undergraduate admission application.

However, applicants must still observe the admission deadlines for their selected programme and intended 2027 intake.

Applicants are encouraged to apply early because individual degree programmes may have different application deadlines, availability and capacity.

Students who require a UK Student visa should also allow sufficient time to complete their admission, tuition deposit and immigration arrangements.

Important: No separate scholarship deadline does not mean that applicants can submit university admission applications at any time.

  • Kenya is one of the 12 eligible countries and regions for 2027 entry.

13. Portico Kakuma Applicant Guidance

The Lancaster University Undergraduate International Regional Scholarship is particularly relevant to students living in Kenya because Kenya is explicitly included among the eligible countries for the 2027 intake.

Undergraduate | Bachelor's Degree | February 2027 Intake | Mauritius

The African Leadership College of Higher Education (ALCHE), in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, offers fully funded undergraduate scholarships to academically strong young people from disadvantaged backgrounds across Africa.

The programme seeks students who demonstrate substantial financial need, academic achievement, leadership potential and a commitment to contributing positively to their communities.

ALCHE describes the award as a full-ride scholarship covering full tuition and additional financial support throughout the scholar's journey at the institution. However, the college does not publicly provide a detailed breakdown of every expense covered.

This is the deadline shown on ALCHE's official application page. Applicants should check the live admissions portal immediately to confirm whether submissions are still being accepted.

The scholarship application is not a separate first step. Applicants must first apply for admission to ALCHE and meet its admission requirements before proceeding to scholarship consideration.

Scholarship: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at ALCHE

Institution: African Leadership College of Higher Education (ALCHE)

Partner: Mastercard Foundation

Host country: Mauritius

Study level: Undergraduate / Bachelor's degree

Intake: February 2027

2. What Does the Scholarship Cover?

ALCHE officially describes its Mastercard Foundation awards as full-ride scholarships covering:

Important funding clarification: ALCHE's published scholarship information does not itemise the additional financial support. It does not specify a guaranteed monthly stipend or individually confirm coverage for accommodation, meals, flights, medical insurance, visa or residence-permit fees, or a laptop.
