B. Academic achievement

  • Applicants must meet ALCHE's admission requirements.
  • ALCHE identifies at least a B average in national examination results as an academic expectation for scholarship applicants.
  • Applicants should demonstrate the academic ability to succeed in their chosen programme.
  • Computer Science and Software Engineering applicants must also satisfy the relevant Mathematics or STEM subject requirements.

C. Leadership and community contribution

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Strong leadership potential.
  • Evidence of active participation or contribution to their communities.
  • A commitment to using their education and opportunities to contribute positively to society.
  • The potential to create meaningful impact after completing their studies.

D. Groups especially encouraged to apply

ALCHE particularly encourages applications from:

  • Female applicants.
  • Individuals with physical or learning disabilities.
  • Applicants aged 26 and below.

These are priority encouragements rather than a statement that applicants outside these groups are automatically excluded. Applicants should still satisfy all the general admission and scholarship requirements.

E. Eligibility to study in Mauritius

  • Applicants must be Mauritian citizens, or
  • Be eligible to obtain a student residence permit in Mauritius.

International applicants should pay particular attention to the passport and immigration requirements. ALCHE's admissions information requires international students to have a valid passport for the student-permit process.

Applicants with refugee or other humanitarian status should disclose their circumstances accurately in the application and contact ALCHE before applying to confirm which travel documents and immigration arrangements will be accepted. Humanitarian status is specifically requested in the application, but this should not be interpreted as an automatic exemption from passport or residence-permit requirements.

5. Academic Requirements for Applicants from Kenya

ALCHE publishes a country-specific academic requirement for applicants holding the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE).

  • Applicants must have taken eight subjects.
  • At least seven subjects must have been passed at B grade or above.
  • Applicants applying for Computer Science or Software Engineering must also meet the programme-specific Mathematics/STEM requirement.

Applicants should compare their complete KCSE results with ALCHE's published requirements. A strong overall mean grade should not be treated as a substitute for checking the individual subject grades and the number of subjects required.

Applicants from other African countries should consult ALCHE's country-specific admissions table to determine the equivalent national examination requirements.

6. English Language Requirements

Applicants must satisfy ALCHE's English-language requirements for admission. Accepted forms of evidence include specified English proficiency examinations and qualifying secondary-school English results.

The published admissions information includes IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic and certain secondary-school English qualifications. The required score depends on the accepted test or qualification.

Applicants should consult the current admissions requirements before paying for an English test. Do not assume that every English test is accepted: for example, the published admissions information checked for this listing does not list the Duolingo English Test as an accepted route.

7. How to Apply

The ALCHE Mastercard Foundation scholarship process begins with an application for admission to ALCHE. Applicants should follow the stages below.

Step 1: Apply for admission to ALCHE

  • Open the official ALCHE application portal.
  • Select the Mauritius campus as your preferred campus.
  • Complete the personal information and contextual information sections.
  • Provide your academic history and preferred degree programmes.
  • Upload the required academic and identification documents.
  • Indicate your interest in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program in the relevant finances section.

Step 2: Wait for the admission decision

ALCHE reviews admissions applications on a rolling basis and indicates that applicants can normally expect an admission decision within two to four weeks after submitting their applications.

Only applicants who meet ALCHE's admission requirements can proceed to the scholarship eligibility stage. An admission application is not itself a scholarship award.

Step 3: Complete the scholarship eligibility check

Applicants who qualify for the next stage will be asked to provide additional information to establish their eligibility for scholarship consideration.

This includes information about their financial circumstances and personal circumstances. Only applicants who pass the eligibility check proceed to the scholarship application.

Step 4: Complete the scholarship application form

The scholarship application may request information and evidence relating to:

  • Household income and financial circumstances.
  • Personal and humanitarian status.
  • Guardianship and family circumstances.
  • Previous education financing, including secondary-school tuition.
  • Leadership potential and community contribution.
  • Written and video narrative submissions on selected themes.
  • Referral letters from people in good standing in the applicant's community.
  • Supporting documents verifying the information provided.

Step 5: Complete the ALCHE Fit Challenge

Applicants who reach this stage must complete the ALCHE Fit Challenge, also referred to as the ALCHE Fitness Test.

According to ALCHE, the online exercise takes approximately 25 minutes. It is designed to help the institution understand applicants as individuals and assess their potential fit with the ALU community and learning model.

Step 6: Scholarship review and selection

Once the required application components have been submitted, the scholarship review committee assesses applications to determine which candidates may be considered for an award.

Selection is competitive. ALCHE states that very limited scholarships are available per intake, so meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee funding.

8. Documents Applicants Should Prepare

A. Documents for admission

  • National examination certificate or results transcript.
  • Secondary-school academic transcripts.
  • English-language proficiency evidence, where required.
  • Valid identification documents.
  • Valid international passport for international applicants.
  • Additional transcripts, certificates or achievements, where relevant.
  • Recommendation letters, if available or requested.

B. Documents for scholarship consideration

  • Official evidence of household income and financial circumstances.
  • Supporting documents relating to guardianship or family circumstances, where applicable.
  • Evidence of previous secondary-school education costs or confirmation that schooling was free.
  • Evidence of humanitarian or refugee status, where applicable.
  • Community referral letters.
  • Any additional documents requested in the scholarship application.

Applicants should use the official scholarship application instructions for the exact document formats and requirements. Documents should be genuine, complete and consistent with the information entered in the application.

9. Information for Refugees and Displaced Applicants

ALCHE's scholarship application requests personal information that includes humanitarian status. This gives applicants an opportunity to disclose relevant circumstances accurately.

Refugees and displaced applicants should prepare official documentation that explains their circumstances and financial barriers to education. However, the published scholarship information does not establish a separate refugee admission route or guarantee that refugee identification documents can replace an international passport.

Before investing time in the application, applicants who do not hold a national passport should contact ALCHE and ask whether their particular travel documents can satisfy the Mauritius student-entry and residence-permit requirements.

Applicants should not conceal their humanitarian circumstances or submit documents that misrepresent their identity or immigration status.

10. Application Deadlines and Intake

  • International applicants: 14 November 2026.
  • Mauritian applicants: 23 January 2027.
  • Target intake: February 2027.

ALCHE's official Apply Now page publishes these dates for the February 2027 intake. The international deadline is a date rather than a published time-of-day deadline.

The scholarship process follows the admissions process. Applicants should therefore not assume that a separate scholarship deadline will allow them to begin an admission application after the international admissions deadline has passed.

Admission decisions are normally expected within two to four weeks. The scholarship decision timeline is not clearly stated on the public scholarship page.

11. Important Immigration and Travel Requirements

International applicants who receive admission to ALCHE must complete the applicable Mauritius student-entry and residence procedures before travelling.

ALCHE's published international-student requirements state that the passport should be valid for the duration of the studies, with at least four years of validity, and should have more than two blank pages.

The admissions and immigration process may require additional documents, including medical reports, photographs, police clearance and financial or sponsorship documentation. Applicants should follow the latest instructions in their admissions portal and confirm any costs or requirements directly with ALCHE.

12. Important Things Applicants Should Know

  • Admission comes first: Applicants must meet ALCHE's admission requirements before being considered for the scholarship.
  • Very limited awards: ALCHE does not publish a guaranteed number of scholarships for each intake.
  • Financial evidence matters: Applicants must be able to substantiate their financial need and socioeconomic circumstances.
  • Funding details need confirmation: The public scholarship page does not itemise all living and travel expenses covered.
  • Passport requirements matter: International applicants should confirm that their travel documents meet Mauritius immigration requirements before proceeding.
  • No application agents: ALCHE states that applicants must submit their own applications and that it does not authorise agents to act on their behalf.
  • Beware of application scams: ALCHE states that it does not charge fees for application services. Applicants should not pay individuals who promise admission or scholarship selection.

14. Portico Applicant Guidance

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to academically strong African students who have demonstrated financial need and meaningful community involvement.

Applicants interested in Computer Science or Software Engineering should pay special attention to the Mathematics/STEM requirements. Applicants from Kenya should also check the specific KCSE requirement rather than relying only on their overall mean grade.

Refugees and displaced applicants should contact ALCHE before applying if they have questions about passport requirements, humanitarian documentation or eligibility for a Mauritius student residence permit.

Portico Kakuma recommends checking the official application portal and scholarship instructions before submitting. Scholarship information, deadlines and available awards can change.
